NAME: EL PASO FIELD SERVICES
NARRATIVE: GARLAND GASPARD OF EL PASO FIELD SERVICES WAS CONTACTED ABOUT A POSSIBLE LEAK ON IN SMI 236 AT 4:30PM, THURSDAY, FEBRUARY 28, 2002.  MR. GASPARD CONTACTED MR. JOE HENNESSEY OF THE MMS TO DISCUSS THE INFORMATION REGARDING A REPORTED LEAK.  MR. HENNESSEY STATED THAT CHEVRON/TEXACO WAS INVESTIGATING A LEAK AND THAT A DETERMINATION HAD NOT YET BEEN MADE AS TO WHETHER THE LEAK WAS ON THE EPFS LATERAL OR CHEVRON/TEXACO SALES LINE WHICH PARALLEL EACH OTHER.  MR. GASPARD CONTACTED MR. JIM PRICE OF CHEVRON/TEXACO AT 5:05 PM THAT SAME DATE.  MR. PRICE, LOCATED AT TEXACO'S SMI 236 PLATFORM INDICATED THAT THEY HAD NOTICED A LEAK AT APPROXIMATELY 10:00AM ON THE 28TH OF FEBRUARY.  HE INDICATED GAS BUBBLES WERE VISIBLE AND THAT NO SHEEN WAS EVIDENT ON THE WATER.  HE ALSO STATED THAT THEY HAD ORDERED A DIVING CREW TO INVESTIGATE.  MR. PRICE ALSO STATED THAT HE FELT THE LEAK WAS ON THEIR LINE SINCE OUR LINE HAD BEEN OUT OF SERVICE AND THE PRESSURE GAUGE ON OUR LINE INDICATED ZERO PRESSURE ON OUR LINE.  HE ALSO NOTED THAT THE VALVES ON THE EPFS LINE WERE CLOSED AND FINALLY THAT THEY BELIEVED THEY HAD NOTICED A PRESSURE DECLINE IN THEIR SYSTEM.  FURTHERMORE, MR. PRICE CONTACTED MR. GASPARD AT APPROXIMATELY 9:05PM AND INFORMED MR. GASPARD THAT THE DIVERS HAD FOUND THE LEAK TO BE ON THE TEXACO/CHEVRON LINE.  CHEVRON/TEXACO TOOK ACTIONS TO ISOLATE THEIR LINE AND BY THE FOLLOWING MORNING, THE BUBBLES HAD STOPPED.  WEATHER CONDITIONS AND WATER CONDITIONS WERE ROUGH.  ON TUESDAY, MARCH 5, 2002 THE WEATHER CLEARED AND CHEVRON/TEXACO WAS ABLE TO SEND DOWN ANOTHER DIVING CREW.  THE DIVERS CONFIRMED THAT THE LEAK WAS ON THE EPFS LINE AND NOT ON THE CHEVRON/TEXACO LINE.  MR. GASPARD RECEIVED THIS CONFIRMATION FROM THE DIVERS AT 9:00 AM ON THE MORNING OF MARCH 5, 2002.  THE NRC WAS NOTIFIED BY JIM MCDONALD, EPFS COMPLIANCE DEPARTMENT, OF THIS INCIDENT AT 10:50 AM ON MARCH 5, 2002 AND THE INCIDENT WAS ASSIGNED CASE NUMBER 595652.  A DECISION TO PREMANENTLY ABANDON THE SMI LATERAL WAS REACHED BY EPFS AND THE ABANDONMENT WAS COMPLETED ON MARCH 13, 2002.  IN A FAX SENT BY MR. JOE HENNESSEY, MMS DATED 3/13/2002, EL PASO FIELD SERVICES RECEIVED CONFIRMATION THAT OUR ABANDONMENT PROCEDURE HAD BEEN APPROVED.  THE ABANDONMENT WAS FOR AN 8 INCH GAS PIPELINE.  SEGMENT NO 6872 ASSOCIATED WITH RIGHT OF WAY OCS-G 5941.  FINAL PROJECT COST INCLUDING ABANDONMENT FEES AND GAS LOSS TOTALED $171.342.

NAME: UNION OIL CO OF CALIFORNIA
CAUSE_DETAILS: CAR, TRUCK OR OTHER VEHICLE NOT RELATED TO EXCAVATION ACTIVITY
NARRATIVE: A ONE TON FLAT BED TRUCK WITH ONE PERSON DRIVING STRUCK A CINDERBLOCK VALVE VAULT (VAULT BOX G) AT A HIGH RATE OF SPEED, KNOCKING THE ROOF OFF THE TOP OF THE VAULT AND SHEARING OFF 3 TIERS OF THE CINDERBLOCK WALLS.  THE TRUCK CAME TO REST ON TOP OF THE VAULT WITH A REAR WHEEL TOUCHING A CINDERBLOCK THAT CAME TO REST ON TOP OF THE VALVE.  THE DRIVER WAS INJURED AND TAKEN TO THE LOCAL HOSPITAL WITH NON-LIFE THREATING INJURIES.  THERE WAS NO GAS LEAK, FIRE OR EXPLOSION.  THE PIPELINE WAS ISOLATED AND DEPRESSURED FROM 720 PSI TO 100 PSI TO ALLOW A 17 TON CRANE TO REMOVE THE TRUCK FROM ON TOP OF THE VAULT BOX.  THE ROAD WAS BLOCKED TO PREVENT CARS PASSING UNTIL AFTER THE TRUCK WAS REMOVED.  ONCE THERE WAS ACCESS TO THE VAULT AND IT WAS AGAIN VERIFIED THERE WAS NO GAS LEAK, A UNOCAL PIPELINE INSPECTOR INSPECTED THE VALVE AND PIPING IN WHAT WAS LEFT OF THE VAULT, CONCLUDING THAT THERE WAS MINOR DAMAGE TO THE VALVE HANDLE, BUT THE VALVE WAS STILL SERVICEABLE WITH NO REQUIREMENT FOR REPLACEMENT OR REPAIR.  THE COATING HAD MINOR DAMAGE FROM THE FALLING BLOCKS AND THE PIPING WAS FIT FOR SERVICE, NO DENTS, GOUGES, OR SCRATHES.  THE SITE WAS SECURED AND THE SYSTEM PRESSURE BACK UP TO NORMAL OPERATING PRESSURE.  PLANS ARE TO REPAIR THE COATING DAMAGE; THE REMAINING BLOCK WALL WILL BE CUT DOWN TO GROUND LEVEL AND A NEW CONCRETE ROOF INSTALLED ON TOP SO IT IS FLUSH WITH THE GROUND; AND FOUR 6" BOLLARDS INSTALLED AT EACH CORNER OF THE VAULT AND PAINTED FOR HIGH VISIBILITY.
narrative_clean: a one ton flat bed truck with one person driving struck a cinderblock valve vault (vault box g) at a high rate of speed, knocking the roof off the top of the vault and shearing off 3 tiers of the cinderblock walls. the truck came to rest on top of the vault with a rear wheel touching a cinderblock that came to rest on top of the valve. the driver was injured and taken to the local hospital with non-life threating injuries. there was no gas leak, fire or explosion. the pipeline was isolated and depressured from 720 psi to 100 psi to allow a 17 ton crane to remove the truck from on top of the vault box. the road was blocked to prevent cars passing until after the truck was removed. once there was access to the vault and it was again verified there was no gas leak, a unocal pipeline inspector inspected the valve and piping in what was left of the vault, concluding that there was minor damage to the valve handle, but the valve was still serviceable with no requirement for replacement or repair. the coating had minor damage from the falling blocks and the piping was fit for service, no dents, gouges, or scrathes. the site was secured and the system pressure back up to normal operating pressure. plans are to repair the coating damage; the remaining block wall will be cut down to ground level and a new concrete roof installed on top so it is flush with the ground; and four 6" bollards installed at each corner of the vault and painted for high visibility.

NAME: ANR PIPELINE CO
NARRATIVE: AN EXPLOSION OCCURRED AT THE TANK TERMINAL FACILITY, RESULTING IN A FIRE.  SEVERAL OIL AND DISTILLATE TANKS WERE DAMAGED.    A NEW LOW PRESSURE TANK VENT SYSTEM WAS PLACED INTO OPERATION AND PRODUCED AN EXPLOSIVE MIXTURE OF HYDROCARBON VAPOR/AIR WITHIN THE DRY OIL TANK #1, AND THE LOW PRESSURE FLARE SYSTEM. THE LOW PRESSURE SUCTION SHUTDOWN SWITCH HAD BEEN DE-ACTIVATED, ALLOWING THE LOW PRESSURE BLOWER TO CONTINUE TO RUN, PULLING THE DEVELOPING EXPLOSIVE FUEL/AIR MIXTURE THROUGH THE FLARE SYSTEM. THE EXPLOSIVE MIXTURE WAS IGNITED WHEN IT WAS VENTED THROUGH THE LOW PRESSURE FLARE SYSTEM AND REACHED THE FLARE FLAME, WHERE IT FLASHED BACK AND BURNED AT THE DETONATION FLAME ARRESTOR OUTLET.  AFTER THE DETONATION FLAME ARRESTOR BECAME COMPROMISED, THE FUEL/AIR MIXTURE FLASHED BACK TO THE BLOWER AND INTO DRY OIL TANK #1, RESULTING IN THE EXPLOSION AND FIRE.
narrative_clean: an explosion occurred at the tank terminal facility, resulting in a fire. several oil and distillate tanks were damaged. a new low pressure tank vent system was placed into operation and produced an explosive mixture of hydrocarbon vapor/air within the dry oil tank #1, and the low pressure flare system. the low pressure suction shutdown switch had been de-activated, allowing the low pressure blower to continue to run, pulling the developing explosive fuel/air mixture through the flare system. the explosive mixture was ignited when it was vented through the low pressure flare system and reached the flare flame, where it flashed back and burned at the detonation flame arrestor outlet. after the detonation flame arrestor became compromised, the fuel/air mixture flashed back to the blower and into dry oil tank #1, resulting in the explosion and fire.

NAME: SOUTHERN STAR CENTRAL GAS PIPELINE
NARRATIVE: ON JUNE 6, 2002 LYONS DISTRICT RECEIVED A ONE CALL ON REPLACING A GAS LINE IN SEC 31,30 OF T 23S R 5 W OF RENO CO, KS FOR KANSAS GAS SERVICE BY BRB CONTRACTORS INC OF TOPEKA, KS.  THIS WAS ON THE HUGOTON LINE ON THE WEST SIDE OF THE ARKANSAS RIVER AT HUTCHINSON, KANSAS.  JOHN DUMOND RESPONDED TO THE ONE CALL (TICKET #204363).  JOHN DUMOND MET JOHN KEENER WITH BRB CONTRACTORS OF TOPEKA, KS.  JOHN DUMOND SPOTTED ALL THREE OF OUR LINES WHICH ALL RAN AT A DEPTH OF 63" TO 66".  THE LINES WERE FLAGGED WITH YELLOW FLAGS THAT HAVE OUR NAME AND PHONE NUMBER ON THEM.  JOHN DUMOND WROTE THE DEPTH OF EACH LINE ON THE FLAGS AT EACH LOCATION WHERE HE SPOTTED THE LINES WITH A LINE FINDER AND PROBED EACH LOCATION WITH A SPOTTING BAR.  BRB IS THE GENERAL CONTRACTOR FOR KANSAS GAS SERVICE WHICH IS A DIVISION ON ONOEK.  A&L UNDERGROUND IS A SUB-CONTRACTOR OF BRB CONTRACTORS INC DOING THE DIRECTIONAL BORE OF THE ARKANSAS RIVER.  A&L UNDERGROUND AND BRB WERE ASKED TO EXPOSE OUR LINES TO THE BOTTOM OF EACH LINE WHERE WE COULD SEE THE DRILL STEM AND BITS WERE WELL BELOW OUR LINE. THEY SAID THAT THEY DIDN'T WANT TO DO THIS BECAUSE THEY WOULD LOSE THE CIRCULATION OF THEIR DRILLING MUD.  THE DRILL STEM WORE A HOLE IN THE BOTTOM OF THE SOUTH 20" RIVER CROSSING. BILL WHITEHEAD WAS CALLED AT 4:10 AM SUNDAY MORNING JUNE 23, 2002, BY JOHN DUMOND, BILL CALLED OPERATIONS CONTROL ON HIS WAY TO THE LOCATION. A & L UNDERGROUND HAD CALLED JOHN.  JOHN DUMOND HAD BEEN WITH BOTH CONTRACTORS WHEN THEY STARTED TO BORE THE RIVER CROSSING, AND REPEATEDLY ASSURED JOHN DUMOND THAT THEY WERE 10' BELOW OUR LINE.  WHEN JOHN DUMOND AND BILL WHITEHEAD GOT TO THE SITE, THE BORING CREW HAD MOVED AWAY FROM THE BORING RIG AND WERE WAITING FOR THEM.  JOHN AND BILL GOT THERE ALONG WITH KANSAS GAS SERVICE.  OPERATIONS CONTROL WAS NOT SEEING ANY LOSS OF PRESSURE.  AFTER THEY DETERMINED THAT IT WAS OUR LINE, THEY STARTED SHUTTING IT IN.  DAN JASO AND MIKE HUGGANS WERE CALLED OUT TO HELP OPERATE THE GATES TO SHUT THE LINE SEGMENT IN.  THE LINE HAD 740 PSIG ON IT AT THE TIME.  THERE WAS NO FIRE, INJURIES, EMERGENCY PERSONNEL OR MEDIA INVOLVED WITH THE INCIDENT.  THE LINE WAS ALLOWED TO BLOW DOWN THROUGH THE DAMAGED SPOT BECAUSE OF THE GROUND WATER THAT SHOWED UP WHEN THEY STARTED DIGGING THE LINE OUT TO INSPECT IT.  BRB AND KANSAS AND KANSAS GAS SERVICE BROUGHT IN TRACK MOUNTED BACKHOES TO DIG THE DAMAGED LINE OUT.  GROUND WATER BECAME A MAJOR PROBLEM WHILE EXPOSING THE DAMAGED LINE.  BRB BROUGHT IN A 6" & 8" DITCH PUMPS WHICH ALLOWED US TO SEE THE LINE WITH THE DRILL STEM UNDER IT.  WE WERE NOT ABLE TO INSTALL A CLAMP ON THE LINE UNTIL ABOUT MIDNIGHT SUNDAY NIGHT JUNE 23, 2002.  A & L UNDERGROUND GOT THE DRILL STEM AND REAMER AWAY FROM OUR LINE AND WILLIAMS EMPLOYEES WERE ABLE TO INSTALL TWO BANDS CLAMPS TO KEEP THE WATER OUT OF THE LINE.  WE KEPT ABOUT 10-20 PSIG ON THE LINE BECAUSE OF THE WATER UNTIL THE LINE WAS READY TO REPAIR. BRB WAS HANDLING THE EXCAVATING OF THE DAMAGED LINE AND PUMPING THE WATER ALONG WITH INSTALLATION OF SAND POINTS TO DRY THE HOLE UP ENOUGH SO WE COULD MAKE THE REPAIR.  DUE TO PUMP PROBLEMS, THE PERMANENT LINE REPAIR WASN'T COMPLETED UNTIL WEDNESDAY JUNE 26 AT 9:00 AM.  RONNIE YOUNG AND PETE GARCIA, WILLIAMS GAS PIPELINE COMPANY WELDERS, INSTALLED A FULL-ENCIRCLEMENT.

NAME: COLUMBIA GAS TRANSMISSION CORP
NARRATIVE: AT APPROXIMATELY 11:15 P.M. ON AUGUST 5, 2002, COLUMBIA GAS TRANSMISSION CORPORATION'S (COLUMBIA) PIPELINE SM-80 LOOP (30") RUPTURED AND IGNITED.THE PIPELINE WAS OPERATING AT 748 PSIG AT THE TIME OF THE RUPTURE.COLUMBIA'S GAS CONTROL IMMEDIATELY WAS AWARE OF THE RUPTURE DUE TO THE RAPID DROP IN PRESSURE AND COLUMBIA FIELD EMPLOYEES SAW THE FLAMES FROM A COMPRESOR STATION APPROXIMATELY ONE MILE AWAY. THE RUPTURE OCCURRED IN A RURAL AREA NEAR THE COMMUNITY OF LANHAM, WV IN PUTNAM COUNTY. NO DEATHS OR INJURIES RESULTED FROM THE INCIDENT.THE NEAREST RESIDENTIAL DWELLING WAS APPROXIMATELY 500 YARDS AWAY AND UNDAMAGED. COLUMBIA QUICKLY RESPONDED BY CLOSING VALVES ON EITHER SIDE OF THE RUPTURE TO STOP THE FLOW OF GAS TO THE DAMAGED PORTION OF PIPELINE. BY 12:45 A.M., THE LINE WAS ISOLATED AND THE FLAMES QUICKLY DIMINISHED. THE CAUSE OF THE RUPTURE IS STILL UNDER INVESTIGATION, HOWEVER, PRELIMINARY INDICATIONS ARE THAT EXTERNAL STRESS, IN PARTICULAR THE WEIGHT OF A HILLSIDE SLIP, MAY HAVE LED TO THE RUPTURE. BASED ON THE PRELIMINARY FINDINGS, COLUMBIA AND THE US DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION'S OFFICE OF PIPELINE SAFETY HAVE JOINTLY DEVELOPED A PLAN OF ACTIONS COLUMBIA WILL TAKE TO SAFELY RESTORE SERVICE TO THE PIPELINE. THE PIPELINE REMAINS OUT OF SERVICE UNTIL THIS PLAN IS FULLY IMPLEMENTED.    FINAL INVESTIGATION AND REPORTING INFORMATION WAS FILED WITH THE OPS EASTERN REGION OFFICE. ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS INDICATES THAT THIS FAILURE WAS DUE TO SLOPE INSTABILITY, WHICH CREATED HIGH AXIAL STRESSES AT THE FAILURE ORIGIN AND PRODUCED BUCKLING NEAR THE ORIGIN OF FAILURE.

EXCAVATION BY THE CONTRACTOR OF THE ELEVATED AREA REMOVED APPROXIMATELY 9 FEET OF EARTH ABOVE AND PROTECTING THE PIPELINE. THE FINISHED ELEVATION OF THE STAGING AREA LEFT APPROXIMATELY 6" OF EARTH PROTECTING THE HIGHEST POINT OF THE PIPELINE. APPROXIMATELY TWO WEEKS AFTER COMPLETION AND USE OF THE STAGING AREA VENOCO'S CONTRACTOR FOR HANDLING UNDERGROUND SERVICE ALERT (USA) NOTIFICATIONS RESPONDED TO A USA NOTIFICATION REGARDING A WATER LINE INSTALLATION NEAR THE VENOCO GAS PIPELINE. NAME: GREAT PLAINS NATURAL GAS CO

NARRATIVE: ON SUNDAY, OCTOBER 20, 2002 AT APPROXIMATELY 3:00 A.M. MS. NICOLE HOTZFIELD WAS DRIVING HER FORD RANGER PICKUP WHEN IT LEFT A RURAL TOWNSHIP ROAD STRIKING AN EIGHT-INCH VALVE SITE ON GREAT PLAINS NATURAL GAS CO.'S (GPNG'S) TRANSMISSION PIPELINE NEAR PELICAN RAPIDS, MN. THIS VALVE SITE IS THE TAKE-OFF POINT FOR A THREE-INCH DIAMETER TRANSMISSION PIPELINE THAT SERVES PELICAN RAPIDS. AFTER THE ACCIDENT, THE DRIVER CALLED FOR 911 EMERGENCY SERVICES, AND THEN LEFT THE SCENE OF HER OWN ACCORD. EMERGENCY RESPONDERS CLOSED THE COUNTY ROAD WHILE GPNG EMPLOYEES DETERMINED THE BEST METHOD TO STOP THE RELEASE OF GAS WITHOUT UNNECESSARILY ENDANGERING ANYONE. AROUND NOON ON OCTOBER 20, THE PRESSURE ON THE LINE HAD BEEN LOWERED TO APPROXIMATELY 350 PSIG AND TWO-EMPLOYEES IN PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT USED AN "EASYOUT" TO REMOVE A BROKEN 1/4" DIAMETER NIPPLE FROM WHERE A PRESSURE TAP WAS BROKEN AS A RESULT OF THE ACCIDENT. A NEW NIPPLE WAS THREADED IN A VALVE IN THE OPEN POSITION INSTALLED. FINALLY, THE VALVE WAS CLOSED, STOPPING THE UNCONTROLLED RELEASE OF NATURAL GAS. AT THIS POINT IT WAS UNCLEAR THAT THE DAMAGES WOULD EXCEED $50,000 AND THERE WAS NO EVIDENCE THAT THERE WERE INJURIES REQUIRING I-PATIENT CARE. ACCORDINGLY, THE INCIDENT WAS NOT REPORTED TO THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER. MINNESOTA OFFICE OF PIPELINE SAFETY OFFICER SWEENEY WAS KEPT INFORMED THROUGHOUT THE EVENT. ON MONDAY, OCTOBER 21,2002,A TEAM ASSESSED THE DAMAGE AND DEVELOPED A COURSE OF ACTION TO REPLACE THE DAMAGED THREE-INCH PIPING THAT SERVES PELICAN RAPIDS AND TO MAKE THE REMAINDER OF THE VALVE SITE SAFE UNTIL THE NEXT WARM SEASON WHEN THE LINE CAN BE REMOVED FROM SERVICE WITHOUT JEOPARDIZING SERVICE TO THOUSAND OF CUSTOMERS. AT THIS TIME AN ESTIMATE WAS MADE FOR THE REPAIRS. THE TEMPORARY REPAIRS WOULD COST APPROXIMATELY $20,000 AND THE PERMANENT REPAIRS, APPROXIMATELY $40,000. THE HIGH COST IS DUE TO THE NEED FOR STOPPER FITTING AND TEMPORARY BYPASS PIPING WHILE REPAIRS ARE MADE. BASED ON THIS INFORMATION, GPNG IMMEDIATELY FIELD AN INCIDENT REPORT WITH THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER, 1730 HOURS, OCTORBER 21, 2002. ON THURSDAY, OCTOBER 24, 2002 AT APPROXIMATELY 9:30 P.M CDT, TEMPORARY REPAIRS TO THE PIPING WERE COMPLETED. GPNG WILL COMPLETE FINAL REPAIRS IN THE SPRING OF 2003.

NAME: HOUSTON PIPELINE CO
NARRATIVE: AT APPROXIMATELY 11:15 PM ON THE EVENING OF MAY 20 A PIPELINE RUPTURE OCCURRED INSIDE THE SUNOCO MARINE TERMINAL AT NEDERLAND, TEXAS.  AT APPROXIMATELY, 1:50 AM MAY 21, 2003, CONFIRMATION WAS MADE THAT THE RUPTURE HAD OCCURRED ON THE HOUSTON PIPE LINE TEXOMA 30" LINE.  IDENTIFICATION OF THE RUPTURED LINE WAS NOT POSSIBLE EARLIER DUE TO SITE LOGISTICS AND BECAUSE OF SEVERAL PIPELINES IN THE VICINITY OF THE RUPTURE SITE.  AN UPSTREAM RAPID FLOW DROP DEVICE CLOSED AND OTHER VALVES ON THE SYSTEM WERE MANUALLY CLOSED.  THE FIRE BURNED ITSELF OUT ABOUT 3 AM.  THE RUPTURE AND FIRE DAMAGED NEARBY ELECTRIC LINES AND SEVERAL UNOCCUPIED BUILDINGS THAT WERE PART OF THE SUNOCO TERMINAL FACILITY.  NO INJURIES OR DEATHS WERE REPORTED.  INVESTIGATION AS TO THE CAUSE AND ORIGIN OF THE INCIDENT IS ONGOING; HOWEVER, IT APPEARS THAT INTERNAL CORROSION MAY HAVE PLAYED A PART.  AFTER THE INVESTIGATION IS COMPLETED, HPL WILL FILE A SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT.  THE RUPTURE OF THE LINE OCCURRED AT A LATERAL AT THE FARTHEST END OF THE LINE, WHICH CONTAINED CUSHION GAS.  THAT LATERAL SECTION WILL NOT BE REPLACED.  THE LINE WILL NOW TERMINATE AT STATION 765,  THE PIPE WAS INSPECTED AT ALL POST-RUPTURE CUTS OF THE PIPE FOR INTERNAL CORROSION.  NO CORROSION WAS IDENTIFIED IN ANY OF THE PIPE THAT HAD BEEN IN CONTINUOUS SERVICE.  AN IN-LINE INSPECTION TOOL ("SMART" PIG) WAS RUN FROM THE NEW TERMINUS OF THE 30" PIPE (STATION 765), THROUGH THE RIVER CROSSING AND UPSTREAM TO A TEMPORARY RECEIVER AT STATION 9794, A TOTAL OF 9029' - OR 1.71 MILES.  THE FOCUS OF THE RUN WAS THE RIVER CROSSING UNDER THE NECHES RIVER.  NO CORROSION OR OTHER ANOMALIES WERE IDENTIFIED.  THE NECHES RIVER CROSSING IS TYPICAL OF OTHER RIVER CROSSING ON THE TEXOMA PIPELINE.  IN FACT, THE ELEVATION AND SLOPE CHANGE IS MOST SIGNIFICANT AT THIS SITE DUE TO THE DEPTH OF THE CHANNEL FOR SHIPPING.  THERE, HPL, IS CONFIDENT THAT OTHER RIVER CROSSINGS ARE IN SIMILARLY GOOD SHAPE.  THE PIPELINE WAS RETURNED TO SERVICE ON JUNE 6, 2003. 10-15-04 - CORROSION APPEARED TO HAVE OCCURRED DUE TO STANDING WATER IN LOW SPOT OF A DEAD LEG.  THE PIPE HAD BEEN CLEANED AND PIGGED DURING CONVERSION FROM LIQUID TO GAS TRANSMISSION IN THE LATE 1980'S.  IT IS BELIEVE THE WATER REMAINED FROM THAT OPERATION.  NO OTHER CORROSION MECHANISM WAS IDENTIFIED.  PUBLIC/PRIVATE PROPERTY DAMAGE INCLUDES INTERRUPTION OF BUSINESS AT THE SUNOCO MARINE TERMINAL.
narrative_clean: at approximately 11:15 pm on the evening of may 20 a pipeline rupture occurred inside the sunoco marine terminal at nederland, texas. at approximately, 1:50 am may 21, 2003, confirmation was made that the rupture had occurred on the houston pipe line texoma 30" line. identification of the ruptured line was not possible earlier due to site logistics and because of several pipelines in the vicinity of the rupture site. an upstream rapid flow drop device closed and other valves on the system were manually closed. the fire burned itself out about 3 am. the rupture and fire damaged nearby electric lines and several unoccupied buildings that were part of the sunoco terminal facility. no injuries or deaths were reported. investigation as to the cause and origin of the incident is ongoing; however, it appears that internal corrosion may have played a part. after the investigation is completed, hpl will file a supplemental report. the rupture of the line occurred at a lateral at the farthest end of the line, which contained cushion gas. that lateral section will not be replaced. the line will now terminate at station 765, the pipe was inspected at all post-rupture cuts of the pipe for internal corrosion. no corrosion was identified in any of the pipe that had been in continuous service. an in-line inspection tool ("smart" pig) was run from the new terminus of the 30" pipe (station 765), through the river crossing and upstream to a temporary receiver at station 9794, a total of 9029' - or 1.71 miles. the focus of the run was the river crossing under the neches river. no corrosion or other anomalies were identified. the neches river crossing is typical of other river crossing on the texoma pipeline. in fact, the elevation and slope change is most significant at this site due to the depth of the channel for shipping. there, hpl, is confident that other river crossings are in similarly good shape. the pipeline was returned to service on june 6, 2003. 10-15-04 - corrosion appeared to have occurred due to standing water in low spot of a dead leg. the pipe had been cleaned and pigged during conversion from liquid to gas transmission in the late 1980's. it is believe the water remained from that operation. no other corrosion mechanism was identified. public/private property damage includes interruption of business at the sunoco marine terminal.

NAME: HOUSTON PIPELINE CO
NARRATIVE: HOUSTON PIPELINE WAS CONDUCTING PIGGING OPERATIONS ON A SECTION OF THE TEXOMA 30" GAS TRANSMISSION LINE. LIQUIDS WERE BEING REMOVED FROM THE SYSTEM AND TRANSFERRED TO TEMPORARY STORAGE TANKS ON THE RIGHT-OF-WAY.VACUUM / TRANSPORT TRUCKS WERE REMOVING LIQUIDS FROM THE TANKS WHEN A APPARENT MALFUNCTION ON ONE OF THE TRUCKS SPARKED CAUSING A FLASH FIRE. THE ACTUAL CAUSE OF THE FIRE IS STILL UNDER INVESTIGATION. LOCAL EMERGENCY PERSONNEL IN CONJUNCTION WITH HPL DECIDED TO LET THE FIRE BURN UNTIL IT COULD BE MORE EASILY EXTINGUISHED. NO INJURIES WERE REPORTED IN THE FIRE AND NO DEATHS OCCURRED. A VOLUNTEER FIREMAN WAS TREATED FOR HEAT EXHAUSTION. BELL HOLES WERE EXCAVATED TO EXAMINE THE PIPELINE FOR POSSIBLE HEAT EFFECTS. NONE WERE DETECTED. NO PIPELINE VALVES OR OTHER SURFACE EQUIPMENT WAS DAMAGED. FOLLOWING EXTINGUISHMENT OF THE FIRE, THE PIGGING OPERATION WAS FINISHED AND THE PIPELINE WAS RETURNED TO SERVICE. NO GAS WAS LOST OR VENTED DUE TO THE FIRE.    FINAL UPDATE...AUGUST 07, 2009    THIS INCIDENT OCCURRED DURING A PIGGING OPERATION OF AN INTRASTATE PIPELINE. PIPELINE PRESSURE WAS EVACUATED DURING THIS LIQUID REMOVAL PROCESS, WITH THE EXCEPTION OF 50 PSIG OF NATURAL GAS, USED TO PUSH THE MAINTENANCE PIG. FINAL INVESTIGATION CONCLUDED THAT A TRANSPORT TRUCK, USED TO HAUL THE CONDENSATE FROM THIS SITE, EXPERIENCED A MALFUNCTION OF A SAFETY SWITCH ON THE DIESEL ENGINE, RESULTING IN IGNITION OF THE VAPORS OFF THE FRAC TANKS.  THE ONLY PRODUCT LOSS DURING THIS INCIDENT WAS THE LIQUID CONDENSATE DURING THE FIRE. PROPERTY DAMAGES WERE LIMITED TO THE FRAC TANKS AND DIESEL TRUCKS OWNED BY THE THIRD PARTY CONTRACTOR. THERE WERE NO ADDITIONAL DAMAGES TO COMPANY FACILITIES OR PROPERTY.
narrative_clean: houston pipeline was conducting pigging operations on a section of the texoma 30" gas transmission line. liquids were being removed from the system and transferred to temporary storage tanks on the right-of-way.vacuum / transport trucks were removing liquids from the tanks when a apparent malfunction on one of the trucks sparked causing a flash fire. the actual cause of the fire is still under investigation. local emergency personnel in conjunction with hpl decided to let the fire burn until it could be more easily extinguished. no injuries were reported in the fire and no deaths occurred. a volunteer fireman was treated for heat exhaustion. bell holes were excavated to examine the pipeline for possible heat effects. none were detected. no pipeline valves or other surface equipment was damaged. following extinguishment of the fire, the pigging operation was finished and the pipeline was returned to service. no gas was lost or vented due to the fire. final update...august 07, 2009 this incident occurred during a pigging operation of an intrastate pipeline. pipeline pressure was evacuated during this liquid removal process, with the exception of 50 psig of natural gas, used to push the maintenance pig. final investigation concluded that a transport truck, used to haul the condensate from this site, experienced a malfunction of a safety switch on the diesel engine, resulting in ignition of the vapors off the frac tanks. the only product loss during this incident was the liquid condensate during the fire. property damages were limited to the frac tanks and diesel trucks owned by the third party contractor. there were no additional damages to company facilities or property.

NARRATIVE: UPON COMPLETION OF THE FAILURE INVESTIGATION, A FINAL REPORT WILL BE SUBMITTED. 3-12-04 A FAILURE ANALYSIS INDICATED THA THE LEAK OCCURRED AS A RESULT OF THE INITIATION AND PROPAGATION OF A CRACK AT THE APEX OF A DENT ON THE ID SURFACE OF THE PIPE. THERE WAS NO EVIDENCE THAT THE CRACKING WAS ASSOCIATED WITH ANY METALLURGICAL DEFICIENCY IN THE PIPE.  THE MECHANICAL PROPERTIES OF THE STEEL MEET THE SPECIFICATIONS FOR API 5L X-65 LINE PIPE AND THE MICROSTRUCTURE IS TYPICAL OF THIS VINTAGE AND GRADE OF PIPE STEEL. NAME: TRUNKLINE GAS CO
NARRATIVE: UNIT #4303 COMPRESSOR WAS BEING PRESSURED UP, WHEN THE GAS PRESSURE ACTING ON THE SUCTION COMPRESSOR VALVE CAP CAUSED 3 BOLTS CONTAINING FATIGUE CRACKS TO FAIL.  FAILURE OF THESE BOLTS PUT ADDITIONAL STRESS ON THE REMAINING BOLTS BEYOND THEIR CAPABILITY TO RESIST THAT STRESS, RESULTING IN THEIR EVENTUAL FAILURE AND FAILURE OF THE COMPRESSOR VALVE CAP THAT THEY WERE RESTRAINING.  THE FAILURE OF THE COMPRESSOR VALVE CAP RESULTED IN A NATURAL GAS RELEASE FROM THE COMPRESSOR CYLINDER INTO THE COMPRESSOR BUILDING.  THE NATURAL GAS FROM THE COMPRESSOR CYLINDER WAS IGNITED BY AN UNKNOWN IGNITION SOURCE, RESULTING IN AN EXPLOSION AND FIRE. THE COMPRESSOR STATION ESD WAS ACTIVATED, WHICH RESULTED IN DEPRIVATION OF A FUEL SOURCE TO THE FIRE AND THE FIRE QUICKLY BURNED ITSELF OUT.
narrative_clean: unit #4303 compressor was being pressured up, when the gas pressure acting on the suction compressor valve cap caused 3 bolts containing fatigue cracks to fail. failure of these bolts put additional stress on the remaining bolts beyond their capability to resist that stress, resulting in their eventual failure and failure of the compressor valve cap that they were restraining. the failure of the compressor valve cap resulted in a natural gas release from the compressor cylinder into the compressor building. the natural gas from the compressor cylinder was ignited by an unknown ignition source, resulting in an explosion and fire. the compressor station esd was activated, which resulted in deprivation of a fuel source to the fire and the fire quickly burned itself out.

NAME: SOUTH CAROLINA PIPELINE CORP
NARRATIVE: AT 12:17 PM ON DECEMBER 17, 2003, SOUTH CAROLINA PIPELINE CORPORATION RECEIVED NOTIFICATION THAT A THIRD PARTY CONTRACTOR CONDUCTING SOIL BORE TESTS HAD STRUCK A NATURAL GAS TRANSMISSION PIPELINE ON FRONT STREET IN THE CITY OF GEORGETOWN NEAR METER & REGULATION STATION 27-200.  THE PIPELINE WAS PUNCTURED BY THE SAMPLING APPARATUS AND GAS WAS ESCAPING. THE GEORGETOWN FIRE DEPARTMENT AND POLICE DEPARTMENT RESPONDED AND ISOLATED THE AREA.  SOUTH CAROLINA PIPELINE CORPORATION PERSONNEL RESPONDED TO THE SCENE, EVALUATED THE SITUATION, AND ISOLATED THE IMPACTED SECTION OF LINE.  THE LINE WAS SUBSEQUENTLY REPAIRED BY CUTTING OUT THE DAMAGED SECTION OF PIPE AND REPLACING IT WITH PRE-TESTED PIPE.  THE INTERNAL INVESTIGATION OF THE INCIDENT DETERMINED THAT THE THIRD PARTY CONTRACTOR APPARENTLY DRILLED OUTSIDE OF THE AREA THAT HAD BEEN PREVIOUSLY CLEARED BY SOUTH CAROLINA PIPELINE CORPORATION RIGHT-OF-WAY DEPARTMENT PERSONNEL.

NARRATIVE: EMPLOYEES PROCEEDED TO BLOWOFF M18B TO SHORT CYCLE VALVE. THEY THEN ATTEMPTED TO OPERATE THE 3 WAY VALVE ON THE EMERGENCY BLOW DOWN SIGNAL LINE COMING INTO THE VALVE TO MAKE THE BLOW OFF VALVE OPERATE. AS THEY STARTED TO TURN THE HANDLE, THE 1/2" NIPPLE THAT IS ON THE UPSTREAM SIDE OF THE 3 WAY VALVE BROKE INTO RELEASING HIGH PRESSURE GAS. NAME: DOMINION TRANSMISSION INC
NARRATIVE: ON 03/12/04 AT APPROXIMATELY 12 AM, BIG RUN COMPRESSOR STATION LOST PURCHASE POWER.  AT APPROXIMATELY 2:45 AM, THE UPS BACKUP BATTERIES FOR COMPUTER CONTROLS LOST THEIR ELECTRIC CURRENT CHARGE.  WITH NO BACKUP BATTERIES OPERATING AS THEY SHOULD, AN ESD OCCURRED ALTHOUGH THE DISCHARGE FIRE GATE DID NOT MOVE TO THE CLOSED POSITION. THEREFORE, THE COMPRESOR STATION WAS NOT ISOLATED FROM THE PIPELINE TL-280.  THE SUCTION FIRE GATE DID OPERATE PROPERLY.  NATURAL GAS PROCEEDED TO VENT OUT OF THE DISCHARGE HEADER FROM THE STATION AND PIPELINE TL-280.  THE TUBING LINE FOR THE PILOT AIR TO THE OPERATOR WAS BELIEVED TO HAVE SOME MOISTURE / CONDENSATE THAT COULD HAVE POSSIBLY FROZEN DUE TO BELOW FREEZING TEMPERATURES PREVENTING THE VALVE TO OPERATE.  A FULL ESD TEST WAS PERFORMED AFTER THE VALVE WAS INSPECTED.  ALL COMPONENTS WORKED PROPERLY.  TOTAL VALVE MOVEMENT WAS COMPLETED IN 15.4 SECONDS.  THE ESD SYSTEM WAS RESET AND THE UNIT WAS PUT BACK ON LINE AT 17:00.  STATION PERSONNEL MONITORED CONDITIONS UNTIL 20:00, WHEN CONDITIONS WERE BACK TO NORMAL.
narrative_clean: on 03/12/04 at approximately 12 am, big run compressor station lost purchase power. at approximately 2:45 am, the ups backup batteries for computer controls lost their electric current charge. with no backup batteries operating as they should, an esd occurred although the discharge fire gate did not move to the closed position. therefore, the compresor station was not isolated from the pipeline tl-280. the suction fire gate did operate properly. natural gas proceeded to vent out of the discharge header from the station and pipeline tl-280. the tubing line for the pilot air to the operator was believed to have some moisture / condensate that could have possibly frozen due to below freezing temperatures preventing the valve to operate. a full esd test was performed after the valve was inspected. all components worked properly. total valve movement was completed in 15.4 seconds. the esd system was reset and the unit was put back on line at 17:00. station personnel monitored conditions until 20:00, when conditions were back to normal.

NAME: SOUTHERN STAR CENTRAL GAS PIPELINE, INC
NARRATIVE: FROM THE STATION EVENT LOG, IT APPEARS THAT DUE TO A LIGHTNING STRIKE NEAR THE CONTROL BUILDING, THE ESD SOLENOID TRIPPED OUT INITIATING ESD.  NORMALLY THE ESD  SOLENOID IS HELD ENERGIZED BY BOTH THE FIRE AND GAS DETECTION SYSTEMS AS WELL AS SOME MANUAL PUSH BUTTONS.  ALL OF THESE THINGS HAVE INDIVIDUAL ANNUNCIATION ATTACHED TO THEM AND NOTHING WAS ANNUCIATED BY SCADA.  IT WOULD APPEAR THAT THE LIGHTNING GENERATED A CHANGE IN VOLTAGE ON THE ESD DC VOLTAGE SYSTEM CAUSING THE ESD TO TRIP. AT 2:00 AM, GAS CONTROL NOTIFIED ANDREW BUCHANON THAT THE STATION HAD ESDED.  WHEN THE OPERATORS ARRIVED AT THE STATION, THE BLOWOFFS WERE STILL BLOWING.  THE BLOWOFFS WERE CLOSED WHEN THE OPERATORS DETERMINED IT WAS SAFE TO CLOSE THEM.  THE REASON THE ESD BLOWOFFS WERE STILL BLOWING WAS BECAUSE GATE NUMBER 55 HAD FAILED TO CLOSE AS IT SHOULD HAVE DURING A NORMAL ESD.  IT WAS DETERMINED THE REASON VALVE 55 DID NOT CLOSE WAS A RUSTED ACTUATOR PISTON ON THE OPERATOR.  THE ACUTATOR WAS REPAIRED AND THE GATE RETURNED TO SERVICE.
narrative_clean: from the station event log, it appears that due to a lightning strike near the control building, the esd solenoid tripped out initiating esd. normally the esd solenoid is held energized by both the fire and gas detection systems as well as some manual push buttons. all of these things have individual annunciation attached to them and nothing was annuciated by scada. it would appear that the lightning generated a change in voltage on the esd dc voltage system causing the esd to trip. at 2:00 am, gas control notified andrew buchanon that the station had esded. when the operators arrived at the station, the blowoffs were still blowing. the blowoffs were closed when the operators determined it was safe to close them. the reason the esd blowoffs were still blowing was because gate number 55 had failed to close as it should have during a normal esd. it was determined the reason valve 55 did not close was a rusted actuator piston on the operator. the acutator was repaired and the gate returned to service.

NARRATIVE: IN 2003, A CONTRACTOR WAS REATTACHING THE PULSATION BOTTLE ON UNIT E201.  HE INSERTED A NEW FLANGE GASKET BETWEEN THE COMPRESSOR CYLINDER AND THE FLANGE OF THE PULSATION BOTTLE.  THE GASKET USED WAS LISTED AS APPROVED IN THE COMPANY PROCEDURES FOR THAT PRESSURE AND APPLICATION.  THE CONTRACTOR TORQUED THE BOLTS ACCORDING TO THE TORQUE VALUE GIVEN TO HIM. A CONTRIBUTING FACTOR WAS THAT THE ACTUAL PRESSURE RATING OF THE GASKET USED WAS LOWER THAN THE RANGE SPECIFIED IN THE COMPANY PROCEDURES.  PRIMARY CAUSE WAS DETERMINED TO BE THE INCORRECTLY TORQUED BOLTS WITH A CONTRIBUTING FACTOR OF INADEQUATE PRESSURE RATING FOR THE GASKET ALLOWED BY THE COMPANY PROCEDURES.

NAME: NORTHERN NATURAL GAS CO
CAUSE: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD
NARRATIVE: AT 11:45 PM ON SEPTEMBER 6, 2004 NORTHERNS GAS CONTROL RECEIVED NOTIFICATION THAT THE NORTHRUP COMPRESSOR STATION  HAD EXPERIENCED AN ESD.  GAS CONTROL HAD ALSO RECEIVED ALARM SIGNALS FROM BOTH THE GAS AND FIRE DETECTION SYSTEMS.  AT 12:02 AM ON SEPTEMBER 7, 2004 NORTHERNS OPERATIONS COMMUNICATION CENTER (OCC) RECEIVED A CALL FROM THE OCHILTREE COUNTY, TX SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT REPORTING AN EXPLOSION AND FIRE AT THE NORTHRUP COMPRESSOR STATION.  THE STATION WAS UNMANNED AT THE TIME AND NO INJURIES WERE REPORTED.  THE NORTHRUP COMPRESSOR STATION IS LOCATED 6 MILES SOUTH OF PERRYTOWN, TX ON US HIGHWAY 83.  THE STATION HAS TWO NATURAL GAS COMPRESSOR UNITS AND A STATION DEHYDRATION UNIT, AND COMPRESSES GAS RECEIVED FROM GATHERING FIELDS INTO THE TEXAS A-LINE (TXM10301) UPSTREAM OF THE BEAVER COMPRESSOR STATION.  THE STATION WAS FLOWING 27 MMCF/D AT THE TIME OF THE ESD.  THE CAUSE OF THE INCIDENT WAS A JACK BOLT ON THE OUTBOUND DISCHARGE VALVE CAP ON COMPRESSOR CYLINDER FOUR OF UNIT ONE CAME LOOSE AND ALLOWED GAS TO ESCAPE INTO THE ENGINE ROOM.  A JACK BOLT IS A VERY LONG BOLT THAT THREADS THROUGH THE CENTER OF THE COMPRESSOR VALVE CAP.  ITS PURPOSE IS TOE PUSH THE VALVE TO THE POINT THAT IT COMPRESSES THE GASKET WHEN THE VALVE IS INSTALLED, THUS FORMING A NECESSARY SEAL.  THE JACK BOLT PROTRUDES OUT OF THE AP COMPLETELY AND HAS A LOCK NUT THAT IS TIGHTENED AGAINST THE CAP.  GAS LEAKING FROM THE MISSING JACK BOLT WAS MOST LIKELY IGNITED BY DEBRIS EXITING THE LEAK AND STRIKING STRUCTURAL STEEL ADJACENT TO THE UNIT. THE RESULTING EXPLOSION CAUSED EXTENSIVE DAMAGE TO THE BUILDING SKIN, DOORS, WINDOWS AND LIGHTER SUPPORT PURLINS.  FIRE DAMAGE WAS LIMITED AND MINIMAL.  IN ORDER TO COME LOOSE THE JACK BOLT WOULD HAVE HAD TO LOSE PRELOAD.  PRELOAD COULD HAVE BEEN LOST DUE TO GASKET FAILURE, VALVE FAILURE, IMPROPER TORQUEING, OR IMPROPER VALVE ASSEMBLY.  AN AUGUST 25, 2004 COMPRESSOR ANALYSIS SHOWED NO INDICATION OF IMPROPER VALVE ASSEMBLY.  THERE ARE NO FINDINGS THAT PROVIDE AN ABSOLUTE DETERMINATION OF THE CAUSE OF THE FAILURE.  IT MAY HAVE BEEN A COMBINATION OF THE FACTORS ABOVE OR IT MAY HAVE BEEN A FACTOR NOT YET CONSIDERED.
narrative_clean: at 11:45 pm on september 6, 2004 northerns gas control received notification that the northrup compressor station had experienced an esd. gas control had also received alarm signals from both the gas and fire detection systems. at 12:02 am on september 7, 2004 northerns operations communication center (occ) received a call from the ochiltree county, tx sheriff's department reporting an explosion and fire at the northrup compressor station. the station was unmanned at the time and no injuries were reported. the northrup compressor station is located 6 miles south of perrytown, tx on us highway 83. the station has two natural gas compressor units and a station dehydration unit, and compresses gas received from gathering fields into the texas a-line (txm10301) upstream of the beaver compressor station. the station was flowing 27 mmcf/d at the time of the esd. the cause of the incident was a jack bolt on the outbound discharge valve cap on compressor cylinder four of unit one came loose and allowed gas to escape into the engine room. a jack bolt is a very long bolt that threads through the center of the compressor valve cap. its purpose is toe push the valve to the point that it compresses the gasket when the valve is installed, thus forming a necessary seal. the jack bolt protrudes out of the ap completely and has a lock nut that is tightened against the cap. gas leaking from the missing jack bolt was most likely ignited by debris exiting the leak and striking structural steel adjacent to the unit. the resulting explosion caused extensive damage to the building skin, doors, windows and lighter support purlins. fire damage was limited and minimal. in order to come loose the jack bolt would have had to lose preload. preload could have been lost due to gasket failure, valve failure, improper torqueing, or improper valve assembly. an august 25, 2004 compressor analysis showed no indication of improper valve assembly. there are no findings that provide an absolute determination of the cause of the failure. it may have been a combination of the factors above or it may have been a factor not yet considered.

NAME: COLUMBIA GAS TRANSMISSION CORP
NARRATIVE: BACKGROUND    AT APPROXIMATELY 11:05 PM ON SEPTEMBER 16, 2004 THE UNLOADER BOTTLE ON COMPRESSOR CYLINDER #5 OF UNIT #4, A CLARK TLA-10, AT LUCAS COMPRESSOR STATION FAILED CAUSING A STATION BLOW-DOWN, WHICH TRIGGERED THE ESD SYSTEM. DURING THE STATION BLOW-DOWN, FIRE GATES ON SL-3054 AND SL-3136 FAILED TO CLOSE RESULTING IN A GAS LOST OF 11,758 MCF. THE TOTAL COST FOR THIS INCIDENT WAS $69,907.     FAILURE ANALYSIS     COOK MANLEY CONDUCTED A FAILURE ANALYSIS ON THE UNLOADER BOTTLE (SEE ATTACHED REPORT) AND DETERMINED THAT THE ROOT CAUSE OF THIS FAILURE WAS A DATA ENTRY ERROR IN THE BOLT SIZING PROGRAM. COOK MANLEY ALSO INVESTIGATED ALL OTHER UNLOADER BOTTLES INSTALLED ON COMPRESSOR UNITS FOR THE LAST FIVE YEARS AND HAVE CONFIRMED THAT CALCULATIONS FOR ALL OTHER ASSEMBLIES ARE CORRECT.    COLUMBIA CONDUCTED A ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS FOR THE ESD FAILURE AND DETERMINED THAT THE 1" COMPRESSED AIR ESD SUPPLY LINE HAD PLUGGED OFF DUE TO BLACK POWDER LIKE MATERIAL. THE SYSTEM WAS CLEANED AND THE ESD WAS RE-TESTED AND PERFORMED TO SATISFACTION.    REMEDIAL ACTION    COOK MANLEY WILL REPLACE THE AFFECTED ASSEMBLIES. COLUMBIA HAS REQUESTED THAT COOK MANLEY SUPPLY 0.750 INCH BOLTS WITH 16 THREADS PER INCH TO SECURE THE ACTUATOR TO THE VALVE CAP. THIS STUD SIZE IS IN EXCESS OF WHAT IS REQUIRED HOWEVER IT WILL SERVE TO FURTHER BOLSTER THE SAFETY FACTOR ON THIS UNIT.   COOK MANLEY WILL ALSO TAKE THE FOLLOWING CORRECTIVE ACTION TO FURTHER REDUCE THE CHANCES OF SUCH AN ERROR FROM HAPPENING AGAIN:    1) THE COMPUTER PROGRAM WILL BE REVISED TO INCLUDE A NOTE, REMINDING DESIGNERS OF THE IMPLICATIONS AND IMPORTANCE OF USING SUCTION PRESSURE INSTEAD OF AMBIENT PRESSURE.   2) A FUTURE REVISION TO THE PROGRAM WILL REQUIRE THE DESIGNER TO SELECT THE PROPER ASSEMBLY AND THEN PROMPT THE USER FOR THE CORRECT PRESSURE.   3) COOK MANLEY IS REVIEWING ALL OF THE CRITICAL CALCULATIONS IN OUR DESIGNS AND VERIFYING THE RESULTS AUTOMATED CALCULATIONS. THE PURPOSE IS TO IDENTIFY AREAS WHERE A DESIGN ERROR COULD RESULT IN THE RELEASE OF GAS. A LIST OF THESE CALCULATIONS/DECISIONS WILL BE INCORPORATED INTO AN ENGINEERING STANDARD. PROCEDURES WILL BE PUT INTO PLACE REQUIRING THE DRAWING ROOM CHECKER TO REVIEW AND INITIAL A COPY OF THE ENGINEERING STANDARD CERTIFYING THAT THE LIST OF CALCULATIONS WAS CRITICALLY REVIEWED.
narrative_clean: background at approximately 11:05 pm on september 16, 2004 the unloader bottle on compressor cylinder #5 of unit #4, a clark tla-10, at lucas compressor station failed causing a station blow-down, which triggered the esd system. during the station blow-down, fire gates on sl-3054 and sl-3136 failed to close resulting in a gas lost of 11,758 mcf. the total cost for this incident was $69,907. failure analysis cook manley conducted a failure analysis on the unloader bottle (see attached report) and determined that the root cause of this failure was a data entry error in the bolt sizing program. cook manley also investigated all other unloader bottles installed on compressor units for the last five years and have confirmed that calculations for all other assemblies are correct. columbia conducted a root cause analysis for the esd failure and determined that the 1" compressed air esd supply line had plugged off due to black powder like material. the system was cleaned and the esd was re-tested and performed to satisfaction. remedial action cook manley will replace the affected assemblies. columbia has requested that cook manley supply 0.750 inch bolts with 16 threads per inch to secure the actuator to the valve cap. this stud size is in excess of what is required however it will serve to further bolster the safety factor on this unit. cook manley will also take the following corrective action to further reduce the chances of such an error from happening again: 1) the computer program will be revised to include a note, reminding designers of the implications and importance of using suction pressure instead of ambient pressure. 2) a future revision to the program will require the designer to select the proper assembly and then prompt the user for the correct pressure. 3) cook manley is reviewing all of the critical calculations in our designs and verifying the results automated calculations. the purpose is to identify areas where a design NAME: GULF SOUTH PIPELINE COMPANY, LP
NARRATIVE: ON OCT 4, 2004 A GULF SOUTH EMPLOYEE REPORTED A LEAK INDICATION AT AN UNDERGROUND TAP VALVE NEAR 304 KOCH RD., ARNAUDVILLE, LA.  THE TIME OF ACTUAL LEAK OCCURRENCE IS UNKNOWN. HOWEVER BECAUSE THE REDUCTION IN PRESSURE DID NOT SIGNIFICANTLY CHANGE IN THE LEAKAGE RATE THE DECISION WAS MADE TO REDUCE THE LINE PRESSURE TO ZERO TO PROVIDE EMPLOYEE SAFETY DURING THE EXCAVATION.  A COMPRESSOR WAS BROUGHT IN TO REDUCE THE AMOUNT OF GAS THAT WOULD BE RELEASED TO ATMOSPHERE TO REMOVE THE PIPELINE FROM SERVICE.  ON 10-12-04 AT 8:30 AM AN EVALUATION OF THE ESTIMATED COST OF REPAIR AND GAS LOST WAS DETERMINE THAT THE THRESHOLD OF $50,000 MIGHT BE MET AND THEREFORE A TELEPHONIC REPORT WAS MADE TO THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER AT 10:15 AM.  AT 11:30 AM 10-12-04 THE REDUCTION TO ZERO PRESSURE WAS INITIATED AND COMPLETED AT 6:14 AM ON 10-14-04.  THE TAP WAS EXCAVATED ON 10-14-04 AND THE CAUSE OF THE LEAK WAS DETERMINED TO BE A CRACK IN A 2" WELD NECK FLANGE.  IT APPEARS A SUMMER DRAUGHT MAY HAVE CAUSED SETTLING OF THE SOIL AROUND THE TAP VALVE ASSEMBLY THUS PUTTING UNDUE PRESSURE ON THE COMPONENT CAUSING IT TO CRACK.  THE CRACKED FLANGE WAS REMOVED AND A NEW ONE INSTALLED ON 10-14-04.
narrative_clean: on oct 4, 2004 a gulf south employee reported a leak indication at an underground tap valve near 304 koch rd., arnaudville, la. the time of actual leak occurrence is unknown. at the time of discovery of the leak was classified as a grade 2 requiring scheduled repair action. a 20% reduction of pressure on the pipeline prior to excavating the leak was initiated on 10-5-04 and was achieved by 10-8-04. however because the reduction in pressure did not significantly change in the leakage rate the decision was made to reduce the line pressure to zero to provide employee safety during the excavation. a compressor was brought in to reduce the amount of gas that would be released to atmosphere to remove the pipeline from service. on 10-12-04 at 8:30 am an evaluation of the estimated cost of repair and gas lost was determine that the threshold of $50,000 might be met and therefore a telephonic report was made to the national response center at 10:15 am. at 11:30 am 10-12-04 the reduction to zero pressure was initiated and completed at 6:14 am on 10-14-04. the tap was excavated on 10-14-04 and the cause of the leak was determined to be a crack in a 2" weld neck flange. it appears a summer draught may have caused settling of the soil around the tap valve assembly thus putting undue pressure on the component causing it to crack. the cracked flange was removed and a new one installed on 10-14-04.

NAME: GULF SOUTH PIPELINE COMPANY, LP
NARRATIVE: ACTUAL CAUSE WILL BE DETERMINED BASED ON METALLURGICAL ANALYSIS.  PIPE SENT TO METALLURGICAL LABORATORY NOVEMBER 30, 2004 AND FINAL REPORT IS EXPECTED TO BE DELIVERED THE WEEK OF DECEMBER 21, 2004.  TIME OF INCIDENT IS THE TIME THAT GULF SOUTH RECEIVED FIRST INDICATION, A ROD LOAD ALARM ON LONGVIEW COMPRESSOR STATION #2 UNITS 2 AND 3 WHICH WERE RUNNING AT THE TIME.  OPERATOR WAS WORKING ON UNIT 1 AND WAS ATTEMPTING TO PUT INTO SERVICE WHEN ALARM ACTIVATED.  OPERATOR OBSERVED THAT SUCTION PRESSURE ON INDEX 8 AT 240 PSIG AT APPROXIMATELY 9:35 PM AND NOTIFIED GAS CONTROL.  GAS CONTROLLER DISPATCHED FIRST RESPONDERS AT 9:40 PM.  THE LOW ALARM ON THE SCADA, SET AT 170 PSIG ACTIVATED AT 9:45PM.  A REVIEW OF THE PRESSURE DATA INDICATES THAT THE ACTUAL RUPTURE PROBABLY OCCURRED BETWEEN 8:53PM AND 8:58PM.  THE ELAPSED TIME UNTIL AREA WAS MADE SAFE IS BASED ON THE TIME THAT THE PRODUCTION THAT FEEDS INTO THE LINE WAS SHUT IN AND ALL ISOLATING VALVES WERE CLOSED.  THE NEAREST DWELLING WAS APPROXIMATELY 2,000 FEET FROM THE RUPTURE SITE.  THEREFORE, THE AREA WAS ACTUALLY SAFE ONCE THE SITE HAD BEEN SECURED UPON ARRIVAL BY THE FIRST RESPONDERS. 1-24-05 METALURGICAL ANALYSIS OF THE FAILED SECTION OF PIPE DETERMINED THAT THE RUPTURE WAS CAUSED BY PITTING CORROSION ON THE INSIDE OF THE PIPE ALONG THE BOTTOM OF THE PIPELINE, WHERE THE SEAM WELD WAS LOCATED.  THE APPEARANCE OF THE CORROSION INDICATED IT WAS MOST LIKELY DUE TO MICROBIOLOGICALLY INDUCED CORROSION (MIC) AND THERE WAS NO INDICATION THAT THE FAILURE INITIATED IN THE WELD, BUT THE PROPERTIES OF THE WELD PROBABLY ACCOUNT FOR FRACTURE PROPAGATION BEYOND THE PITTED AREA.
narrative_clean: actual cause will be determined based on metallurgical analysis. pipe sent to metallurgical laboratory november 30, 2004 and final report is expected to be delivered the week of december 21, 2004. time of incident is the time that gulf south received first indication, a rod load alarm on longview compressor station #2 units 2 and 3 which were running at the time. operator was working on unit 1 and was attempting to put into service when alarm activated. operator observed that suction pressure on index 8 at 240 psig at approximately 9:35 pm and notified gas control. gas controller dispatched first responders at 9:40 pm. the low alarm on the scada, set at 170 psig activated at 9:45pm. a review of the pressure data indicates that the actual rupture probably occurred between 8:53pm and 8:58pm. the elapsed time until area was made safe is based on the time that the production that feeds into the line was shut in and all isolating valves were closed. the nearest dwelling was approximately 2,000 feet from the rupture site. therefore, the area was actually safe once the site had been secured upon arrival by the first responders. 1-24-05 metalurgical analysis of the failed section of pipe determined that the rupture was caused by pitting corrosion on the inside of the pipe along the bottom of the pipeline, where the seam weld was located. the appearance of the corrosion indicated it was most likely due to microbiologically induced corrosion (mic) and there was no indication that the failure initiated in the weld, but the properties of the weld probably account for fracture propagation beyond the pitted area.

NARRATIVE: A CRACK FORMED BETWEEN THE BALL VALVE¿S BODY AND ONE OF ITS FLANGES.  THE CRACK WAS APPROXIMATELY 12 INCHES LONG AS MEASURED CIRCUMFERENTIALLY. STRESS IMPARTED FROM THE CONNECTED PIPING CONTRIBUTED TO SUBSEQUENT CRACK GROWTH. MICROSTRUCTURE LIKELY PLAYED A ROLE IN THE CRACK PROPAGATION TOO.  THE PRESENCE OF GRAPHITE FLAKES WITHIN THE MATRIX IS INDICATIVE OF A WEAKER MICROSTRUCTURE.  SEM EXAMINATION OF THE FRACTURE SURFACE INDICATED BRITTLE-LIKE PROPAGATION OF THE CRACK.  THE CHEMICAL ANALYSIS CONFIRMS THAT THE MATERIAL IS A CAST IRON, WITH A CARBON COMPOSITION OF 3 PERCENT.
narrative_clean: a crack formed between the ball valve¿s body and one of its flanges. the crack was approximately 12 inches long as measured circumferentially. the failed valve is being sent to an independent lab for crack morphology and analysis. because the pipeline was a sole market feed, the valve could not be readily isolated. this resulted in blowing gas being managed while a stoppled bypass could be fabricated, thus resulting in costs exceeding $50k. synopsis of march 21, 2005, edison welding institute report ewi project no. 48804csp: the likely cause of failure was crack initiation from a void type casting defect. stress imparted from the connected piping contributed to subsequent crack growth. the crack propagated from the outside surface of the ball valve as evident by the increased corrosion products found across the fracture surface. microstructure likely played a role in the crack propagation too. the presence of graphite flakes within the matrix is indicative of a weaker microstructure. sem examination of the fracture surface indicated brittle-like propagation of the crack. the chemical analysis confirms that the material is a cast iron, with a carbon composition of 3 percent.

NARRATIVE: WHILE PERFORMING HIGHWAY CROSSING PATROL OF 400/77 HIGHWAY ON LINE AK, SSCGP EMPLOYEES CHECKED THE VENT MARKER ON NORTH SIDE OF HIGHWAY WITH A PRAGMATICS LEAK DETECTOR. AT THAT POINT IN TIME THE SSCGP OPERATOR'S CONTINUED THEIR INVESTIGATION AND DISCOVERED THAT THE LEAK AREA WAS CONFINED TO THE CASING UNDER THE ROAD CROSSING AND NO FARTHER AWAY THAN FIVE FEET FROM THE NORTH END OF THE CASING. TEST HOLES WERE ESTABLISHED AND WERE CHECKED THREE TIMES PER DAY AS ADVISED BY THE OPS.  ON JANUARY 25TH THE DAY WAS SPENT FILLING OUT PAPERWORK AND CALLING IN ONE CALLS TO ESTABLISH WHERE THE OTHER UTILITIES WERE IN THE AREA.  ALSO, ON THIS DAY, UNDER THE ADVISE OF THE OPS, WE WERE ASKED TO LOWER THE LINE PRESSURE FROM 253# TO 200#.   THIS FUNCTION WAS PERFORMED.  ON JANUARY 26TH SSCGP EMPLOYEES SHOWED UP ON SITE TO PERFORM EXCAVATION TO SEE IF THE LEAK COULD BE FOUND. NAME: MISSISSIPPI RIVER TRANSMISSION CORP.
NARRATIVE: ON APRIL 12, 2005 AT APPROXIMATELY 05:11 THE MRT GAS CONTROLLER RECEIVED A LOW PRESSURE SCADA ALARM ON OUR ML-1 PIPELINE.  THE CONTROLLER REQUESTED A LOCAL FIELD PERSON TO RESPONSE TO AND INVESTIGATES THE AREA.   AT APPROXIMATELY 6:11 THE FIELD PERSON, WHO WAS STILL IN TRANSIT, RECEIVED A CELL PHONE CALL FROM A LOCAL RESIDENT WHO REPORTED WHAT THEY THOUGHT THERE WAS A BLOW OUT AROUND MP 95 OR 96.  THE MRT FIELD PERSON CALLS GAS CONTROL REQUESTING HELP TO ISOLATE THE SUSPECTED AREA AND INITIATED OUR EMERGENCY RESPONSE PLAN.   THE SUSPECTED AREA WAS ISOLATED BY 06:55, AND FIELD PERSONNEL REPORTED TO GAS CONTROL THE EXACT LOCATION OF THE RUPTURE AT APPROXIMATELY 07:15, WITH NO FIRE AND NO INJURIES.  THE LINCOLN COUNTY SHERIFF DEPARTMENT EVACUATED 4 PERSONS FROM A LOCAL DEER CAMP THAT WAS IN THE AREA OF THE RUPTURE.  THE AREA WAS MONITORED AND THE PIPELINE WAS ALLOWED TO BLOW DOWN.  AREA WAS DEEMED SAFE, AND ALL ISOLATION VALVES WERE LOCKED AND TAGGED OUT.   THE RUPTURE SECTION OF PIPE WAS TRANSPORTED TO THE LOCAL TEAM PERSONNEL OFFICE.  THE PIPE WAS INSPECTED BY MRT CORROSION MANAGER AND HE DETERMINED THAT THE RUPTURE WAS DUE TO MICROBIOLOGICALLY INFLUENCED CORROSION (MIC).
narrative_clean: on april 12, 2005 at approximately 05:11 the mrt gas controller received a low pressure scada alarm on our ml-1 pipeline. the controller requested a local field person to response to and investigates the area. at approximately 6:11 the field person, who was still in transit, received a cell phone call from a local resident who reported what they thought there was a blow out around mp 95 or 96. the mrt field person calls gas control requesting help to isolate the suspected area and initiated our emergency response plan. the suspected area was isolated by 06:55, and field personnel reported to gas control the exact location of the rupture at approximately 07:15, with no fire and no injuries. the lincoln county sheriff department evacuated 4 persons from a local deer camp that was in the area of the rupture. the area was monitored and the pipeline was allowed to blow down. area was deemed safe, and all isolation valves were locked and tagged out. the rupture section of pipe was transported to the local team personnel office. the pipe was inspected by mrt corrosion manager and he determined that the rupture was due to microbiologically influenced corrosion (mic).

NAME: MISSISSIPPI RIVER TRANSMISSION CORP.

NARRATIVE: WE HAD REPORTS OF BUBBLES ON DECEMBER 6, 2004, HOWEVER THE LOCATION OF THE BUBBLES WERE OVER 100 FEET FROM OUR ALTON PIPE LOCATION AND GAS SENSORS DID NOT DETECT GAS. THE CRACK WAS IN A WRINKLE BEND THAT ALSO RAN FROM THE 6 O'CLOCK  TO 12 O'CLOCK POSITION.  THE LINE WAS REPAIRED AND PLACED BACK IN SERVICE MAY 13, 2005.

NAME: COLUMBIA GULF TRANSMISSION
NARRATIVE: UNIT HAD GONE DOWN ON ALARM.  COMPANY RESPONDER CLEARNED ALARMS, AND STARTED UNIT.  UNIT WENT THROUGH WARM UP, AND WENT ON LINE TO MAINTAIN LINE PRESSURE.  COMPANY PERSON PLACED UNIT IN AUTOMATIC START MODE, AND WAS LEAVING BUILDING WHEN THE UNIT POWER TURBINE FAILED.  TURBINE FAILURE RESULTED IN DAMAGE TO UNIT AND ADJOINING UNIT.  FAILED UNIT CAUGHT FIRE.  COMPANY PERSON HIT ESD FOR APPROPRIATE ENGINE BLOCKS.       INVESTIGATION REVEALED A SEGMENT OF THE FIRST STAGE REACTION TURBINE DISK BROKE AWAY CAUSING THE ROTOR TO BECOME SEVERALLY OUT OF BALANCE.  THIS SITUATION RESULTED IN THE COMPLETE CATASTROPHIC FAILURE OF THE REACTION TURBINE.      THE INITIAL CAUSE OF THE ROTOR DISK FAILURE WAS SHOWN TO BE DUE TO A LOW CYCLE FATIGUE CRACK RESULTING OVER SEVERAL CYCLES.  THIS CRACK WAS INITIATED BY THE FAILURE OF ONE OF THE LOWER SEAL RING SEGMENTS, WHICH CAME UNFASTENED AND RUBBED AGAINST THE ROTOR DISK.  THE ROOT CAUSE OF THIS FAILURE HAS BEEN DETERMINED TO BE THE RELEASE OF ONE OF THE LOWER SEAL RING SEGMENTS FROM ITS FASTENERS.  NO DEFINITIVE REASON CAN BE DETERMINED FOR THE RELEASE OF THESE FASTENERS.
narrative_clean: unit had gone down on alarm. company responder clearned alarms, and started unit. unit went through warm up, and went on line to maintain line pressure. company person placed unit in automatic start mode, and was leaving building when the unit power turbine failed. turbine failure resulted in damage to unit and adjoining unit. failed unit caught fire. company person hit esd for appropriate engine blocks. investigation revealed a segment of the first stage reaction turbine disk broke away causing the rotor to become severally out of balance. this situation resulted in the complete catastrophic failure of the reaction turbine. the initial cause of the rotor disk failure was shown to be due to a low cycle fatigue crack resulting over several cycles. this crack was initiated by the failure of one of the lower seal ring segments, which came unfastened and rubbed against the rotor disk. the root cause of this failure has been determined to be the release of one of the lower seal ring segments from its fasteners. no definitive reason can be determined for the release of these fasteners.

NARRATIVE: NEWBERRY STATION  IVESTIGATION REPORT  DOT/CPUC REPORTABLE 7/13/2005    SEQUENCE OF EVENTS    AT APPROXIMATELY 6:00 PM, GAS CONTROL REPORTED THAT STARTING AIR PRESSURE AT NEWBERRY STATION WAS LOW, SETTING INTO MOTION RESPONSE AND INVESTIGATION.    THE AIR DRYER WAS ISOLATED AND AIR PRESSURE BUILT BACK UP, AND THE GAS VENT VALVES CLOSED.  THE AIR SYSTEMS PRESSURE DROPPED DUE TO THE AIR LINE HOSE FAILURE, BUT THE AIR COMPRESSURE CONTINEUED TO SUPPLY AIR, ULTIMATELY HOLDING A PRESSURE OF 35# IN TEH AIR SYTEM.  ONCE THE AIR DRYER WAS ISOLATED, AIR PRESSURE BUILT BACK UP AND THE GAS VENT VALVES CLOSED.    MAINTAINING THE 35# EQUILIBRIUM RESULTED IN A PRESSURE LOW ENOUGH TO TRIP THE GAS VENTING VALVES (65# DESIGNED SET  POINT) TO ATMPOSPHERE BUT NOT LOWE ENOUGH TO CLOSE THE BLOCK VALVLES (30# DESIGNED SET POINT) WHICH WOULD HAVE ISOLATED TRANSMISSION LINES 235 AND 3000 FROM THE STATION.    UPON DISCOVERY OF THE HOSE FAILURE, THE AIR DRYER WAS BYPASSED AND REMOVED FROM SERVICE.  STATION PERSONNEL REMAINED AT THE STATION THROUGH THE NIGHT OT MONITOR OPERATIONS.    THE STATION WAS PLACED BACK ONLINE AT APPROXIMATELY 8:45 PM.    DUE TO QUICK ACTION BY GAS OPERATIONS TO MAINTAIN THE GAS SYSTEM AND BY PUTTING STORAGE ON WITHDRAWAL, THERE WAS NO LOSS OF SERVICE OR CUSTOMER IMPACT.    NOTE:  THE VENTING OF GAS TO ATMOSPHERE WAS NOT THE RESULT OF ANY MALFUCTION OF THE ESD SYSTEM NOR A TRIGGER OF THE ESD SYSTEM.  DURING THIS INCIDENT, THE ESD SYSTEM COULD HAVE BEEN ACTUATED BY A NUMBER OF SAFETY-TRIGGERED CONDITIONS, AND THIS WOULD HAVE RESULTED IN A COMPLETE ISOLATION AND BLOW-DOWN OF THE STATION.    IMMEDIATE MITIGATION EFFORTS    UNTIL COMPLETEION OF COMPREHENSIVE ENGINEERING ANALYSIS, THE AIR DRYER WILL REMAIN OUT OF SERVICE.    A NITROGEN SUPPLY SYSTEM TO PROVIDE BACK-UP PRESSURE TO THE ESD SYSTEM NOT INSTALLED ON FRIDAY JULY 15, 2005.  THE SYTEM IS SET TO PROVIDE CONSTANT 80# OF NITROGEN FEED TO THE ESD SYSTEM, SHOULD THE EXISTING SYSTEM PRESSURE DROP BELOW 80#.  THE NITROGEN FEED IS SUPPLIED THROUGH A CHECK VALVE AND ORIFICE SO AS TO NOT IMPACT OR AFFECT NORMAL OPERATION OF THE ESD SYSTEM, IF ACTUATED.    ON GOING ENGINEERING REVIEW OF CURRENT AIR SYSTEMS AT NEW BETTER STATION (STARTING AIR, UTILITY AIR, AND INSTRUMENT AIR), AND WILL IMPLEMENT ANY MODIFICATIONS IDENTIFIED FROM ENGINEERING REVIEW DEEMED NECESSARY.    PLEASE CONTACT JEFF KOSKIE AT (213) 244-3283 IF YOU HAVE ANY QUESTIONS OR NEED ADDITIONAL INFORMATION.

NAME: EQUITRANS, LP
NARRATIVE: CONSTRUCTION WORK WAS IN PROGRESS AT GLENVILLE COMPRESSOR STATION.  THE STATION HAD BEEN SHUT DOWN, BLOWN DOWN AND LOCKED OUT/TAGGED OUT. NO GAS HAD BEEN DETECTED PRIOR TO THE INCIDENT.  A CONTRACTOR EMPLOYEE WAS USING AN ELECTRIC GRINDER TO REMOVE A GASKET AT TEH 3" ELEVATED ABOVEGROUND FLANGE WHILE ANOTHER CONTRACTOR EMPLOYEE WAS WORKING BELOW THE 3" VALVE FLANGE ON AN 8" ABOVEGROUND VALVE FLANGE.  A FLASH OCCURRED AT THE 8" VALVE FLANGE WHICH BURNED THE CONTRACTOR EMPLOYEE THAT WAS WORKING ON THE 8" VALVE FLANGE AND THE CONTRACOTR EMPLOYEE WORKING ON THE 3" VALVE FLANGE.  IT IS BELIEVED THE SPARKS EMANATING FROM THE GRINDER WHEEL WERE THE HEAT SOURCE FOR THE FLASH.  IT IS BELIEVED THE FUEL FOR THE FIRE CAME FROM INSIDE THE 8" PIPE.  THE EXACT LOCATION AND SOURCE OF FUEL INVOLVED IN THE FLASH FIRE COULD NOT BE DETERMINED.
narrative_clean: construction work was in progress at glenville compressor station. the station had been shut down, blown down and locked out/tagged out. one 3" and two 8" aboveground valves had been removed by contractor personnel as part of the contruction and a gas-trac was utilized periodically to check for the presence of gas at the open valve flanges. no gas had been detected prior to the incident. a contractor employee was using an electric grinder to remove a gasket at teh 3" elevated aboveground flange while another contractor employee was working below the 3" valve flange on an 8" aboveground valve flange. a flash occurred at the 8" valve flange which burned the contractor employee that was working on the 8" valve flange and the contracotr employee working on the 3" valve flange. it is believed the sparks emanating from the grinder wheel were the heat source for the flash. it is believed the fuel for the fire came from inside the 8" pipe. the exact location and source of fuel involved in the flash fire could not be determined.

NAME: NORTHERN NATURAL GAS COMPANY
NARRATIVE: ON DED.19, A SERVICE TO THREE AQUILA COMMUNITIES WAS INTERRUPTED WHEN A BRANCHLINE REGULATOR, OWNED BY NORTHERN NATURAL GAS, FAILED TO OPERATE CORRECTLY AND PRESSURES DROPPED TO CRITICAL LEVELS AT THE DELIVERY POINTS TO THE COMMUNITIES. AQUILA EXPERIENCED LOSS OF SERVICE TO A PORTION OF THEIR CUSTOMERS IN THE COMMUNITIES OF PINE ISLAND, WANAMINGO AND ZUMBROTA,MN. APPROX 250 HOMES AND BUSINESSES LOST NATURAL GAS SERVICE IN THE THREE COMMUNITIES.    THE ZUMBROTA AREA HAD EXPERIENCED SEVERE WINTER WEATHER TEMPERATURES PRIOR TO THE INCIDENT. THE EVENING OF THE INCIDENT TEMPERATURES WERE IN THE SINGLE DIGITS WITH WIND CHILL BELOW ZERO. THE LACK OF PILOT GAS HEAT ALLOWED THE TEMPERATURES IN THE PILOT GAS LINE TO DROP TO AMBIENT TEMPERATURES, WHICH WERE AS LOW AS 8 DEGREES FAHRENHEIT. THE LOW GAS TEMPERATURES, COUPLED WITH THE  TEMPERATURE DROP THROUGH THE PILOT REGULATOR, DROPPED THE  TEMPERATURE OF THE GAS TO A POINT THAT MATCHED OR EXCEEDED THE DEW POINT OF THE GAS STREAM. WATER DROPPED OUT IN THE ORIFICE OF THE PILOT GAS REGULATOR AND FROZE, THUS IMPEDING FULL OPERATION OF THE REGULATOR.    NORTHERN IS FILING THIS INCIDENT REPORT BECAUSE IT CONSIDERS THIS AS A SIGNIFICANT EVENT UNDER 191.3.  THIS REPORT IS BEING SUBMITTED LATE AS THERE WAS AN OVERSIGHT IN FOLLOW-UP DUE TO THE FACT THAT THE INCIDENT DID NOT MEET THE $50,000 DOLLAR REQUIREMENT, THERE WERE NO INJURIES AND NO RELEASE OF PRODUCT.
narrative_clean: on ded.19, a service to three aquila communities was interrupted when a branchline regulator, owned by northern natural gas, failed to operate correctly and pressures dropped to critical levels at the delivery points to the communities. aquila experienced loss of service to a portion of their customers in the communities of pine island, wanamingo and zumbrota,mn. approx 250 homes and businesses lost natural gas service in the three communities. the zumbrota area had experienced severe winter weather temperatures prior to the incident. the evening of the incident temperatures were in the single digits with wind chill below zero. the lack of pilot gas heat allowed the temperatures in the pilot gas line to drop to ambient temperatures, which were as low as 8 degrees fahrenheit. the low gas temperatures, coupled with the temperature drop through the pilot regulator, dropped the temperature of the gas to a point that matched or exceeded the dew point of the gas stream. water dropped out in the orifice of the pilot gas regulator and froze, thus impeding full operation of the regulator. northern is filing this incident report because it considers this as a significant event under 191.3. this report is being submitted late as there was an oversight in follow-up due to the fact that the incident did not meet the $50,000 dollar requirement, there were no injuries and no release of product.

NAME: ENOGEX INC
NARRATIVE: A MANUAL BLOCK VALVE SEPARATING THE PRIMARY CONTROL VALVE OUTLET HEADER FROM THE SECONDARY CONTROL VALVE OUTLET HEADER WAS CLOSED FOLLOWING A SHUTDOWN OF THE CUSTOMER'S POWER GENERATION UNITS 6 & 7 IN OCTOBER 2005. NAME: MISSISSIPPI RIVER TRANSMISSION
NARRATIVE: SYSTEM CONTROL NOTICED A REDUCTION IN THE NORMAL INLET PRESSURE TO THE A-194 METER STATION EARLY IN THE MORNING OF FEBRUARY 6, 2006. THE FIELD PERSONNEL VERIFIED THAT THE INLET PRESSURE WAS BEING RESTRICTED BY THE 2" WKM TAP VALVE FOR THE A-194 LINE. HE CALLED IN A CREW TO DIG UP AND DETERMINE WHAT WAS CAUSING THIS PROBLEM. THE STEM IN THE VALVE BROKE AND BLEW OUT OF THE VALVE AFTER THE EXTENSION WAS REMOVED, CAUSING GAS TO START EXCAPING FROM THE VALVE. WHEN THE STEM BROKE APPARENTLY THE GATE ON THE 2" WKM VALVE BECAME ALMOST COMPLETELY CLOSED RESULTING IN THE LOSS OF GAS SERVICE TO THE A-194 CUSTOMER. IN ORDER TO REPLACE THIS FAULTY VALVE WE HAD TO BLOWDOWN OUR A-151 AND A-183 LINES, WHICH RESULTED IN THE LOSS OF SERVICE TO THE CUSTOMERS ON THOSE LINES ALSO. WE INSTALLED A NEW 2" ORBIT VALVE TO REPLACE THE WKM VALVE.

NARRATIVE: 04/16/2014 -     FAILED COUPLING CAUSED BY VIBRATION & PRESSURE ON PIPING.     LESLIE STEVENS  COMPLIANCE COORDINATOR  832-214-1649  LESLIE.STEVENS@ENBRIDGE.COM    THE FOLLOWING IS BASED ON INFORMATION OBTAINED FROM THE CONTRACTOR AND ITS EMPLOYEES AND THE ONE ENBRIDGE EMPLOYEE AT THE SITE. THE INITIAL OPERATION INVOLVED THE REPLACEMENT OF A 20¿ LOOP LINE VALVE LOCATED ON THE 20¿ LOOP LINE.  PARALLEL TO THE 20¿ LOOP LINE IS ENBRIDGE¿S 22¿ MAIN LINE.  THE LOOP LINE AND MAIN LINE ARE CONNECTED BY AN 18¿ CROSSOVER LINE.  THE 18¿ CROSSOVER LINE VALVE HAD BEEN CLOSED AND THE 20¿ LOOP LINE SEGMENT HAD BEEN ISOLATED AT THE MAIN HEADER SOUTH OF THE 20¿ LOOP LINE VALVE TO BE REPLACED AND AT ANOTHER LOOP LINE VALVE LOCATED TO THE NORTH OF THE EXCAVATED SITE.  THE ISOLATED SEGMENT WAS BLED DOWN TO ATMOSPHERE AT THIS POINT.  THE 18¿ CROSSOVER LINE VALVE HAD BEEN SKIDDED OR SUPPORTED WITH BLOCKS SO THERE WOULD BE NO MOVEMENT WHEN THE 18¿ CROSSOVER LINE WOULD BE CUT DOWNSTREAM OF THE 18¿ CROSSOVER LINE VALVE.  CUTS ONE, TWO AND THREE WERE THEN MADE. THE NOW FREE TEE SECTION WAS REMOVED FROM THE EXCAVATION AS WAS THE WEST CONCRETE WALL OF THE 18¿ CROSSOVER LINE VALVE BOX.  THE SKIDDED 18¿ CROSSOVER LINE VALVE REMAINED STABLE AND UNMOVED AFTER THE CUTS WERE MADE.  THE PORTION OF THE 20¿ LOOP LINE CONTAINING THE 20¿ LOOP LINE VALVE TO BE REPLACED, EXPOSED IN THE EXCAVATION, WAS CUT AGAIN (CUT 4) ON THE NORTH SIDE OF THE 20¿ LOOP LINE VALVE.  THIS LEFT THE 20¿ LOOP LINE VALVE FREE TO BE REMOVED FOR REPLACEMENT.  BECAUSE THE 20¿ LOOP LINE SEGMENT HAD A HUGE BLOCK OF CONCRETE POURED AROUND IT FOR SUPPORT WHEN ORIGINALLY LAID, THE BLOCK OF CONCRETE HAD TO BE BROKEN UP IN ORDER FOR THE 20¿ LOOP LINE VALVE AND 20¿ LOOP LINE CUT SEGMENT TO BE LIFTED OUT OF THE EXCAVATION.  CONTRACTOR¿S CREWS BEGAN JACK HAMMERING ON THE BLOCK OF CONCRETE AND WITHIN 30 MINUTES TO AN HOUR THE GAS RELEASE OCCURRED.  LATER IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT A COUPLING  ON THE 18¿ CROSSOVER LINE BETWEEN THE 18¿CROSSOVER LINE VALVE AND THE 22¿ MAIN LINE, WHICH WAS STILL UNDER PRESSURE, HAD UNCOUPLED.   ALSO PRESENT BETWEEN THE EXCAVATION AND THE COUPLING ON THE 18¿ CROSSOVER LINE WAS AN OLD ABANDON UNEXPOSED CISTERN.  IT IS POSSIBLE THAT THESE WERE THE THREE MAIN CONTRIBUTING FACTORS TO THE RELEASE EVENT.  IT IS BELIEVED THAT THE CROSSOVER COUPLING PROVIDED MINIMAL STRENGTH, TO THE HORIZONTAL PRESSURE CREATED WHEN THE 18¿ CROSSOVER LINE WAS CUT AND REMOVED FROM THE 20¿ LOOP LINE AND THAT THE ABANDON CISTERN PROVIDED REDUCED SOIL COMPACTION, VOLUME AND STRENGTH HOLDING CAPACITIES AFTER THE CUT AND REMOVAL WERE MADE.  FINALLY, THE JACK HAMMERING ON THE CONCRETE POURED OVER THE CUT 20¿ LOOP LINE PROVIDED EXTERNAL VIBRATION TO THE REDUCED VOLUME OF UNDISTURBED, COMPACTED SOIL CREATED BY THE CISTERN. A SKETCH OF THE INCIDENT AREA WAS NOT ATTACHED BECAUSE OF LIMITATIONS REGARDING THE OPS ONLINE DATA ENTRY AND OPERATOR REGISTRATION SYSTEM, HOWEVER A SKETCH CAN BE PROVIDED UPON REQUEST.

information obtained from the contractor and its employees and the one enbridge employee at the site. the initial operation involved the replacement of a 20¿ loop line valve located on the 20¿ loop line. parallel to the 20¿ loop line is enbridge¿s 22¿ main line. the loop line and main line are connected by an 18¿ crossover line. the 18¿ crossover line valve had been closed and the 20¿ loop line segment had been isolated at the main header south of the 20¿ loop line valve to be replaced and at another loop line valve located to the north of the excavated site. the isolated segment was bled down to atmosphere at this point. the 18¿ crossover line valve had been skidded or supported with blocks so there would be no movement when the 18¿ crossover line would be cut downstream of the 18¿ crossover line valve. cuts one, two and three were then made. the now free tee section was removed from the excavation as was the west concrete wall of the 18¿ crossover line valve box. the skidded 18¿ crossover line valve remained stable and unmoved after the cuts were made. the portion of the 20¿ loop line containing the 20¿ loop line valve to be replaced, exposed in the excavation, was cut again (cut 4) on the north side of the 20¿ loop line valve. this left the 20¿ loop line valve free to be removed for replacement. because the 20¿ loop line segment had a huge block of concrete poured around it for support when originally laid, the block of concrete had to be broken up in order for the 20¿ loop line valve and 20¿ loop line cut segment to be lifted out of the excavation. pressure created when the 18¿ crossover line was cut and removed from the 20¿ loop line and that the abandon cistern provided reduced soil compaction, volume and strength holding capacities after the NAME: ENOGEX INC

NAME: COLORADO INTERSTATE GAS
NARRATIVE: THE WIC 124A PIPELINE (OPERATED BY COLORADO INTERSTATE GAS PIPELINE), NEAR CHEYENNE, WY RUPTURED FOLLOWING APPARENT THIRD-PARTY DAMAGE BY AN EXCAVATION CONTRACTOR WORKING FOR KINDER MORGAN ON THE ROCKIES EXPRESS PROJECT.  THERE WAS A FIRE AND EXPLOSION, AND ONE FATALITY RESULTED FOLLOWING THE INCIDENT.      ** AFTER EXCAVATION BY KINDER MORGAN CONTRACTOR AND SUBSEQUENT RUPTURE, PIPELINE COVER WAS MEASURED AT 26.40 INCHES.    AFTER COMPLETING THE INTERNAL INVESTIGATION, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THIS INCIDENT WAS CAUSED BY A CONFLUENCE OF EVENTS BY A VARIETY OF ACTIONS, AND MORE SPECIFICALLY THAT:    1. CONSTRUCTIONG PARTY DID NOT LOCATE AND MARK THE LOCATION OF WIC'S PIPELINE PRIOR TO STARTING CONSTRUCTION AS REQUIRED BY ITS FERC CERTIFICATE OF PUBLIC CONVENIENCE AND NECESSITY.    2. SURVEY COMPANIES DID NOT PHYSICALLY LOCATE NEARBY EXISTING UNDERGROUND FACILITIES, INCLUDING THE WIC PIPELINE, WHEN CREATING SURVEYS USED IN THE REX PROJECT.  WHEN STAKING THE EDGE OF REX'S TEMPORARY CONSTRUCTION RIGHT-OF-WAY, SURVEY COMPANIES REPEATEDLY PLACED STAKES NEAR, ON AND TO THE NORTH OF THE WIC PIPELINE.  THE CONSTRUCTION INSPECTION COMPANY DID NOT DETECT AND/OR CORRECT THE DEFICIENCIES IN THE SURVEY OR THE STAKING OF THE RIGHT-OF-WAY.    3. CONSTRUCTION CONTRACTOR DID NOT PHYSICALLY LOCATE OR MARK EXISTING UNDERGROUND FACILITIES, INCLUDING THE WIC PIPELINE, WHEN THOSE FACILITIES WERE PARALLEL TO THE NEW PIPELINE BEING CONSTRUCTED (REX) NOR DID CONSTRUCTION USE POTHOLING TO DISCOVER THE LOCATION OF THE PARALLEL WIC PIPELINE ONCE THE ENCROACHMENTS BY THE REX TEMPORARY CONSTRUCTION RIGHT-OF-WAY HAD BEGUN TO OCCUR.  CONSTRUCTION CONTRACTOR DID NOT UNDERTAKE EFFORTS PRIOR TO INVESTIGATE THE NATURE OF THE HARD SUBSURFACE MATERIAL ENCOUNTERED IN THE AREA OF THE RUPTURE.    4. DECEASED EMPLOYEE OF CONSTRUCTION CONTRACTOR WAS PROBABLY UNAWARE OF THE LOCATION OF THE WIC PIPELINE WHILE USING THE BULLDOZER TO RIP THE GROUND BETWEEN THE WESTERN AND EASTERN PERMANENT WIC PIPELINE MARKERS OF THE RUPTURE SITE.    5. EMPLOYEE OF CONTRACTOR HIRED TO LOCATE, AND WHEN NECESSARY FLAG THE LOCATION OF THE WIC PIPELINE DID NOT FLAG THE LOCATION OF THE PIPELINE BETWEEN THE WESTERN AND EASTERN PERMANENT WIC PIPELINE MARKERS NEAR THE RUPTURE SITE.
narrative_clean: the wic 124a pipeline (operated by colorado interstate gas pipeline), near cheyenne, wy ruptured following apparent third-party damage by an excavation contractor working for kinder morgan on the rockies express project. there was a fire and explosion, and one fatality resulted following the incident. ** after excavation by kinder morgan contractor and subsequent rupture, pipeline cover was measured at 26.40 inches. after completing the internal investigation, it was determined that this incident was caused by a confluence of events by a variety of actions, and more specifically that: 1. constructiong party did not locate and mark the location of wic's pipeline prior to starting construction as required by its ferc certificate of public convenience and necessity. 2. survey companies did not physically locate nearby existing underground facilities, including the wic pipeline, when creating surveys used in the rex project. when staking the edge of rex's temporary construction right-of-way, survey companies repeatedly placed stakes near, on and to the north of the wic pipeline. the construction inspection company did not detect and/or correct the deficiencies in the survey or the staking of the right-of-way. 3. construction contractor did not physically locate or mark existing underground facilities, including the wic pipeline, when those facilities were parallel to the new pipeline being constructed (rex) nor did construction use potholing to discover the location of the parallel wic pipeline once the encroachments by the rex temporary construction right-of-way had begun to occur. construction contractor did not undertake efforts prior to investigate the nature of the hard subsurface material encountered in the area of the rupture. 4. deceased employee of construction contractor was probably unaware of the location of the wic pipeline while using the bulldozer to rip the ground between the western and eastern permanent wic pipeline markers of the rupture site. 5. employee of contractor hired to locate, and when necessary flag the location of the wic pipeline did not flag the location of the pipeline between the western and eastern permanent wic pipeline markers near the rupture site.

THE WORK INCLUDED INVESTIGATION OF A GRADE 3 LEAK AND ABANDONING TWO 4-INCH STEEL SUBS, ONE OF WHICH INCLUDED A 2-INCH STEEL SIDE-TAP VALVE.  BOTH STUBS WERE WELDED TO A 16-INCH STEEL TRANSMISSION PIPELINE.    AT 23:28 ON 12/6/06, WHILE THE SOUTHWEST GAS CREW WAS REMOVING DIRT, DAMAGE OCCURED ON THE 16-INCH PIPE NEAR THE FILLET WELD FOR THE 2-INCH SIDE-TAP VALVE STUB, CAUSING LEAKAGE TO OCCUR. ATMOSPHERIC GAS DETECTED IN THE PARKING GARAGE AT THE NEW YORK-NEW YORK HOTEL DURING THE INITIAL PERIMETER SURVEY RESULTED IN CLOSURE OF THE GARAGE.  THE INCIDENT PERIMETER WAS SECURED AT 01:15 ON 12/07/06.  THE PERIMETER WAS LATER EXPANDED AT 03:20 ON 12/7/06 DUE TO SHIFTING WINDS.  CONTINUAL SURVEILLANCE OF THE AFFECTED AREA CONFIRMED THAT NO UNDERGROUND LEAK MIGRATION WAS OCCURRING. narrative_clean: on wednesday, april 11, 2007 at approximately 12:25 pm a natural gas leak was discovered on a section of transmission system piping located near the northwest corner of the intersection of county roads, 2700 north and 200 east, in champaign county. company personnel immediately closed valves and isolated the section of piping that was suspected of leaking. the piping section was brought to 0 psig within an hour by venting gas into the atmosphere through connections at a nearby gas storage well. the leak caused no injuries and there was no damage to any property other than the company facilities that were involved. the area of the leak was excavated on monday, april 16, 2007 and the leak was found to be associated with a pipeline drip that was attached to the pipeline. the leak was located on a 6" 90 degree elbow of the drip. a metallurigical analysis revealed that the leak was due to microbial corrosion on the interior of the elbow. 09/27/2012: updated final report to include coordinates for location of incident. tdc

NAME: ENERGY TRANSFER COMPANY
NARRATIVE: MULTIPLE OCCURRENCES CONTRIBUTED TO THIS EVENT; THE HANDLEY POWER PLANT WAS NOT ON-LINE, THEREFORE GAS WAS NOT BEING DELIVERED TO THE POWER PLANT, FROM THE PIPELINE.  ALSO, THE ETC COMPRESSOR #1 AT OUR MAYPEARL COMPRESSOR STATION TRIPPED OFF-LINE.  THIS UNIT WAS BEING USED TO MOVE GAS FROM HANDLEY TO MAYPEARL; CONSEQUENTLY THIS CAUSED THE PIPELINE TO START BUILDING PRESSURE.  THE 9500 MERCER SAFETY RELIEF VALVE, LOCATED AT THE HANDLEY STATION OPERATED CORRECTLY AND RELIEVED GAS, AT 753 PSIG, TO THE ETC SILENCER/BLOWDOWN STACK LOCATED IN THE ETC HANDLEY METER STATION YARD.  THE GAS WAS EMITTED TO THE ATMOSPHERE.  THE GAS ENCOUNTERED AN UNEXPECTED IGNITION SOURCE AND IGNITED, CAUSING ENOUGH HEAT SOURCES TO MELT A POWER LINE THAT FELL TO THE GROUND.  AFTER A THOROUGH INVESTIGATION, IT IS BELIEVED THAT THERE WAS ARCHING AROUND THE AREA OF AN INSULATOR IN THE POWER LINE BEFORE THE RELEASE OF GAS, CAUSING THE GAS TO IGNITE.  THE ETC BLOWDOWN STACK IS DESIGNED TO SPECIFICALLY DISPERSE THE RELEASE OF GAS WITHOUT INCIDENT AND DESIGNED TO PREVENT THE POSSIBILITY OF IGNITION.      *  TOTAL TIME UNTIL AREA WAS MADE SAFE INCLUDED TIME FOR ELECTRICITY TO BE DISCONNECTED. GAS OFF AND FIRE OUT @ 7:55 AM      REPORTED TO TRRC @ 8:05 AM ON 4/23/07   REPORTED TO NRC @ 8:50 AM ON 4/23/07  (NRC 833123) OFFICER MALLICK    FINAL UPDATE: 01/04/2010  ADDITIONAL MEASURES TAKEN TO PREVENT SIMILIAR REOCCURRENCES:  1. RELOCATED RV DISTANCES AWAY FROM SIMILIAR POWER SOURCES, AS SECONDARY OPP.  2. INSTALLED INDIVIDUAL PRIMARY PRESSURE CONTROL DEVICES AT EACH PRODUCER TIE-IN (INLETS)THAT WILL SHUT-IN EACH PRODUCER, IF THE LINE PRESSURE APPROACHES MAOP.
narrative_clean: multiple occurrences contributed to this event; the handley power plant was not on-line, therefore gas was not being delivered to the power plant, from the pipeline. also, the etc compressor #1 at our maypearl compressor station tripped off-line. this unit was being used to move gas from handley to maypearl; consequently this caused the pipeline to start building pressure. the 9500 mercer safety relief valve, located at the handley station operated correctly and relieved gas, at 753 psig, to the etc silencer/blowdown stack located in the etc handley meter station yard. the gas was emitted to the atmosphere. the gas encountered an unexpected ignition source and ignited, causing enough heat sources to melt a power line that fell to the ground. after a thorough investigation, it is believed that there was arching around the area of an insulator in the power line before the release of gas, causing the gas to ignite. the etc blowdown stack is designed to specifically disperse the release of gas without incident and designed to prevent the possibility of ignition. * total time until area was made safe included time for electricity to be disconnected. gas off and fire out @ 7:55 am reported to trrc @ 8:05 am on 4/23/07 reported to nrc @ 8:50 am on 4/23/07 (nrc 833123) officer mallick final update: 01/04/2010 additional measures taken to prevent similiar reoccurrences: 1. relocated rv distances away from similiar power sources, as secondary opp. 2. installed individual primary pressure control devices at each producer tie-in (inlets)that will shut-in each producer, if the line pressure approaches maop.
