NAME: MICHIGAN CONSOLIDATED GAS COMPANY
CAUSE: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD
NARRATIVE: ON 7 JUNE 2007, A MICHCON CONTRACTOR PERFORMING RECONNAISSANCE FOR ENVIRONMENTAL PERMITTING REPORTED LEAKAGE INDICATIONS APPROXIMATELY 200 YARDS WEST OF BLOCK VALVE 5 ALONG THE AUSTIN-DETROIT A PIPELINE.  THE PIPELINE WAS ISOLATED BETWEEN ADJACENT BLOCK VALVES, AND THE PIPLE LINE PRESSURE WAS REDUCED FROM 700 TO APPROXIMATELY 163 PSIG USING STORAGE FIELD COMPRESSORS.  THE REMAINING PRESSURE WAS BLOWN TO ATMOSPHERE, THE PIPELINE WAS DE-PRESSURIZED, AND REPAIRS COMMENCED ON 8 JUNE 2007. A SEVEN FOOT SEGMENT OF PIPE WAS REMOVED AND A NEW SEGMENT OF PRE-TESTED 24" PIPE WAS INSTALLED TO ELIMINATE THE LEAK.  THE PIPELINE WAS PURGED OF AIR, PRESSURIZED, AND RETURNED TO SERVICE ON 11 JUNE 2007.    THE INCIDENT WAS REPORTED TO THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER AT 1543 HOURS ON 8 JUNE 2007 WHEN IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE TOTAL COST OF THE REPAIR WOULD EXCEED $50,000, PRIMARILY DUE TO THE VOLUME OF GAS BEING BLOWN TO ATMOSPHERE BETWEEN ADJACENT ISOLATING VALVES.    UPON EXCAVATING THE PIPELINE THE LEAK WAS FOUND ON AN OLD, PREVIOUS REPAIR CONSISTING OF A 2-INCH STEEL COUPLING WELDED OVER A LEAKING GIRTH WELD.  THE COUPLING AND PLUG HAD BEEN INSTALLED AT THE 12 O'CLOCK (TOP) POSITION OF THE PIPELINE OVER THE FIELD GIRTH WELD AND A LONGITUDINAL WELD SEAM OF THE PIPE.  THE COUPLING HAD BEEN PLUGGED WITH A TWO-INCH THREADED STEEL BULL PLUG WHERE THE THREADS HAD THEN BEEN SEALED BY WELDING.  LEAKAGE WAS OBSERVED AT THE WELDED THREADS BETWEEN THE COUPLING AND THE BULL PLUG.
narrative_clean: on 7 june 2007, a michcon contractor performing reconnaissance for environmental permitting reported leakage indications approximately 200 yards west of block valve 5 along the austin-detroit a pipeline. the pipeline was isolated between adjacent block valves, and the piple line pressure was reduced from 700 to approximately 163 psig using storage field compressors. the remaining pressure was blown to atmosphere, the pipeline was de-pressurized, and repairs commenced on 8 june 2007. a seven foot segment of pipe was removed and a new segment of pre-tested 24" pipe was installed to eliminate the leak. the pipeline was purged of air, pressurized, and returned to service on 11 june 2007. the incident was reported to the national response center at 1543 hours on 8 june 2007 when it was determined that the total cost of the repair would exceed $50,000, primarily due to the volume of gas being blown to atmosphere between adjacent isolating valves. upon excavating the pipeline the leak was found on an old, previous repair consisting of a 2-inch steel coupling welded over a leaking girth weld. the coupling and plug had been installed at the 12 o'clock (top) position of the pipeline over the field girth weld and a longitudinal weld seam of the pipe. the coupling had been plugged with a two-inch threaded steel bull plug where the threads had then been sealed by welding. leakage was observed at the welded threads between the coupling and the bull plug.

THE COST ESTIMATE IS LESS THAN THE $50,000 THRESHOLD FOR REPORTING. NAME: NORTHERN NATURAL GAS CO
NARRATIVE: ON NOVEMBER 3, 2007 @ APPROXIMATELY 8:51 A.M. THE TEXAS OCHILTREE COUNTY SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT RECEIVED A 911 CALL REPORTING A FIRE AT NORTHERN'S PERRYTON-BARLOW FIELD COMPRESSOR STATION. NORTHEN WAS IMMEDIATELY NOTIFIED AN PERSONNEL WERE DISPATCHED. UPON ARRIVAL IT WAS CONFIRMED THAT THE GLYCOL DEHYDRATOR UNIT, LOCATED AT THE PERRYTON-BARLOW COMPRESSOR STATION WAS ON FIRE. AFTER ASSESSING THE SITUATION, AND TAKING INTO CONSIDERATION THE PROXIMITY OF THE FIRE TO THE EMERGENCY BLOW-DOWN PIPING, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN SYSTEM FOR THE STATION COULD SAFELY BE ACTIVATED. THE LOCAL FIRE DEPARTMENT EXITINGUISHED THE FIRE. INVESTIGATION INTO THE INCIDENT FOUND THAT THE FIRE HAD OCCURRED ON THE DEHYDRATOR SKID WITH MOST OF THE DAMAGE CENTERED AT THE VARIABLE FREQUENCY DRIVE (VFD) FOR THE GLYCOL PUMPS, WHICH IS BELIEVED TO BE THE ORIGIN OF THE FIRE. IT APPEARS THE FIRE WAS FUELED BY HYDROCARBON CONDENSATE AND GLYCOL SPILLING OUT THE OVERFLOW VENT STACK, LOCATED ON THE DEHYDRATOR SKID, ONTO THE VFD CONTROLS FOR THE VFD. THE POSITIONING OF THE VFD AS IT RELATED TO THE OVERFLOW VENT STACK WAS A CONTRIBUTING FACTOR. ADDITIONAL INVESTIGATION INDICATES THAT AS SOME POINT THE GLYCOL RECIRCULATING PUMPS MUST HAVE STOPPED WORKING WHICH ALLOWED THE MIXTURE OF HYDROCARBON CONDENSTATE AND GLYCOL TO DRAIN BACK TO THE OVERFLOW TANK RESULTING IN A SPILL FROM THE OVERFLOW PIPING ONTO THE VFD CONTROLS. NORTHERN IS CURRENTLY WORKING WITH EQUIPMENT VENDORS TO ACQUIRE COST AND AVILABILITY OF REPLACING THE DEHYDRATOR UNIT. A CURRENT ESTIMATE OF REPLACEMENT IS ESTIMATED AT APPROXIMATELY $140,000.  SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT FILED TO INDICATE/CLARIFY PART A, ITEM G CLASS LOCATION DESCRIPTION IS: ONSHORE, CLASS 1.  SUPPLEMENTAL/FINAL REPORT - A FINAL COST OF $152,907 HAS BEEN DETERMINED TO REPLACE THE DAMAGED DEHY UNIT AND THE ASSOCIATED ELECTRICAL AND CONTROL PANELS. THIS ITEM IS CONSIDERED CLOSED WITH NO FURTHER ACTIONS PLANNED.
narrative_clean: on november 3, 2007 @ approximately 8:51 a.m. the texas ochiltree county sheriff's department received a 911 call reporting a fire at northern's perryton-barlow field compressor station. northen was immediately notified an personnel were dispatched. upon arrival it was confirmed that the glycol dehydrator unit, located at the perryton-barlow compressor station was on fire. after assessing the situation, and taking into consideration the proximity of the fire to the emergency blow-down piping, it was determined that the emergency shutdown system for the station could safely be activated. the local fire department exitinguished the fire. investigation into the incident found that the fire had occurred on the dehydrator skid with most of the damage centered at the variable frequency drive (vfd) for the glycol pumps, which is believed to be the origin of the fire. it appears the fire was fueled by hydrocarbon condensate and glycol spilling out the overflow vent stack, located on the dehydrator skid, onto the vfd controls for the vfd. the positioning of the vfd as it related to the overflow vent stack was a contributing factor. additional investigation indicates that as some point the glycol recirculating pumps must have stopped working which allowed the mixture of hydrocarbon condenstate and glycol to drain back to the overflow tank resulting in a spill from the overflow piping onto the vfd controls. northern is currently working with equipment vendors to acquire cost and avilability of replacing the dehydrator unit. a current estimate of replacement is estimated at approximately $140,000. supplemental report filed to indicate/clarify part a, item g class location description is: onshore, class 1. supplemental/final report - a final cost of $152,907 has been determined to replace the damaged dehy unit and the associated electrical and control panels. this item is considered closed with no further actions planned.

NAME: CROSSTEX LIG, LLC
NARRATIVE: ON OCTOBER 30, 2007, AT 0927 HOURS, CROSSTEX LIG, L.L.C. (CROSSTEX), A SUBSIDIARY OF CROSSTEX ENERGY SERVICES, L.P. REPORTED A NATURAL GAS AND CONDENSATE RELEASE FROM THEIR 6-INCH UNDERGROUND TRANSMISSION PIPELINE IN DE SOTO PARISH, LOUISIANA. THE RELEASE WAS CAUSED BY A  BACKHOE STRIKING AND DAMAGING THE PIPELINE DURING EXCAVATION. CROSSTEX REPORTED THE UNAUTHORIZED RELEASE TO THE LOUISIANA EMERGENCY HAZARDOUS MATERIALS HOTLINE (INCIDENT NO. 07-06604), AND THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER (NRC) WAS ALSO NOTIFIED OF THE EVENT (INCIDENT NO. 853067).    AFTER THE INITIAL EMERGENCY RESPONSE, IT WAS DETERMINED DURING THE INVESTIGATION THAT THE CAUSE OF THE RELEASE AND SUBSEQUENT CONDENSATE SPILL WAS FROM AN UNIDENTIFIED TAP VALVE THAT WAS INADVERTENTLY BROKEN OFF BY A CONTRACTOR UTILIZING EXCAVATION EQUIPMENT DURING CONSTRUCTION ACTIVITIES, CREATING AN APPROXIMATE 2-INCH HOLE IN THE PIPELINE. CROSSTEX PERSONNEL WERE PREVIOUSLY UNAWARE OF THE PRESENCE OF SUCH TAP VALVE AS IT WAS NOT INDICATED ON FACILITY DRAWINGS. CROSSTEX PERSONNEL ON THE SCENE OF THE INCIDENT QUICKLY ISOLATED THE AFFECTED PIPELINE SEGMENT, AND CAREFULLY EXCAVATED AROUND THE DAMAGED TAP VALVE GAINING ACCESS TO THE DAMAGED PORTION OF THE PIPELINE. REPAIRS TO THE PIPELINE AND PURGING ACTIVITIES WERE FINALIZED BY 1645 HOURS AND GAS SERVICE TO THE TOWN OF LOGANSPORT WAS RESTORED BY 1750 HOURS THE DAY OF THE INCIDENT.    THERE WAS ONE INJURY ASSOCIATED WITH INCIDENT WHICH OCCURRED WHEN THE CONTRACT BACKHOE OPERATOR EXITED THE EXCAVATOR AND TWISTED HIS KNEE. HE WAS TAKEN TO A LOCAL HOSPITAL FOR A DOCTOR'S EXAMINATION AND WAS RELEASED THE SAME DAY. HOWEVER IT IS ANTICIPATED THAT ADDITIONAL TREATMENT WILL BE REQUIRED DUE THE NATURE OF THE INJURY.    200 MCF (THOUSAND CUBIC FEET)OR APPROXIMATELY 9,341 POUNDS OF SWEET NATURAL GAS AND LESS THAN TWO (2) BARRELS OF CONDENSATE WERE RELEASED. A CLEANUP CREW TRAINED IN EMERGENCY RESPONSE WAS SUMMONED BY CROSSTEX TO REMOVE SOILS IMPACTED BY CONDENSATE. THE EXCAVATED MATERIALS WERE PROPERLY STORED IN THE COVERED ROLL-OFF BINS PENDING TRANSPORTATION TO AN OFF-SITE LOCATION FOR PROPER DISPOSAL. SUBSEQUENT TO THE CLEANUP ACTIVITIES, A NUMBER OF CONFIRMATORY SOIL SAMPLES ARE SCHEDULED FOR COLLECTION BY 11/09/07. UPON RECEIPT OF THE ANALYTICAL DATA DEOMONSTRATING NO PRESENCE OF CONDENSATE IN THE AFFECTED AREA, CLEAN FILL WILL BE PLACED OVER THE EXCAVATED AREA.
narrative_clean: on october 30, 2007, at 0927 hours, crosstex lig, l.l.c. (crosstex), a subsidiary of crosstex energy services, l.p. reported a natural gas and condensate release from their 6-inch underground transmission pipeline in de soto parish, louisiana. the release was caused by a backhoe striking and damaging the pipeline during excavation. crosstex reported the unauthorized release to the louisiana emergency hazardous materials hotline (incident no. 07-06604), and the national response center (nrc) was also notified of the event (incident no. 853067). after the initial emergency response, it was determined during the investigation that the cause of the release and subsequent condensate spill was from an unidentified tap valve that was inadvertently broken off by a contractor utilizing excavation equipment during construction activities, creating an approximate 2-inch hole in the pipeline. crosstex personnel were previously unaware of the presence of such tap valve as it was not indicated on facility drawings. crosstex personnel on the scene of the incident quickly isolated the affected pipeline segment, and carefully excavated around the damaged tap valve gaining access to the damaged portion of the pipeline. repairs to the pipeline and purging activities were finalized by 1645 hours and gas service to the town of logansport was restored by 1750 hours the day of the incident. there was one injury associated with incident which occurred when the contract backhoe operator exited the excavator and twisted his knee. he was taken to a local hospital for a doctor's examination and was released the same day. however it is anticipated that additional treatment will be required due the nature of the injury. 200 mcf (thousand cubic feet)or approximately 9,341 pounds of sweet natural gas and less than two (2) barrels of condensate were released. a cleanup crew trained in emergency response was summoned by crosstex to remove soils impacted by condensate. the excavated materials were properly stored in the covered roll-off bins pending transportation to an off-site location for proper disposal. subsequent to the cleanup activities, a number of confirmatory soil samples are scheduled for collection by 11/09/07. upon receipt of the analytical data deomonstrating no presence of condensate in the affected area, clean fill will be placed over the excavated area.

NAME: SOUTHERN NATURAL GAS CO
NARRATIVE: A LOCAL HUNTER WAS SHOOTING AT A COYOTE IN POLK COUNTY, GA, NEAR SOUTHERN NATURAL GAS COMPANY'S CEDARTOWN GATE SETTING ON ITS 14" CHATTANOOGA BRANCH PIPELINE.  THE HUNTER ACCIDENTALLY HIT THE 4" BLOWOFF RISER PIPE UPSTREAM OF THE ISOLATION VALVE AT THE GATE SETTING.  THE BULLET PUNCTURED THE PIPE RESULTING IN A HOLE ABOOUT ONE-HALF INCH IN DIAMETER (THIS REPORT SHOWS A 1" HOLE BUT THAT FIELD ON THE FORM WOULD NOT TAKE A DECIMAL NUMBER NOR A FRACTION).  GAS ESCAPED UNTIL THE LINE SEGMENT WAS ISOLATED.  AFTER ISOLATION, THE PIPE WAS BLOWN DOWN AND A WELDOLET WAS INSTALLED AT THE POINT OF THE BULLET HOLE WITH A THREADED PLUG INSERTED INTO THE HOLE.  ABOUT TEN HOMES WERE EVACUATED SHORTLY AFTER THE INCIDENT BEGAN AS A PRECAUTIONARY MEASURE BY LOCAL OFFICIALS.  THE NEARBY ROAD WAS CLOSED AS WAS A NEARBY RAILROAD OPERATED BY CSX.

narrative_clean: at 6:06 pm on december 1, 2007, a pot drip located on pipeline tl-453 ruptured, in potter county, pa. the pipeline was isolated (by dominion personnel) and evacuated of natural gas by 9:30 pm. the cause of the incident was initially identified as internal corrosion. the pipe has been sent to cc technologies for analysis in order to confirm the failure mechanism. the pipeline remained out of service while assessment work was performed. the pipeline was placed back in service on december 12, 2007. update - cc technologies has determined that the primary casue of the internal corrosion was a high chloride level, and under-seposit corrosion. the secondary cause was acid-producing bacteria (apb)

NAME: CENTERPOINT ENERGY GAS TRANSMISSION
NARRATIVE: METALLURGICAL REPORT SHOWED THE FAILURE INITIATED AT A BUCKLE THAT AFFECTED THE LONG SEAM OF THE PIPE.  IT IS NOT KNOW FOR SURE WHAT CAUSED THE BUCKLE, BUT ONE POSSIBLE SCENARIO WHICH COULD EXPLAIN THE INCIDENT IS THE BUCKLE DEVELOPED IN RESPONSE TO GROUND MOVEMENT OR SUBSIDENCE.  THIS SITUATION APPEARED TO HAVE EXISTED FOR A NUMBER OF YEARS SLOWLY WORSENING UNTIL IT FAILED.  THERE WAS NO EVIDENCE THIS WAS A SHORT TERM EVENT SUCH AS AN EARTHQUAKE AND THE EVIDENCE AT THE SURFACE SEEMED TO SUPPORT THAT AS WELL.  ONE IMPORTANT THING FROM THE REPORT IS THAT THIS DOES NOT APPEAR TO BE A SYSTEMIC EPISODE.  THE PIPE ANALYSIS AND TESTING INDICATES WE HAVE A SOUND PIPE, THAT IS, THERE ARE NO INHERENT SEAM ISSUES AND THERE IS ADEQUATE TOUGHNESS TO ARREST AND CONTROL FRACTURES.   COPY OF REPORT SENT TO OPS.
narrative_clean: metallurgical report showed the failure initiated at a buckle that affected the long seam of the pipe. it is not know for sure what caused the buckle, but one possible scenario which could explain the incident is the buckle developed in response to ground movement or subsidence. this situation appeared to have existed for a number of years slowly worsening until it failed. there was no evidence this was a short term event such as an earthquake and the evidence at the surface seemed to support that as well. one important thing from the report is that this does not appear to be a systemic episode. the pipe analysis and testing indicates we have a sound pipe, that is, there are no inherent seam issues and there is adequate toughness to arrest and control fractures. copy of report sent to ops.

NAME: ANR PIPELINE CO

ONCE GROUND GAS LEVELS WERE LOWERED TO A SAFE LEVEL, THE PIPELINE WAS EXCAVATED TO LOCATE THE SOURCE OF THE LEAK.  UPON DETERMINING THE LEAK LOCATION, A 50-FOOT SEGMENT WAS REMOVED AND REPLACED.  THE REPLACEMENT SEGMENT AND THE REMAINING SEGMENTS OF THE EXISTING 8¿ LOW PRESSURE RECYCLE LINE WERE PRESSURE TESTED FOR 8 HOURS. WE CONTINUED TO MONITOR THE LEAK SITE ON A 24HR SHIFT, WE MANNED THE BLOCK VALVES AT EACH END ON 24 HR SHIFT AND MANUALLY FED THAT SECTION TO KEEP AT 320 #¿S AND MAINTAIN CUSTOMERS.  2/29/08 7:30AM, WE PROCCURED FITTINGS AND BEGAN INSTALLING STOPPLE FITTINGS ON EACH SIDE OF SECTION OF PIPE LEAKING. NAME: VIKING GAS TRANSMISSION CO

NARRATIVE: THE 6" 45 DEGREE FITTING WAS SENT TO A TESTING LAB FOR FAILURE ANALYSIS. DURING CONSTRUCTION OF THE GRAND FORKS LEVEE BY THE ARMY CORPS OF ENGINEERS, HEAVY EQUIPMENT MAY HAVE CROSSED THE PIPELINE IN THIS LOCATION, WHICH MAY HAVE INITIATED THE CRACKING OF THE FITTING AND RESULTANT FAILURE. THE RESULTS OF THE ANALYSIS CONCLUDED:  1) EXCESSIVE EXTERNAL STRAIN CAUSED TRANSVERSE CRACKS IN THE EPOXY COATING AND AND WERE PROBABLY RELATED TO ABOVE GROUND FORCES DIRECTLY OVER THE PIPELINE ELBOW.  2) THE CRACKS IN THE EPOXY COATING RESULTED IN SEPARATION OF THE COATING FROM THE PIPE.   3) THERE WERE NUMEROUS CRACK LIKE FEATURES (CLF) ON THE INSIDE SURFACE OF THE ELBOW. TWO FATIGUE CRACKS INITATED AT THESE CLF'S AND CONTINUED TO CRACK THROUGH THE ENTIRE WALL THICKNESS UNTIL LEAKAGE OCCURRED. THE PRIMARY CAUSE OF THE FAILED FITTING AND GAS LEAKAGE WAS EXTERNAL STRESSES.
narrative_clean: the 6" 45 degree fitting was sent to a testing lab for failure analysis. during construction of the grand forks levee by the army corps of engineers, heavy equipment may have crossed the pipeline in this location, which may have initiated the cracking of the fitting and resultant failure. the results of the analysis concluded: 1) excessive external strain caused transverse cracks in the epoxy coating and and were probably related to above ground forces directly over the pipeline elbow. 2) the cracks in the epoxy coating resulted in separation of the coating from the pipe. 3) there were numerous crack like features (clf) on the inside surface of the elbow. two fatigue cracks initated at these clf's and continued to crack through the entire wall thickness until leakage occurred. the primary cause of the failed fitting and gas leakage was external stresses.

NAME: ENTERPRISE PRODUCTS OPERATING LLC
CAUSE: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD
NARRATIVE: GAS BUBBLES WERE DETECTED AT THE SURFACE OF MC 920.  AFTER INVESTIGATION, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE FLEX JOINT SEAL RING WAS LEAKING.  PIPELINE WAS SECURED AND REPAIR PROCEDURES HAVE BEEN IMPLEMENTED AND WORK IS ONGOING.    THE OFFSHORE REPLACEMENT OPERATION OF THE 20¿ FLEX-JOINT O-RING WAS PERFORMED IN THREE (3) PHASES:     PHASE I, DETAILED INSPECTION AND INITIAL BOLT TIGHTENING APRIL 9, TO APRIL 23, 2008   PHASE II, FLEX-JOINT O-RING REPLACEMENT APRIL 24, TO JUNE 16, 2008   PHASE III, FINAL BOLT TIGHTENING, UT VERIFICATION, TESTING JULY 28, TO AUGUST 8, 2008      ENTERPRISE CONFIRMS THE 20 INCH FLEX-JOINT O-RING REMEDIATION WAS SUCCESSFULLY COMPLETED IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE WORK PLAN, AND ON AUGUST 9, 2008 NORMAL PRODUCTION WAS RESUMED IN THE GAS EXPORT PIPELINE. FOR THE POST INSPECTION PERIOD, AUGUST 8, TO SEPT 8, 2008, ¿REMOTE CAMERAS¿ WERE USED TO MONITOR THE FLEX-JOINT.     ENTERPRISE AND OIL STATES HAVE WORKED CLOSELY TO ANALYZE AND EVALUATE BOTH HISTORIC AND PROJECT DATA ON THE FLEX-JOINT AND INCIDENT TO BEST DETERMINE THE DIRECT CAUSE OF THE LEAK.      THERE WAS NO IDENTIFIED SINGLE ITEM OR CLEAR DIRECT CAUSE FOR THE LEAK.  HOWEVER, THE EVALUATION AND ANALYSIS POINTS TO A SERIES OF EVENTS THAT TOGETHER MOST LIKELY CONTRIBUTED TO THE CAUSE OF THE LEAK.  THE FACTORS IDENTIFIED INCLUDED POSSIBLE INCORRECT ATTACH FLANGE BOLT TORQUE VALUE READINGS DURING THE FINAL MANUFACTURING SHOP ASSEMBLY, WHICH COULD ALLOW EXCESS ATTACH FLANGE DEFLECTION, AND SLIGHT BOLT RELAXATION DURING HYDROTESTING.  THE O-RING DESIGN, DIMENSION, AND DISSIMILAR MATERIALS WERE ALSO A FACTOR.  AFTER OFFSHORE INSTALLATION OF THE FLEX-JOINT AND DURING PIPELINE OPERATIONS, FRETTING BEGAN TO TAKE PLACE WITHIN THE O-RING SEAL SYSTEM.  THIS DEVELOPMENT THEN LED TO THE PROGRESSION OF MINOR CORROSION, AND INDUCTION OF SEA WATER, WHICH AFTER A PERIOD OF TIME PROGRESSED UNTIL THE LEAK STARTED.    DURING THE OFFSHORE REPAIR PHASES, CORRECTIVE ACTIONS WERE IMPLEMENTED TO ADDRESS EACH OF THE POTENTIAL CAUSES, WHICH INCLUDED A NEWLY DESIGNED LARGER O-RING WHICH IS NOW THE SAME MATERIAL AS THE ATTACH FLANGE, AND ACCURATE BOLT TORQUING MEASURED AND VERIFIED BY UT STUD ELONGATION PROCESS.  THIS UT PROCESS ELIMINATES ANY UNKNOWN FRICTION FACTORS WHICH AFFECT BOLT TORQUE VALUES.
narrative_clean: gas bubbles were detected at the surface of mc 920. after investigation, it was determined that the flex joint seal ring was leaking. pipeline was secured and repair procedures have been implemented and work is ongoing. the offshore replacement operation of the 20¿ flex-joint o-ring was performed in three (3) phases: phase i, detailed inspection and initial bolt tightening april 9, to april 23, 2008 phase ii, flex-joint o-ring replacement april 24, to june 16, 2008 phase iii, final bolt tightening, ut verification, testing july 28, to august 8, 2008 enterprise confirms the 20 inch flex-joint o-ring remediation was successfully completed in accordance with the work plan, and on august 9, 2008 normal production was resumed in the gas export pipeline. for the post inspection period, august 8, to sept 8, 2008, ¿remote cameras¿ were used to monitor the flex-joint. enterprise and oil states have worked closely to analyze and evaluate both historic and project data on the flex-joint and incident to best determine the direct cause of the leak. there was no identified single item or clear direct cause for the leak. however, the evaluation and analysis points to a series of events that together most likely contributed to the cause of the leak. the factors identified included possible incorrect attach flange bolt torque value readings during the final manufacturing shop assembly, which could allow excess attach flange deflection, and slight bolt relaxation during hydrotesting. the o-ring design, dimension, and dissimilar materials were also a factor. after offshore installation of the flex-joint and during pipeline operations, fretting began to take place within the o-ring seal system. this development then led to the progression of minor corrosion, and induction of sea water, which after a period of time progressed until the leak started. during the offshore repair phases, corrective actions were implemented to address each of the potential causes, which included a newly designed larger o-ring which is now the same material as the attach flange, and accurate bolt torquing measured and verified by ut stud elongation process. this ut process eliminates any unknown friction factors which affect bolt torque values.

NAME: ATLANTA GAS LIGHT CO
NARRATIVE: THIS INCIDENT BEGAN AS A GRADE 2 LEAK DISCOVERED AT A VALVE BOX OVER A 6-INCH VALVE CONNECTING TO A 24-INCH MAIN DURING THE ANNUAL LEAKAGE SURVEY WHICH DID NOT REQUIRE IMMEDIATE ATTENTION AT THE TIME OF DISCOVEREY. AN INVESTIGATION DETERMINED THAT THE SUPPORT UNDERNEATH THE 6-INCH CONNECTION SUBSIDED DUE TO INCREASED WATER LEVELS IN A LOW AREA. AS A RESULT, THE 24" LINE FAILED IN THE BASE METAL DUE TO DUCTILE OVERLOAD ADJACENT TO THE WELDED JOINT.

NAME: NORTHERN NATURAL GAS CO
CAUSE: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD
NARRATIVE: ON MAY 18, 2008, AT APPROXIMATELY 5:30 P.M., NORTHERN'S OPERATIONS COMMUNICATION CENTER (OCC), RECEIVED A CALL FROM DANA ELIKER, A TECHNICIAN WITH AQUILA, REPORTING THAT THERE WAS A LEAK ON NORTHERN'S TWO-INCH CLATONIA, NE BRANCH LINE (NEB42201)IN A CORNFIELD APPROXIMATELY 1/4 MILE NORTHWEST OF THE TOWN OF CLATONIA, NE. THE LEAK SITE IS LOCATED IN SECTION 21, TOWNSHIP 6N, RANGE 5E, GAGE COUNTY, NE. NORTHERN PERSONNEL UTILIZED A BOTTLE TRUCK AT THE CLATONIA TOWN BORDER STATION TO PROVIDE GAS SERVICE TO THE TOWN WHILE THE BRANCH LINE WAS SHUT OFF FROM THE TAKE OFF TO THE TBS TO SAFELY ASSESS AND REPAIR THE LINE. THIS LINE'S CONSTRUCTION INCLUDES DRESSER COUPLING, ELECTRIC WELDS AND SCREWED COUPLINGS. UPON ASSESSMENT, IT WAS FOUND THAT THE THREADS ON THE PIPE GOING INTO A TWO-INCH SCREWED COUPLING HAD FAILED RESULTING IN LEAKING GAS. LINE PRESSURE WAS REDUCED TO ZERO AND REPAIRS WERE MADE BY CUTTING OUT THE FAILED COUPLING ALONG WITH SMALL PIECES OF THE LINE, ON EACH SIDE OF THE COUPLING, AND INSTALLING APPROXIMATELY 10 FEET OF NEW, TESTED TWO-INCH, .218 WALL THICKNESS PIPE. PRESSURE WAS RESTORED TO 100 PSIG AND THE COMPLETE 1.26 MILES OF LINE WAS INSTRUMENT LEAK DETECTED. THE PRESSURE WAS THEN INCREASED TO NORMAL OPERATING PRESSURE AND THE FULL LENGTH OF THE LINE WAS AGAIN INSTRUMENT LEAK DETECTED. UPON SUCCESSFUL LOADING OF THE LINE TO NORMAL PRESSURE AND NO LEAKS DISCOVERED NORMAL GAS SERVICE WAS RESTORED TO THE TOWN BORDER STATION OF CLATONIA. THE SMALL PIECES OF PIPE AND THE FAILED COUPLING ARE BEING SENT TO A LABORATORY FOR FAILURE ANALYSIS TO ASSIST WITH DETERMINING THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE FAILURE. THERE WAS NO FIRE, NO INJURIES AND NO LOSS OF SERVICE AS THERE ARE NO FARM TAP CUSTOMERS ON THE LINE AND THE CLATONIA TOWN BORDER STATION SERVICE WAS MAINTAINED WITH A BOTTLE TRUCK. THIS REPORT IS BEING FILED AS IT IS EXPECTED THAT REPAIRS, INCLUDING GAS LOSS, WILL EXCEED THE $50,000 REPORTING THRESHOLD.  SUPPLEMENTAL/FINAL REPORT - TOTAL FINAL COST OF REPAIRS, INCLUDING GAS LOSS, ETC IS $283,192. BASED UPON A OUTSIDE SERVICES FAILURE ANALYSIS LABORATORY REPORT, THE ROOT CAUSE OF THIS FAILURE IS BELEIVED TO BE FRACTURING OF THE PIPE BY CLEAVAGE (A FORM OF BRITTLE CRACKING) ORIGINATING IN THE THREAD ROOT IMMEDIATELY ADJACENT TO THE CONNECTION COUPLING. THIS EVENT IS CONSIDERED CLOSED WITH NO FURTHER ACTIONS PENDING OR PLANNED. NORTHERN IS SCHEDULUED ADDITION PRECUATIONARY EQUIPMENT LEAK TESTING OF OTHER SMALL DIAMTER PIPELINES OF THIS SAME VINATAGE AND CONSTRUCTION TO ENABLE EARLY DETECTION OF LEAK SHOULD A SIMILAR CONDITION OCCUR ON ANY OF THESE FACILITIES. THE LINE WAS FOUND TO BE DENTED AND LEAKING, APPARENTLY AS A RESULT OF BEING HIT BY A TILING MACHINE. A 30 FOOT SEGMENT OF PIPE WAS REPLACED WITH NEW, TESTED PIPE. DUE TO THE COATING APPEARING TO BE DISBONDED AND CRACKED A MAGNETIC PARTICLE INSPECTION WAS CONDUCTED ON AREAS OF THE PIPE. A FOUR FOOT PIECE OF THE PIPE WAS REMOVED AND TRANSPORTED TO A LABORATORY FOR ANALYSIS. THE REPAIRED, DAMAGED AREA WAS RE-COATED AND BACK FILLED. LABORATORY ANALYSIS WAS COMPLETED AND NO OTHER FACTORS WERE FOUND TO HAVE CONTRIBUTED TO THE LEAK BEYOND THE DAMAGED SUSTAINED DURING THE DRAINAGE TILE INSTALLATION IN 2006. NARRATIVE: ON MAY 23, AT APPROXIATELY 14:57 THE CARLTON LOCATION WAS NOTIFIED BY ANGEL SERVICE ITT CORP, THAT THEY HAD COMPLETED THEIR AERIAL LEAK SURVEYING. UPON REVIEW OF THE INFORMATION IT APPEARED THAT THERE WAS A DETECTION OF A SINGLE METHANE INDICATION IN LAKE COUNTY, MN ON THE 16-INCH RESERVE (MNB69801) BRANCH LINE ON THE PIPELINE RIGHT OF WAY APPROXIMATELY 1.1 MILES WEST OF LAX LAKE ROAD @ APPROXIMATE MILEPOST 59.5. NORTHERN PERSONNEL PROCEEDED TO REDUCE THE PRESSURE FROM 405 TO 300 PSIG AND SENT PERSONNEL TO THE SITE TO UTILIZE PORTABLE LEAK DETECTION EQUIPMENT TO VERIFY IF THERE WAS A LEAK. A LEAK WAS DETECTED @ THE APPROXIMATE LOCATION INDICATED. A STRONG HYDRO CARBON SMELL WAS DETECTED, A READING OF 5% LEL WAS INDICATED AND A PATCH OF DEAD VEGETATION APPROXIMATELY 15 FT IN DIAMETER WAS NOTED. ACTIONS WERE TAKEN TO ACQUIRE THE SERVICES OF A CONTRACTOR AND ARRANGE FOR NORTHERN'S STOPPLE CREW TO PROCEED TO THE SITE. AN 8-INCH STOPPLE AND BYPASS WAS INSTALLED AROUND THE LEAK AREA, THEN THE SECTION OF LINE WAS BLOWN DOWN AND EXCAVATED. A ROCK WAS FOUND TO HAVE IMPINGED ON THE PIPELINE AT THE 6 O'CLOCK POSITION. THE OWASA BRANCH LINE IS APPROXIMATELY 0.932 MILES LONG AND ORIGINATES FROM A SIDE VALVE ON THE 6-INCH IOWA FALLS BRANCH LINE. THE POINT OF FIRE WAS LOCATED AT APPROXIMATE MILE POST .49. THERE WAS DISBONDED COATING AT THE DISCHARGE POINT ON AN OTHERWISE WELL COATED LINE. THE PIPE WALL WAS SHINY AND HAD NOT EVEN FLASH RUSTED YET. NAME: NORTHERN NATURAL GAS CO
NARRATIVE: ON JULY 18, 2008, AT APPROXIMATELY 1 A.M., A PRESSURE DROP ON THE BEATRICE A LINE (NEM40101) MAINLINE WAS NOTED BY NORTHERN'S GAS CONTROL DEPARTMENT. PRESSURE ON THE LINE HAD BEEN CONSISTENTLY OPERATING IN THE 490 PSIG PRESSURE RANGE. THIS PIPELINE IS A DRESSER COUPLED PIPELINE. THE BEATRICE AREA HAD BEEN SUBJECT TO VERY HEAVY RAIN AND THUNDERSTORMS AND WARNINGS OF POTENTIAL FLASH FLOODING ON RIVERS AND  WATERWAYS. AN ALL-CALL WAS ISSUED TO THE BEATRICE REGION TEAMS. BASED ON  THE PRESSURE DROP STEPS WERE TAKEN TO IMMEDIATELY IDENTIFY TOWNS THAT COULD BE ADVERSELY IMPACTED  AND THEY WERE SWITCHED OVER TO OTHER GAS SOURCE SERVICES. ONCE THIS WAS COMPLETED STEPS WERE TAKEN TO ISOLATE AN APPROXIMATE 13 MILES OF THIS LINE BY CLOSING BLOCK A  BLOCK VALVES ON THE LINE AT THE BEATRICE COMPRESSOR PLANT AND BLOCK VALVE # 6 ON THE MAINLINE. FIVE SMALL VOLUME CUSTOMERS WERE IDENTIFIED AND NOTIFIED. FOUR WERE DOMESTIC  USE FARM TAPS AND ONE WAS AN IRRIGATION SETTING. AS THERE WAS NO OUTSIDE NOTIFICATION OF A POTENTIAL DAMAGE SITE APPROPRIATE STEPS WERE TAKEN FOR TWO PEOPLE TEAMS TO VISUALLY CHECK THE 13 MILE SEGMENT OF PIPE FOR POTENTIAL SIGNS OF BLOWING GAS AND/OR DAMAGE.IT WAS FOUND THAT A JOINT OF PIPE APPROXIMATELY 25 FEET LONG, IN A WATERWAY, HAD BLOWN OUT OF THE GROUND. THIS SITE IS LOCATED APPROXIMATELY 500 FEET NORTH OF MILEPOST 50.67 IN SECTION 32, TOWNSHIP 3N, RANGE 6E, ALL IN GAGE COUNTY NEBRASKA. THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER AND PHMSA CENTRAL REGION WAS NOTIFIED. THERE WAS NO FIRE, NO INJURIES AND NO LOSS OF SERVICE TO ANY TOWNS. NORTHERN IS CURRENTLY TAKING APPROPRIATE ACTIONS TO MAKE REPAIRS TO THE LINE. THIS EVENT WAS REPORTED TO THE NRC AND PHMSA AND A 7100 REPORT IS BEING FILED AS THE COST OF THE FAILURE, INCLUDING GAS LOSS WILL EXCEED THE $50,000 REPORTING THRESHOLD LEVEL. A FINAL CAUSE FOR THE FAILURE IS UNDER INVESTIGATION, HOWEVER IT IS CURRENT BELIEVED THAT THE HEAVY RAINS AND FLOODING OF THE  WATERWAY RESULTED IN EROSION OF SUPPORTING DIRT AROUND THE PIPELINES DRESSER COUPLING WHICH RESULTED IN ADDITIONAL FORCE OF WATER FLOW ON THE DRESSER COUPLINGS WHICH   ULTIMATELY LEAD TO THE FAILURE OF A DRESSER COUPLING. APPROPRIATE SUPPLEMENTAL INFORMATION SUCH AS TOTAL COST OF REPAIRS AND MATERIALS REQUIRED TO EFFECT REPAIRS WILL  BE REPORTED.  SUPPLEMENTAL/FINAL REPORT: AN INVESTIGATION INTO THE CAUSE OF THE FAILURE DETERMINED THAT THE CAUSE WAS HEAVY LOCALIZED RAIN FALL WASH OUT THE DIRT ON THE BANKS AROUND DRESSER COUPLING WHICH ALLOWED THE WATER FORCE TO SEPARATE THE PIPE FROM A DRESSER COUPLING. APPROXIMATELY 269 FEET OF NEW 24 INCH TESTED PIPE WAS INSTALLED TO COMPLETE THE REPAIR PROCESS. AN UPDATED ESTIMATE OF TOTAL COST HAS BEEN ENTERED ON THIS FINAL REPORT. THIS EVENT IS CONSIDERED COMPLETE AND CLOSED WITH NO FURTHER ACTIONS PENDING OR PLANNED.  09/18/2012 ADDED INCIDENT COORDINATES AS PER REQUST OF JIM BUNN, PHMSA.

NAME: CORNHUSKER ENERGY LEXINGTON, L.L.C.
NARRATIVE: MULTIPLE REGULATOR MALFUNCTION INVOLVING PRESSURE CONTROL REGULATORS AND MONITOR REGULATORS.  THE REGULATOR STATION WAS INSPECTED AND SERVICED AFTER THE INCIDENT BY RON FICHTNER WITH KAL INC. UTILITY OPERATIONS SERVICE AND HIS REPORT STATES THE FOLLOWING:  "THE FAILURE OF THE REGULATORS AT CORNHUSKER ENERGY WAS CAUSED BY FREEZE OFF IN THE PILOT REGULATORS CAUSING THE OPERATING RUN REGULATORS TO FAIL OPEN AND OVER PRESSURING THE PLASTIC PIPELINE.   THE INSPECTION OF THE FIRST CUT OPERATING REGULATOR RUN FOUND THE WORKING REGULATOR'S PILOT REGULATOR COMPLETELY FULL OF LIQUIDS CAUSING THE FREEZE OFF.  THE PILOT REGULATOR SEAT WAS TORN WHICH COULD ALSO CAUSE THE REGULATOR TO FAIL IN AN OPEN POSITION.  THE PILOT FILTER WAS ALSO INSPECTED AND IT TOO HAD LIQUIDS IN IT.  THE MONITOR REGULATOR PILOT, IN THE FIRST CUT OPERATING REGULATOR RUN, HAD SOME LIQUID IN IT AND ALSO THE PILOT FILTER HAD TRACES OF LIQUID IN IT.  THE DIAPHRAM OF THE MONITOR REGULATOR HAD SOME SEPARATION SPOTS AROUND THE CAGE SLOTS WHICH WOULD PREVENT 100% LOCK UP OF THE MONITOR REGULATOR.     THE STAND BY REGULATORS OF THE FIRST CUT REGULATOR RUN HAD TRACES OF LIQUIDS IN TEH PILOTS OF BOTH THE WORKING AND MONITOR REGULATOR WITH TRACES OF LIQUID FOUND IN BOTH OF THE PILOT FILTERS.  WELDING SLAG WAS FOUND IN THE CAGE SLOTS OF BOTH TEH OPERATING AND MONITOR REGULATORS WHICH WOULD PREVENT 100% LOCK UP OF THE REGULATORS.  THERE WERE ALSO SMALL SPOTS OF DIAPHRAGM SEPARATION IN THE DIAPHRAGMS OF BOTH REGULATORS WHICH CAN PREVENT 100% LOCKUP.   THE STRAINERS FOR THE FIRST CUT REGULATOR RUNS WERE ALSO INSPECTED.  THEY WERE MODERATELY CLEAN WITH SOME PLUG GREASE FOUND ALONG WITH TRACES OF LIQUID IN THEM.  THE INSPECTION OF THE SECOND CUT OPERATING REGULATOR RUN FOUND BOTH THE WORKING AND THE MONITOR REGULATOR PILOTS COMPLETELY FULL OF LIQUIDS CAUSING THE FREEZE OFF.  THE FILTERS FOR BOTH OF THE PILOT REGULATORS WERE ALSO COMPLETELY FULL OF LIQUIDS.  THE BODIES OF BOTH OF THE WORKING AND MONITOR REGULATORS HAD ICE CRYSTALS IN THE CAGE SCREEN.  THERE WERE ALSO SMALL SPOTS OF SEPARATION IN BOTH REGULATORS WHICH CAN PREVENT 100% LOCKUP.  THE STRAINER FOR THIS RUN WAS INSPECTED AND FOUND TO CONTAIN QUITE A BIT OF PLUG GREASE IN IT ALONG WITH TRACES OF LIQUID.  THE INSPECTION OF THE SECOND CUT STAND BY REGULATOR RUN SHOWED NO GAS FLOW WHICH IS EXACTLY AS IT SHOULD HAVE BEEN.  THE REGULATOR BODIES OF BOTH TEH WORKER AND MONITOR WERE CLEAN AND DRY AS WERE THE PILOTS AND THE PILOT FILTERS.  THE STRAINER FOR THIS RUN WAS ALSO INSPECTED AND FOUND TO BE CLEAN AND DRY."    FOLLOWING THE INSPECTION BY KAL INC. ALL REGULATORS WERE SERVICED AND REPAIRED.    IN CONSIDERATION OF THE FINDINGS OF KAL INC., CORNHUSKER ENERGY HAS ADDED SAFETY MEASURES TO PREVENT SIMILAR INCIDENTS IN THE FUTURE.  A FULL RELIEF POP-OFF HAS BEEN INSTALLED FOLLOWING THE REGULATOR STATION AND THE RELIEF IS SET TO A VALUE EQUAL TO THE MAOP OF THE PLASTIC LINE.  IN THE EVENT OF OVERPRESSURIZATION DUE TO MULTIPLE REGULATOR FAILURE THE RELIEF WILL LIFT AND RELIEVE PRESSURE TO THE MAOP VALUE.  IN ADDITION, WITH CONSIDERATION OF THE FINDINGS OF KAL INC., CORNHUSKER ENERGY HAS INITIATED COMMUNICATIONS WITH KINDER MORGAN IN AN EFFORT TO EXPLAIN THE FINDINGS OF THE REPORT.
narrative_clean: multiple regulator malfunction involving pressure control regulators and monitor regulators. the regulator station was inspected and serviced after the incident by ron fichtner with kal inc. utility operations service and his report states the following: "the failure of the regulators at cornhusker energy was caused by freeze off in the pilot regulators causing the operating run regulators to fail open and over pressuring the plastic pipeline. the inspection of the first cut operating regulator run found the working regulator's pilot regulator completely full of liquids causing the freeze off. the pilot regulator seat was torn which could also cause the regulator to fail in an open position. the pilot filter was also inspected and it too had liquids in it. the monitor regulator pilot, in the first cut operating regulator run, had some liquid in it and also the pilot filter had traces of liquid in it. the diaphram of the monitor regulator had some separation spots around the cage slots which would prevent 100% lock up of the monitor regulator. the stand by regulators of the first cut regulator run had traces of liquids in teh pilots of both the working and monitor regulator with traces of liquid found in both of the pilot filters. welding slag was found in the cage slots of both teh operating and monitor regulators which would prevent 100% lock up of the regulators. there were also small spots of diaphragm separation in the diaphragms of both regulators which can prevent 100% lockup. the strainers for the first cut regulator runs were also inspected. they were moderately clean with some plug grease found along with traces of liquid in them. the inspection of the second cut operating regulator run found both the working and the monitor regulator pilots completely full of liquids causing the freeze off. the filters for both of the pilot regulators were also completely full of liquids. the bodies of both of the working and monitor regulators had ice crystals in the cage screen. there were also small spots of separation in both regulators which can prevent 100% lockup. the strainer for this run was inspected and found to contain quite a bit of plug grease in it along with traces of liquid. the inspection of the second cut stand by regulator run showed no gas flow which is exactly as it should have been. the regulator bodies of both teh worker and monitor were clean and dry as were the pilots and the pilot filters. the strainer for this run was also inspected and found to be clean and dry." following the inspection by kal inc. all regulators were serviced and repaired. in consideration of the findings of kal inc., cornhusker energy has added safety measures to prevent similar incidents in the future. a full relief pop-off has been installed following the regulator station and the relief is set to a value equal to the maop of the plastic line. in the event of overpressurization due to multiple regulator failure the relief will lift and relieve pressure to the maop value. in addition, with consideration of the findings of kal inc., cornhusker energy has initiated communications with kinder morgan in an effort to explain the findings of the report.

BIDS HAVE BEEN RECEIVED FROM CONTRACTORS TO COMPLETE THE REPAIRS AND ARE CURRENTLY BEING EVALUATED. TO DATE IT HAS NOT BEEN DETERMINED WHAT WAS THE ROOT CAUSE. IT IS EXPECTED THAT THIS WILL BE COMPLETED SOME TIME IN JUNE 2009, CONTINGENT UPON CONTRACTOR, MATERIALS AND WEATHER CONDITIONS. A FINAL REPORT WILL BE SUBMITTED UPON PROJECT AND FAILURE ANALYSIS COMPLETION.  SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT: THE TOTAL ESTIMATED COST FOR GAS LOSS AND OPERATOR DAMAGE HAS BEEN UPDATED. A FAILURE ANALYSIS WAS COMPLETED BY STORK TESTING & METALLURGICAL CONSULTING, INC. AFTER EXTENSIVE ANALYSIS AND TESTING IT APPEARS THAT THE FAILURE IS LIKELY TO BE ATTRIBUTABLE TO A COMBINATION OF FACTORS WHICH ARE AN INCOMPLETE ENGAGEMENT BY THE SLIP ANCHOR AROUND ITS CIRCUMFERENCE ON THE MECHNAICAL COUPLING, PIPE OVALITY AND IT'S STRENGHT. narrative_clean: on february 18, 2009, northern received notification of a possible leak in block 686 (offshore) in matagordo island. notification was made to the nrc (ticket # 897807 dtd 2/18/09). additional notifications were made to the coast guard, mms and sw opns of phmsa. it was determined that the leak was on northern's 24-inch pipeline (tos80631). actions were taken to shut in the line and make sure that all platforms were isolated from the line. preliminary indications are that a mechanical coupling on a 24 inch bypass piping, that was installed prior to removal of platform 686, had separated from the pipeline. the root cause of the event is still under investigation. plans are currently underway to evaluate necessary repairs and develop a repair plan. this report is being filed as the cost of repairs and gas loss are definately going to exceed the $50,000 reporting threshold level. there was no fire, no injuries, no explosions and no evacations experienced during this event. additional supplemental/final reports will be filed upon completion of the investigation and final cost of repairs is determined. supplemental report - april 27, 2009: a repair plan has been submitted and approved by the minerals management service (mms). bids have been received from contractors to complete the repairs and are currently being evaluated. to date it has not been determined what was the root cause. the intent, during the repair process, is to bring back to shore all materials of the bypass piping and to conduct a failure analysis. it is expected that this will be completed some time in june 2009, contingent upon contractor, materials and weather conditions. a final report will be submitted upon project and failure analysis completion. supplemental report: the total estimated cost for gas loss and operator damage has been updated. completion of this repair was included with two other mms approved projects. availability of contractors, materials and weather conditions have hampered expedited completion of repairs. currently piping is being de-watered and barring adverse weather conditions it is possible that this project will be compelted by september 1st. the piping with the failed mechanical coupling has been retreived and is being analyzed by an outside laboratory to assist with determining the root cause of the event. a final report on this event will be filed upon completion of project and concurrence on the root cause. final report: repairs were completed as outline in a repair plan that was submitted and approved by the minerals management services (mms). the line was returned to service effective august 13, 2009. a failure analysis was completed by stork testing & metallurgical consulting, inc. after extensive analysis and testing it appears that the failure is likely to be attributable to a combination of factors which are an incomplete engagement by the slip anchor around its circumference on the mechnaical coupling, pipe ovality and it's strenght. all bypass piping, the failed coupling and another mechanical coupling were removed and repairs were completed by installation of approximately 133 feet of new 24-inch, prefabricated, welds radiographed, coated piping, which was hydro tested on shore to a pressure between 2,150 and 2,300 psig, which is 1.5 to 1.6 of maop with water prior to installation/completion of NAME: VECTOR PIPELINE, L.P.
NARRATIVE: WITH THE JOLIET COMPRESOR STATION OFF LINE AND ISOLATED, STAFF WERE INSTALLING A FACTORY REPAIRED ETHERNET AND CENTRAL PROCESSING UNIT (CPU) CARD TO VERIFY THE RELIABILITY OF THE CARDS.  THE JOLIET COMPRESSOR STATION IS EQUIPPED WITH A REDUNDANT EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN PROGRAMMABLE LOGIC CONTROLLER WHICH AFFORDS THE OPPORTUNITY FOR THIS TYPE OF FIELD TESTING.    REPLACEMENT OF THESE BOARDS INVOLVED REPROGRAMMING OF THE ERASABLE PROGRAMMABLE READ ONLY MEMORY (EPROM) ON EACH BOARD AND CARD WITH THE CURRENT CUSTOM INSTRUCTION SETS SUITED TO VECTOR OPERATIONS.  DURING THE ETHERNET CARD REPROGRAMMING PROCESS; AN EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN (ESD) WAS INADVERTENTLY TRIGGERED, SENDING GAS TO THE SILENCER, AS DESIGNED.  THE GAS WAS THEN IGNITED (STATIC CHARGE) AND A FIRE PLUME FROM THE TOP OF THE SILENCER ENSUED.  OPERATIONS PERSONNEL IMMEDIATELY CONTACTED THE CONTROL ROOM AND MANAGEMENT TO INFORM THEM THAT THE EVENT HAD OCCURRED (CONTROL CENTRE WAS ALREADY AWARE VIA SCADA LINK) AND THAT THE SYSTEM WAS FUNCTIONING AS DESIGNED, WITH THE EXCEPTION OF THE RESULTANT FIRE.  ONCE EVACUATION OF THE GAS WAS COMPLETED, THE FIRE DISSIPATED.  NO INJURIES OCCURRED AND DAMAGE WAS LIMITED TO PORTIONS OF THE SILENCER AND SOME NEARBY TREES (ON VECTOR PROPERTY) WERE SINGED.
narrative_clean: with the joliet compresor station off line and isolated, staff were installing a factory repaired ethernet and central processing unit (cpu) card to verify the reliability of the cards. the joliet compressor station is equipped with a redundant emergency shutdown programmable logic controller which affords the opportunity for this type of field testing. replacement of these boards involved reprogramming of the erasable programmable read only memory (eprom) on each board and card with the current custom instruction sets suited to vector operations. during the ethernet card reprogramming process; an emergency shutdown (esd) was inadvertently triggered, sending gas to the silencer, as designed. the gas was then ignited (static charge) and a fire plume from the top of the silencer ensued. operations personnel immediately contacted the control room and management to inform them that the event had occurred (control centre was already aware via scada link) and that the system was functioning as designed, with the exception of the resultant fire. once evacuation of the gas was completed, the fire dissipated. no injuries occurred and damage was limited to portions of the silencer and some nearby trees (on vector property) were singed.

NAME: HAMPSHIRE GAS CO
NARRATIVE: WHILE PERFORMING PIPELINE CLEANING WITH A SCRAPER PIG, THE PIG ARRIVED IN THE PIG RECEIVER. RECEIVER ISOLATION VALVES WERE CLOSED. PRESSURE IN THE RECEIVER WAS RELEASED THROUGH MANUALLY OPERATED BALL VALVES (4) LOCATED IN FRONT AND BEHIND THE PIG. AFTER VENTING GAS STOPPED, AND WITH VENT VALVES IN THE OPEN POSITION, THE SAFETY INTERLOCK DEVICE WAS REMOVED FROM THE HINGED CLOSURE TO PERMITE OPENING OF THE MAIN DOOR. WITH NO FURTHER GAS ESCAPING FRO EITHER THE VALVES OR THE PRESSURE WARNING INTERLOCK DEVICE, PERSONNEL BEGAN REMOVING THE CLAMP WHICH SECURES THE MAIN DOOR. AS THE CLAMP WAS LOOSENED, THE 14" NOMINAL DIAMETER MAIN DOOR OPENED ABRUPTLY AND WITH FORCE DUE TO UNVENTED GAS PRESSURE TRAPPED IN THE VESSEL BEHIND THE BLOCKED VENT VALVES AND SAFETY INTERLOCK. THE DOOR STRUCK AN EMPLOYEE IN THE ABDOMEN AS IT SWUNG OPEN.    THE ESTIMATED PRESSURE IN SECTION A.8.A IS BASED IN THE NATURE OF THE BLOCKAGE, TYPE OF DEBRIS, ARE OF THE DOOR, AND RELTIVELY MINOR INJURY TO THE EMPLOYEE.
narrative_clean: while performing pipeline cleaning with a scraper pig, the pig arrived in the pig receiver. receiver isolation valves were closed. pressure in the receiver was released through manually operated ball valves (4) located in front and behind the pig. after venting gas stopped, and with vent valves in the open position, the safety interlock device was removed from the hinged closure to permite opening of the main door. with no further gas escaping fro either the valves or the pressure warning interlock device, personnel began removing the clamp which secures the main door. as the clamp was loosened, the 14" nominal diameter main door opened abruptly and with force due to unvented gas pressure trapped in the vessel behind the blocked vent valves and safety interlock. the door struck an employee in the abdomen as it swung open. the estimated pressure in section a.8.a is based in the nature of the blockage, type of debris, are of the door, and reltively minor injury to the employee.

NAME: TENNESSEE GAS PIPELINE CO (EL PASO)
NARRATIVE: A TENNESSEE GAS PIPELINE EMPLOYEE FOUND, THROUGH ROUTINE OPERATIONS & MAINTENANCE WORK, INDICATIONS OF A GAS LEAK EVIDENCED BY WATER BUBBLING ABOVE A PIPELINE AT THE SURFACE OF WET GROUND.  THE PIPELINE IS TGP'S 30" 800-1 LINE.  EXCAVATION REVEALED WHAT APPEARED TO BE A CRACK IN A FILLET WELD WHERE A 12" PIPE TAPPED THROUGH A FULL ENCIRCLEMENT SLEEVE INTO THE 30" CARRIER PIPE.  REPAIRS WERE COMPLETED AROUND APRIL 27, 2009 BY INSTALLING A WELD TEE. THE RESULTS FROM INVESTIGATION CONFIRM THAT THE BRANCH-TO-CARRIER PIPE FILLET WELD UNDER THE FULL ENCIRCLEMENT SADDLE CONTAINED A CRACK EXTENDING THROUGH THE WELD CAP AND STOPPING JUST BEFORE THE ROOT BEAD LEAVING A SMALL LIGAMENT OF METAL PREVENTING THROUGH-WALL PENETRATION. BASED ON THE LAB RESULTS, THE CRACK APPEARED TO HAVE PROPAGATED RAPIDLY MANY YEARS AGO AND THEN REMAINED STABLE FOR AN EXTENDED PERIOD OF TIME THEREAFTER. MINOR STRESS APPEARS TO HAVE CAUSED A DUCTILE FAILURE IN THE REMAINING METAL LIGAMENT BETWEEN THE OLD EXISTING CRACK AND THE INADEQUATELY FUSED ROOT BEAD WHICH RESULTED IN THE GAS LEAK.
narrative_clean: a tennessee gas pipeline employee found, through routine operations & maintenance work, indications of a gas leak evidenced by water bubbling above a pipeline at the surface of wet ground. the pipeline is tgp's 30" 800-1 line. excavation revealed what appeared to be a crack in a fillet weld where a 12" pipe tapped through a full encirclement sleeve into the 30" carrier pipe. repairs were completed around april 27, 2009 by installing a weld tee. the results from investigation confirm that the branch-to-carrier pipe fillet weld under the full encirclement saddle contained a crack extending through the weld cap and stopping just before the root bead leaving a small ligament of metal preventing through-wall penetration. based on the lab results, the crack appeared to have propagated rapidly many years ago and then remained stable for an extended period of time thereafter. minor stress appears to have caused a ductile failure in the remaining metal ligament between the old existing crack and the inadequately fused root bead which resulted in the gas leak.

INITIAL INVESTIGATION INDICATED THAT APPROXIMATELY 66 FEET OF PIPE HAD BLOWN OUT OF THE GROUND. THE NEW PIPE WAS PRESSURE TESTED TO A MINIMUM TEST PRESSURE OF 1620 PSIG. A RETURN TO SERVICE PLAN WAS DEVELOPED AND SUBMITTED TO THE CENTRAL REGION OFFICE OF PHMSA FOR REVIEW. PHMSA DID NOT IDENTIFY ANY CONCERNS WITH THE PLAN THEREFORE NORTHERN WAS AUTHORIZED TO RE-START THE CARLTON TO MARQUETTE LINE AT A REDUCED PRESSURE AS REQUIRED BY A CORRECTIVE ACTION ORDER ISSUED BY THE ASSOCIATE ADMINISTRATOR FOR PIPELINE SAFETY. THE CORRECTIVE ACTION ORDER REQUIRES THAT THE PRESSURE AT THE FAILURE SITE AND DOWNSTREAM OF THE FAILURE SITE IS NOT TO EXCEED 80% OF THE OPERATING PRESSURE IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FAILURE. SPECIFICALLY, THE PRESSURE AT THE FAILURE SITE IS NOT TO EXCEED 739 PSIG. THIS PRESSURE RESTRICTION WILL REMAIN IN EFFECT UNTIL WRITTEN APPROVAL TO INCREASE THE PRESSURE OR RETURN THE PIPELINE TO ITS PRE-FAILURE OPERATING PRESSURE IS OBTAINED FROM THE REGIONAL DIRECTOR, PHMSA. PIECES OF THE FAILED PIPE HAVE BEEN SENT TO BRYAN LAB IN HOUSTON, TX FOR FAILURE ANALYSIS. AN ADDITIONAL SECTION OF PIPE WERE SENT TO KEIFNER & ASSOCIATES LABORATORY IN OHIO. KEIFNER AND BRYAN LABS WILL ASSIST NORTHERN WITH IDENTIFYING THE CAUSE OF THE FAILURE AND THE INSPECTION TECHNIQUES NORTHERN WILL USE TO IDENTIFY OTHER RISKS TO THE PIPELINE SYSTEM. ADDITIONAL SUPPLEMENTAL REPORTS WILL BE FILED AS THE ROOT CAUSE AND FINAL, ACCURATE COST OF GAS LOSS/REPAIRS ARE DETERMINED.  SUPPLEMENTAL/FINAL REPORT: THIS REPORT IS BEING SUBMITTED TO UPDATE THE COTS INCURRED IN THE REPAIR PROCESS OF THIS INCIDENT. IN ADDITION, THE ROOT CAUSE HAS BEEN IDENTIFIED AS STRESS CORROSION CRACKING (SCC). A CORRECTIVE ACTION ORDER (CAO) WAS ISSUED BY PHMSA, RE; CPF NO.3-2009-1010H. ADDITIONAL ACTIONS AND COST ARE BEING INCURRED TO COMPLY WITH THE CAO, AND MUST BE COMPLETED PRIOR TO RESTORATION OF THE LINE PRESSURE BACK TO IT'S CAPABILITY PRIOR TO THE RUPTURE. THESE ACTIONS AND COST ARE BEING ADDRESSED VIA QUARTERLY REPORTS TO THE DIRECTOR, CENTRAL REGION OF OPS. AS FAR AS COST AND REPAIR ACTIONS TAKEN TO ADDRESS THE RUPTURE EVENT, PER THIS 7100 REPORT, THERE ARE CONSIDERED COMPLETE.  SUPPLEMENTAL/FINAL REPORT: DO TO THE IDENTIFICATION OF ADDITONAL COST, FROM EMPLOYEE EXPENSE AND OUTSIDE SERVICES, THIS SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT IS BEING SUBMITTED TO CORRECT THE PREVIOUS TOTAL COST OF $674,379 TO $692, 449.   09/18/2012 ADDED INCIDENT COORDINATES AS PER REQUEST OF JIM BUNN, PHMSA.

rupture had occurred on the m432b (mim10101) 16-inch carlton-wakefield b line @ approximate milepost 121.26. local law enforcement evacuated approximately 15 home sites and established a 1/2 mile safe zone. the incident occurred in the se1/4 of section 3, t47n, r46w in gogebic county, michigan. line pressure at the time of the incident was approximately 923 psig. the event was immediately reported bessemer and ramsay. gas service to approximately 380 homes in ramsay was lost and had to be restored by xcel energy. service to interruptible businesses in bessemer was interrupted. the pipe in the NAME: ONEOK WESTEX TRANSMISSION, INC.
NARRATIVE: THE WESTEX PIPELINE 0441-000 RUPTURED AT APPROXIMATELY 0545 ON JUNE 16, 2009 AT LINE PRESSURE OF 585 PSIG WITH NO IGNITION OR EXPLOSION.  REPAIR OF THE LINE WAS HAMPERED BY WATER FLOODING THE IMMEDIATE AREA FROM AN 18INCH FIBERGLASS WATER LINE LOCATED 36 INCHES BELOW THE RUPTURED 20INCH NATURAL GAS LINE.  A 4INCH FIBERGLASS WELL FLOW LINE WAS ALSO DAMAGED.  THE RUPTURED PIPE SECTION WAS SENT TO AN INDEPENDENT THIRD PARTY LAB FOR FAILURE ANALYSIS.  THE CAUSE OF FAILURE WAS SHALLOW PIT CORROSION ON THE OUTSIDE DIAMETER OF THE PIPE WHICH REDUCED THE WALL THICKNESS TO THE POINT OF FAILURE.  DUE TO THE RUPTURE DISRUPTING THE ENVIRONMENT AROUND THE FAILURE SITE, IT WAS NOT CLEAR WHAT INITIALLY CAUSED THE GENERAL CORROSION.  THERE WAS ELECTROLYE AND / OR LOCALIZED COATING ISSUES SINCE THERE WAS GENERAL CORROSION PRESENT.
narrative_clean: the westex pipeline 0441-000 ruptured at approximately 0545 on june 16, 2009 at line pressure of 585 psig with no ignition or explosion. repair of the line was hampered by water flooding the immediate area from an 18inch fiberglass water line located 36 inches below the ruptured 20inch natural gas line. a 4inch fiberglass well flow line was also damaged. the ruptured pipe section was sent to an independent third party lab for failure analysis. the cause of failure was shallow pit corrosion on the outside diameter of the pipe which reduced the wall thickness to the point of failure. due to the rupture disrupting the environment around the failure site, it was not clear what initially caused the general corrosion. there was electrolye and / or localized coating issues since there was general corrosion present.

NAME: CHESAPEAKE MIDSTREAM PARTNERS, L.P.
NARRATIVE: EXCAVATION OF THE FAILED SECTION OF PIPE REVEALED CHARRED TIMBERS ON TOP OF AND AROUND THE PIPE.  SINCE NO IGNITION OR FIRE OCCURRED AT THIS INCIDENT, THE CHARRED TIMBERS ARE POSSIBLY THE RESIDUAL FROM AN OLD BURN PILE.  THE EXCAVATION ALSO REVEALED GOUGES ON THE TOP OF THE PIPE WALL THAT RAN IN THE LONGITUDINAL DIRECTION OF THE PIPE FOR APPROXIMATELY 77 INCHES AS WELL AS A QUARTER SIZED DENT NEAR THE BEGINNING OF ONE OF THE GOUGES AND DIRECTLY BESIDE THE FAILURE.  IT APPEARS THAT THE GOUGES AND DENT COULD HAVE BEEN MADE BY THE TEETH OF A TRACK HOE BUCKET AND THAT THE DAMAGE COULD HAVE OCCURRED WHILE USING A TRACK HOE TO BURY THE CHARRED TIMBERS.  SINCE THE 70 INCH LONGITUDINAL SPLIT IN THE PIPE WAS NOT ALONG THE SEAM OF THE PIPE AND WAS ON A DENT AND LONGITUDINAL GOUGE, THE FAILURE WAS PROBABLY THE RESULT OF THE DAMAGE (DENT AND GOUGES) IN THE PIPE WALL.
narrative_clean: excavation of the failed section of pipe revealed charred timbers on top of and around the pipe. since no ignition or fire occurred at this incident, the charred timbers are possibly the residual from an old burn pile. the excavation also revealed gouges on the top of the pipe wall that ran in the longitudinal direction of the pipe for approximately 77 inches as well as a quarter sized dent near the beginning of one of the gouges and directly beside the failure. it appears that the gouges and dent could have been made by the teeth of a track hoe bucket and that the damage could have occurred while using a track hoe to bury the charred timbers. since the 70 inch longitudinal split in the pipe was not along the seam of the pipe and was on a dent and longitudinal gouge, the failure was probably the result of the damage (dent and gouges) in the pipe wall.

FRACTURE ORIGINATED IN THE CARRIER PIPE AT THE APPROXIMATE 7:30 POSITION ON THE UNDERSIDE OF THE TAP.  -BENDING STRESSES ON THE ABANDONED BRANCH CONNECTION TAP PLACED TENSILE STRESSES ACROSS THE THICKNESS OF THE CARRIER PIPE.  -THERE WAS NO INDICATION OF PROGRESSIVE CRACK GROWTH, SUCH AS ENVIRONMENTAL CRACKING OR FATIGUE IN THE FRACTURE.  -THERE WAS NO EVIDENCE OF A LEAK PRESENT IN THE PIPE PRIOR TO THE OVERLOAD EVENT THAT CAUSED THE RUPTURE.  -CORROSION DAMAGE WAS NOT INVOLVED IN THE RUPTURE OF THE PIPE.  -NO DEFECTS WERE OBSERVED IN THE SADDLE TO CARRIER PIPE WELD THAT CONTRIBUTED TO THE RUPTURE OF THE PIPE. NAME: COLUMBIA GAS TRANSMISSION CORP

NEW UNITS ARE IN THE PROCESS OF BEING INSTALLED.      THE MAIN CAUSE THAT LED TO THE FAILURE OF THE DEHYDRATION UNIT AND INITIATED A FIRE WAS IDENTIFIED AS FOLLOWS:    THE EXCESSIVE FLUIDS IN THE SYSTEM OVERLOADED THE REBOILER AND CAUSED THE RELIEF VALVES TO OPEN, VENTING THE VAPORS AND LIQUIDS.  THE VAPORS IGNITED AND THE ENSUING FIRE DAMAGED FUEL LINES ON THE REBOILERS.  THE QUALITY OF THE GAS TO THE COMPRESSOR STATION WAS OUTSIDE OF COMPANY STANDARDS. THERE WERE NO FLUID HANDLING FACILITIES IN PLACE CAPABLE OF REMOVING THE HYDROCARBON FLUIDS IN A SAFE AND EFFICIENT MANNER.      IN THE ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS (RCA) REPORT, A LIST OF RECOMMENDATIONS WERE PROVIDED TO AVOID SIMILAR INSTANCES FOR ANY FLUID (HYDROCARBON) TO BACK-UP AND  CAUSE A SIMILAR EVENT THAT LEAD TO THE FIRE IN THE DEHYDRATION UNITS. NARRATIVE: CLEBURNE COUNTY (ALABAMA) EMA REPORTED A SUSPECTED NATURAL GAS RELEASE IN THE VICINITY OF SOUTHERN NATURAL GAS (SNG) COMPANY'S 24" NORTH MAIN LOOP PIPELINE ON DECEMBER 31, 2009. THE 24-INCH NORTH MAIN LOOP LINE LEAKED DUE THE CUMULATIVE EFFECTS OF STRESSES (TENSILE AND TORSIONAL) ACTING ON A WRINKLE BEND CONTAINING A LONGITUDINAL WELD SEAM. THE FAILURE CONSISTED OF A 2- 7.5 LONG CIRCUMFERENTIAL CLEAVAGE FRACTURE ALONG THE APEX OF THE CONVOLUTION OF AN UNDER BEND.  STRUCTURAL CAPACITY WAS EXCEEDED DUE TO THE FOLLOWING FACTORS: (A) NATURAL SOIL MOVEMENT DUE TO THE GEOLOGICAL CHARACTERISTICS COMBINED WITH THE PRESENCE OF WATER (B) GEOMETRICAL STRESSES INHERENT IN THE BENDING OF THE PIPE MATERIAL AND PROPERTIES OF THE LONGITUDINAL WELD METAL (C) NORMAL INTERNAL PRESSURES ASSOCIATED WITH THE OPERATION OF THE NATURAL GAS PIPELINE (D)  EXCAVATIONS AND SOIL DISTURBANCES NEARBY THE PIPELINES RIGHT-OF-WAY.   THE WRINKLE BEND WAS INSTALLED DURING THE PIPELINE'S ORIGINAL CONSTRUCTION AND WAS USED IN A SAG BEND WITH THE PIPE'S LONGITUDINAL SEAM HAVING BEEN PLACED IN THE INSIDE PORTION OF THE BEND.  THE FAILURE SITE WAS REPAIRED BY REPLACEMENT WITH A NEW PIPELINE SEGMENT.
narrative_clean: cleburne county (alabama) ema reported a suspected natural gas release in the vicinity of southern natural gas (sng) company's 24" north main loop pipeline on december 31, 2009. dispatched sng personnel confirmed the existence of the gas release at approximate pipeline milepost 399.631, about 835 feet east of cleburne county road 488. the 24-inch north main loop line leaked due the cumulative effects of stresses (tensile and torsional) acting on a wrinkle bend containing a longitudinal weld seam. the failure consisted of a 2- 7.5 long circumferential cleavage fracture along the apex of the convolution of an under bend. structural capacity was exceeded due to the following factors: (a) natural soil movement due to the geological characteristics combined with the presence of water (b) geometrical stresses inherent in the bending of the pipe material and properties of the longitudinal weld metal (c) normal internal pressures associated with the operation of the natural gas pipeline (d) excavations and soil disturbances nearby the pipelines right-of-way. the wrinkle bend was installed during the pipeline's original construction and was used in a sag bend with the pipe's longitudinal seam having been placed in the inside portion of the bend. the failure site was repaired by replacement with a new pipeline segment.

NAME: WILLIAMS GAS PIPELINE - TRANSCO
NARRATIVE: 6" STRINER LID (YALE CAP CLOSURE) FAILED ALLOWING CONDENSATE AND GAS TO ESCAPE TO THE ATMOSPHERE. OPERATOR ON DUTY ISOLATED STRAINER POT WITH VALVING UPSTREAM AND DOWNSTREAM. GAS LOSS WITH CONDENSATE/SALTWATER WAS RELEASED.      METALURGICAL REPORT REVEALED THE FOLLOWING FINDINGS: SEVERAL CIRCUMSTANCES WORKED IN COMBINATION TO ALLOW THE CAP TO FAIL AND COME OFF OF THE BARREL. THERE WAS A LOSS OF FIT-UP BETWEEN THE MATING THREADS ON THE CAP AND BARREL AS A RESULT OF CORROSION, WEAR, AND PRIOR MECHANICAL DAMAGE (POSSIBLE OVER-TIGHTENING AND/OR CROSSTHREADING).    ·  THE CAP WAS TIGHTENED BY HAMMER BLOWS TO ITS DAMAGED EARS, WHICH RESULTED IN THE CAP BEING INSTALLED OFF-CENTER RELATIVE TO THE BARREL.   ·  THE NUMBER OF THREADS CAPABLE OF CARING LOADS WAS REDUCED BY PRIOR DAMAGE TO NO MORE THAN TWO.   ·  THE THREADS ON ONE SIDE OF THE CONNECTION WERE FULLY ENGAGED AND THE TRHEADS ON THE OPPOSITE SIDE WERE ONLY SLIGHTLY ENGAGED.  ·  THE THREADS LOCATED 90° RELATIVE TO THE ENGAGED THREADS WERE ONLY PARTIALLY ENGAGED; THESE WERE OVERLOADED AND SHEARED OFF AT THE TIME OF FAILURE.

NAME: TRANSWESTERN PIPELINE COMPANY LLC
NARRATIVE: AN ILI TOOL WAS RUN ON THE PANHANDLE LATERAL (TXBP132) ON MARCH 9, 2010.   THE ILI COMPANY NOTED DURING THE INITIAL EVALUATION OF THE DATA FROM THE ILI TOOL, THAT AN ANOMALY WAS DETECTED AND MAY HAVE A WALL LOSS GREATER THAN 70% OF THE WALL THICKNESS OF THE PIPE.  WITHIN A FEW HOURS OF NOTIFICATION TO TW, THE PIPELINE WAS REDUCED IN PRESSURE AND AN EXCAVATION CREW WAS SENT OUT TO THE SITE.  DURING THE BELL HOLE INVESTIGATION GAS DRIED SOIL WAS NOTED, SO THE EXCAVATION WAS TEMPORARILY STOPPED UNTIL A GAS DETECTOR HAD "SNIFFED" THE AREA FOR GAS.   THE GAS DETECTOR INDICATED A HIGH PPM OF METHANE GAS SO ALL CONSTRUCTION WAS STOPPED UNTIL THE PIPELINE WAS BLOWN DOWN TO ATMOSPHERE.  CONTINUED INVESTIGATION FOUND A PIN HOLE LEAK UNDER A THERMITE WELD THAT WAS PARTIALLY BONDED TO THE PIPE.  THE THERMITE WELD CONNECTED BOTH THE NEGATIVE HEADER CABLE THAT GOES TO THE RECTIFIER AND THE TEST LEAD WIRE THAT GOES TO THE CP TEST STAND.  THE THERMITE WELD WAS EASILY REMOVED WITH JUST A SMALL PULL ON THE WIRING.  THE NEGATIVE HEADER CABLE LEAD WAS A TRIANGLE PWC, INC S N-A 1-AWG TYPE THHN/THWN, GASOLINE AND OIL RESISTANT WIRE.  THE INSULATION ON THE WIRE HAD BEEN HEATED AND HAD MELTED THE INSULATION BACK APPROXIMATELY 3.5 INCHES FROM THE THERMITE CONNECTION.  SOME OF THE METAL CABLE STRANDS WHERE THE INSULATION HAD MELTED BACK SHOWED DISCOLORATION.   ADDITIONALLY THERE WAS A SMALL AMOUNT OF DISCOLORATION ON THE SURFACE OF THE PIPE SURROUNDING THE LEAK.   NO CORROSION, DENTS, CRACKS OR GOUGES WERE FOUND ON THE SURFACE OF THE PIPE.  THE LEAK WAS THE SIZE OF A PIN HOLE AND APPEARS TO HAVE OCCURRED DUE TO ELECTRICAL ARCING FROM THE NEGATIVE HEADER CABLE TO THE PIPE SURFACE.     CORROSION TECHNICIAN REPORTS THE CPU UNIT "SIMMS" WAS INSTALLED IN AUGUST 1990, AND IS SUBJECT TO HIGH LIGHTNING STRIKES AND POWER SURGES.  THE RECTIFIER HAS BEEN STRUCK BY LIGHTING A NUMBER OF TIMES BLACKING THE INSIDE OF THE RECTIFIER CASE.  ON ONE OCCURRENCE, A  LIGHTING STRIKE DISLODGED THE CONNECTION BLOCK FROM THE CASE OF THE RECTIFIER.  THE CORROSION TECHNICIAN INSTALLED A SURGEX UNIT IN JUNE 2000 TO HELP REDUCE THE NUMBER OF REPAIRS TO THE RECTIFIER AND MINIMIZE DAMAGE FROM LIGHTING STRIKES.    THE RECTIFIER UNIT IS LOCATED WITHIN 30 FT FROM WHERE THE LEAK OCCURRED.     TRANSWESTERN DID A THROUGH REVIEW OF CP RECORDS FROM 2003 AND FOUND NO INDICATION OF THE CP PROBLEMS OR A CHANGE IN THE CP SYSTEMS CIRCUIT RESISTANCE.  THE OVER ALL CIRCUIT RESISTANCE WAS FROM 0.47 OHMS TO 0.85 OHMS.  THE PIPE TO SOIL POTENTIALS ARE BETWEEN -3 TO -4 VOLTS, WITH INSTANT OFF READINGS BETWEEN -1 TO -1.25 VOLTS.   THE HIGH VOLTAGE POTENTIALS ARE ASSOCIATED WITH THE CP GROUND BED BEING LOCATED WITHIN 30 FT. OF THE PIPELINE.       CONCLUSION ' THE CAUSE OF THE LEAK IS ATTRIBUTED TO METAL LOSS FROM ELECTRICAL ARCING BETWEEN THE NEGATIVE HEADER CABLE AND THE PIPE SURFACE FROM LIGHTING STRIKES.  A PREVIOUS ILI TOOL RUN THAT WAS CONDUCTED MARCH 2003 SHOWED NO WALL LOSS ANOMALY'S AT THIS LOCATION.     **THIS REPORT IS BEING SUBMITTED IN RESPONSE TO PHMSA'S REQUEST, (DOCKET ID PHMSA-2013-0028), FOR SUPPLEMENTAL REPORTS FROM OPERATORS WHO SUBMITTED REPORTS FOR INCIDENTS OCCURRING AFTER JANUARY 1, 2010, WITH ANY OF THE FOLLOWING:  (1) ``PIPE GIRTH WELD'' WAS SELECTED AS THE ``ITEM INVOLVED IN INCIDENT'' IN PART C3 OF THE REPORT. THE REVISED REPORT COLLECTS DATA ABOUT THE PIPE ADJACENT TO THE GIRTH WELD. (2) ``FUNCTION OF PIPELINE SYSTEM'' IS NULL IN PART E5F OF THE REPORT. THE REVISED REPORT COLLECTS THE FUNCTION OF THE PIPELINE SYSTEM FOR ALL INCIDENTS.**    THIS SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT IS TO ACKNOWLEDGE THAT THE TWO RELEVANT SECTIONS IN PHMSA'S REQUEST HAVE BEEN REVIEWED AND NO FURTHER ACTIONS WERE NEEDED.

NAME: NORTHERN NATURAL GAS CO
NARRATIVE: ON JANUARY 10, 2010, AT APPROXIMATELY 21:24 P.M. A FIRE WAS DISCOVERED, BY A NORTHERN NATURAL GAS COMPANY EMPLOYEE, AT THE REDFIELD UNDERGROUND STORAGE FIELD, LOCATED NEAR REDFIELD, IOWA, IN THE SL PETER UNDERGROUND STORAGE FORMATION AT WHAT IS CALLED THE MAHER #3  WELL SITE IN SECTION 12, T19N, R29W, DALLAS COUNTY, IOWA. THERE WAS NO EXPLOSION, NO INJURIES, NO EVACUATIONS AND NO LOSS OF SERVICE TO CUSTOMERS.     AT APPROXIMATELY 24:00 HOURS THE ST PETER FORMATION PIPELINE SYSTEM PORTION, OF THE STORAGE FIELD, WAS ISOLATED AND PRESSURE WAS BLOWN DOWN ON THE PIPING TO 5 PSIG TO ENABLE SAFE CLOSURE OF THE MAHER #3 WELL HEAD VALVE (SEE PAGE 2, ITEM 15A). THE FIRE WAS EXTINGUISHED BY 01:50 A.M. THE FIRE DESTROYED THE WELL HOUSE BUILDING AND ALL OF THE COMPONENTS WITHIN THE BUILDING BUT THE WELL HEAD VALVE AND PIPING WERE UNAFFECTED. THE PORTION OF THE ST. PETER PIPING, THAT WAS ISOLATED IN ORDER TO FACILITATE REDUCTION IN PRESSURE FOR THE CLOSURE OF THE MAHER #3 WELL HEAD VALVE, WAS RETURN TO NORMAL OPERATION PRESSURES AT APPROXIMATELY 12:00 A.M. ON MONDAY, JANUARY 11TH (SEE PAGE 2, ITEM 15B).    PRELIMINARY RESULTS OF A POST INCIDENT INVESTIGATION IDENTIFIED THAT THE GAS LEAKAGE APPEARED TO BE FROM A BROKEN ONE-INCH UNION ON THE WELL SEPARATOR DRAIN LINE. THE UNION'S THREADS APPEARED TO BE STRIPPED OR PULLED. AT THE TIME OF THE EVENT THE AMBIENT TEMPERATURE WAS 21 DEGREES FAHRENHEIT AND THE WIND WAS OUT OF THE WEST AT APPROXIMATELY 14 MILES PER HOUR. IT IS POSSIBLE THAT FREEZING AND HEAVING MAY HAVE CREATING SUFFICIENT THERMAL STRESS WHICH CONTRIBUTED TO THE SEPARATION OF THE THREADS ON THE ONE-INCH UNION. THE NIGHT BEFORE THE FAILURE THERE WAS AN APPROXIMATE LOW TEMPERATURE OF - 19 DEGREES FAHRENHEIT IN THE AREA. ADDITIONAL METALLURGICAL FAILURE ANALYSIS IS BEING CONDUCTED TO ASSIST WITH DETERMINING WHETHER THERMAL STRESS FROM THE COLD TEMPERATURES COULD BE A ROOT CAUSE FOR STRIPPING OF THE THREADS AND THE UNION'S FAILURE.    FINAL REPORT: A METALLURGICAL EXAMINATION OF THE FAILED ONE-INCH UNION INDICATED THAT TWO PORTIONS OF THE UNION'S THREADS DEMONSTRATED ROLLED DAMAGE TO THE TOP OF THE THREADS, WHICH INDICATES THE COMPONENT PULLED OVER THE PEAK OF THE THREAD AS IT DISENGAGED. AN EXAMINATION OF THE THREADS ALSO INDICATES ONE FLATTENED/ROUNDED LOCATION THAT MAY HAVE BEEN DAMAGED OR IMPROPERLY MACHINED PREVIOUS TO THE FAILURE. THE FITTING WAS INSTALLED IN 2006, AND MAY HAVE BEEN FAULTY AND THE FROZEN CONDITION OF THE DRAIN LINE, ON DECEMBER 10, 2010, MOST LIKELY CREATED THERMAL STRESS, WHICH RESULTED IN FAILURE OF THE FITTING. AS A MEASURE TO PREVENT RECURRENCE, ALL WELL SEPARATOR DRAIN LINES AT THE REDFIELD, IOWA UNDERGROUND STORAGE FACILITY WERE DISSEMBLED AND INSPECTED. NO OTHER ISSUES OR PROBLEMS WERE FOUND. THE FIRE APPEARS TO HAVE STARTED IMMEDIATELY AS THERE WAS NO INDICATION OF AN EXPLOSION. THE WIRING IN THE CONDUIT, STATIC ELECTRICITY OR SPARKS FROM THE BUILDING STRUCTURE OR THE ONE-INCH PIPE STRIKING OTHER PIPING WHEN IT SEPARATED WAS THE LIKELY IGNITION SOURCE. THIS EVENT IS CONSIDERED COMPLETE AND CLOSED.   SUPPLEMENTAL/FINAL TO REPORT 20100019 PER PHMSA REQUEST IDENTIFIED PART E5F AS TRANSMISSION.
narrative_clean: on january 10, 2010, at approximately 21:24 p.m. a fire was discovered, by a northern natural gas company employee, at the redfield underground storage field, located near redfield, iowa, in the sl peter underground storage formation at what is called the maher #3 well site in section 12, t19n, r29w, dallas county, iowa. there was no explosion, no injuries, no evacuations and no loss of service to customers. at approximately 24:00 hours the st peter formation pipeline system portion, of the storage field, was isolated and pressure was blown down on the piping to 5 psig to enable safe closure of the maher #3 well head valve (see page 2, item 15a). the fire was extinguished by 01:50 a.m. the fire destroyed the well house building and all of the components within the building but the well head valve and piping were unaffected. the portion of the st. peter piping, that was isolated in order to facilitate reduction in pressure for the closure of the maher #3 well head valve, was return to normal operation pressures at approximately 12:00 a.m. on monday, january 11th (see page 2, item 15b). preliminary results of a post incident investigation identified that the gas leakage appeared to be from a broken one-inch union on the well separator drain line. the union's threads appeared to be stripped or pulled. at the time of the event the ambient temperature was 21 degrees fahrenheit and the wind was out of the west at approximately 14 miles per hour. it is possible that freezing and heaving may have creating sufficient thermal stress which contributed to the separation of the threads on the one-inch union. the night before the failure there was an approximate low temperature of - 19 degrees fahrenheit in the area. additional metallurgical failure analysis is being conducted to assist with determining whether thermal stress from the cold temperatures could be a root cause for stripping of the threads and the union's failure. final report: a metallurgical examination of the failed one-inch union indicated that two portions of the union's threads demonstrated rolled damage to the top of the threads, which indicates the component pulled over the peak of the thread as it disengaged. an examination of the threads also indicates one flattened/rounded location that may have been damaged or improperly machined previous to the failure. the fitting was installed in 2006, and may have been faulty and the frozen condition of the drain line, on december 10, 2010, most likely created thermal stress, which resulted in failure of the fitting. as a measure to prevent recurrence, all well separator drain lines at the redfield, iowa underground storage facility were dissembled and inspected. no other issues or problems were found. the fire appears to have started immediately as there was no indication of an explosion. the wiring in the conduit, static electricity or sparks from the building structure or the one-inch pipe striking other piping when it separated was the likely ignition source. this event is considered complete and closed. supplemental/final to report 20100019 per phmsa request identified part e5f as transmission.

NAME: ENOGEX LLC
NARRATIVE: COMPRESSOR STATION WAS ISOLATED AND VENTED TO ATMOSPHERE FOR CONSTRUCTION TIE-INS RELATED TO EXPANSION PROJECT.  A SHORT SECTION (APPROXIMATELY 12-18 INCHES) OF A 16 INCH RECYCLE PIPING SYSTEM WAS TO BE REMOVED AND A 16 X 8 REDUCING TEE ADDED TO CONNECT A NEW RECYCLE PIPING SYSTEM TO THE EXISTING RECYCLE PIPING SYSTEM.  A LOCK-OUT/TAG-OUT PROCEDURE AND AN AIR MOVER WERE IN PLACE TO ELIMINATE OR MITIGATE HAZARDS DURING THE HOT WORK OPERATION.    MEANWHILE, WORKERS WERE INSTALLING A NEW METER TUBE ON AN ADJACENT PIPING MANIFOLD THAT WAS CONNECTED TO THE RECYCLE PIPING SYSTEM.    A 12" BLIND FLANGE WAS REMOVED FROM THE PIPING MANIFOLD TO INSTALL AN ISOLATION VALVE BETWEEN THE NEW METER TUBE AND THE EXISTING PIPING MANIFOLD.  A CONTRACT EMPLOYEE WAS STANDING BESIDE THE OPEN ENDED PIPE FLANGE AT THE SAME TIME THE NEARBY HOT WORK IGNITED VAPORS INSIDE THE PIPING SYSTEM.  CONTRACT EMPLOYEE WAS INJURED AS A RESULT OF A FLASH FIRE WHICH IMMEDIATELY EXTINGUISHED ITSELF.  CONTRACT EMPLOYEE'S INJURIES REQUIRED IN-PATIENT HOSPITALIZATION.      UPDATE NOVEMBER 23, 2010  AN INVESTIGATION TEAM WAS ASSEMBLED IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWING THE INCIDENT AND AN INVESTIGATION WAS CONDUCTED TO DETERMINE THE CAUSE OR CAUSES OF THE INCIDENT.  THE FOLLOWING CAUSAL FACTORS WERE IDENTIFIED:     1. TWO INDEPENDENT JOBS WERE ON-GOING AT THE SAME TIME WHICH IMPACTED ONE ANOTHER AND EFFECTIVE COMMUNICATION BETWEEN THESE JOBS  WAS NOT ADEQUATE TO CONSIDER THE IMPACT OF INDEPENDENT ACTIONS TAKEN.  2. THREE VALVES (XV #853, XV # 861, AND XV # 871) FAILED OPEN WHEN THE INSTRUMENT AIR BLED OFF FOLLOWING THE INITIAL ESD.  THIS CONDITION MAY HAVE UNKNOWINGLY INCREASED THE VOLUME OF VAPORS WITHIN THE PIPING REQUIRED TO BE PURGED PRIOR TO THE HOT WORK BEING CONDUCTED THEREBY DECREASING THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THE AIR MOVER.    3. A12-INCH BLIND FLANGE WAS REMOVED, POTENTIALLY CHANGING THE AIR FLOW DYNAMICS WITHIN THE PIPE AND POSSIBLY LIMITING THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THE AIR MOVER IN THE LOCATION OF THE 16-INCH TEE ON THE UPSTREAM SIDE OF THE EXISTING RECYCLE METER RUN.  4. THE SCOPE OF THE SAFE WORK PERMIT (WRITTEN PRIOR TO WORK BEING PERFORMED), WHICH INCLUDED MULTIPLE CONTRACTORS OVER AN ENTIRE SHIFT, WAS LIKELY TOO BROAD TO BE EFFECTIVE IN CONTROLLING MULTIPLE TASKS.    THE FOLLOWING ROOT CAUSE(S) WERE IDENTIFIED:    1. THE POTENTIAL HAZARDS ASSOCIATED WITH MULTIPLE ONGOING AND SEEMINGLY UNRELATED JOBS WITHIN THE SAME GENERAL WORK AREA WERE NOT SUFFICIENTLY ANALYZED TO CONSIDER THE POTENTIAL IMPACTS OF ONE JOB ON THE OTHER.  2. THREE VALVES THAT WERE CLOSED DURING LO/TO FAILED OPEN DUE TO THE LOSS OF INSTRUMENT GAS AFTER THE ESD.  THIS CONDITION WAS EITHER NOT ANTICIPATED OR NOT CONSIDERED TO BE RELEVANT DURING JOB PLANNING.  3. AN UNDETECTED FLAMMABLE ATMOSPHERE EXISTED WITHIN THE PIPING DURING AUTHORIZED HOT WORK ACTIVITIES.    RECOMMENDATIONS ARE BEING IMPLEMENTED TO ADDRESS THE FINDINGS ABOVE TO PREVENT A RECURRENCE.  UPDATE MARCH 5, 2013: COMPLETED SECTION E.5.F.
narrative_clean: compressor station was isolated and vented to atmosphere for construction tie-ins related to expansion project. a short section (approximately 12-18 inches) of a 16 inch recycle piping system was to be removed and a 16 x 8 reducing tee added to connect a new recycle piping system to the existing recycle piping system. a lock-out/tag-out procedure and an air mover were in place to eliminate or mitigate hazards during the hot work operation. meanwhile, workers were installing a new meter tube on an adjacent piping manifold that was connected to the recycle piping system. a 12" blind flange was removed from the piping manifold to install an isolation valve between the new meter tube and the existing piping manifold. a contract employee was standing beside the open ended pipe flange at the same time the nearby hot work ignited vapors inside the piping system. contract employee was injured as a result of a flash fire which immediately extinguished itself. contract employee's injuries required in-patient hospitalization. update november 23, 2010 an investigation team was assembled immediately following the incident and an investigation was conducted to determine the cause or causes of the incident. the following causal factors were identified: 1. two independent jobs were on-going at the same time which impacted one another and effective communication between these jobs was not adequate to consider the impact of independent actions taken. 2. three valves (xv #853, xv # 861, and xv # 871) failed open when the instrument air bled off following the initial esd. this condition may have unknowingly increased the volume of vapors within the piping required to be purged prior to the hot work being conducted thereby decreasing the effectiveness of the air mover. 3. a12-inch blind flange was removed, potentially changing the air flow dynamics within the pipe and possibly limiting the effectiveness of the air mover in the location of the 16-inch tee on the upstream side of the existing recycle meter run. 4. the scope of the safe work permit (written prior to work being performed), which included multiple contractors over an entire shift, was likely too broad to be effective in controlling multiple tasks. the following root cause(s) were identified: 1. the potential hazards associated with multiple ongoing and seemingly unrelated jobs within the same general work area were not sufficiently analyzed to consider the potential impacts of one job on the other. 2. three valves that were closed during lo/to failed open due to the loss of instrument gas after the esd. this condition was either not anticipated or not considered to be relevant during job planning. 3. an undetected flammable atmosphere existed within the piping during authorized hot work activities. recommendations are being implemented to address the findings above to prevent a recurrence. update march 5, 2013: completed section e.5.f.

NAME: GREAT LAKES GAS TRANSMISSION CO
CAUSE: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD
NARRATIVE: DURING A ROUTINE WALK-THROUGH OF THE COMPRESSOR UNIT 303 BUILDING, A STATION TECHNICIAN WAS ABLE TO SMELL GAS IN THE COMPRESSOR BUILDING.  THE TECHNICIAN HAD THE UNIT SHUTDOWN AND UNIT PIPING EVACUATED OF GAS.  THE PIPING WAS THEN REPRESSURIZED TO A POINT WHERE THE GAS LEAK COULD BE HEARD AND DETECTED USING A PORTABLE LEAK DETECTOR.  THE LEAK WAS EMANATING AT A FILLET WELD THAT CONNECTED A WELD-O-LET TO THE DISCHARGE HORN PIPING OF THE UNIT GAS COMPRESSOR.  THE PIPING WAS THEN DEPRESSURIZED TO ALLOW FOR FURTHER ANALYSIS.  A MAGNETIC PARTICLE EXAMINATION OF THE FILLET WELD REVEALED A CIRCUMFERENTIAL CRACK AROUND PART OF THE BASE OF THE WELD.  DUE TO UNCERTAINTY OF THE INTEGRITY OF THE PIPE (CONTAINING THE WELD-O-LET) AND AN ASSOCIATED FLANGE, IT WAS DECIDED TO REMOVE AND REPLACE THE AFFECTED PIPE SEGMENT AND FLANGE. THE REMOVED MATERIAL WAS SENT TO A LABORATORY FOR ANALYSIS, WHICH DETERMINED THAT THE FRACTURE MECHANISM CAUSING THE THROUGH-WALL CRACK ON THE 30-INCH HEADER PIPE (DISCHARGE HORN) WAS HIGH CYCLE, LOW STRESS FATIGUE.
narrative_clean: during a routine walk-through of the compressor unit 303 building, a station technician was able to smell gas in the compressor building. the technician had the unit shutdown and unit piping evacuated of gas. the piping was then repressurized to a point where the gas leak could be heard and detected using a portable leak detector. the leak was emanating at a fillet weld that connected a weld-o-let to the discharge horn piping of the unit gas compressor. the piping was then depressurized to allow for further analysis. a magnetic particle examination of the fillet weld revealed a circumferential crack around part of the base of the weld. due to uncertainty of the integrity of the pipe (containing the weld-o-let) and an associated flange, it was decided to remove and replace the affected pipe segment and flange. the removed material was sent to a laboratory for analysis, which determined that the fracture mechanism causing the through-wall crack on the 30-inch header pipe (discharge horn) was high cycle, low stress fatigue.

NAME: MISSISSIPPI RIVER TRANSMISSION CORP
NARRATIVE: THIS EVENT WAS REPORTED BECAUSE IT WAS CONSIDERED SIGNIFICANT IN THE JUDGMENT OF THE OPERATOR, EVEN THOUGH THIS EVENT DID NOT MEET THE CRITERIA OF THE DEFINITION OF AN INCIDENT IN §191.3 PARAGRAPHS (1)(I) OR (1)(II), IT WAS REPORTED BECAUSE IT WAS CONSIDERED SIGNIFICANT IN THE JUDGMENT OF THE OPERATOR SINCE WE EXPERIENCED AN IGNITION OF LEAKING GAS.         AT 1230 ON MAY 10, 2010 AN MRT EMPLOYEE ARRIVED AT THE SWIFTON M&R STATION ON LINE A-45-A TO REPLACE A LOCK AND DISCOVERED THE RELIEF VALVE VENTING. HE FOUND UPON ENTERING THE BUILDING THAT THE CONTROLLER FOR THE PRIMARY REGULATOR WAS ENGULFED IN FLAMES. FIRE WAS EXTINGUISHED AND REGULATOR WAS ISOLATED. THE SECOND CUT REGULATOR BEGAN TO REGULATE AND THE RELIEF VALVE STOPPED VENTING. THE SUPPLY LINE TO THE CONTROLLER FOR THE PRIMARY REGULATOR HAD A HOLE IN IT, APPARENTLY FROM HIGH VOLTAGE (LIGHTNING) ARCING BETWEEN IT AND THE PIPING TO THE REGULATOR RESULTING IN A FIRE THAT ENGULFED THE CONSTANT BLEED CONTROLLER CAUSING IT TO FAIL. ALL TUBING AND PIPING IN THIS FACILITY WERE INSULATED FOR CP REASONS. THE INSULATOR FOR THE SUPPLY TUBING THAT DEVELOPED A HOLE WAS DOWNSTREAM OF THE INSULATOR FOR THE MAIN GAS PIPING. WHEN THE HIGH VOLTAGE INTRODUCED INTO THE PIPING AND TUBING THERE WAS A LARGE POTENTIAL DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE TWO RESULTING IN THE ARCING. THE PRIMARY REGULATOR WAS REPLACED WITH A FISHER 627 (SPRING OPERATED), ELIMINATING NEED FOR SUPPLY TUBING.
