NAME: NATURAL GAS PIPELINE CO OF AMERICA (KMI)
NARRATIVE: ON 10/17/2021 AT APPROXIMATELY 6:48 AM, AN OPERATOR FROM NATURAL GAS PIPELINE COMPANY OF AMERICA (NGPL) ARRIVED AT STATION 346 AND HEARD GAS VENTING TO ATMOSPHERE. THE OPERATOR IMMEDIATELY STARTED THE INVESTIGATION AND DISCOVERED A FUEL GAS RELIEF VALVE OPEN ALLOWING GAS TO VENT. THE OPERATOR VERIFIED THE FUEL GAS PRESSURES MAKING SURE THEY WERE NORMAL AND THEN CLOSED THE ISOLATION VALVE BELOW THE RELIEF VALVE ENDING THE RELEASE. SUBSEQUENTLY AN EMERGENCY RESPONSE LINE (ERL) WAS INITIATED AND THE INCIDENT WAS DEEMED REPORTABLE.     THE INVESTIGATION CONCLUDED THAT A GROVE FLEXFLOW REGULATOR WAS LEAKING INTERNALLY ALLOWING PRESSURE TO BUILD IN THE PIPING DOWNSTREAM. THE STATION HAS AN UPSTREAM PRESSURE MONITOR REGULATOR THAT CLOSES ON INCREASING DOWNSTREAM PRESSURE. HOWEVER, THE MONITOR REGULATOR IS NOT A POSITIVE SEAL VALVE. THUS, ALLOWED GAS TO CONTINUE TO FLOW TO THE GROVE FLEXFLOW REGULATOR. THE PRESSURE CONTINUED TO RISE UNTIL THE RELIEF VALVE ACTUATED AS DESIGNED. UPON ACTUATION, THE FUEL GAS RELIEF VALVE DID NOT RE-SEAT PROPERLY RESULTING IN A SLOW GAS RELEASE FOR APPROXIMATELY 23HRS. BECAUSE THE FUEL GAS RELIEF VALVE FAILED TO RE-SEATING PROPERLY, THIS INCIDENT WAS REPORTABLE DUE TO THE VOLUME RELEASE, WHICH WAS MORE THAN THE 3,000 MCF THRESHOLD.     OPERATIONS DISCOVERED THAT THE RELIEF VALVE FAILED TO RE-SEAT DUE TO DEBRIS ACCUMULATION IN THE VALVE SEAT. IN ORDER TO PREVENT REOCCURRENCE OPERATIONS REPAIRED THE FLEXFLOW REGULATOR AND CLEANED THE FUEL GAS VALVE SEAT. IN ADDITION, CALLOUT ALARMS FOR HIGH FUEL GAS PRESSURE AND HMI CONFIGURATIONS HAVE BEEN INSTALLED FOR UNITS 1, 2 AND 3 AT NGPL COMPRESSOR STATION 346.
narrative_clean: on 10/17/2021 at approximately 6:48 am, an operator from natural gas pipeline company of america (ngpl) arrived at station 346 and heard gas venting to atmosphere. the operator immediately started the investigation and discovered a fuel gas relief valve open allowing gas to vent. the operator verified the fuel gas pressures making sure they were normal and then closed the isolation valve below the relief valve ending the release. subsequently an emergency response line (erl) was initiated and the incident was deemed reportable. the investigation concluded that a grove flexflow regulator was leaking internally allowing pressure to build in the piping downstream. the station has an upstream pressure monitor regulator that closes on increasing downstream pressure. however, the monitor regulator is not a positive seal valve. thus, allowed gas to continue to flow to the grove flexflow regulator. the pressure continued to rise until the relief valve actuated as designed. upon actuation, the fuel gas relief valve did not re-seat properly resulting in a slow gas release for approximately 23hrs. because the fuel gas relief valve failed to re-seating properly, this incident was reportable due to the volume release, which was more than the 3,000 mcf threshold. operations discovered that the relief valve failed to re-seat due to debris accumulation in the valve seat. in order to prevent reoccurrence operations repaired the flexflow regulator and cleaned the fuel gas valve seat. in addition, callout alarms for high fuel gas pressure and hmi configurations have been installed for units 1, 2 and 3 at ngpl compressor station 346.

NAME: TENNESSEE GAS PIPELINE COMPANY
NARRATIVE: ON 10/16/2021 AT 21:59 EASTERN, GAS CONTROL RECEIVED A STATION WARNING ASSOCIATED WITH TENNESSEE GAS PIPELINE (TGP) STATION 264 AND IMMEDIATELY COMMUNICATED THE WARNING TO THE OPERATIONS TECHNICIAN ON CALL. AT THE SAME TIME, A NEARBY RESIDENT CALLED THE FIRE DEPARTMENT TO REPORT LOUD NOISE AND GAS SMELL IN THE AREA. AT 22:40, THE OPERATIONS TECHNICIAN AND THE CHARLTON FIRE DEPARTMENT ARRIVED ON SITE. THE OPERATIONS TECHNICIAN STARTED HIS INVESTIGATION AND FOUND GAS VENTING THROUGH A VENT VALVE ON COMPRESSOR UNIT 1C. AT 22:45 THE OPERATION TECHNICIAN MANUALLY CLOSED, THE 4" VENT VALVE, ENDING THE EVENT. THE EVENT WAS DETERMINED TO EXCEED THE REPORTABLE THRESHOLD OF 3,000 MCF AND SUBSEQUENTLY REPORTED TO THE NRC.     THE INTERNAL INCIDENT INVESTIGATION CONCLUDED THAT THE STATION WARNING OCCURRED BECAUSE UNIT 1C EXPERIENCED A FAILURE OF THE 120VDC/24VDC POWER SUPPLY THAT POWERS THE SOLAR PANEL, PLC AND ASSOCIATED I/O'S. THE PLC CONTROLS THE POSITIONS (OPEN OR CLOSE) FOR THE COMPRESSOR UNIT MANIFOLD VALVES. BECAUSE THE PLC POWER FAILED, THE MANIFOLD VALVES REMAINED IN THE LAST POSITION AND THE UNIT BLOWDOWN VALVE OPENED. THE UNIT WAS RUNNING AT THE TIME OF THE PLC FAILURE. THEREFORE, THE UNIT SHUT DOWN THE MANIFOLD VALVES AND THE BLOWDOWN VALVE REMAINED OPEN ALLOWING GAS TO VENT.    IN ORDER TO PREVENT REOCCURRENCE AT TGP STATION 264, OPERATIONS WILL INSTALL A REDUNDANT POWER SUPPLY FOR UNIT 1C. IN ADDITION, OPERATIONS ISSUED AN INCIDENT FLASH FORM FOR DIVISION 10 TO EVALUATE COMPRESSOR STATIONS TO IDENTIFY UNIT MANIFOLD VALVES THAT DO NOT CLOSE OR UNIT BLOWDOWN VALVES THAT DO NOT OPEN UPON FAILURE OF UNIT PLC. THE REVIEW WILL IDENTIFY UNITS WHERE MODIFICATIONS ARE REQUIRED.
narrative_clean: on 10/16/2021 at 21:59 eastern, gas control received a station warning associated with tennessee gas pipeline (tgp) station 264 and immediately communicated the warning to the operations technician on call. at the same time, a nearby resident called the fire department to report loud noise and gas smell in the area. at 22:40, the operations technician and the charlton fire department arrived on site. the operations technician started his investigation and found gas venting through a vent valve on compressor unit 1c. at 22:45 the operation technician manually closed, the 4" vent valve, ending the event. the event was determined to exceed the reportable threshold of 3,000 mcf and subsequently reported to the nrc. the internal incident investigation concluded that the station warning occurred because unit 1c experienced a failure of the 120vdc/24vdc power supply that powers the solar panel, plc and associated i/o's. the plc controls the positions (open or close) for the compressor unit manifold valves. because the plc power failed, the manifold valves remained in the last position and the unit blowdown valve opened. the unit was running at the time of the plc failure. therefore, the unit shut down the manifold valves and the blowdown valve remained open allowing gas to vent. in order to prevent reoccurrence at tgp station 264, operations will install a redundant power supply for unit 1c. in addition, operations issued an incident flash form for division 10 to evaluate compressor stations to identify unit manifold valves that do not close or unit blowdown valves that do not open upon failure of unit plc. the review will identify units where modifications are required.

NAME: TENNESSEE GAS PIPELINE COMPANY
NARRATIVE: ON 10/22/2021 AT 9:02AM CENTRAL TIME, AN ESD OCCURRED AT TENNESSEE GAS PIPELINE COMPANY, L.L.C. (TGP) COMPRESSOR STATION 550 IN HAMILTON, ALABAMA. (tgp) compressor station 550 in hamilton, alabama. at approximately 9:04am tgp personnel at the station began to notice that the station was not isolated. esd valve 550-ad2 was found in the open position allowing gas to pass through and out of the vent stack. at approximately 9:06am the valve was shut, ending the event. at approximately 9:54am, the gas release was determined to exceed the reportable threshold of 3,000 mcf. the event was subsequently reported to the nrc at 10:29am. during the investigation, it was found that the pilot on the esd valve controller for valve 550-ad2 had failed during the esd and did not allow enough gas to pass through and actuate the valve. the pilot was replaced and the station was returned to service at 6:55pm on 10/22/2021. the esd was triggered by an inadvertent key turn in the control cabin of the station, caused by clothing on a contractor catching and turning the key on the panel as the individual was passing by. the investigation into the failure of the pilot on valve 550-ad2 revealed that, per the manufacturer, the life expectancy of the pilot was one year. the pilot had been in-service since 2015. at station 550, tgp will review the life expectancy of all esd pilots and replace any that are past the life expectancy stated by the manufacturer. tgp revoked oq's pertaining to the automated valve maintenance task for the individuals who serviced esd valve 550-ad2. those individuals will be retrained on valve maintenance procedures. the answer to question e1a was updated and the answers to a8 and d7g were corrected.

NARRATIVE: ON OCTOBER 20, 2021 AT APPROXIMATELY 08:25 A.M. OPERATOR WAS NOTIFIED BY LANDOWNER OF PIPELINE RUPTURE NEAR BRANDENBURG, KENTUCKY, RESULTING IN AN UNCONTROLLED NATURAL GAS RELEASE. OPERATOR ARRIVED ON SITE AT APPROXIMATELY 08:45 A.M. AND THE VALVES WERE ISOLATED BY 09:06 A.M. RUPTURE OCCURRED ON AN 8-INCH CARBON STEEL PIPELINE LOCATED IN THE DOE RUN STORAGE FIELD. THE RUPTURE DID NOT CAUSE ANY INJURIES OR SIGNIFICANT THIRD-PARTY PROPERTY DAMAGE. NO IGNITION OF GAS OCCURRED DURING THIS EVENT.     A SECTION OF THE PIPELINE MEASURING 7,677 FEET, INCLUDING THE SEGMENT OF PIPING INVOLVED IN THIS INCIDENT, WAS ABANDONED. THE BULK OF THE ABANDONED PIPE HAD BEEN ISOLATED BY VALVES DURING THE INCIDENT RESPONSE. SELECTIVE SEAM INTERNAL WELD CORROSION WAS IDENTIFIED AS THE CAUSE OF THE INCIDENT. LINE PIPE METALLURGY AND PIPELINE CONSTRUCTION ALSO WERE CONTRIBUTING FACTORS IN THE RUPTURE. EARLY VINTAGE (PRE-1970S) ERW LINE PIPE IS PARTICULARLY SUSCEPTIBLE TO SELECTIVE SEAM WELD CORROSION AS A RESULT OF THE STEEL CHEMISTRY AND THE ABSENCE OF A POST WELD HEAT TREATMENT THAT FULLY NORMALIZED THE SEAM WELD OF THE LINE PIPE. INSTALLING THE SEAM WELD NEAR THE 6:00 ORIENTATION CONTRIBUTED TO THE INCIDENT AS WELL BECAUSE ANY WATER AND/OR DEPOSITS THAT ACCUMULATE IN THE PIPE WILL BE IN CONTACT WITH THE CORROSION-SUSCEPTIBLE MICROSTRUCTURE OF THE SEAM WELD.

THE INTENT OF THE PCP WAS TO RUN THE STATION ON BYPASS BUT OPERATIONS MISINTERPRETED  ENGINEERING'S PLANNED FLOW PATH IN THE PCP AND OPENED A LEG OF THE STATION PIPING FOR PURGING  WHICH ALLOWED THIS NEW RELIEF VALVE TO BE EXPOSED TO THIS HIGHER PRESSURE ONCE THE SYSTEM WAS REPRESSURIZED.
narrative_clean: (on july 18th, 2024, a supplemental-final was resubmitted per the following request from darren lemmerman, phmsa investigator, accident investigation division on june 25, 2024: our information resources manager has identified an issue with how the 30-day report calculated the released gas volume and the cost of the gas/mcf. the fix has been implemented and we have been told that if the report is resubmitted as a supplemental final that the error will be corrected. if you could help out, it would be much appreciated.) a relief valve went off at leelanau gate station at approximately 8:35 pm on november 4, 2021 (at this time dte gas was not aware of the release). dte gas received a call of odor in the air/gas blowing at 1:00 am and dte distribution arrived at 1:20 am. dte gas transmission operations were called at 1:30 am. the transmission tech arrived at 03:30 am on november 5 and blocked in the relief, as there is no need to protect a lower maop downstream. only 1 qualified person was available. he had to get a confirmation (from the other tech) to shut it in. the gas continued to be released into the air until approximately 3:30 am on november 5, resulting in odor in the air. this released 5.8 mmcf of gas into the atmosphere, making it reportable to both the state of michigan, phmsa, and egle. gas control was given the release to bring the petoskey/traverse city system pressure back up (had been on a pressure reduction to below 500 psig since june, to normal line pressure, generally just above 500 psig ) and started bringing pressure up to around 8:00 pm on november 4, 2021. as part of the traverse city alpena reinforcement program (tcarp), we were installing a brand new station/totally rebuilt an existing station; NARRATIVE: ON 11/6/21 AT 07:26, CON EDISON'S GAS EMERGENCY RESPONSE CENTER (GERC) RECEIVED A REPORT FROM ITS CUSTOMER OPS. CALL CENTER OF A GAS ODOR INSIDE AND OUTSIDE OF A RESIDENTIAL BUILDING LOCATED AT 733 PARK AVE.  THE GAS ODOR HAD BEEN REPORTED TO THE CALL CENTER BY AN OCCUPANT OF THE SAME BUILDING.  THE AREA IS SUPPLIED BY A 6-INCH LOW-PRESSURE CAST IRON GAS MAIN (INSTALLED IN 1897) AND A 30-INCH STEEL GAS TRANSMISSION MAIN (INSTALLED IN 1959), AS WELL AS UNDERGROUND ELECTRIC FACILITIES.  CON EDISON GAS DISTRIBUTION SERVICES (GDS) RESPONDED TO THE LOCATION, INVESTIGATED, AND REPORTED A TYPE 1 GAS LEAK, WITH A NATURAL GAS READING OF 0.4% DETECTED IN THE GAS POINT-OF-ENTRY (POE) AT 733 PARK AVENUE.  ADDITIONALLY, GDS DETECTED NATURAL GAS READINGS OF 15% IN TWO NEARBY ELECTRIC SUBSURFACE STRUCTURES (SSS'S) MANHOLE #M41786 AND SERVICE BOX #12935; THE COVERS OF THOSE TWO SSS'S WERE REMOVE BY GDS FOR VENTING.  THE GERC THEN INITIATED A CODE MURRE, NOTIFIED THE FDNY, AND DISPATCHED ADDITIONAL CON EDISON GDS SUPERVISION TO THE LOCATION.  UPON FURTHER INVESTIGATION, GDS DETECTED NATURAL GAS READINGS OF 0.3% IN THE ATMOSPHERE OF TWO BUILDING BASEMENTS AT 106 & 110 E. 71ST STREET.  GDS SEALED THE ELECTRIC POE'S TO THOSE BUILDINGS AND VENTED THE READINGS IN THE TWO BASEMENTS TO 0% WITH ASSISTANCE FROM THE FDNY.  GDS REPORTED THAT ALL OTHER BUILDINGS AND ADJACENT SSS'S WERE CLEAR OF GAS READINGS, AND THAT ELECTRIC MH #M41786 AND SB #12935 HAD BEEN VENTED TO 0%.  CON EDISON EMERGENCY GAS CONSTRUCTION PERSONNEL WERE DISPATCHED TO THE LOCATION TO PINPOINT THE SOURCE OF THE LEAK.     ON 11/7/21 AT 00:50, EMERGENCY GAS CONSTRUCTION REPORTED FINDING A POTENTIAL LEAK ON THE 30-INCH TRANSMISSION MAIN AFTER DETECTING NATURAL GAS READINGS OF ~100% IN THE VICINITY OF THE MAIN.  ALL ADJACENT SSS'S, BUILDINGS, AND PROTECTION TEST POINTS WERE CHECKED AND FOUND TO BE CLEAR OF GAS READINGS.  THE TRANSMISSION MAIN WAS OPERATING AT ~300 PSIG.  NO OUTAGES OR NEGATIVE GAS SYSTEM IMPACT WERE REPORTED.  GAS TRANSMISSION ENGINEERING AND GAS CONTROL WERE NOTIFIED OF THE POTENTIAL TRANSMISSION MAIN LEAK.  CONTINGENCY CASE 6-C WAS ESTABLISHED AND PUT INTO EFFECT, AND GAS OPERATIONS PERSONNEL WERE ASSIGNED TO STAFF MULTIPLE MAIN VALVES AS PART OF THE CONTINGENCY.  GAS OPERATIONS CREWS REMAINED ON LOCATION AND MONITORED THE CONDITION THROUGHOUT THE NIGHT.      ON 11/7/21 AT 13:49, TWO TRANSMISSION MAIN VALVES WERE CLOSED TO ISOLATE A SEGMENT OF THE 30-INCH TRANSMISSION MAIN DUE TO THE LEAK CONDITION, WHICH APPEARED TO PROGRESSIVELY WORSEN.  THE ISOLATION OF THE TRANSMISSION MAIN INTERRUPTED SERVICE TO FIFTEEN (15) GAS SERVICES AND NINE HUNDRED THIRTY-TWO (932) CUSTOMERS.  CON EDISON GAS CONTROL ISSUED A LIMIT WORK ORDER AND A CONDITION YELLOW SYSTEM STATUS.  CONSTRUCTION ACTIVITIES BEGAN AND THE COATING ON THE TRANSMISSION MAIN WAS SAFELY REMOVED.  ONCE FULLY EXPOSED, A LEAK WAS FOUND ON THE TRANSMISSION MAIN AT THE 1 O'CLOCK POSITION.  A NITROGEN BARRIER WAS INSTALLED, AND A HIGH HAT (A PERMANENT STEEL CAP) WAS WELDED OVER THE LEAK THAT WAS FOUND ON THE BODY OF THE TRANSMISSION MAIN.  A PRESSURE TEST WAS CONDUCTED, AND THE TEST PASSED.  TRANSMISSION PRESSURE WAS REINTRODUCED TO THE MAIN UP TO FULL OPERATING PRESSURE (327 PSIG) AT 50 PSIG INCREMENTS WITH LEAK SURVEYS CONDUCTED OVER THE AFFECTED AREA AT EVERY INCREMENTAL PRESSURE INCREASE, WITHOUT ANY FURTHER LEAKS DETECTED.  THE REPAIR PROCEDURE WAS SUCCESSFULLY COMPLETED, AND SERVICE WAS SAFELY RESTORED ON 11/9/21 AT 18:09.  THE SUSPECTED CAUSE OF THE NATURAL GAS LEAK WAS A HIGH-PRESSURE STEAM LEAK THAT WAS BLOWING DIRECTLY ON THE GAS TRANSMISSION MAIN.  THERE WERE NO REPORTED INJURIES OR EVACUATIONS ASSOCIATED WITH THIS INCIDENT.  NOTIFICATIONS WERE MADE TO PSC, DEP AND PHMSA.

PAVONIA IS A TRANSMISSION CS IS LOCATED IN RICHLAND COUNTY, OHIO THAT IS OPERATED AND MAINTAINED BY COLUMBIA GAS TRANSMISSION, LLC (COMPANY), A TC ENERGY ENTITY. AN INVESTIGATION WAS COMPLETED, AND IT WAS CONFIRMED THAT MOISTURE IN THE TRIGGER AIRLINE FREEZING-OFF IS THE MOST LIKELY CASUAL FACTOR FOR THE UNINTENTIONAL OPENING OF THE BLOW-OFF VALVE. THE TRIGGER AIR SYSTEM FOR BLOW-OFF VALVE IS A STAGNATE SYSTEM UNLESS A LEAK ALLOWS FLOW IN THE TRIGGER AIRLINES. THEY WERE: I) CHECK ALL ABOVE GRADE ESD TRIGGER AIR PIPING AND CONNECTIONS FOR LEAKS, II) ADD A PROJECT TO INSTALL A MOISTURE ANALYZER ON THE AIR DRYER. PLANT 1 PROCESSING EQUIPMENT WAS  SHUT-IN AND ISOLATED FROM THE STORAGE FIELD ELIMINATING ANY POTENTIAL HAZARDS AND ALLOWING FOR FURTHER INVESTIGATION.      OPERATIONS EMPLOYEES BEGAN INVESTIGATING ON JANUARY 24, 2022.  DURING THE INVESTIGATION, IT WAS DETERMINED RAY COMPRESSOR STATION RELIEF VALVE (RV-22) EXPERIENCED AN ABNORMAL OPERATING CONDITION, RV-22 ACTIVATION OCCURRED AT 1389 PSIG INSTEAD OF THE SET POINT ACTIVATION OF 1926 PSIG.  THE PREMATURE ACTIVATION OCCURRED BECAUSE OF THE PRESENCE OF FOREIGN MATERIAL. DURING AN EXTERNAL EVALUATION OF THE RELIEF VALVE, EXCESSIVE LUBRICANT WAS VISUALLY OBSERVED AND AN INTERNAL INSPECTION OF THE RELIEF BLOWDOWN VALVE IDENTIFIED A FAILED O-RING, THE COMBINATION OF THE EXCESSIVE LUBRICANT AND THE FAILED O-RING CAUSED TO RELIEF VALVE TO FAIL. NAME: NORTHWEST PIPELINE LLC
NARRATIVE: ON FEBRUARY 24TH, 2022 THERE WAS A WATER MAIN RUPTURE INSIDE THE CONTROLS ROOM AT NORTHWEST PIPELINE RANGELY COMPRESSOR STATION. EMERGENCY CONTROL DEVICES WERE IMPACTED AND EXPOSED TO WATER AS A RESULT OF THE LEAK, CAUSING OPERATIONS TO MAKE THE DECISION TO BLOW THE STATION DOWN. WHILE THE STATION WAS BLOWING DOWN, OPERATIONS PERSONNEL NOTICED THE BLOWDOWN WAS TAKING LONGER THAN IT TYPICALLY WOULD AND STARTED TO INVESTIGATE. OPERATIONS IDENTIFIED THAT THE SIDEGATE ACTUATOR HAD ONLY CLOSED 75% OF THE WAY. AS A RESULT, TWO OF THE STATION BLOWDOWN VALVES (3" AND 8" PLUG VALVES) WERE VENTING  MAINLINE PRESSURE GAS TO THE ATMOSPHERE FROM THE TIME THE ESD SYSTEM WAS ACTIVATED TO THE TIME THE SIDEGATE WAS MANUALLY CLOSED BY OPERATIONS PERSONNEL. IT IS ESTIMATED THAT IT TOOK OPERATIONS 15 MINUTES BETWEEN ORIGINAL ESD ACTIVATION AND COMPLETE SHUT IN OF THE MALFUNCTIONING SIDE GATE VALVE AND COMPRESSOR STATION. ONCE THE SIDEGATE WAS PROPERLY CLOSED, AND THE STATION WAS SHUT IN FROM THE MAINLINE, A PROPER ESD WAS SUCCESSFULLY EXECUTED. IT WAS IDENTIFIED THAT THE SIDEGATE VALVE ACTUATOR DID NOT PROPERLY SHUT THE VALVE AS A RESULT OF THE ACTUATOR CONTROLS MALFUNCTIONING DUE TO THE WATER EXPOSURE IN THE CONTROL ROOM. SINCE THE INCIDENT ALL AFFECTED CONTROL SYSTEMS HAVE BEEN REPLACED.
narrative_clean: on february 24th, 2022 there was a water main rupture inside the controls room at northwest pipeline rangely compressor station. emergency control devices were impacted and exposed to water as a result of the leak, causing operations to make the decision to blow the station down. while the station was blowing down, operations personnel noticed the blowdown was taking longer than it typically would and started to investigate. operations identified that the sidegate actuator had only closed 75% of the way. as a result, two of the station blowdown valves (3" and 8" plug valves) were venting mainline pressure gas to the atmosphere from the time the esd system was activated to the time the sidegate was manually closed by operations personnel. it is estimated that it took operations 15 minutes between original esd activation and complete shut in of the malfunctioning side gate valve and compressor station. once the sidegate was properly closed, and the station was shut in from the mainline, a proper esd was successfully executed. it was identified that the sidegate valve actuator did not properly shut the valve as a result of the actuator controls malfunctioning due to the water exposure in the control room. since the incident all affected control systems have been replaced.

narrative_clean: on february 13, 2022, southern natural gas company, llc (sng) 18-inch south main line experienced an in-service failure resulting in a pipeline rupture with fire. the preliminary timeline of events is as follows: 16:15-hours, an undesired release of natural gas occurred on the sng 18-inch south main line. 16:20-hours, perry county sherriff arrived on scene, blocked a local road and instructed arriving deputies to secure the area. 16:31-hours, a citizen called sng gas control and reported a fire near the 18-inch south main line row. 16:33-hours, sng gas control received a call from another citizen regarding the fire. 16:34-hours, sng gas control notified sng operations of a pressure drop at the gallion compressor station and selma compressor station and a potential rupture near the 18-inch south main line system. 16:52-hours, sng operations located the pipeline rupture on the south main line system at mp 155.755. 17:15-hours, sng emergency response line+ (erl+) call notifications initiated per sng procedures to coordinate the emergency response. 17:26-hours, sng operator #1 closed upstream gate valve #18 located at, mp 150.783. 17:33-hours, sng initiated call to nrc. (report number 1328835) 17:39-hours, sng operator #2 closed crossover valve 155 located at, mp 155.000. 17:41-hours, sng operator #3 closed downstream gate valve #19 located at, mp 159.054, completely isolating the south main line system. 22:01-hours, the fire was extinguished. sng's investigation began on february 14, 2022 and received a correction action order (cao) cpf no. 2-2022-007-cao from phmsa on february 18, 2022. sng sent the failed specimen to a third-party metallurgical laboratory. the metallurgical report was completed on april 4, 2022 and concluded that the sng 18-inch south main line ruptured likely from a hydrogen stress crack initiated at the pipe od in a localized hard spot. in order to prevent reoccurrence sng and its ili vendor performed a foot-by-foot manual analysis of all available residual data sets on the 18-inch line to identify similar conditions to those in the failed joint. sng remediated 21 features with similar characteristics to the anomaly in the failed joint. in addition to the remediation project sng will implement testing, and integrity verification measures, to promote the ongoing safe operation of the pipeline considering the results of the analyses, inspections, evaluations, and corrective measures undertaken pursuant to the cao. the pipeline was returned to service on august 31, 2022, following the requirements from the cao. sng submitted the final quarterly report on september 29, 2022 and requested cao closure.

NAME: COLUMBIA GULF TRANSMISSION, LLC
NARRATIVE: ON THE EVENING OF WEDNESDAY FEBRUARY 16TH, 2022 A PIPELINE RELIEF VALVE, ON COLUMBIA GULF TRANSMISSION'S EAST LATERAL 200 (EL200) LINE, AT VALVE SETTING VS-1204, FAILED TO THE OPEN POSITION RELEASING (AT THE TIME) AN UNKNOWN VOLUME OF NATURAL GAS. THE VALVE SETTING IS LOCATED NEAR 2037 DURPHY ROAD, IN ABBEVILLE LOUISIANA. THE ODOR OF GAS WAS REPORTED BY A PRIVATE CITIZEN; LOCAL EMERGENCY SERVICES WERE DISPATCHED AND CLOSED THE NEARBY ROAD. A LOSS OF COMMUNICATIONS WITH SCADA TRANSMITTER WAS NOTED BY THE GAS CONTROLLER, THEN UPON RESTORING COMMUNICATIONS, A DROP IN PIPELINE PRESSURE WAS OBSERVED. AT 4:19 PM CENTRAL TIME, WHEN TRANSMITTER COMMS WAS LOST, THE PRESSURE ON EL200 WAS 825 PSIG; THE PRESSURE WHEN COMMS RESUMED AT 4:54 PM CENTRAL WAS 816 PSIG.    EL200 FROM RAYNE COMPRESSOR STATION TO VS-1204 HAS AN MAOP OF 973 PSIG. HOWEVER, EL200 IS CURRENTLY IN COMMON WITH EAST LATERAL 300 LINE, RESULTING IN AN OVERRIDE MAOP OF 839 PSIG FOR THE LIMITING COMPONENT IN THIS MODE OF OPERATION. THIS CONFIGURATION DOES NOT ALLOW A CONTROLLED PRESSURE REDUCTION, BUT INSTEAD AN IMMEDIATE PRESSURE REDUCTION BY A GAS RELEASE. NAME: NATURAL GAS PIPELINE CO OF AMERICA (KMI)
NARRATIVE: ON 3/09/2022, AT 05:43 NATURAL GAS PIPELINE COMPANY (NGPL) GAS CONTROL SHUT DOWN UNIT 14 REMOTELY VIA SCADA SYSTEM. SUBSEQUENTLY, NGPL OPERATIONS SPECIALIST RECEIVED AN ALARM REGARDING STATION 104, UNIT 14 AND STARTED TO INVESTIGATE THE CAUSE. AT 07:00, OPERATIONS SPECIALIST ARRIVED ON SITE TO START TROUBLESHOOTING THE ALARM. AT 08:15, AN OPERATIONS SPECIALIST #2 ARRIVED ON SITE TO SUPPORT MITIGATE THE ALARM. UPON ARRIVAL WAS ABLE TO HEAR GAS VENTING THROUGH A SILENCER ON UNIT 14. AT 09:59, OPERATIONS SPECIALIST #2 CLOSED THE VENT VALVE AND CALLED NGPL OPERATIONS SUPERVISOR. AT 11:00, OPERATIONS SUPERVISOR ARRIVED ON SITE TO INVESTIGATE THE EVENT. AT 11:45, THE EMERGENCY RESPONSE LINE (ERL) CALL COMMENCED AND DURING THE CALL, OUT OF ABUNDANCE OF CAUTION NGPL DECIDED TO REPORT THE EVENT TO THE NRC FROM A VOLUME RELEASE STANDPOINT.     NGPL STARTED THE INVESTIGATION AND CONCLUDED THAT THE VOLUME RELEASED EXCEEDED THE REPORTING THRESHOLD PER THE COMPRESSOR UNIT PLC DATA. THE UNIT 14 SUCTION VALVE DID NOT CLOSE COMPLETELY AFTER SHUT DOWN, ALLOWING GAS TO VENT THROUGH THE VENT VALVE SILENCER. FURTHERMORE, THE INVESTIGATION ALSO DISCOVERED THAT THE SUCTION VALVE DID NOT CLOSE PROPERLY DUE TO THE LIMIT SWITCHES FOR THE VALVE POSITIONER AND THE SOLENOID OPERATOR. NGPL DETERMINED THAT THE LIMIT SWITCH THAT DE-ENERGIZES THE CLOSED SOLENOID ON THE VALVE OPERATOR NEEDED TO BE READJUSTED. NGPL E&C TECH READJUSTED THE LIMIT SWITCH AND CYCLED THE VALVE NUMEROUS TIMES TO ASSURE THE VALVE OPERATION. NGPL PUT UNIT 14 BACK IN SERVICE THE SAME DAY.    IN ORDER TO PREVENT REOCCURRENCE NGPL WILL BE REVISING THE UNIT PLC LOGIC AND REMOVING THE LIMIT SWITCHES IN THE VALVE CONTROL CIRCUITS TO THE VALVE CONTROL SOLENOIDS TO AVOID INTERRUPTION OF THE UNIT VALVE OPEN AND CLOSE SIGNALS FROM THE PLC.
narrative_clean: on 3/09/2022, at 05:43 natural gas pipeline company (ngpl) gas control shut down unit 14 remotely via scada system. subsequently, ngpl operations specialist received an alarm regarding station 104, unit 14 and started to investigate the cause. at 07:00, operations specialist arrived on site to start troubleshooting the alarm. at 08:15, an operations specialist #2 arrived on site to support mitigate the alarm. upon arrival was able to hear gas venting through a silencer on unit 14. at 09:59, operations specialist #2 closed the vent valve and called ngpl operations supervisor. at 11:00, operations supervisor arrived on site to investigate the event. at 11:45, the emergency response line (erl) call commenced and during the call, out of abundance of caution ngpl decided to report the event to the nrc from a volume release standpoint. ngpl started the investigation and concluded that the volume released exceeded the reporting threshold per the compressor unit plc data. the unit 14 suction valve did not close completely after shut down, allowing gas to vent through the vent valve silencer. furthermore, the investigation also discovered that the suction valve did not close properly due to the limit switches for the valve positioner and the solenoid operator. ngpl determined that the limit switch that de-energizes the closed solenoid on the valve operator needed to be readjusted. ngpl e&c tech readjusted the limit switch and cycled the valve numerous times to assure the valve operation. ngpl put unit 14 back in service the same day. in order to prevent reoccurrence ngpl will be revising the unit plc logic and removing the limit switches in the valve control circuits to the valve control solenoids to avoid interruption of the unit valve open and close signals from the plc.

NARRATIVE: ON MARCH 15, 2022 AT APPROXIMATELY 16:20 HOURS CONSUMERS ENERGY GAS CONTROL RECEIVED A FIREGATE TROUBLE ALARM AT THE WHITE PIGEON COMPRESSOR STATION. THE MECHANIC ACTIVATED THE FIREGATE SYSTEM AT APPROXIMATELY 16:39 HOURS TO ISOLATE AND RELIEVE ALL GAS FROM THE PLANT 3 PIPING. THE VENTING WAS COMPLETE AT APPROXIMATELY 16:43 HOURS AND A SITE INSPECTION WAS COMPLETED TO CONFIRM ALL POTENTIAL HAZARDS WERE ELIMINATED. THE CAUSE INVESTIGATION CONTINUED FOR SEVERAL WEEKS AND INCLUDED ELECTRICAL TESTING AND FUNCTIONAL TESTING OF THE VALVE. ADDITIONAL ACTIONS WERE COMPLETED ON SIMILAR EQUIPMENT PRIOR TO RETURNING PLANT 3 TO SERVICE ON APRIL 1, 2022 AT APPROXIMATELY11:50 HOURS.     AT THE TIME OF THIS REPORT, THE PROBABLE CAUSE HAS BEEN DETERMINED TO BE AN ELECTRIC FAULT THAT OCCURRED IN THE VALVE ACTUATOR TERMINAL BOX DUE TO MOISTURE THAT EITHER ENERGIZED THE OPEN SOLENOID OR DE-ENERGIZED THE ESD SOLENOID CAUSING THE VALVE TO OPERATE AND GAS TO BE RELEASED. THIS WAS CONFIRMED WHEN THE LAB REPLACED THE COIL IN THE VALVE AND THE OPEN CIRCUIT ISSUE WAS NOT OBSERVED. CONFIRMING THE ROOT CAUSE TO BE THE ESD SOLENOID FAILING AND OPERATING THE VALVE.
narrative_clean: on march 15, 2022 at approximately 16:20 hours consumers energy gas control received a firegate trouble alarm at the white pigeon compressor station. white pigeon compressor station is located at 68536 a road, white pigeon township, (st. joseph county) michigan. a station mechanic was dispatched and arrived at the site at approximately16:37 hours. the mechanic observed multiple esd valve position faults at the station control screen and gas was being released near plant 3, later determined to be a release at the plant 3 suction blowdown valve (valve 635). the mechanic activated the firegate system at approximately 16:39 hours to isolate and relieve all gas from the plant 3 piping. the venting was complete at approximately 16:43 hours and a site inspection was completed to confirm all potential hazards were eliminated. on march 16, 2022 an initial site assessment and incident review was conducted with the michigan public service commission. the cause investigation continued for several weeks and included electrical testing and functional testing of the valve. based on the evaluation, repair and replacement of selected components were completed and sent to the vendor for further evaluation. additional actions were completed on similar equipment prior to returning plant 3 to service on april 1, 2022 at approximately11:50 hours. at the time of this report, the probable cause has been determined to be an electric fault that occurred in the valve actuator terminal box due to moisture that either energized the open solenoid or de-energized the esd solenoid causing the valve to operate and gas to be released. the esd solenoid and the relay module have been sent to rotork and det-tronics respectively for additional vendor evaluation to determine if either component may have caused or contributed to the event. the laboratory reports from the vendor, peter paul electronics concluded the failure to be open circuits within the coil. this occurs when there is a break in the wires or connection. the lab analysis shows the lead connectors were intact, confirming the break was inside the coil. this was confirmed when the lab replaced the coil in the valve and the open circuit issue was not observed. confirming the root cause to be the esd solenoid failing and operating the valve.

NAME: TRANSCONTINENTAL GAS PIPE LINE COMPANY
CAUSE: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD
CAUSE_DETAILS: ORIGINAL MANUFACTURING-RELATED (NOT GIRTH WELD OR OTHER WELDS FORMED IN THE FIELD)
NARRATIVE: ON 4/12/22, A SEGMENT OF MAINLINE A RUPTURED IN THE VALVE YARD OF STATION 90 COMPRESSOR FACILITY.  NO EXPLOSION, FIRE OR INJURY OCCURRED.  LOCAL OPERATING PERSONNEL PROVIDED TEMPORARY TRAFFIC CONTROL FOR ~30 MINUTES FOLLOWING THE RELEASE.  NO OTHER PUBLIC IMPACT RESULTED FORM THE RELEASE.    MAINLINE A IS ONE OF 5 PARALLEL PIPELINES THAT RUN THROUGH THE FACILITY.  NO OTHER PIPELINE WAS INVOLVED OR DAMAGED DURING THE INCIDENT.  OPERATING PERSONNEL AT THE FACILITY IMMEDIATELY INITIATED A COMPLETE COMPRESSOR STATION ESD AND PRESSURE BLOWDOWN.  MAINLINE A WAS ISOLATED BETWEEN STATION 90 AND THE NEAREST PIPELINE ISOLATION VALVE WITHIN 12 MINUTES OF THE RUPTURE.  THE NRC WAS NOTIFIED OF THE INCIDENT 45 MINUTES FOLLOWING THE RUPTURE.     THE PIPELINE SEGMENT THAT FAILED WAS A 30-INCH OUTSIDE DIAMETER, 0.500-INCH WALL THICKNESS BETHLEHEM STEEL PIPE MANUFACTURED IN 1957 THAT WAS PROTECTED FORM CORROSION WITH EXTERNAL COATING AND IMPRESSED CURRENT CATHODIC PROTECTION.  THE FRACTURE INVOLVED PIPE INSTALLED WITH A PIG LAUNCHER IN 1959 AND PIPE INSTALLED DURING MODIFICATION OF THIS PIG LAUNCHER IN 1997.  METALLURGICAL ANALYSIS CONCLUDED THE RUPTURE ORIGINATED IN A HARD SPOT IN THE BODY OF PIPE INSTALLED IN 1959.  ANALYSIS FURTHER IDENTIFIED A CRACK HAD DEVELOPED AT THE RUPTURE ORIGIN IN A MICROSCOPIC CORROSION PIT.    INVESTIGATION CONCLUDED THE PIPELINE RUPTURE RESULTED FROM A HYDROGEN-ASSISTED STRESS CRACK THAT DEVELOPED IN A PREEXISTING HARD SPOT, WHICH EXTENDED THROUGH THE ENTIRE PIPE WALL.  THE BRITTLE STRUCTURE OF THE HARD METAL ALLOWED THE STRESS CRACK TO PROPAGATE TO THE POINT OF FRACTURE.  INVESTIGATION FURTHER IDENTIFIED ENVIRONMENTALLY ASSISTED CORROSION IN THE FORM OF A MICROSCOPIC PIT AND ELEVATED CATHODIC PROTECTION ELECTRONEGATIVITY AS CONTRIBUTING FACTORS TO DIRECT CAUSES.
narrative_clean: on 4/12/22, a segment of mainline a ruptured in the valve yard of station 90 compressor facility. no explosion, fire or injury occurred. local operating personnel provided temporary traffic control for ~30 minutes following the release. no other public impact resulted form the release. mainline a is one of 5 parallel pipelines that run through the facility. no other pipeline was involved or damaged during the incident. operating personnel at the facility immediately initiated a complete compressor station esd and pressure blowdown. mainline a was isolated between station 90 and the nearest pipeline isolation valve within 12 minutes of the rupture. the nrc was notified of the incident 45 minutes following the rupture. the pipeline segment that failed was a 30-inch outside diameter, 0.500-inch wall thickness bethlehem steel pipe manufactured in 1957 that was protected form corrosion with external coating and impressed current cathodic protection. the fracture involved pipe installed with a pig launcher in 1959 and pipe installed during modification of this pig launcher in 1997. metallurgical analysis concluded the rupture originated in a hard spot in the body of pipe installed in 1959. analysis further identified a crack had developed at the rupture origin in a microscopic corrosion pit. investigation concluded the pipeline rupture resulted from a hydrogen-assisted stress crack that developed in a preexisting hard spot, which extended through the entire pipe wall. the brittle structure of the hard metal allowed the stress crack to propagate to the point of fracture. investigation further identified environmentally assisted corrosion in the form of a microscopic pit and elevated cathodic protection electronegativity as contributing factors to direct causes.

NAME: ARCHAEA ENERGY OPERATING, LLC

A FINAL CLEANING PIG WAS INSERTED INTO PIPELINE TO COLLECT ANY REMAINING BUILD-UP IN THE LINE.  THE PIG WAS BEING FORCED THROUGH THE PIPELINE WITH NATURAL GAS, RATHER THAN AIR OR NITROGEN.  THE PIG RECEIVER DOOR WAS IN THE OPEN POSITION DURING THE PIG RUN.  DURING THE PIG RUN, IGNITION OF THE NATURAL GAS OCCURRED WITH THE SUBSEQUENT GAS RELEASE AND IGNITION AT THE PIG RECEIVER LOCATION WHERE SEVERAL EMPLOYEES WERE LOCATED TO RECEIVE THE PIG.  ONE EMPLOYEE WAS INJURED DURING THE INCIDENT.  LOCAL RESPONDERS WERE DISPATCHED IMMEDIATELY TO THE SCENE TO ASSIST THE FIRE.  THE FIRE AND GAS IN THE PIPELINE WERE ALLOWED TO EXTINGUISH ITSELF.  THE FACILITY THAT PRODUCES NATURAL GAS TO SUPPLY THE PIPELINE WAS IMMEDIATELY SHUTDOWN AT 14:05 AFTER THE GAS RELEASE AND IGNITION TO PREVENT ADDITIONAL NATURAL GAS FROM BEING INTRODUCED INTO THE PIPELINE. PIPELINE 1656 IS A 6-INCH DIAMETER, CARBON STEEL, 0.28-INCH WALL THICKNESS, BARE STEEL PIPELINE, WHICH IS CATHODICALLY PROTECTED IN THE AREA OF THE REPORTED LEAK. LINE 1656 HAS A MAXIMUM ALLOWABLE OPERATING PRESSURE OF 175 PSIG AND ITS OPERATING PRESSURE AT THE TIME OF DISCOVERY WAS APPROXIMATELY 165 PSIG.   WHILE PERFORMING SCHEDULED CATHODIC PROTECTION SURVEYS, COLUMBIA OPERATIONS DISCOVERED THE PRESENCE OF NATURAL GAS IN A TEST STATION NEAR THE 100 BLOCK OF PENNSINGER ROAD, GREENCASTLE, PA. THE LINE PRESSURE WAS REDUCED TO 100 PSIG TO MAINTAIN LOCAL MARKET. BELL HOLES WERE OPENED ON EITHER SIDE OF PENNSINGER ROAD, AND GAS MIGRATION SURVEYS HAVE BEEN PERFORMED TWICE DAILY SINCE DISCOVERY.   AS OF JULY 7, 2022, PIPELINE 1656 HAS BEEN BLOW DOWN TO 0 PSIG AND 19 LDC CUSTOMERS HAVE BEEN PLACED ON TEMPORARY BOTTLED COMPRESSED NATURAL GAS (CNG) SERVICE. THEREFORE, THE TOTAL TIME OF THE RELEASE CHANGED FROM 8 MINUTES TO 26 MINUTES AND, THE TOTAL RELEASE VOLUME WITH THE REVISED ORIFICE SIZE EXCEEDED THE REPORTING THRESHOLD. NAME: TRANSCOLORADO GAS TRANSMISSION COMPANY LLC
NARRATIVE: ON 6/25 AT 9:12AM, TRANSCOLORADO GAS TRANSMISSION COMPANY LLC'S OLATHE COMPRESSOR STATION LOCATED IN MONTROSE COUNTY, COLORADO EXPERIENCED AN ABNORMAL EVENT WHILE IN STANDBY MODE WITH NO COMPRESSION IN OPERATION AT THE TIME.   THE STATION EXPERIENCED A COMMUNICATION FAILURE BETWEEN THE STATION PLC, ESD PLC AND THE I/O MODULE CONTROLLING THE ESD VALVES.  THE I/O MODULE CONTROLLING THE ESD VALVES ALSO FAILED TO "HOLD LAST STATE" UPON LOSS OF COMMUNICATION.  THIS RESULTED IN THE STATION VENT VALVE OPENING (INSTEAD OF REMAINING CLOSED) AND AN UNPLANNED GAS RELEASE EVENT FOR 112 MINUTES. THE TOTAL VOLUME RELEASED WAS  24,659.50 MCF.    THE IMMEDIATE CAUSE OF THE EVENT WAS DETERMINED TO BE THE FAILURE OF THE I/O CONTROLLER DESIGNED TO PROVIDE A "HOLD LAST STATE" COMMAND THAT KEEPS THE STATION VALVES IN THE CURRENT STATE WHEN COMMUNICATIONS ARE LOST.  INVESTIGATION REVEALED THAT THERE WERE SHORT LOSSES OF COMMUNICATION PRIOR TO THIS EVENT, BUT THE I/O MODULE "HOLD LAST STATE" SETTING ALWAYS FUNCTIONED AS DESIGNED.  ANOTHER CONTRIBUTING CAUSE WAS IDENTIFIED TO BE LOSS OF COMMUNICATION BETWEEN THE STATION & ESD PLCS AND THE I/O MODULES.  THE INTERMITTENT LOSS OF COMMUNICATION WAS CAUSED BY POOR CONNECTIONS ON THE COMMUNICATION WIRES AT THE PLCS, I/O MODULES, AND SURGE-SUPPRESSION EQUIPMENT.   ALL CONNECTIONS WITH THE COMMUNICATIONS WIRE HAVE BEEN CHECKED AND CORRECTED AS REQUIRED.   THERE HAS BEEN NO COMMUNICATIONS FAILURES SINCE.  THE I/O MODULE WAS ALSO REPLACED.

NAME: NORTHWEST PIPELINE LLC
NARRATIVE: ON JULY 28TH, 2022 THERE WAS AN IMPROPER SEALING OF A UNIT VALVE AT NORTHWEST PIPELINE WILLARD COMPRESSOR STATION. WILLIAMS OPERATIONS RECEIVED A CALL FROM SKAMANIA COUNTY 911 DISPATCH AT 22:10 LOCAL TIME REPORTING A STRONG SMELL OF GAS FROM A NEIGHBOR NEAR THE COMPRESSOR STATION. WILLIAMS OPERATIONS PERSONNEL IMMEDIATELY RESPONDED TO THE CALL AND ARRIVED ON-SITE AT 23:50 LOCAL TIME TO ASSESS THE SITUATION.     WHILE ON-SITE IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE VENT VALVE ON UNIT ONE AT THE COMPRESSOR STATION WAS SHOWING CLOSED ON THE HMI BUT WAS STILL VENTING GAS. IN AN EFFORT TO STOP THE GAS FROM VENTING AS QUICKLY AS POSSIBLE OPERATIONS TECHNICIANS AT THE SITE CONSULTED WITH PIPELINE CONTROL AND THE OPERATIONS SUPERVISOR AND AGREED TO ISSUE A START COMMAND TO UNIT ONE. ISSUING THIS START COMMAND WAS FOUND TO CAUSE ALL VALVES TO POSITION THEMSELVES CORRECTLY, THUS STOPPING THE GAS FROM VENTING TO THE ATMOSPHERE. SHORTLY AFTER, A STOP COMMAND WAS SUBSEQUENTLY ISSUED TO THE SAME UNIT, WITH OPERATIONS NOTING THAT ALL VALVES ALSO CORRECTLY POSITIONED THEMSELVES AGAIN. IT WAS NOTED BY PIPELINE CONTROL THAT THIS UNIT WOULD NOT BE NEEDED FOR THE REST OF THE NIGHT, SO UNIT ONE WAS LEFT OFF AND UNAVAILABLE UNTIL THE NEXT DAY.     ONCE THE UNIT HAD BEEN SHUT DOWN AND NO ADDITIONAL VENTING WAS CONFIRMED, OPERATIONS CONTACTED THE SECURITY OPERATIONS CENTER (SOC) AT 01:40 LOCAL TIME. AT THIS TIME, THE SOC RAN GAS LOSS ESTIMATION CALCULATIONS AND WAS ABLE TO CONFIRM DISCOVERY THAT THE 3MMSCF RELEASE THRESHOLD WAS REACHED. SHORTLY AFTER, AT 01:52, AFTER A CONVERSATION BETWEEN THE SOC AND PIPELINE SAFETY, IT WAS DETERMINED TO REPORT THE INCIDENT TO THE NRC. OPERATIONS PERSONNEL THAT RESPONDED TO THE INCIDENT WENT HOME TO REST BEFORE ARRIVING ON-SITE THE NEXT MORNING TO CONTINUE THE TROUBLESHOOTING PROCESS.     THE FOLLOWING MORNING OPERATIONS AND TECH SERVICES EMPLOYEES WORKED TO TROUBLESHOOT THE VALVE POSITION INDICATORS AND WERE NOT ABLE TO RECREATE THE PROBLEM THAT CAUSED UNIT ONE SUCTION VALVE TO REMAIN CRACKED DURING A REMOTE STOP. TO BETTER ALERT OPERATION PERSONNEL OF A SIMILAR INCIDENT OCCURRING, PIPELINE CONTROL PLACED A TEMPORARY PRESSURE ALARM TO MONITOR CASE PRESSURE. OVER THE COURSE OF THE FOLLOWING WEEKS, OPERATIONS PERSONNEL ATTEMPTED TO RECREATE THE ISSUE TO BETTER UNDERSTAND WHAT CAUSED THE INITIAL INCIDENT.     MULTIPLE EFFORTS TO RECREATE THE ISSUE WERE UNSUCCESSFUL AND A FULL ROOT-CAUSE INVESTIGATION HAS SINCE TAKEN PLACE. THE FINDINGS OF THE INVESTIGATION REVEALED THAT THE UNIT 1 BLOWDOWN VALVE HAD BEEN LEAKING 12 HOURS PRIOR TO PIPELINE CONTROL RECEIVING NOTIFICATION FROM THE EMERGENCY DISPATCH. THE INVESTIGATION INTO WHY THE BLOWDOWN VALVE FAILED TO SEAL FOUND THAT THERE WAS LIKELY SOME DEBRIS IN THE SEAT OF THE UNIT VALVE THAT CAUSED IT TO NOT SEAL PROPERLY. IT'S BELIEVED THAT THESE DEBRIS MAY HAVE ORIGINATED FROM PIPELINE CLEANING / PIGGING EFFORTS AS PART OF A SERIES OF HYDROTEST PROJECTS THAT HAD RECENTLY OCCURRED IN THE AREA. IT WAS ALSO FOUND THAT POWER TURBINE PERCENT SPEED AND SUCTION/DISCHARGE PRESSURES WERE NOT UTILIZED TO SHOW INDICATION OF A POTENTIAL ISSUE WITH THE COMPRESSOR. THESE ITEMS WEREN'T SPECIFICALLY REVIEWED AT THE TIME AS THERE WERE NO ALARMS GIVEN TO PIPELINE CONTROL. TO PREVENT THIS FROM HAPPENING IN THE FUTURE, WILLIAMS IS IMPLEMENTING A CONTINUOUS VENTING UNIT ALARM WITHIN SCADA, STATION, AND UNIT CONTROL SYSTEMS.

HE SPRAYED DOWN THE NEST AND RETURNED THE CAN TO HIS TRUCK.  HE THEN PROCEEDED TO TECHNICIAN 2 TO DISCUSS THE NEXT STEPS IN THE PROCEDURE.  THE LINES CONTINUED TO PACK UP TO LINE PRESSURE. ON SATURDAY, SEPTEMBER 17TH A THUNDERSTORM ROLLED THROUGH THE AREA, AND A LIGHTNING STRIKE CAUSED A STATION EBD.  GAS CONTROL CALLED TECHNICIAN 1 WHO WAS WORKING ON EQUIPMENT AT ANOTHER STATION WHEN PIPELINE CONTROL CALLED HIM TO MAKE HIM AWARE OF THE BLOWDOWN EVENT. THE MANAGER OF OPERATIONS LOGGED INTO THE SECURITY CAMERAS AND WAS ABLE TO DETERMINE THAT GAS WAS STILL BLOWING FROM THE SUCTION LINE BLOWDOWN VENT. GAS VENTED FOR 90 MINUTES AT 300PSI FOR A TOTAL OF 8.145MMSCF  THE LIGHTNING STRIKE HAD BLOWN 2 FUSES AND BURNED UP THE SOLENOID ON THE SUCTION BLOW-DOWN VALVE, WHICH IS WHY IT ACTUATED AND THE DISCHARGE BLOWDOWN DID NOT.  EMPLOYEES WERE NOT ABLE TO MAKE REPAIRS THAT EVENING AS THE THUNDERSTORM CONTINUED WITH HEAVY RAIN AND LIGHTNING.  EMPLOYEES RETURNED THE NEXT MORNING AND MADE REPAIRS AND PUT THE STATION BACK IN SERVICE. repressurizing the suction and discharge headers utilizing the 4" loading lines around the station side gates. technician 1 was taking care of the suction header, and technician 2 was taking care of the discharge header. once the valves were partially opened, and the lines were being pressured up technician 1 noticed a wasp nest near him and returned to his vehicle to grab a can of wasp spray. he sprayed down the nest and returned the can to his truck. he then proceeded to technician 2 to discuss the next steps in the procedure. the lines continued to pack up to line pressure. technician 1 failed to return to and close the 4" loading line on the suction header. both technicians continued and brought the station back into service. on saturday, september 17th a thunderstorm rolled through the area, and a lightning strike caused a station ebd. gas control called technician 1 who was working on equipment at another station when pipeline control called him to make him aware of the blowdown event. the station was not online at the time, so the employee informed gas control he would swing by on his way home. the employee wrapped up what he was doing and logged in remotely to the station hmi and noticed only the suction header had blown down, but the transmitter was still showing 300 psi. technician 1 recognized this was abnormal and called the manager of operations. the manager of operations logged into the security cameras and was able to determine that gas was still blowing from the suction line blowdown vent. this was approximately 30 minutes after the initial call that the station had blown down. technician 1 started heading to the station but was an hour away, manager of operations called technician 2, and he also started heading to the station. both techs arrived at station 430c at approximately the same time and found the 4" suction loading valve partially open from the esd test that was performed on wednesday. gas vented for 90 minutes at 300psi for a total of 8.145mmscf the lightning strike had blown 2 fuses and burned up the solenoid on the suction blow-down valve, which is why it actuated and the discharge blowdown did not. employees were not able to make repairs that evening as the thunderstorm continued with heavy rain and lightning. employees returned the next morning and made repairs and put the station back in service. an investigation will be conducted and moving forward the loading valves on the station suction and discharge will be added to the safety critical device list and will have car seals installed that will require removal and installation anytime the valves are operated in order to confirm they are left in the correct position.

NAME: NORTHERN NATURAL GAS CO
NARRATIVE: AT 20:40 ON SATURDAY OCTOBER 01, 2022, NORTHERN RECEIVED A CALL FROM THE OPERATIONS COMMUNICATION CENTER (OCC) STATING THAT A PASSERBY HEARD A LOUD NOISE FROM CHANCELLOR ETHANOL TBS. THE LOCAL TECHNICIAN WAS SENT TO THE STATION TO INVESTIGATE. THE TECHNICIAN CONTACTED GAS CONTROL AND DISCOVERED THAT NO ALARMS WERE REPORTING, AND SCADA WAS NOT COMMUNICATING.  NORTHWESTERN (THE LDC) WAS ONSITE AND REPORTED THAT GAS WAS BLOWING.   NORTHERN'S TECHNICIAN ARRIVED ON SCENE AT APPROXIMATELY 21:15 AND FOUND THE RELIEF VALVE RELIVING STACKS HALF OPEN. THE TECHNICIAN CHECKED PRESSURES FROM THE ELECTRONIC FLOW MEASUREMENT (EFM) AND NOTICED THAT NO DISPLAYS WERE WORKING. HE ALSO NOTICED THE EFM WAS NOT BEING POWERED. THE TECHNICIAN CORRECTED THE RELIEF VENTING BY LOWERING THE SET POINT OF THE SECONDARY PNEUMATIC VALVE CONTROLLER.  THE PRIMARY REGULATOR IS CONTROLLED WITH A DIGITAL VALVE CONTROLLER WHICH IS POWERED WITH 24 VOLTS. WHEN THE POWER WAS LOST TO THE DIGITAL VALVE CONTROLLER, THE REGULATOR FAILED OPEN CAUSING THE RELIEF TO VENT DUE TO THE SECONDARY REGULATOR BEING SET SLIGHTLY HIGHER THAN THE RELIEF. IF THE RELIEF WAS SET HIGHER THAN THE SECONDARY REGULATORS, THE RELIEF MAY NOT HAVE OPENED.  ON OCTOBER 3, 2022, FURTHER INVESTIGATION WAS CONDUCTED CONCERNING THE POWER FAILURE TO THE STATION. IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE SOLAR PANELS WERE NOT WIRED CORRECTLY TO CHARGE THE BATTERIES. THE BATTERIES WERE ONLY GETTING 19 VOLTS TO CHARGE 24-VOLT BATTERIES. THE BATTERIES WERE FULLY CHARGED WHEN THE STATION WAS PUT INTO SERVICE ON SEPTEMBER 28, 2022. THE BATTERIES SLOWLY DEPLETED FROM NOT BEING CHARGED CORRECTLY. UPON FURTHER REVIEW OF THE REGULATOR, THIS MODEL REGULATOR HAS A LOW VOLTAGE PROTECT FUNCTION THAT DISCONNECTS ALL THE LOAD ONCE THE BATTERIES REACH 23 VOLTS. NORTHERN NATURAL GAS SETS A LOW VOLTAGE ALARM AT 22 VOLTS. DUE TO THE VOLTAGE REGULATOR DISCONNECTING POWER AT 23 VOLTS, NO ALARMS WERE RECEIVED, NOR COULD ANY OTHER MONITORING BE PERFORMED REMOTELY.
narrative_clean: at 20:40 on saturday october 01, 2022, northern received a call from the operations communication center (occ) stating that a passerby heard a loud noise from chancellor ethanol tbs. the local technician was sent to the station to investigate. the technician contacted gas control and discovered that no alarms were reporting, and scada was not communicating. northwestern (the ldc) was onsite and reported that gas was blowing. northern's technician arrived on scene at approximately 21:15 and found the relief valve reliving stacks half open. the technician checked pressures from the electronic flow measurement (efm) and noticed that no displays were working. he also noticed the efm was not being powered. the technician corrected the relief venting by lowering the set point of the secondary pneumatic valve controller. the primary regulator is controlled with a digital valve controller which is powered with 24 volts. when the power was lost to the digital valve controller, the regulator failed open causing the relief to vent due to the secondary regulator being set slightly higher than the relief. if the relief was set higher than the secondary regulators, the relief may not have opened. on october 3, 2022, further investigation was conducted concerning the power failure to the station. it was discovered that the solar panels were not wired correctly to charge the batteries. the batteries were only getting 19 volts to charge 24-volt batteries. the batteries were fully charged when the station was put into service on september 28, 2022. the batteries slowly depleted from not being charged correctly. upon further review of the regulator, this model regulator has a low voltage protect function that disconnects all the load once the batteries reach 23 volts. northern natural gas sets a low voltage alarm at 22 volts. due to the voltage regulator disconnecting power at 23 volts, no alarms were received, nor could any other monitoring be performed remotely.

NAME: ANR PIPELINE CO
NARRATIVE: ON 29 SEPTEMBER 2022, TC ENERGY TECHNICIANS WERE PERFORMING A CORRECTIVE WORK ORDER TO REPLACE THE HYDRAULIC FLUID IN THE 501-45A-34 VALVE. WHILE PERFORMING THE WORK, AN INCIDENT OCCURRED RESULTING IN INJURIES AND A RELEASE OF GAS. THE INCIDENT WAS REPORTED TO THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER, #1348627. THE ANR 2-501 PIPELINE MP582.6 TO MP585.1 - 2-501 LOOP SOUTH END TO MAINLINE VALVE 46 (ISOLATED SEGMENT), HAS BEEN BLOWN DOWN AND ISOLATED. IN ADDITION, TC ENERGY HAS SUSPENDED QUALIFICATIONS ON COVERED TASKS ASSOCIATED WITH THE WORK BEING PERFORMED ASSOCIATED WITH THE INCIDENT AND CONDUCTED DRUG TESTING.    THE PIPELINE SEGMENT REMAINED OUT OF SERVICE UNTIL REPAIR OF THE PIPELINE WAS COMPLETED.  REPAIR TO THE PIPELINE INCLUDED THE REPLACEMENT OF THE VALVE AND VALVE OPERATOR.  THE PIPELINE WAS RESTARTED AND RETURNED TO FULL SERVICE ON JANUARY 13, 2023 AT 11:39 CST.    THE PRIMARY CAUSE OF THE FAILURE HAS BEEN DETERMINED TO BE THE RESULT OF THE TECHNICIAN FAILING TO CONFIRM MANUFACTURER'S REPAIR PROCEDURE AND OPENING THE VALVE DURING CORRECTIVE MAINTENANCE TO REPLACE THE HYDRAULIC HAND PUMP.  FOLLOWING THE REPAIR, WHEN THE VALVE WAS ACTUATED USING THE HAND PUMP, HYDRAULIC OIL BEGAN TO MOVE TO THE OPEN SIDE OF THE VALVE STEM AND THE VALVE GATE DISENGAGED AND MOVED IN AN UNCONTROLLED MANNER.  THE RESULT OF THIS ACTION CAUSED A FAILURE IN THE VALVE ACTUATOR CONNECTION AND A RELEASE OF PIPELINE FLUIDS AND HYDRAULIC OIL TO THE SURROUNDING AREA.
narrative_clean: on 29 september 2022, tc energy technicians were performing a corrective work order to replace the hydraulic fluid in the 501-45a-34 valve. while performing the work, an incident occurred resulting in injuries and a release of gas. the incident was reported to the national response center, #1348627. the anr 2-501 pipeline mp582.6 to mp585.1 - 2-501 loop south end to mainline valve 46 (isolated segment), has been blown down and isolated. in addition, tc energy has suspended qualifications on covered tasks associated with the work being performed associated with the incident and conducted drug testing. the pipeline segment remained out of service until repair of the pipeline was completed. repair to the pipeline included the replacement of the valve and valve operator. the pipeline was restarted and returned to full service on january 13, 2023 at 11:39 cst. the primary cause of the failure has been determined to be the result of the technician failing to confirm manufacturer's repair procedure and opening the valve during corrective maintenance to replace the hydraulic hand pump. following the repair, when the valve was actuated using the hand pump, hydraulic oil began to move to the open side of the valve stem and the valve gate disengaged and moved in an uncontrolled manner. the result of this action caused a failure in the valve actuator connection and a release of pipeline fluids and hydraulic oil to the surrounding area.

THE IDENTIFIED INTERNAL CORROSION WAS CONSISTENT WITH MESA CORROSION, TYPICALLY OCCURRING IN A CARBON DIOXIDE (CO2) ENVIRONMENT LIKELY EXACERBATED VIA THE PRESENCE OF SALT WATER AND SAND (RESULTING IN AN UNDER-DEPOSIT PHENOMENON). GUIDED WAVE TECHNOLOGY WAS UTILIZED UPSTREAM AND DOWNSTREAM OF REPLACED PIPE, OF WHICH NO ADDITIONAL INTEGRITY ISSUES WERE FOUND AND NO FOLLOW-UPS WERE RECOMMENDED.   THE 2 INCH LOW POINT DRAIN WAS THE FIRST PHASE OF STEPS MGS IS TAKING TO PREVENT RECURRENCE, THE SECOND INCLUDES DEVELOPING AND IMPLEMENTING A PIGGING AND CHEMICAL TREATMENT PLAN PRIOR TO BRINGING THE 12' EAST LATERAL IN SERVICE.

NAME: NORTHWEST PIPELINE LLC
NARRATIVE: ON NOVEMBER 9, 2022 OPERATIONS PERSONNEL ON SITE AT THE KEMMERER COMPRESSOR STATION HEARD WHAT APPEARED TO BE A COMPRESSOR RELIEF VALVE RELIEVING GAS. UPON FURTHER INVESTIGATION THE OPERATIONS TECHNICIAN DISCOVERED THE UNIT 1 PSV WAS RELIEVING. IN ORDER TO REMEDY THE SITUATION AS QUICKLY AS POSSIBLE, THE TECHNICIAN SHUT THE UNIT DOWN, ISOLATED IT FROM PRESSURE, AND BLEW IT DOWN. IT WAS NOTED BY THE TECHNICIAN AT THE TIME THAT THE RELIEF VALVE WOULD NOT RESEAT ITSELF AFTER DECREASING PRESSURE. IT WAS ALSO NOTED THAT THE RELIEF VALVE HAD OPENED UP PREMATURELY AT A PRESSURE OF AROUND 770PSI, WHERE THE SET PRESSURE ON THE RELIEF VALVE WAS 928 PSI. SINCE OPERATIONS DIDN'T KNOW EXACTLY WHEN THE RELIEF VALVE STARTED RELEASING GAS, THEY WORKED WITH TECH SERVICES AND GAS CONTROL TO ATTEMPT TO FIND ANY DATA SIGNIFYING WHEN THE RELEASE STARTED TO OCCUR. HMI TRENDS AND STATION CCTV CAMERAS WERE UTILIZED TO TRY AND DETERMINE WHEN THE UNIT STARTED TO RELIEVE, BUT WERE UNSUCCESSFUL IN DETERMINING THE EXACT TIME. AFTER REVIEWING THAT DATA THROUGHOUT THE DAY ON NOVEMBER 9TH AND NOT FINDING A DEFINITIVE ANSWER, IT WAS DECIDED TO CALCULATE A GAS LOSS ESTIMATION FROM THE MOMENT THE OPERATOR ARRIVED ON SITE AT 06:45 TO THE TIME THE UNIT WAS COMPLETELY ISOLATED AND GAS HAD STOPPED RELEASING AT 07:22. ONCE THIS TIMEFRAME WAS DECIDED, THE GAS LOSS CALCULATION WAS PROMPTLY RUN AND FOUND TO BE IN EXCESS OF THE 3MMSCF THRESHOLD. THAT GAS LOSS ESTIMATION WAS THEN COMMUNICATED TO THE SECURITY OPERATIONS CENTER AT WILLIAMS AND WAS IMMEDIATELY REPORTED TO THE NRC THAT AFTERNOON.    OVER THE COURSE OF THE FOLLOWING WEEKS, OPERATIONS WORKED WITH GAS CONTROL, SCADA, AND TECH SERVICES TO INVESTIGATE WHY THE VALVE HAD OPENED AT A LOWER PRESSURE THAN DESIGNED. IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE PILOT ON THIS PSV FAILED DUE TO A HARMONIC FREQUENCY AT THE STATION. IN ORDER TO REMEDY THE SITUATION, OPERATIONS WORKED TO GET A NEW AND DIFFERENT PILOT INSTALLED ON THIS PSV THAT WOULDN'T BE SUSCEPTIBLE TO PREMATURE RELIEVING AS A RESULT OF HARMONICS. OPERATIONS SUCCESSFULLY INSTALLED THE NEW PILOT ON THE PSV AND RETURNED THE COMPRESSOR UNIT TO SERVICE ON 11/18/2022.
narrative_clean: on november 9, 2022 operations personnel on site at the kemmerer compressor station heard what appeared to be a compressor relief valve relieving gas. upon further investigation the around 770psi, where the set pressure on the relief valve was 928 psi. since operations didn't know exactly when the relief valve started releasing gas, they worked with tech services and gas control to attempt to find any data signifying when the release started to occur. hmi trends and station cctv cameras were utilized to try and determine when the unit started to relieve, but were unsuccessful in determining the exact time. after reviewing that data throughout the day on november 9th and not finding a definitive answer, it was decided to calculate a gas loss estimation from the moment the operator arrived on site at 06:45 to the time the unit was completely isolated and gas had stopped releasing at 07:22. once this timeframe was decided, the gas loss calculation was promptly run and narrative_clean: equitrans rager mountain storage field was shut-in on 11/1/2022 to perform routine shut-in inventory verification testing. on november 6, 2022, equitrans personnel was notified of an the other wells with a high definition, metal loss vertilog tool. 4- evaluating any other mechanical gas migration pathways between the production and intermediate casing 5- reviewing existing storage well emergency preparedness and response procedures based on lessons learned from shutting in well 2244 to identify and implement potential improvements. ***february 2023 supplement*** notification of NARRATIVE: ON NOVEMBER 21, 2022, AT APPROXIMATELY 06:00 HOURS, A STATION MECHANIC REPORTING TO WORK AT THE CONSUMERS ENERGY'S  FREEDOM COMPRESSOR STATION OBSERVED GAS BLOWING AT/NEAR THE CONDENSATE STORAGE TANK.  FREEDOM COMPRESSOR STATION IS LOCATED AT 12201 E. PLEASANT LAKE ROAD, MANCHESTER, (WASHTENAW COUNTY) MICHIGAN.    THE EMPLOYEE RESPONDED BY UTILIZING ISOLATION VALVE (30SDV-012) TO STOP THE GAS FROM BLOWING AND BEGAN A PRELIMINARY INVESTIGATION TO DETERMINE THE CAUSE OF THE GAS RELEASE. A REVIEW OF THE SECURITY FOOTAGE AND CONFIRMATION OF HISTORIAN DATA DETERMINED THE RELEASE BEGAN ON SUNDAY, NOVEMBER 20, 2022, AT APPROXIMATELY 05:48 HOURS.     THE INITIAL INVESTIGATION ON NOVEMBER 21, 2022 DETERMINED THE FILTER SEPARATOR DUMP VALVE (30GV-528) DID NOT CLOSE AFTER THE CONDENSATE DUMP OPERATION AND ALLOWED GAS TO FLOW FREELY FROM THE FILTER-SEPARATOR TO THE CONDENSATE STORAGE TANK AND RELEASE TO ATMOSPHERE. CONSUMERS ENERGY PERSONNEL INITIATED AN ABNORMAL EQUIPMENT ALIGNMENT/CONFIGURATION REQUEST (AEC) TO ISOLATE THE FILTER-SEPARATOR CONDENSATE SYSTEM TO ALLOW FOR MANUAL OPERATION.    FURTHER INVESTIGATION DETERMINED THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE RELEASE WAS DUE TO THE FILTER SEPARATOR SOUTH SUMP LEVEL CONTROLLER (LC_3001500).  THE LEVEL CONTROLLER SENT A PNEUMATIC SIGNAL TO THE DUMP VALVE WHICH OPENED THE VALVE TO INITIATE THE CONDENSATE DUMP PROCESS.  AFTER THE DUMP OPERATION WAS COMPLETE, THE SIGNAL TO CLOSE THE VALVE WAS NOT INITIATED (REMOVED) CAUSING THE DUMP VALVE TO REMAIN OPEN.       ON DECEMBER 7, 2022, CONSUMERS ENERGY (CE) PERSONNEL MET WITH THE LOCAL MAGNETROL LEVEL CONTROLLER SALES ENGINEER TO TROUBLESHOOT THE LEVEL CONTROLLER OPERATION. DURING THE INVESTIGATION IT WAS DISCOVERED THE LEVEL ADJUSTMENT KNOB WAS SET AT 1 WHICH WAS LOWER THAN RECOMMENDED FOR THIS OPERATION. STATION PERSONNEL PROCEEDED TO INCREASE THE LEVEL CONTROL SET POINT WHILE MONITORING SYSTEM RESPONSE.  AFTER ADJUSTING THE LEVEL TO A SET POINT OF 5, WHICH WAS DETERMINED TO BE AN ACCEPTABLE LEVEL SET POINT FOR OPERATION.    CE PERSONNEL WILL CONTINUE TO EVALUATING GAS COMPRESSION STATION LEVEL CONTROLLERS AND GAS CONTROL NOTIFICATION METHODS TO ALARM IN THE EVENT OF GAS RELEASE ASSOCIATED WITH PNEUMATIC LEVEL CONTROL DEVICES. THE UNIT WILL REMAIN IN BY-PASS MODE UNTIL THE EVALUATION IS COMPLETED AND ACTIONS TO MITIGATE ARE IMPLEMENTED.    THE EVALUATION OF THE LEVEL CONTROLLER AND GAS CONTROL NOTIFICATION METHODS AT THE FREEDOM COMPRESSOR STATION WAS COMPLETED.  AS A RESULT, LOW LEVEL LIQUID ALARMS AS WELL AS CONDENSATE TANK ACOUSTIC MONITORING WERE IMPLEMENTED. THE AEC WAS REMOVED AND THE UNIT IS NO LONGER IN BY-PASS MODE, NORMAL OPERATION RESUMED ON JANUARY 24, 2023.    CE HAS COMPLETED PROBLEM SOLVING SESSIONS REGARDING CONDENSATE DRAIN SYSTEM ALARMING AND FILTER-SEPARATOR COMMISSIONING/OPERATIONAL TESTING.  LONG-TERM COUNTERMEASURES WERE GENERATED WITH A PLAN TO INCORPORATE FLEETWIDE.
narrative_clean: on november 21, 2022, at approximately 06:00 hours, a station mechanic reporting to work at the consumers energy's freedom compressor station observed gas blowing at/near the condensate storage tank. freedom compressor station is located at 12201 e. pleasant lake road, manchester, (washtenaw county) michigan. the employee responded by utilizing isolation valve (30sdv-012) to stop the gas from blowing and began a preliminary investigation to determine the cause of the gas release. a review of the security footage and confirmation of historian data determined the release began on sunday, november 20, 2022, at approximately 05:48 hours. the initial investigation on november 21, 2022 determined the filter separator dump valve (30gv-528) did not close after the condensate dump operation and allowed gas to flow freely from the filter-separator to the condensate storage tank and release to atmosphere. consumers energy personnel initiated an abnormal equipment alignment/configuration request (aec) to isolate the filter-separator condensate system to allow for manual operation. further investigation determined the root cause of the release was due to the filter separator south sump level controller (lc_3001500). the level controller sent a pneumatic signal to the dump valve which opened the valve to initiate the condensate dump process. after the dump operation was complete, the signal to close the valve was not initiated (removed) causing the dump valve to remain open. on december 7, 2022, consumers energy (ce) personnel met with the local magnetrol level controller sales engineer to troubleshoot the level controller operation. during the investigation it was discovered the level adjustment knob was set at 1 which was lower than recommended for this operation. station personnel proceeded to increase the level control set point while monitoring system response. after adjusting the level to a set point of 5, which was determined to be an acceptable level set point for operation. ce personnel will continue to evaluating gas compression station level controllers and gas control notification methods to alarm in the NARRATIVE: ON 11/28/22 AT APPROX 23:22, TL-442 RUPTURED AT STA 5+00 UNDER AN ACCESS ROAD ON COMPANY PROPERTY IN PINE GROVE, WV. INITIAL NOTICE WAS RECEIVED FROM AN OUTSIDE PARTY AT APPROX 23:23. TL-442 IS A 16 IN OD TRANSMISSION PIPELINE APPROX 0.30 MI LONG AND TRANSPORTS NATURAL GAS FROM HASTINGS CS TO MOCKINGBIRD HILL CS. THE MAOP OF TL-442 IS 990 PSIG. A PRESSURE RESTRICTION OF 960 PSIG WAS ESTABLISHED IN 2003 FOR TL-442 DUE TO ITS CONNECTION TO TL-430 AT HAUGHT JCT. TL-442 WAS IN NORMAL OPERATION WITH AN OP OF 947 PSIG WHEN THE INCIDENT OCCURRED. AT APPROX 23:30, OPS PERSONNEL CALLED 911. ALSO AT APPROX 23:30, THE C-300 UNIT AT HASTINGS CS SHUTDOWN AND THE ASSOCIATED UNIT VALVES CLOSED, ISOLATING TL-442 UPSTREAM OF THE RUPTURE. AT APPROX 23:33, GAS CONTROL REMOTELY CLOSED VALVE-420JJ, ISOLATING TL-442 DOWNSTREAM OF THE RUPTURE. AT APPROX 23:50, OPS PERSONNEL ARRIVED AT THE SITE. THE RUPTURE RESULTED IN AN APPROX 40 FT LENGTH OF PIPE OPENING CIRCUMFERENTIALLY AND LONGITUDINALLY (NOT SEAM ORIENTED) AND BOTH ENDS FOLDING UP AND COMING OUT OF THE GROUND; APPROX 23,403 MCF OF GAS LOSS; DAMAGE TO THE ACCESS ROAD; AND DEBRIS BEING BLOWN ON THE RIGHT-OF-WAY, S.R. 20, AND A RAILROAD. S.R. 20 AND THE RAILROAD WERE TEMPORARILY CLOSED AT 23:40 TO REMOVE DEBRIS. THE GAS DID NOT IGNITE AND THERE WERE NO FIRES, INJURIES, FATALITIES, OR EVACUATIONS. IT WAS DETERMINED ON 11/29/2022 AT 00:44 THAT THE INCIDENT INVOLVED AN UNINTENTIONAL ESTIMATED VOLUME OF GAS LOSS OF 3 MMSCF OR MORE. INITIAL NOTIFICATION (#1353645) WAS MADE TO THE NRC ON 11/29/22 AT 01:04. FOLLOW UP NOTIFICATION (#1353781) WAS MADE TO THE NRC ON 11/30/22 AT 11:46 TO CONFIRM THE INITIAL NOTIFICATION AND UPDATE THE CURRENT STATUS OF THE TL-442, THE GPS COORDINATES, THE ESTIMATED VOLUME OF UNINTENTIONAL GAS LOSS, AND THE TEMPORARY CLOSURE (AND REOPENING) OF S.R. 20 AND THE RAILROAD IN ORDER TO REMOVE DEBRIS. THE ESTIMATED VOLUME OF UNINTENTIONAL GAS LOSS WAS LATER CONFIRMED TO BE 23,403 MCF. TL-442 WAS RESTARTED ON 12/30/22 AT 14:09 AFTER COMPLETION OF THE FOLLOWING REMEDIATION: APPROX 485 FT OF STATION PIPING AT HASTINGS CS ASSOCIATED WITH TL-442 WAS REMOVED AND REPLACED ALONG WITH VALVE-425D TO RESUME THE FLOW OF GAS BETWEEN HASTINGS CS AND MOCKINGBIRD HILL CS THROUGH TL-597 AND INTO TL-430 WHILE THE REMEDIATION OF TL-442 WAS COMPLETED. BOTH ENDS OF THE PIPE WERE CUT AT THE RUPTURE ON TL-442, UPSTREAM AND DOWNSTREAM OF THE HINGED AREAS WHERE THE PIPE FOLDED UP AND CAME OUT OF THE GROUND. THE TWO PIECES OF PIPE THAT WERE CUT-OUT AT THE RUPTURE WERE SENT TO KIEFNER FOR METALLURGICAL ANALYSIS AND REPLACEMENT PIPE WAS INSTALLED. THE METALLURGICAL ANALYSIS REPORT FROM KIEFNER DETERMINED THAT EXTERNAL CORROSION WHERE DISBONDED POLYETHYLENE COATING WAS SHIELDING CATHODIC PROTECTION WAS THE APPARENT CAUSE OF THE FAILURE. PIPE WAS CUT-OUT AT SELECTED LOCATIONS TO PROVIDE ACCESS TO THE INSIDE OF TL-442 FOR WIRELINE INSPECTIONS. WIRELINES USING CAL AND MFL TOOLS WERE CONDUCTED TO ASSESS THE INTEGRITY OF TL-442 AND REPLACEMENT PIPE WAS INSTALLED AT THE ACCESS LOCATIONS. INITIAL VERIFICATION DIGS WERE COMPLETED ON EITHER SIDE OF THE RUPTURE TO ASSIST IN VALIDATING THE ACCURACY OF THE DATA FROM THE WIRELINES. BASED ON THE DATA FROM THE WIRELINES, THE RESULTS FROM THE INITIAL VERIFICATION DIGS, AND THE EVALUATION OF ANOMALIES AS DESCRIBED BELOW, APPROX 950 FT OF TL-442 WAS REPLACED. THIS INVOLVED REPLACING TWO SECTIONS OF TL-442, FROM VALVE-425D TO THE SOUTH SIDE OF FISHING CREEK AND FROM THE NORTH SIDE OF S.R. 20 TO MOCKINGBIRD HILL JCT. THE ANOMALIES LOCATED IN THESE TWO SECTIONS WERE EVALUATED AS THE PIPE WAS EXCAVATED PRIOR TO REMOVAL AND FURTHER VERIFIED THE ACCURACY OF THE DATA FROM THE WIRELINES. APPROX 120 FT OF TL-442 LOCATED IN A CASING UNDER THE RAILROAD AND S.R. 20 WAS REMOVED AND REPLACEMENT PIPE WAS INSTALLED. AN ANOMALY LOCATED ON THE CASED PIPE THAT WAS REMOVED WAS EVALUATED AND FURTHER VERIFIED THE ACCURACY OF THE DATA FROM THE WIRELINES.

NAME: NORTHWEST PIPELINE LLC
NARRATIVE: ON DECEMBER 19, 2022 WILLIAMS GAS CONTROL SENT A START COMMAND TO UNIT 1 AT VERNAL COMPRESSOR STATION, LOCATED ON THE NORTHWEST PIPELINE SYSTEM. SHORTLY AFTER THE START COMMAND WAS SENT, GAS CONTROL RECEIVED A VOLTAGE IMBALANCE ALARM. GAS CONTROL FURTHER INVESTIGATED THIS ALARM VIA THE HMI SYSTEM AND NOTICED THAT THE UNIT 1 LOADING VALVE WAS ISSUING A COMMAND DISAGREE ALARM. IT WAS ALSO NOTED AT THIS TIME THAT THE HMI SCHEMATIC SHOWED THE LOADING VALVE WAS OPEN (IT SHOULD'VE BEEN CLOSED). GAS CONTROL CALLED THE LOCAL ON-CALL TECHNICIANS TO HEAD TO THE SITE TO INVESTIGATE. WHEN OPERATIONS PERSONNEL ARRIVED ON SITE THEY WERE ABLE TO CONFIRM THAT THE LOADING VALVE WAS IN FACT OPEN AND VENTING GAS TO THE ATMOSPHERE. IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE VALVE WAS FROZEN IN THE OPEN POSITION. THE TECHNICIANS QUICKLY ACTED TO CLOSE THE LOADING VALVE BY WARMING THE VALVE AND MANUALLY MOVING IT TO THE CLOSED POSITION, CAUSING THE VENTING TO STOP. ONCE THE VALVES WERE COMPLETELY THAWED, OPERATIONS AND GAS CONTROL MANUALLY AND REMOTELY OPENED AND CLOSED THE VALVE TO ENSURE THAT PROPER FUNCTION HAD BEEN RESTORED. OVER THE NEXT SEVERAL HOURS, OPERATIONS WORKED WITH TECH SERVICES TO DEVELOP AN ACCURATE ESTIMATE FOR THE QUANTITY OF GAS THAT WAS RELEASED. A FINAL NUMBER OF 3,790 MSCF WAS CALCULATED. SINCE THE INITIAL OCCURRENCE, THE VALVE HAS OPERATED CORRECTLY EACH TIME AN OPEN / CLOSE COMMAND HAS BEEN ISSUED.    ADDITIONAL DETAIL ADDED 02/13/23: THE LOADING VALVE IS A 2' VALVE THAT IS USED TO PURGE AND BRING THE COMPRESSOR UP TO PIPELINE PRESSURE BEFORE THE MAIN UNIT VALVES CAN BE OPENED.  THIS IS A FAIL CLOSED VALVE THAT USES PNEUMATIC POWER TO OPEN.  ICING WAS PRESENT IN THE OPERATOR AND PNEUMATIC VENT, HOLDING THE VALVE IN THE OPEN POSITION.  AFTER HEAT WAS APPLIED TO REMOVE THE ICE, THE VALVE WAS ABLE TO BE MOVED AND CYCLED NORMALLY.
narrative_clean: on december 19, 2022 williams gas control sent a start command to unit 1 at vernal compressor station, located on the northwest pipeline system. shortly after the start command was sent, gas control received a voltage imbalance alarm. gas control further investigated this alarm via the hmi system and noticed that the unit 1 loading valve was issuing a command disagree alarm. it was also noted at this time that the hmi schematic showed the loading valve was open (it should've been closed). gas control called the local on-call technicians to head to the site to investigate. when operations personnel arrived on site they were able to confirm that the loading valve was in fact open and venting gas to the atmosphere. it was discovered that the valve was frozen in the open position. the technicians quickly acted to close the loading valve by warming the valve and manually moving it to the closed position, causing the venting to stop. once the valves were completely thawed, operations and gas control manually and remotely opened and closed the valve to ensure that proper function had been restored. over the next several hours, operations worked with tech services to develop an accurate estimate for the quantity of gas that was released. a final number of 3,790 mscf was calculated. since the initial occurrence, the valve has operated correctly each time an open / close command has been issued. additional detail added 02/13/23: the loading valve is a 2' valve that is used to purge and bring the compressor up to pipeline pressure before the main unit valves can be opened. this is a fail closed valve that uses pneumatic power to open. icing was present in the operator and pneumatic vent, holding the valve in the open position. after heat was applied to remove the ice, the valve was able to be moved and cycled normally.

NAME: NORTHERN NATURAL GAS CO
NARRATIVE: ON DECEMBER 22, 2022, AT 2106 FIELD OPERATIONS TECHNICIAN WAS NOTIFIED OF A VENTING RELIEF VALVE IN THE OGDEN COMPRESSOR STATION. IT WAS DETERMINED TO BE THE RELIEF VALVE DOWNSTREAM OF VALVE 113 ON THE DES MOINES A-LINE (IAB65001). ACCORDING TO DATA TRENDS THE RELIEF VALVE VENTED 20 TIMES FOR AN AVERAGE OF 40 SECONDS EACH FROM 2100 HOURS TO 2116 HOURS. HIGHEST PRESSURE RECORDED WAS 456 PSIG AT 2109 HOURS. AT 2116 HOURS THE PRESSURE RETURNED TO NORMAL OPERATING PRESSURE OF 355PSIG.     THE INVESTIGATION REVEALED THE CAUSE OF THE OVERPRESSURE WAS DUE TO CONSTRUCTION DEBRIS IN THE WHISPER TRIM CAGE OF THE VALVE 49 REGULATOR. THE DEBRIS CAUSED THE REGULATOR TO NOT CLOSE COMPLETELY. THE TEAM HAD MIDWEST VALVE TO INSPECT THE VALVE AND FOUND THE DEBRIS IN THE REGULATOR CAGE. THE CAGE WAS CLEANED OF ALL DEBRIS. THE STEM AND SEAT WERE VERIFIED TO HAVE NO DAMAGE. NEW SOFT GOODS AND SEALS WERE INSTALLED IN THE REGULATOR. WORK WAS COMPLETED ON JANUARY 5, 2023. THE CONTRACTOR TESTED THE VALVE FOR PROPER OPERATION AND FOUND NO ISSUES WITH THE VALVE OPENING AND CLOSING.    04/05/23 UPDATE - THE DEBRIS FOUND IN THE WHISPER TRIM CAGE WAS MOST LIKELY FROM PIGGING OPERATIONS NOT CONSTRUCTION. ALSO, THE DES MOINES A-LINE (IAB65001) WAS MISTAKENLY LISTED AS A 380 MAOP. IT SHOULD READ 500 MAOP. IN 2016 NORTHERN HAD AN INCIDENT ON THE M640A BUSHTON TO TESCOTT MAINLINE NEAR I-70 IN KANSAS. NORTHERN WAS ISSUED A CORRECTIVE ACTON ORDER. AS A RESULT, NORTHERN VOLUNTARILY LOWERED THE MAOP ON ALL BARE, DRESSER COUPLED MAINLINES. NORTHERN HAS BEEN ABANDONING AND REMOVING THOSE MAINLINES. THE CAO DID NOT INCLUDE BRANCH LINES SO DES MOINES SHOULD NOT HAVE BEEN INCLUDED. THIS BRANCHLINE IS BEING REPLACED WITH A NEW 16-INCH C-LINE (IAB65003). THAT PIPELINE WILL BE IN-SERVICE BY NOVEMBER 1, 2023. AT THAT TIME THE A-LINE WILL BE SHUT OFF AND READIED FOR ABANDONMENT. THAT SHOULD ELIMINATE THE LAST 16-INCH AND ABOVE BARE, DRESSER COUPLED PIPELINE.
