NAME: ENERGY TRANSFER COMPANY
NARRATIVE: ON DECEMBER 30, 2022 AT APPROXIMATELY 01:15 LOCAL TIME, A FIRE OCCURRED AT THE DOMINATOR COMPRESSOR STATION ON UNIT #6, 30 MILES WEST OF JAL, NEW MEXICO IN LEA COUNTY.    OPERATIONS RECEIVED A CALL FROM THE 911 DISPATCHER AND THE FIRE DEPARTMENT WAS DISPATCHED TO THE STATION. THE OPERATIONS MECHANIC, WHO IS ALSO A VOLUNTEER FIRE FIGHTER, ARRIVED WITH THE FIRE DEPARTMENT AND ESD'D THE STATION.    A DECISION WAS MADE TO LET THE FIRE BURN ITSELF OUT.    AT 06:00 MOUNTAIN TIME, THE STATION WAS SAFE TO ENTER AND OPERATIONS MADE AN INITIAL ASSESSMENT AND IT WAS DETERMINED THE REPAIRS AND DAMAGES WOULD EXCEED THE $123,900.00 REPORTABLE DOLLAR CRITERIA.    AT APPROXIMATELY 15:30, UNIT #6 WAS ISOLATED AND THE STATION WAS PUT BACK ONLINE BY USING THE OTHER COMPRESSORS.    THE UNINTENTIONAL GAS LOSS WAS CALCULATED AT 1500 MCF.    THE CAUSE OF THE FIRE IS STILL UNDER INVESTIGATION.    COMPONENTS HAS BEEN SENT TO THE LAB FOR ANALYSIS TO DETERMINE THE CAUSE OF THE FIRE. AND UNIT #6 WILL BE SENT TO THE MANUFACTURER TO BE DISMANTLED AND EXAMINED.    A SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT WILL BE SUBMITTED ONCE THE DETERMINATION HAS BEEN MADE.    **3/22/2023 UPDATE**    AFTER THE COMPLETION OF THE LAB ANALYSIS, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE CAUSE OF THE FIRE WAS DUE TO A LEAK ON THE COMPRESSOR FUEL RAIL.     THE INVESTIGATION REVEALED THAT THE FUEL RAIL AND HANDRAIL WERE IN CONTACT FOR SOME PERIOD OF TIME BASED ON THE APPEARANCE OF WEAR ON THE HANDRAIL.  THE HANDRAIL EXPERIENCED VIBRATIONS OVER TIME, EVENTUALLY SHEARING THE BOLT PROVIDED AND INCREASING THE CONTACT BETWEEN THE FUEL RAIL AND HANDRAIL, THUS CAUSING THE FUEL RAIL TO LEAK FUEL GAS AND IGNITE FROM A HEAT SOURCE IN CLOSE PROXIMITY.     TO PREVENT REOCCURRENCE, OPERATIONS WILL BE VISUALLY INSPECTING, IDENTIFYING, AND CORRECTING UNITS THAT MAY HAVE SIMILAR INSTALLATIONS AND PERFORM PACKAGE ASSESSMENTS DURING ROUTINE PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE.
narrative_clean: on december 30, 2022 at approximately 01:15 local time, a fire occurred at the dominator compressor station on unit #6, 30 miles west of jal, new mexico in lea county. operations received a call from the 911 dispatcher and the fire department was dispatched to the station. the operations mechanic, who is also a volunteer fire fighter, arrived with the fire department and esd'd the station. a decision was made to let the fire burn itself out. at 06:00 mountain time, the station was safe to enter and operations made an initial assessment and it was determined the repairs and damages would exceed the $123,900.00 reportable dollar criteria. at approximately 15:30, unit #6 was isolated and the station was put back online by using the other compressors. the unintentional gas loss was calculated at 1500 mcf. the cause of the fire is still under investigation. components has been sent to the lab for analysis to determine the cause of the fire. and unit #6 will be sent to the manufacturer to be dismantled and examined. a supplemental report will be submitted once the determination has been made. **3/22/2023 update** after the completion of the lab analysis, it was determined that the cause of the fire was due to a leak on the compressor fuel rail. the investigation revealed that the fuel rail and handrail were in contact for some period of time based on the appearance of wear on the handrail. the handrail experienced vibrations over time, eventually shearing the bolt provided and increasing the contact between the fuel rail and handrail, thus causing the fuel rail to leak fuel gas and ignite from a heat source in close proximity. to prevent reoccurrence, operations will be visually inspecting, identifying, and correcting units that may have similar installations and perform package assessments during routine preventive maintenance.

NAME: FLORIDA GAS TRANSMISSION CO
NARRATIVE: ON JANUARY 2, 2023, AT APPROXIMATELY 1206 HOURS, AN FGT TECHNICIAN WAS NOTIFIED BY A DOWNSTREAM CUSTOMER THAT A RELIEF VALVE AT THE CLEARWATER SOUTH REGULATOR STATION WAS CURRENTLY ACTIVATED.  THE CLEARWATER STATION IS SHARED WITH ANOTHER OPERATOR (CLEARWATER GAS COMPANY).  THE FGT TECHNICIAN PROMPTLY RESPONDED TO THE AREA AND ISOLATED THE SOURCE AT APPROXIMATELY 1300 HRS.  LOCAL FIRE DEPARTMENT AND POLICE RESPONDED TO A 3RD PARTY NOTIFICATION, AND THEY BLOCKED TRAFFIC IN BOTH DIRECTIONS UNTIL THE COMPANY TECHNICIAN ISOLATED THE REGULATOR RUN.  ACCORDING TO SCADA, THE RELIEF VALVE BEGAN VENTING AT APPROXIMATELY 1030 HRS THAT DAY.  THE PRESSURE EXCEEDED THE HI ALARM LIMIT THAT WOULD HAVE INITIATED CLOSER MONITORING BY GAS CONTROL HOWEVER THE PRESSURE DID NOT EXCEED THE HIHI CRITICAL ALARM LIMIT THAT WOULD HAVE GENERATED A CALL OUT AND FIELD INVESTIGATION.         THE VOLUME RELEASED WAS CALCULATED TO BE APPROXIMATELY 3.45 MMSCF NATURAL GAS.  THE DETERMINATION TIME FOR THIS ESTIMATE WAS APPROXIMATELY 1452 HRS.  NRC NOTIFICATION OCCURRED AT APPROXIMATELY 1551 HRS.  THE CLEARWATER SOUTH REGULATOR STATION DOES CONTAIN COVERED SEGMENTS IN THE COMPANY IMP, HOWEVER THE PIPING ASSOCIATED WITH THIS INCIDENT IS NOT A COVERED SEGMENT AS DETERMINED BY METHOD 2 (PIR).    UPON INVESTIGATION THE CAUSE OF THE INCIDENT WAS CONFIRMED AS A DAMAGED DIAPHRAGM IN A MOODY PILOT ON THE REGULATOR WHICH ALLOWED HIGHER PRESSURE FLOW THROUGH THE STATION WHICH ACTIVATED THE RELIEF VALVE.  THE RELIEF CAPACITY WAS VALIDATED DURING THE RELEASE VOLUME CALCULATION.  THE DAMAGED EQUIPMENT WAS IMMEDIATELY REPLACED BY THE TECHNICIAN.     TO PREVENT RECURRENCE THE COMPANY IS REVIEWING THE HIHI CRITICAL ALARM SETTING AT THIS LOCATION IN RELATION TO RELIEF VALVE SETTING AND WILL RESET THE HIHI ALARM AT A LEVEL BELOW THE RELIEF VALVE SETTING.  THIS WILL RESULT IN A CALL OUT TO THE FIELD TO PERFORM INVESTIGATION BEFORE THE RELIEF ACTIVATES OR SHORTEN THE LENGTH OF TIME A RELIEF IS ACTIVATED.
narrative_clean: on january 2, 2023, at approximately 1206 hours, an fgt technician was notified by a downstream customer that a relief valve at the clearwater south regulator station was currently activated. the clearwater station is shared with another operator (clearwater gas company). the fgt technician promptly responded to the area and isolated the source at approximately 1300 hrs. local fire department and police responded to a 3rd party notification, and they blocked traffic in both directions until the company technician isolated the regulator run. according to scada, the relief valve began venting at approximately 1030 hrs that day. the pressure exceeded the hi alarm limit that would have initiated closer monitoring by gas control however the pressure did not exceed the hihi critical alarm limit that would have generated a call out and field investigation. the volume released was calculated to be approximately 3.45 mmscf natural gas. the determination time for this estimate was approximately 1452 hrs. nrc notification occurred at approximately 1551 hrs. the clearwater south regulator station does contain covered segments in the company imp, however the piping associated with this incident is not a covered segment as determined by method 2 (pir). upon investigation the cause of the incident was confirmed as a damaged diaphragm in a moody pilot on the regulator which allowed higher pressure flow through the station which activated the relief valve. the relief capacity was validated during the release volume calculation. the damaged equipment was immediately replaced by the technician. to prevent recurrence the company is reviewing the hihi critical alarm setting at this location in relation to relief valve setting and will reset the hihi alarm at a level below the relief valve setting. this will result in a call out to the field to perform investigation before the relief activates or shorten the length of time a relief is activated.

NAME: MPLX LP
NARRATIVE: THIS REPORT IS FOR THE FIXED FACILITY EVENT THAT OCCURRED ON OCTOBER 11, 2022:    AT 9:45 PM ON OCTOBER 11TH, ARKOMA 1 COMPRESSOR STATION WAS IN NORMAL OPERATIONS AT STEADY STATE CONDITIONS WHEN ENGINE/COMPRESSOR UNIT #2203 SHUT DOWN ON HIGH ENGINE COOLANT TEMPERATURE. THE ON-SITE OPERATOR INSPECTED THE UNIT AND INITIATED A BLOW DOWN TO PREPARE IT FOR RE-START.     AT APPROXIMATELY 10:12 PM, DURING THE UNIT BLOW DOWN, TWO (2) LEL GAS MONITORS ACTIVATED WITHIN THE ENCLOSED COMPRESSOR BUILDING, ACTIVATING AN ESD WHICH TRIPPED ALL COMPRESSORS (4 TOTAL) AND SHUT ELECTRICAL POWER TO THE SITE AS DESIGNED.     THE OPERATOR EVACUATED THE BUILDING. GAS WAS RELEASED AND IGNITED, AND THE BUILDING BECAME ENGULFED IN FLAMES AT APPROXIMATELY 10:16 PM. THERE WERE MULTIPLE LOSS OF CONTAINMENT (LOPC) POINTS AND EQUIPMENT FAILURES.    THE EVENT WAS CLASSIFIED AS AN ENCLOSED VAPOR CLOUD DEFLAGRATION FOLLOWED BY A FIRE.    THE INITIAL CAUSE OF THE ESD AND THE INITIATING IGNITION SOURCE COULD NOT BE DEFINITIVELY IDENTIFIED. IT IS SUSPECTED THAT LOPC ASSOCIATED WITH UNIT #2202 INITIATED THE ESD.    INCIPIENT FIRES FUELED BY THE RESIDUAL ENGINE OIL, COOLANT, AND INSULATION CONTINUED TO BURN UNTIL THE FIRE WAS EXTINGUISHED ON OCTOBER 12, 2022, AT APPROXIMATELY 11:00 AM CST.    ROOT CAUSE: WE HAVE DETERMINED THAT MULTIPLE FACTORS CAUSED THE EVENT, INCLUDING FAULTY AND MISSING CHECK VALVES AND LOW-PRESSURE BRAIDED HOSES EXPOSED TO HIGH PRESSURE FROM THE VENT SYSTEM.    PATH FORWARD: WE HAVE SINCE COMPLETED ISOLATING INDIVIDUAL VENTILATION LINES FROM THE PRE-LUBE PUMPS AND STARTERS, WHICH WILL SEPARATE HIGH-PRESSURE FROM LOW-PRESSURE COMPONENTS.  FOR THREE DAYS, WE ALSO HAD 20 + PEOPLE GO FLANGE TO FLANGE COMPLETE A PROCESS HAZARD ANALYSIS, CONFIRMING ALL THE DESIGNS AND P&IDS ARE CORRECT AND CORRECTED WHERE NEEDED.    RE-DESIGNING SKIDS TO REMOVE AS MANY THREADED CONNECTIONS AS POSSIBLE.    IMPLEMENTED AND SCHEDULED REPLACEMENTS OF WORN ITEMS SUCH AS BRAIDED HOSES.    INSTRUMENT AND COMPRESSOR START GAS HAVE BEEN CONVERTED TO AIR.    THE NEW BUILDING WILL BE OPEN WITH NO WALLS FOR IMPROVED VENTILATION.    ONCE THE COMPRESSOR STATION IS COMMISSIONED, A SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT TO THIS ONE WILL BE SUBMITTED.
narrative_clean: this report is for the fixed facility event that occurred on october 11, 2022: at 9:45 pm on october 11th, arkoma 1 compressor station was in normal operations at steady state conditions when engine/compressor unit #2203 shut down on high engine coolant temperature. the on-site operator inspected the unit and initiated a blow down to prepare it for re-start. at approximately 10:12 pm, during the unit blow down, two (2) lel gas monitors activated within the enclosed compressor building, activating an esd which tripped all compressors (4 total) and shut electrical power to the site as designed. the operator evacuated the building. gas was released and ignited, and the building became engulfed in flames at approximately 10:16 pm. there were multiple loss of containment (lopc) points and equipment failures. the event was classified as an enclosed vapor cloud deflagration followed by a fire. the initial cause of the esd and the initiating ignition source could not be definitively identified. it is suspected that lopc associated with unit #2202 initiated the esd. incipient fires fueled by the residual engine oil, coolant, and insulation continued to burn until the fire was extinguished on october 12, 2022, at approximately 11:00 am cst. root cause: we have determined that multiple factors caused the event, including faulty and missing check valves and low-pressure braided hoses exposed to high pressure from the vent system. path forward: we have since completed isolating individual ventilation lines from the pre-lube pumps and starters, which will separate high-pressure from low-pressure components. for three days, we also had 20 + people go flange to flange complete a process hazard analysis, confirming all the designs and p&ids are correct and corrected where needed. re-designing skids to remove as many threaded connections as possible. implemented and scheduled replacements of worn items such as braided hoses. instrument and compressor start gas have been converted to air. the new building will be open with no walls for improved ventilation. once the compressor station is commissioned, a supplemental report to this one will be submitted.

NAME: TENNESSEE GAS PIPELINE COMPANY

narrative_clean: on 12/23/2022 at 9:39 am est, station 200 experienced an abnormal operation with the station discharge relief valve (rv) 200-1a. tennessee gas pipeline (tgp) operator that was at the station heard the audible sound of gas release and assessed the event. the relief valve re-seated and sealed after 8 minutes. at 10:30am est tennessee gas pipeline (tgp) initiated the erl call and the event was deemed reportable. the root cause analysis/internal investigation was completed 01/31/2023. in order to prevent reoccurrence, the relief valve manufacturer technician's recommended to tgp to have a 5% separation margin setpoint. in addition, tgp increased the relief valve set points for all three relief valves at the station per the manufacturer's recommendation. the relief valve in question was disassembled, cleaned, and rectified by a vendor's technician and new valve soft parts and controls were installed.

NAME: FRONTIER NATURAL GAS COMPANY
CAUSE_DETAILS: DAMAGE BY OPERATOR OR OPERATOR'S CONTRACTOR NOT RELATED TO EXCAVATION AND NOT DUE TO MOTORIZED VEHICLE/EQUIPMENT DAMAGE
NARRATIVE: WHEN THE AREA WAS EXCAVATED IN 2022 TO REPAIR THE LEAK, IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE PIPING INSTALLED UNDER THE ROAD DID NOT ALIGN WITH ANOTHER SECTION OF PIPE AND A WRINKLE BEND EXISTED BETWEEN THE TWO SECTIONS. RATHER THAN REWORKING THE AREA SO THAT THE PIPES WOULD MORE CLOSELY ALIGN, FRONTIER BELIEVES THAT THE CONTRACTOR WHO INSTALLED THE PIPE IN 1999 USED EQUIPMENT TO MANIPULATE THE LOCATION OF THE PIPE THROUGH PULLING AND/OR PUSHING TO ALIGN THE PIPES SO THAT THEY COULD BE JOINED VIA WELDING. THE SECTION OF PIPE WITH THE WRINKLE BEND IS BELIEVED TO HAVE BEEN INSTALLED WITH A DIRECTIONAL DRILL AS IT IS UNDER A ROAD SO THE CONTRACTOR DID NOT WANT TO OPEN CUT THE ROAD TO CORRECT THE ISSUE. DURING THE PROCESS TO MANIPULATE THE PIPING, THE WRINKLE BEND WAS CREATED WHICH CRACKED THE COATING AND OVER TIME ALLOWED FOR CORROSION TO CREATE A HOLE INSIDE OF THE WRINKLE BEND. FRONTIER HAD A FAILURE TO PINPOINT AND REPAIR THE LEAK IN 2018 WHEN WE DUG WHERE WE WERE INITIALLY GETTING GAS READINGS. WE DID NOT FIND ANYTHING ON THE TRANSMISSION LINE, THEREFORE WE ASSUME THOSE IN CHARGE AT THE TIME THOUGHT IT HAD TO BE ON OUR PLASTIC DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM LOCATED IN THE SAME VICINITY. THIS SHOULD HAVE BEEN MONITORED AND TRACKED AS A LEAK FROM THIS POINT ON, BUT THAT WAS NOT THE CASE. COMPLIANCE TASKS SUCH AS LEAK SURVEY/VALVE MAINTENANCE FOUND THIS LEAK AGAIN BETWEEN THE YEARS OF 2018-2022, BUT IT WAS STILL ASSUMED TO BE ON THE PLASTIC SYSTEM AND WAS NOT PROPERLY WRITTEN UP BY THOSE IN CHARGE AT THE TIME. HIGH GAS READINGS WERE FOUND DURING 2022 LEAK SURVEY, AND THOSE CURRENTLY IN CHARGE IMMEDIATELY PUT PLANS IN PLACE TO DIG WHERE THE GAS READINGS WERE POINTING US TOWARDS. THE PLEDCO WAS USED IN AUGUST 2022 TO STOP THE LEAK WE FOUND IN THE WRINKLE BEND. THE PLEDCO SHOULDN'T HAVE BEEN USED ACCORDING TO MANUFACTURER'S SPECIFICATIONS, WHICH IS A LESSON LEARNED.  THE PLEDCO FAILED IN JANUARY 2023, AND WE CALLED TDW TO STOPPLE TO REPLACE THE PIPE. THE GAS LOST CALCULATION IN THIS REPORT IS AN ESTIMATE OVER THE 5 YEARS WE ARE AWARE OF THAT THE PIPE WAS LEAKING.
narrative_clean: when the area was excavated in 2022 to repair the leak, it was discovered that the piping installed under the road did not align with another section of pipe and a wrinkle bend existed between the two sections. rather than reworking the area so that the pipes would more closely align, frontier believes that the contractor who installed the pipe in 1999 used equipment to manipulate the location of the pipe through pulling and/or pushing to align the pipes so that they could be joined via welding. the section of pipe with the wrinkle bend is believed to have been installed with a directional drill as it is under a road so the contractor did not want to open cut the road to correct the issue. during the process to manipulate the piping, the wrinkle bend was created which cracked the coating and over time allowed for corrosion to create a hole inside of the wrinkle bend. frontier had a failure to pinpoint and repair the leak in 2018 when we dug where we were initially getting gas readings. we did not find anything on the transmission line, therefore we assume those in charge at the time thought it had to be on our plastic distribution system located in the same vicinity. this should have been monitored and tracked as a leak from this point on, but that was not the case. compliance tasks such as leak survey/valve maintenance found this leak again between the years of 2018-2022, but it was still assumed to be on the plastic system and was not properly written up by those in charge at the time. high gas readings were found during 2022 leak survey, and those currently in charge immediately put plans in place to dig where the gas readings were pointing us towards. the pledco was used in august 2022 to stop the leak we found in the wrinkle bend. the pledco shouldn't have been used according to manufacturer's specifications, which is a lesson learned. the pledco failed in january 2023, and we called tdw to stopple to replace the pipe. the gas lost calculation in this report is an estimate over the 5 years we are aware of that the pipe was leaking.

NAME: ANR PIPELINE CO
NARRATIVE: ON FEBRUARY 4, 2023, AN UNINTENTIONAL RELEASE OF 6.7 MILLION CUBIC FEET OF NATURAL GAS OCCURRED WHEN A 2-INCH 2-PIECE, THREADED VALVE PULLED APART, ON THE HIGH-PRESSURE DUMP LINE ON THE WELL HEAD SEPARATOR. A TECHNICIAN WAS NEARBY AT THE TIME OF THE RELEASE. NO INJURIES, NO FATALITIES AND NO DAMAGES WERE REPORTED.      THE ISOLATION PLAN GENERATED FOR THE SECTION REQUIRED LATERAL VALVES TO BE CLOSED AND THE RELEASE WAS ISOLATED WITHIN 78 MINUTES. AFTER THE NATURAL GAS RELEASE, THERE WAS A SMALL RELEASE OF CRUDE OIL THAT IS A BYPRODUCT OF THE STORAGE WELL SYSTEM. A PRIMARY CAUSE OF THE EQUIPMENT FAILURE HAS YET TO BE DETERMINED AS THE INCIDENT IS CURRENTLY UNDER INVESTIGATION.  A SUPPLEMENT REPORT WILL BE FILED UPON THE COMPLETION OF THE INVESTIGATION.       UPDATE 7/3/2023 FAILURE INVESTIGATION FINAL SUMMARY REPORT     THE RESULTS OF THE ANALYSIS INDICATE THAT THE BALL VALVE AND THREADED CONNECTION FAILED DUE TO EXPANSION OF THE FEMALE THREADED SECTION ON THE BALL VALVE, MOST LIKELY AS A RESULT OF WATER FREEZING INSIDE THE VALVE. THE EXPANSION LED TO PARTIAL DISENGAGEMENT OF THE MALE THREADS ON THE THREADED CONNECTION AND THE FEMALE THREADS ON THE VALVE BODY. AN AXIL TENSILE STRESS, LIKELY FROM THE FREEZING WATER ACTING ON THE VALVE AND THREADED CONNECTION RESULTED IN DEFORMATION OF THE OF MALE THREADS FROM THE THREADED CONNECTIONS. WHICH SEPARATED THE VALVE BODY FROM THE MALE THREADED CONNECTION.
narrative_clean: on february 4, 2023, an unintentional release of 6.7 million cubic feet of natural gas occurred when a 2-inch 2-piece, threaded valve pulled apart, on the high-pressure dump line on the well head separator. a technician was nearby at the time of the release. no injuries, no fatalities and no damages were reported. the isolation plan generated for the section required lateral valves to be closed and the release was isolated within 78 minutes. after the natural gas release, there was a small release of crude oil that is a byproduct of the storage well system. a primary cause of the equipment failure has yet to be determined as the incident is currently under investigation. a supplement report will be filed upon the completion of the investigation. update 7/3/2023 failure investigation final summary report the results of the analysis indicate that the ball valve and threaded connection failed due to expansion of the female threaded section on the ball valve, most likely as a result of water freezing inside the valve. the expansion led to partial disengagement of the male threads on the threaded connection and the female threads on the valve body. an axil tensile stress, likely from the freezing water acting on the valve and threaded connection resulted in deformation of the of male threads from the threaded connections. which separated the valve body from the male threaded connection.

NAME: EQUITRANS MIDSTREAM CORPORATION
NARRATIVE: AT 9:41AM, SUNDAY FEBRUARY 5, 2023, GAS CONTROL NOTICED A DECLINE OF 135 PSIG AT RAGER STORAGE ALONG THE SP-7912 PIPELINE. THE NEXT POLL SHOWED ANOTHER 40 PSIG DECREASE. AT 9:45AM, GAS CONTROL SHUT IN ALL FLOW COMING OUT OF RAGER STORAGE. AT 9:51AM, COMPLIANCE-ON CALL RECEIVED A CALL FROM GAS CONTROL SAYING THAT THEY NOTICED A SUDDEN DROP OF PRESSURE ALONG THE SP-7912 PIPELINE AND THAT A TECHNICIAN WAS EN ROUTE. COMPLIANCE SUPERVISION WAS IMMEDIATELY NOTIFIED AFTERWARD. AT 11:13AM, COMPLIANCE WAS NOTIFIED THAT A 2-INCH DUMP VALVE WAS STUCK OPEN AND WAS VENTING TO ATMOSPHERE. AFTER TALKING WITH OPERATIONS, THE FOLLOWING TIMEFRAME WAS ESTABLISHED. AT APPROXIMATELY 9:30AM, THE DUMP VALVE STARTED VENTING GAS. THE LOCAL FIRE DEPARTMENT WAS NOTIFIED AND ARRIVED ON SCENE AT 10:02AM. AT 10:34AM THE FIRE DEPARTMENT NOTED THAT THE VENTING SOUND STOPPED.   OPERATIONS ARRIVED ON SITE AT 11AM. THE DUMP VALVE OPENED INITIALLY BECAUSE THE LIQUID LEVEL CONTROLS REACHED THEIR THRESHOLD, WHICH SENT A SIGNAL TO THE VALVE TO OPEN. IT IS SPECULATED THAT THERE WAS A ROCK OR OTHER DEBRIS CAUGHT IN THE VALVE THAT WAS NOT ALLOWING IT TO CLOSE AFTER REMOVING THE LIQUID. SINCE THE VALVE SHUT BEFORE OPERATIONS ARRIVED ON SITE, THERE IS NO EVIDENCE OF WHAT EXACTLY OCCURRED, BUT OPERATIONS WAS ABLE TO OPEN AND CLOSE THE VALVE WITHOUT ISSUE AFTER THEY ARRIVED ONSITE.
narrative_clean: at 9:41am, sunday february 5, 2023, gas control noticed a decline of 135 psig at rager storage along the sp-7912 pipeline. the next poll showed another 40 psig decrease. at 9:45am, gas control shut in all flow coming out of rager storage. at 9:51am, compliance-on call received a call from gas control saying that they noticed a sudden drop of pressure along the sp-7912 pipeline and that a technician was en route. compliance supervision was immediately notified afterward. at 11:13am, compliance was notified that a 2-inch dump valve was stuck open and was venting to atmosphere. after talking with operations, the following timeframe was established. at approximately 9:30am, the dump valve started venting gas. the local fire department was notified and arrived on scene at 10:02am. at 10:34am the fire department noted that the venting sound stopped. operations arrived on site at 11am. the dump valve opened initially because the liquid level controls reached their threshold, which sent a signal to the valve to open. it is speculated that there was a rock or other debris caught in the valve that was not allowing it to close after removing the liquid. since the valve shut before operations arrived on site, there is no evidence of what exactly occurred, but operations was able to open and close the valve without issue after they arrived onsite.

NAME: ANR PIPELINE CO
NARRATIVE: ON FEBRUARY 1, 2023 A SEVERE COLD WEATHER STORM WITH HEAVY RAIN AND SNOW MIX PASSED THROUGH THE BROWNSVILLE, TN AREA. AT 02:50 CT, A MEMBER OF THE GENERAL PUBLIC AND LOCAL LANDOWNER HEARD GAS VENTING FROM BROWNSVILLE COMPRESSOR STATION YARD AND MADE A CALL TO 811, WHICH WAS DISPATCHED TO THE CALL TO TC ENERGY GAS CONTROL CENTER. IN RESPONSE, A TECHNICIAN WAS DEPLOYED TO THE COMPRESSOR STATION TO INVESTIGATE THE REPORTED EVENT.     UPON ARRIVAL AT THE SITE AT 04:35 CT, THE TECHNICIAN FOUND THAT THE REGULATOR ON VALVE 501-33-J HAD FROZEN, RESULTING IN AN OPEN VALVE RELEASING GAS TO ATMOSPHERE AND MANUALLY CLOSED THE OPEN VALVE. VALVE 501-33-J IS A BLOWOFF VALVE ASSOCIATED WITH THE EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN (ESD) SYSTEM.     FOLLOWING THE EVENT, STATION TECHNICIANS INSPECTED THE VALVE, POWER/PILOT GAS LINES, REGULATOR COMPONENTS, LINES, FITTINGS AND MECHANICAL FUNCTIONALITY. IT WAS DETERMINED THAT ICE FORMATION FOUND INSIDE THE REGULATOR BODY AND SPRING COMPONENTS CAUSED THE REGULATOR TO FAIL TO OPERATE AND RESULTED IN A PARTIALLY CLOSED ESD VALVE. THE VALVE REGULATOR IS EQUIPPED WITH SPARE VALVE DISK REVERSAL CAPABILITIES, AND THE SPRING-LOADED DISK WAS REPLACED AND REGULATOR PLACED BACK INTO NORMAL OPERATION ON FEBRUARY 1, 2023.
narrative_clean: on february 1, 2023 a severe cold weather storm with heavy rain and snow mix passed through the brownsville, tn area. at 02:50 ct, a member of the general public and local landowner heard gas venting from brownsville compressor station yard and made a call to 811, which was dispatched to the call to tc energy gas control center. in response, a technician was deployed to the compressor station to investigate the reported event. upon arrival at the site at 04:35 ct, the technician found that the regulator on valve 501-33-j had frozen, resulting in an open valve releasing gas to atmosphere and manually closed the open valve. valve 501-33-j is a blowoff valve associated with the emergency shutdown (esd) system. following the event, station technicians inspected the valve, power/pilot gas lines, regulator components, lines, fittings and mechanical functionality. it was determined that ice formation found inside the regulator body and spring components caused the regulator to fail to operate and resulted in a partially closed esd valve. the valve regulator is equipped with spare valve disk reversal capabilities, and the spring-loaded disk was replaced and regulator placed back into normal operation on february 1, 2023.

NAME: EL PASO NATURAL GAS CO
NARRATIVE: AT 10:09AM MST ON FEBRUARY 5, 2023, A FAULTY HAZARDOUS GAS DETECTOR IN THE CONTROL ROOM OF EL PASO NATURAL GAS (EPNG) EUNICE B COMPRESSOR STATION CAUSED THE COMPRESSOR STATION TO UNDERGO AN EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN (ESD). DURING THE SHUTDOWN, SUCTION VALVE VB1 DID NOT CLOSE FULLY CAUSING GAS TO CONTINUE TO VENT. THIS LED TO A RELEASE OF 5,459 MCF GAS RELEASE. NAME: ENERGY TRANSFER COMPANY
NARRATIVE: ON MARCH 3, 2023 AT APPROXIMATELY 14:52, A NATURAL GAS RELEASE OCCURRED AT THE 20150013 ATHLON DISCHARGE 12-INCH PIG LAUNCHER SITE LOCATED 23 MILES SOUTHEAST OF ODESSA, TX IN MIDLAND COUNTY.    WHILE PREPARING TO LAUNCH A CLEANING PIG, THE OPERATOR MOVED ALL VALVES INVOLVED TO THEIR PROPER POSITIONS AS PER SOP. THE OPERATOR VISUALLY AND AUDIBLY WITNESSED THE PIG TRAP BLOW DOWN. ONCE THE PIG TRAP WAS COMPLETELY BLOWN DOWN THE OPERATOR BEGAN TO OPEN THE PIG TRAP DOOR AS PER SOP. THE OPERATOR WALKED AWAY FROM THE PIG TRAP DOOR TO RETRIEVE THE CLEANING PIG FROM HIS TRUCK AND HEARD A HISSING SOUND COMING FROM THE PIG TRAP. THE HISSING SOUND WAS GROWING LOUDER AND THE OPERATOR REMOVED HIMSELF FROM THE AREA TO BE SAFE. THAT IS WHEN THE GAS PRESSURE CAUSED THE PIG TRAP DOOR TO OPEN CAUSING THE RELEASE OF GAS FROM THE 16-INCH PIG TRAP DOOR.     AT APPROXIMATELY 16:35, IT WAS CALCULATED AND CONFIRMED THAT THE UNINTENTIONAL GAS LOSS WAS AT 3.69 MMCF, WHICH EXCEEDED THE 3 MMCF REPORTING CRITERIA AND THE NRC WAS NOTIFIED AT 16:49.    THE BETTIS ACTUATOR AND VERSE VALVE WERE REMOVED AND SENT FOR INSPECTION AND REPAIRS.      A NEW MANUAL GEAR OPERATOR WAS INSTALLED AND AT 14:00 ON 04MAR THE PIPELINE WAS PUT BACK INTO SERVICE.    **JUNE 1, 2023, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE 1-INCH MAIN LINE SUPPLY GAS BALL VALVE WAS LEAKING BY AND LIKELY RE-SUPPLIED THE ACTUATOR ASSEMBLY WITH ENOUGH PRESSURE TO ACTUATE THE VALVE OPEN ALLOWING GAS TO RE-ENTER THE PIG LAUNCHING BARREL THUS CAUSING THE UNINTENTIONAL GAS RELEASE.    THE LEAKING 1-INCH BALL VALVE WAS REPLACED WITH A NEW ONE.      THIS WAS AN ISOLATED INCIDENT AND TO PREVENT THIS FROM OCCURRING IN THE FUTURE AND THIS SITE, THE ACTUATORS WERE REMOVED AND REPLACED WITH MANUAL GEAR OPERATORS.     THE SITE SPECIFIC PIGGING PROCEDURES HAVE BEEN UPDATED TO INCLUDE AREAS WITH ACTUATORS TO LOCK OUT THE SUPPLY SOURCE BLOWDOWN VALVE IN THE OPEN POSITION IN CASE THERE IS A LEAKING VALVE AND TO PREVENT GAS FROM RE-ENTERING THE PIG LAUNCHER BARREL.
narrative_clean: on march 3, 2023 at approximately 14:52, a natural gas release occurred at the 20150013 athlon discharge 12-inch pig launcher site located 23 miles southeast of odessa, tx in midland county. while preparing to launch a cleaning pig, the operator moved all valves involved to their proper positions as per sop. the operator visually and audibly witnessed the pig trap blow down. once the pig trap was completely blown down the operator began to open the pig trap door as per sop. the operator walked away from the pig trap door to retrieve the cleaning pig from his truck and heard a hissing sound coming from the pig trap. the hissing sound was growing louder and the operator removed himself from the area to be safe. that is when the gas pressure caused the pig trap door to open causing the release of gas from the 16-inch pig trap door. at approximately 16:35, it was calculated and confirmed that the unintentional gas loss was at 3.69 mmcf, which exceeded the 3 mmcf reporting criteria and the nrc was notified at 16:49. the bettis actuator and verse valve were removed and sent for inspection and repairs. a new manual gear operator was installed and at 14:00 on 04mar the pipeline was put back into service. **june 1, 2023, it was determined that the 1-inch main line supply gas ball valve was leaking by and likely re-supplied the actuator assembly with enough pressure to actuate the valve open allowing gas to re-enter the pig launching barrel thus causing the unintentional gas release. the leaking 1-inch ball valve was replaced with a new one. this was an isolated incident and to prevent this from occurring in the future and this site, the actuators were removed and replaced with manual gear operators. the site specific pigging procedures have been updated to include areas with actuators to lock out the supply source blowdown valve in the open position in case there is a leaking valve and to prevent gas from re-entering the pig launcher barrel.

NAME: TRANSCONTINENTAL GAS PIPE LINE COMPANY
CAUSE: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD
NARRATIVE: ON 3/8/2023 WILLIAMS PIPELINE CONTROL WAS NOTIFIED BY A LANDOWNER OF A GAS SMELL NEAR HIS PROPERTY IN THE AREA OF A WILLIAMS PIPELINE. TECHNICIANS RESPONDED TO THE AREA AND BEGAN INVESTIGATING TO DETERMINE THE SOURCE OF THE SMELL. TECHNICIANS UTILIZED AN INFRARED LEAK DETECTION TOOL AND CONFIRMED A LEAK FROM THE PIPELINE. ONCE CONFIRMED THE PIPELINE WAS ISOLATED USING BLOCK VALVES AND THE GAS WAS EVACUATED FROM THE PIPE. AFTER GAS WAS REMOVED FROM THE SYSTEM AND THE LEAK WAS STOPPED, THE PIPELINE WAS EXCAVATED AND THE SOURCE OF THE LEAK WAS DETERMINED TO BE A CRACK ON MAINLINE B.     IN-FIELD HARDNESS WAS PERFORMED AT THE CRACK LOCATION TO CONFIRM A HARD SPOT DEFECT WAS PRESENT AT THE LOCATION OF THE CRACK. THE HARD SPOT MEASURED 364 BHN X 6.5" LONG X 6" WIDE.     ON OCTOBER 7, 2021 WILLIAMS CONTRACTED ROSEN TO INSPECT MAINLINE B (MLV 180B10 TO MLV 185B5) WITH THEIR HARD SPOT ILI (DMG) TECHNOLOGY TO ASSESS FOR THE HARD SPOT THREAT. THERE WERE A TOTAL OF 6 HARD SPOT ANOMALIES REPORTED BY ROSEN AND 4 OF THOSE 6 HARD SPOT FEATURES WERE EXCAVATED/EVALUATED FOR VERIFICATION. THE HARDNESS VALUES CONFIRMED FROM THESE 4 FEATURES RANGED FROM 192-208 BHN, WHICH WAS SLIGHTLY HARDER THAN BASE HARDNESS (~170-180 BHN). ALL 4 FEATURES WERE RECOATED PER WILLIAMS REPAIR PROCEDURE. THE HARD SPOT DEFECT THAT CRACKED (AND LEAKED) AT MP 1558.66 WAS NOT REPORTED BY ROSEN FROM THEIR 2021 HARD SPOT ILI. RE-ANALYSIS IS ONGOING WITH ROSEN BASED ON THE HARD SPOT DEFECT FOUND. LAB TESTING ON HARD SPOT WITH CRACK NOT YET COMPLETED AS PIPE WAS SENT TO TDW FOR PULL TESTING WITH THEIR HARD SPOT ILI TOOL TO VERIFY CAPABILITIES. WE HAVE NOT CONFIRMED HYDROGEN STRESS CRACKING.
narrative_clean: on 3/8/2023 williams pipeline control was notified by a landowner of a gas smell near his property in the area of a williams pipeline. technicians responded to the area and began investigating to determine the source of the smell. technicians utilized an infrared leak detection tool and confirmed a leak from the pipeline. once confirmed the pipeline was isolated using block valves and the gas was evacuated from the pipe. after gas was removed from the system and the leak was stopped, the pipeline was excavated and the source of the leak was determined to be a crack on mainline b. in-field hardness was performed at the crack location to confirm a hard spot defect was present at the location of the crack. the hard spot measured 364 bhn x 6.5" long x 6" wide. on october 7, 2021 williams contracted rosen to inspect mainline b (mlv 180b10 to mlv 185b5) with their hard spot ili (dmg) technology to assess for the hard spot threat. there were a total of 6 hard spot anomalies reported by rosen and 4 of those 6 hard spot features were excavated/evaluated for verification. the hardness values confirmed from these 4 features ranged from 192-208 bhn, which was slightly harder than base hardness (~170-180 bhn). all 4 features were recoated per williams repair procedure. the hard spot defect that cracked (and leaked) at mp 1558.66 was not reported by rosen from their 2021 hard spot ili. re-analysis is ongoing with rosen based on the hard spot defect found. lab testing on hard spot with crack not yet completed as pipe was sent to tdw for pull testing with their hard spot ili tool to verify capabilities. we have not confirmed hydrogen stress cracking.

NAME: TARGA NORTHERN DELAWARE LLC

NAME: MIDCONTINENT EXPRESS PIPELINE LLC
NARRATIVE: ON 06/27/2023 AT 12:00 PM, MIDCONTINENT EXPRESS PIPELINE (MEP) HAD A REPORTABLE GAS RELEASE THAT OCCURRED AT THE MEP 2 COMPRESSOR STATION WHEN THE ESD SYSTEM WAS ACTIVATED AND THE DISCHARGE SIDE OF THE ESD SYSTEM DID NOT OPERATE AS DESIGNED. THE ESD WAS ACTIVATED AS A RESULT OF LOSS OF UPS POWER SUPPLY. THE USE OF THE UPS POWER WAS INITIATED BY A TRIPPED ELECTRICAL BREAKER THAT WAS CAUSED BY AN ELECTRICALLY SHORTED AIR COMPRESSOR.      THE ESD BLOCK VALVE THAT IS HELD CLOSED BY AN ENERGIZED SOLENOID, WHEN SUPPLIED BY COMMERCIAL OR UPS POWER. WHEN UPS BATTERIES WERE DRAINED, THE STATION LOST CONTROL POWER TO THE STATION COMPUTERS, PLCS AND UNIT HMIS. THE LOSS OF COMMERCIAL POWER DUE TO TRIPPED BREAKER AND THE LOSS OF UPS POWER ALLOWED THE ESD VALVE TO OPEN CAUSING THE STATION TO BLOWDOWN THROUGH A FULLY PNEUMATIC SYSTEM.    WHEN RESPONSE PERSONNEL ARRIVED THEY FOUND THE STATION DISCHARGE SIDE GATE AND DISCHARGE BLOWDOWN VENT VALVE IN AN OPEN POSITION WHICH LED TO THE 50,086.93 MCF RELEASE OF NATURAL GAS.  THE ESD SYSTEM BY DESIGN  HAS AN INTERLOCK PROCESS SO THAT THE BLOWDOWN VALVES WILL NOT OPEN UNLESS THE ASSOCIATED STATION SIDE GATE VALVES CLOSE. THIS IS ACCOMPLISHED THROUGH A SERIES OF TRIGGER VALVES.  THE SUCTION SIDE OF THE STATION WORKED AS DESIGNED DURING THE ESD.  HOWEVER, THE DISCHARGE SIDE EXPERIENCED FAILURES IN TWO SHAFER TRIGGER VALVES WHICH ALLOWED THE BLOWDOWN VENT VALVE TO OPEN WITH THE DISCHARGE SIDE GATE OPEN.  THE INVESTIGATION FOUND EXCESSIVE CORROSION/RUST WITHIN THE INTERNAL WORKINGS OF THE TWO SHAFER VALVES. THE SHAFER TRIGGER VALVES WERE REPLACED, THE TRIPPED BREAKER WAS RESET, THE SHORTED AIR COMPRESSOR WAS REMOVED FROM SERVICE UNTIL THE MOTOR WAS REPLACED, THE DISCHARGE SIDE GATE AND EDS DISCHARGE BLOWDOWN VALVE WERE RETURN TO THEIR NORMAL STATE AND THE STATION WAS PLACED BACK ONLINE.
narrative_clean: on 06/27/2023 at 12:00 pm, midcontinent express pipeline (mep) had a reportable gas release that occurred at the mep 2 compressor station when the esd system was activated and the discharge side of the esd system did not operate as designed. the esd was activated as a result of loss of ups power supply. the use of the ups power was initiated by a tripped electrical breaker that was caused by an electrically shorted air compressor. the esd block valve that is held closed by an energized solenoid, when supplied by commercial or ups power. when ups batteries were drained, the station lost control power to the station computers, plcs and unit hmis. the loss of commercial power due to tripped breaker and the loss of ups power allowed the esd valve to open causing the station to blowdown through a fully pneumatic system. when response personnel arrived they found the station discharge side gate and discharge blowdown vent valve in an open position which led to the 50,086.93 mcf release of natural gas. the esd system by design has an interlock process so that the blowdown valves will not open unless the associated station side gate valves close. this is accomplished through a series of trigger valves. the suction side of the station worked as designed during the esd. however, the discharge side experienced failures in two shafer trigger valves which allowed the blowdown vent valve to open with the discharge side gate open. the investigation found excessive corrosion/rust within the internal workings of the two shafer valves. the shafer trigger valves were replaced, the tripped breaker was reset, the shorted air compressor was removed from service until the motor was replaced, the discharge side gate and eds discharge blowdown valve were return to their normal state and the station was placed back online.

NAME: NORTHERN NATURAL GAS CO

NARRATIVE: ON JULY 10, 2023, A WELDER WAS WELDING A LINE-STOP FITTING ON NORTHERN NATURAL GAS COMPANY'S WIB14801 LADYSMITH BRANCH LINE AT MILEPOST 1.15 TO ACCOMMODATE A NEW PIPELINE SEGMENT TIE-IN. AT 1100 HOURS, THE WELDER BEGAN WELDING THE "BUTTER TEMPER BEAD PASS" REQUIRED PRIOR TO WELDING THE LINE-STOP FITTING TO THE PIPELINE. SEVEN MINUTES LATER, THE WELDER BURNED THROUGH THE PIPELINE, CREATING A 1/16-INCH HOLE. WHEN THE LEAK STARTED, ALL PARTIES EXITED THE BELL HOLE AND STOPPED ALL IGNITION SOURCES.    THE BEST LOCATION FOR THE LINE STOP FITTING WAS FOUND TO BE 0.150" WALL THICKNESS. THIS IS WHERE THE BURN THROUGH OCCURRED.    THE INCIDENT'S ROOT CAUSE WAS THE WELDER DID NOT FOLLOW THE PROCEDURE FOR WELDING ON THIN-WALL PIPE WHILE IN-SERVICE. THE WELDER WAS OUT OF POSITION AND DID NOT HAVE THE MINIMUM EXPERIENCE NORTHERN REQUIRES TO COMPLETE THIS CHALLENGING WELDING PROCESS.    ON JULY 16, 2023, AT 14:50 THE PROJECT WAS COMPLETED, AND THE LADYSMITH BRANCH LINE WAS RETURNED TO NORMAL SERVICE.
narrative_clean: on july 10, 2023, a welder was welding a line-stop fitting on northern natural gas company's wib14801 ladysmith branch line at milepost 1.15 to accommodate a new pipeline segment tie-in. at 1100 hours, the welder began welding the "butter temper bead pass" required prior to welding the line-stop fitting to the pipeline. seven minutes later, the welder burned through the pipeline, creating a 1/16-inch hole. when the leak started, all parties exited the bell hole and stopped all ignition sources. the best location for the line stop fitting was found to be 0.150" wall thickness. this is where the burn through occurred. the incident's root cause was the welder did not follow the procedure for welding on thin-wall pipe while in-service. the welder was out of position and did not have the minimum experience northern requires to complete this challenging welding process. on july 16, 2023, at 14:50 the project was completed, and the ladysmith branch line was returned to normal service.

NAME: KINDER MORGAN TEXAS PIPELINE CO
NARRATIVE: ON JULY 27TH KMTP WAS CURRENTLY CONSTRUCTING A TIE IN ONTO THE PERMIAN HIGHWAY PIPELINE. IN ORDER TO TIE-IN THE NEWLY CONSTRUCTED LINE, KMTP ELECTED TO USE A LINE STOP TO KEEP THE GAS FLOWING IN THE MAINLINE WHILE TYING IN THE NEW LINE. WHILE OPERATORS WERE ALREADY ON SITE, THEY DISCOVERED THAT THE GASKET ON THE LINE STOP HAD FAILED AT 7:20 PM. AN EMERGENCY RESPONSE CALL WAS HELD AT 8:00 PM, AND IT WAS DETERMINED THAT KMTP WOULD REPORT THE INCIDENT OUT OF AN ABUNDANCE OF CAUTION SINCE THE RELEASE VOLUME AND REPAIR COSTS WERE UNKNOWN. IT WAS LATER DETERMINED THAT THE RELEASE VOLUME DID NOT EXCEED THE 3000 MCF THRESHOLD UNTIL 8:37 PM. KMTP ISOLATED AND SHUT DOWN THE LINE AT 9:15 PM AND SUBSEQUENTLY PROCEEDED TO BLOW DOWN 12 MILES OF PIPE. APPLICABLE REPAIRS WERE MADE, AND THE LINE WAS BACK IN SERVICE ON JULY 31ST AT 1:00 PM. KMTP'S INCIDENT INVESTIGATION DETERMINED THAT THE DOUBLE POSITION BYPASS BISEP OPERATION PROCEDURE'S TORQUING SAFETY FACTOR WAS INSUFFICIENT, AND IT LACKED DETAILS REGARDING THE APPLICATION OF MOLY LUBRICANT TO BOLTS AND NUTS PRIOR TO THE TORQUING PROCESS. THESE FINDINGS WERE   VALIDATED WHEN ADDITIONAL PROJECTS WERE CONDUCTED WITH THE REVISED PROCEDURES CHANGES LISTED BELOW AND NO REOCCURRENCES WERE FOUND. KMTP'S INVESTIGATION AND THESE PROCEDURE IMPROVEMENTS LED KMTP TO CONCLUDE THAT THIS INCIDENT WAS CAUSED BY AN INADEQUATE PROCEDURE. TO MINIMIZE THE REOCCURRENCE OF THIS INCIDENT, THE FOLLOWING PROCEDURE IMPROVEMENTS WERE IMPLEMENTED.   -IMPROVED CONTROLS OVER BOLT TORQUING (PARTICULARLY FITTING TO SLAB VALVE) INCLUDING:          O DOCUMENTED PROCEDURE REVIEW          O      RECORDING PUMP PRESSURES & CALCULATING TORQUE VALUES, INCLUDING ON SITE SIGN OFF.          O MOLY LUBRICANT AS REQUIRED AND RECOMMENDED UNDER ASME PCC-1-2022          O FULL DOCUMENTATION AND OVERSIGHT  -USE SPIRAL WOUND GASKET WITH INNER RING ON ALL FLANGED CONNECTIONS.  -INCREASED TORQUE TO 50% OF YIELD IN ACCORDANCE WITH GASKET PARAMETERS AND PRESSURE REQUIREMENTS.
narrative_clean: on july 27th kmtp was currently constructing a tie in onto the permian highway pipeline. in order to tie-in the newly constructed line, kmtp elected to use a line stop to keep the gas flowing in the mainline while tying in the new line. while operators were already on site, they discovered that the gasket on the line stop had failed at 7:20 pm. an emergency response call was held at 8:00 pm, and it was determined that kmtp would report the incident out of an abundance of caution since the release volume and repair costs were unknown. it was later determined that the release volume did not exceed the 3000 mcf threshold until 8:37 pm. kmtp isolated and shut down the line at 9:15 pm and subsequently proceeded to blow down 12 miles of pipe. applicable repairs were made, and the line was back in service on july 31st at 1:00 pm. kmtp's incident investigation determined that the double position bypass bisep operation procedure's torquing safety factor was insufficient, and it lacked details regarding the application of moly lubricant to bolts and nuts prior to the torquing process. these findings were validated when additional projects were conducted with the revised procedures changes listed below and no reoccurrences were found. kmtp's investigation and these procedure improvements led kmtp to conclude that this incident was caused by an inadequate procedure. to minimize the reoccurrence of this incident, the following procedure improvements were implemented. -improved controls over bolt torquing (particularly fitting to slab valve) including: o documented procedure review o recording pump pressures & calculating torque values, including on site sign off. o moly lubricant as required and recommended under asme pcc-1-2022 o full documentation and oversight -use spiral wound gasket with inner ring on all flanged connections. -increased torque to 50% of yield in accordance with gasket parameters and pressure requirements.

NAME: TENNESSEE GAS PIPELINE COMPANY
NARRATIVE: ON OCTOBER 5, 2023 AT 06:58 (EST), STATION 267 IN HOPKINTON, MA EXPERIENCED AN ESD EVENT. THE INITIAL NOTIFICATION WAS RECEIVED VIA SCADA ALARMS. GAS CONTROL PERSONNEL NOTIFIED TGP OPERATIONS PERSONNEL WHO WERE IN ROUTE TO THE STATION FOR DAILY ACTIVITIES. TGP OPERATIONS PERSONNEL ARRIVED ONSITE AT 07:11 (EST). THE HOPKINTON FIRE DEPARTMENT HAD BEEN NOTIFIED BY A THIRD-PARTY AND ARRIVED ONSITE AT 07:18 (EST).  ONCE TGP OPERATIONS PERSONNEL ARRIVED ONSITE, THEY OBSERVED THAT STATION 267 WAS VENTING, BUT THE COMPRESSOR STATION WAS NOT FULLY ISOLATED FROM THE MAINLINE. DURING A STATION WALKTHROUGH BY OPERATIONS PERSONNEL, IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE COMPRESSOR STATION SIDE GATE VALVES WERE PARTIALLY OPEN. THUS GAS FROM THE MAINLINE WAS VENTING THROUGH THE STATION. AT 7:38 (EST), TGP OPERATIONS PERSONNEL CLOSED THE COMPRESSOR STATION BLOWOFF VALVES TO STOP VENTING OF THE GAS. AT 3:00 (EST), STATION 267 WAS CONFIRMED TO BE ISOLATED FROM THE MAINLINE. SINCE THIS EVENT, STATION 267 HAS REMAINED ISOLATED.   FOLLOWING THE INTERNAL INVESTIGATION, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT A POWER FAULT IN THE AREA RESULTED IN THE FAILURE OF THE STATION PLC. THE PLC FAILURE ACTIVATED THE BUILDING PROTECTION SYSTEM, TRIGGERING THE ESD. DUE TO THE ESD COMMAND, THE COMPRESSOR STATION VENT VALVES WERE OPENED TO BLOW DOWN THE UNITS. HOWEVER, THE COMPRESSOR SIDE GATE VALVES FAILED TO PROPERLY CLOSE AND ISOLATE THE STATION. THE GAS LOSS DUE TO THIS EVENT WAS CALCULATED TO BE 8664 MCF.  IN ORDER TO PREVENT REOCCURRENCE, NEW PLCS HAVE BEEN ORDERED AND WILL BE INSTALLED. ADDITIONALLY, ALL OF THE COMPRESSOR STATION SIDE GATE VALVES HAVE BEEN EVALUATED TO ENSURE CORRECT FUNCTIONALITY.  AS AN ADDED PRECAUTION, OPERATIONS HAS DEVELOPED A PROCEDURE FOR ISOLATING THE STATION FROM THE MAINLINE DURING EXTENDED PERIODS WHEN THE STATION IS NOT IN DEMAND.  THE ACTION ITEMS ABOVE ARE INTENDED TO REDUCE THE POTENTIAL FOR REOCCURRENCE OF THIS EVENT.
narrative_clean: on october 5, 2023 at 06:58 (est), station 267 in hopkinton, ma experienced an esd event. the initial notification was received via scada alarms. gas control personnel notified tgp operations personnel who were in route to the station for daily activities. tgp operations personnel arrived onsite at 07:11 (est). the hopkinton fire department had been notified by a third-party and arrived onsite at 07:18 (est). once tgp operations personnel arrived onsite, they observed that station 267 was venting, but the compressor station was not fully isolated from the mainline. during a station walkthrough by operations personnel, it was discovered that the compressor station side gate valves were partially open. thus gas from the mainline was venting through the station. at 7:38 (est), tgp operations personnel closed the compressor station blowoff valves to stop venting of the gas. at 3:00 (est), station 267 was confirmed to be isolated from the mainline. since this event, station 267 has remained isolated. following the internal investigation, it was determined that a power fault in the area resulted in the failure of the station plc. the plc failure activated the building protection system, triggering the esd. due to the esd command, the compressor station vent valves were opened to blow down the units. however, the compressor side gate valves failed to properly close and isolate the station. the gas loss due to this event was calculated to be 8664 mcf. in order to prevent reoccurrence, new plcs have been ordered and will be installed. additionally, all of the compressor station side gate valves have been evaluated to ensure correct functionality. as an added precaution, operations has developed a procedure for isolating the station from the mainline during extended periods when the station is not in demand. the action items above are intended to reduce the potential for reoccurrence of this event.

NARRATIVE: ON NOVEMBER 27, 2023 AT 11:07 (CST), STATION 527 IN PORT SULPHUR, LA EXPERIENCED AN EMERGENCY SHUT DOWN (ESD) EVENT. THE INITIAL NOTIFICATION WAS COMPLETED BY LOCAL TGP OPERATIONS PERSONNEL WHO WERE ONSITE AT THE TIME OF THE EVENT. UPON STATION WALKTHROUGH, IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE STATION BLOCK VALVE WAS NOT FULLY CLOSED, ALLOWING FOR VENTING OF GAS THROUGH THE BLOW-DOWN VALVE. NARRATIVE: AT 6:50AM ON DECEMBER 26TH, AN OFF-SITE EMPLOYEE RECEIVED A CALLOUT FROM THE AUTOMATED SYSTEM FOR AN EQUIPMENT FAILURE ALARM. AT 7:02AM, WHILE THE EMPLOYEE WAS RESPONDING TO THE ALARM, HE RECEIVED A CALL FROM GAS CONTROL. GAS CONTROL INFORMED THE EMPLOYEE OF A PERCENT CHANGE ALARM ON THE #3-LINE SUCTION PRESSURE TRANSMITTER. SEPARATE OPERATOR RESOURCES ARRIVED AT THE STATION AND DISCOVERED THAT THE STATION WAS VENTING GAS THROUGH BOTH SUCTION BLOWDOWN VALVES. THE #3 SUCTION SIDE GATE VALVE WAS OPEN AND ALLOWED GAS TO VENT. AT 7:55AM, THE #3 SUCTION SIDE GATE VALVE WAS CLOSED MANUALLY BY THE EMPLOYEE AND THE STATION COMPLETED THE BLOW DOWN PROCESS. INVESTIGATION DETERMINED THAT THE ROBERTSHAW RELAY, WHICH KEEPS THE 1-INCH ESD BLOCK VALVE IN THE CLOSED POSITION, WAS FAULTY. THIS ALLOWED THE 1-INCH ESD BLOCK VALVE TO LEAK THROUGH THE VENT AND CAUSED THE VALVE TO PARTIALLY OPEN AND PRESSURE UP THE ESD SUPPLY GAS SYSTEM, THUS TRIGGERING A STATION ESD. ADDITIONALLY, MOISTURE HAD ACCUMULATED IN THE ESD SENSING LINES (NORMALLY DEPRESSURIZED) AND SHAFER TRIGGER VALVE THAT SENDS A CLOSE SIGNAL TO THE ESD SUCTION SIDE GATE VALVE. THE MOISTURE FROZE DURING THE COLD AMBIENT TEMPERATURES EXPERIENCED AT NGPL 305 ON THE MORNING OF 12/26/2023. THE PRESENCE OF ICE IN THE ESD SENSING LINES PREVENTED THE #3 SUCTION SIDE GATE VALVE FROM CLOSING AS DESIGNED. NGPL REPLACED THE ROBERTSHAW RELAY AND USED NITROGEN TO BLOW OUT ANY WATER IN THE ESD SYSTEM. THE ESD SYSTEM WAS PRESSURED UP AND SUCCESSFULLY CHECKED FOR LEAKS.

NAME: NORTHERN NATURAL GAS CO
NARRATIVE: ON DECEMBER 07, 2023, A FIELD TECHNICIAN IDENTIFIED AN AREA APPROXIMATELY 75 FEET IN DIAMETER OF STUNTED GROWTH IN A WHEAT FIELD ON THE 20-INCH-DIAMETER M730A SUBLETTE-TO-FOWLER A-LINE AT MP 06.10.  THE FIELD TECHNICIAN COMPLETED A LEAK INVESTIGATION UTILIZING A SOUTHERN CROSS 46 HAWK LASER DIODE METHANE LEAK DETECTOR AND CONFIRMED THERE WAS A LEAK PRESENT.  THE LEAK DETECTOR REGISTERED 380 PPM AT THE LOCATION. REPAIR EFFORTS WERE DELAYED SEVERAL WEEKS DUE TO INCLEMENT WEATHER FROM HEAVY RAIN, SNOWSTORMS, AND BLIZZARD CONDITIONS MOVING THROUGH THE AREA, LIMITING ACCESS TO THE SITE.     INITIAL EXCAVATION BEGAN ON JANUARY 2, 2024. FIVE FEET OF THE M730A LINE WAS EXPOSED WHERE THE LEAK WAS THOUGHT TO HAVE ORIGINATED. AFTER INVESTIGATING THE EXPOSED AREA, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE LEAK WAS NOT IN THIS AREA. FIELD OPERATIONS BEGAN PROBING THE AREA WEST AND EAST OF THE EXPOSED PORTION OF THE LINE TO INVESTIGATE FURTHER. BOTH AREAS THAT WERE PROBED AND BAR-HOLE TESTED WITH THE 46 HAWK LEAK DETECTOR. ON THE EAST SIDE OF THE EXCAVATION THE READING WAS 8% GAS WHILE THE WEST SIDE READING WAS 14% GAS. THE READINGS WERE ABOVE THE PERMISSIBLE 10% LEL LIMIT FOR OPERATION OF THE TRACK HOE IN THIS AREA. A SAFETY STAND DOWN WAS INITIATED AND IT WAS DETERMINED THAT IT WAS NOT SAFE TO PROCEED WITH THE EXISTING CONDITIONS. FIELD OPERATIONS WORKED WITH FACILITY PLANNING TO DEVELOP A PLAN TO LOWER THE OPERATION PRESSURE OF THE M730A TO AS LOW AS 50 PSIG IN ORDER TO SLOW THE LEAK AS WELL AS KEEP FARM TAP CUSTOMERS IN SERVICE.     ON JANUARY 5, 2024, THE DECISION WAS MADE TO HIRE A CONTRACTOR TO ASSIST WITH ACCESSING THE SITE AND REPAIR THE LEAK. THE INITIAL ESTIMATE FOR MATTING THE ROUTE INTO THE LEAK SITE EXCEEDED THE PROPERTY DAMAGE THRESHOLD OF A REPORTABLE INCIDENT, SO THE LEAK WAS REPORTED TO THE NRC.     ON JANUARY 16, 2024, THE LINE PRESSURE HAD REACHED 174 PSIG AND THE SITE COULD BE SAFELY ACCESSED BY EQUIPMENT AND WELDING RIGS. EXCAVATION BEGAN ON THE LEAK SITE. A DRESSER COUPLING WAS FOUND TO BE LEAKING. REPAIRS WERE COMPLETED ON JANUARY 18, 2024, BY WELDING A STYLE 220 PUMPKIN SLEEVE OVER THE LEAKING COUPLING.     BACKFILL AND TOPSOIL RESTORATION WAS COMPLETED ON JANUARY 23, 2024. SUBSEQUENT GAS MONITORING DETECTED NO FURTHER LEAKS, AND A GAS SURVEY EXTENDING 500 FEET UPSTREAM AND DOWNSTREAM OF THE EXCAVATIONS REVEALED NO ADDITIONAL LEAKS.

registered 380 ppm at the location. repair efforts were delayed several weeks due to inclement weather from heavy rain, snowstorms, and blizzard conditions moving through the area, limiting access to the site. initial excavation began on january 2, 2024. five feet of the m730a line was exposed where the leak was thought to have originated. after investigating the exposed area, it was determined with the 46 hawk leak detector. on the east side of the excavation the reading was 8% gas while the west side reading was 14% gas. the readings were above the permissible 10% lel limit for operation of the track hoe in this area. a safety stand down was initiated and it was determined that it was not safe to proceed with the existing conditions. field operations worked with facility planning to develop a plan to lower the operation pressure of the m730a to as low as 50 psig in order to slow the leak as well as keep farm tap customers in service. on january 5, 2024, the decision was made to on january 23, 2024. subsequent gas monitoring detected no further leaks, and a gas survey extending 500 feet upstream and downstream of the excavations revealed no additional leaks.

NAME: COLUMBIA GULF TRANSMISSION, LLC
NARRATIVE: ON JANUARY 17, 2024, AT APPROXIMATELY 06:20 HRS. CST, TC ENERGY WAS NOTIFIED BY THE PUBLIC OF A POTENTIAL GAS RELEASE AT THE CORINTH COMPRESSOR STATION. TC ENERGY OPERATIONS PERSONNEL ARRIVED AT THE CORINTH COMPRESSOR STATION, LOCATED IN ALCORN COUNTY, MISSISSIPPI, AND DISCOVERED NATURAL GAS BEING RELEASED TO ATMOSPHERE. THE UNINTENTIONAL GAS RELEASE WAS CONFIRMED BY TC ENERGY OPERATIONS AT APPROXIMATELY 07:16 HRS. CST. IT WAS LATER CONFIRMED THAT THE BLOWDOWN VALVE'S (5SH-2D BD) STRATIX SWITCH, WHICH COMMUNICATES THE VALVE STATUS TO THE PROGRAMMABLE LOGIC CONTROLLER (PLC), HAD MALFUNCTIONED. THIS LOSS OF COMMUNICATION CAUSED THE BLOWDOWN VALVE TO LOSE ITS HOLD CLOSED COMMAND FROM THE PLC. THE VALVE TRAVELED OPEN DUE TO THE LOSS OF SIGNAL WHEN THE SWITCH FAILED. THE MALFUNCTIONING SWITCH ALSO CAUSED NO ALARM TO BE CONVEYED TO THE EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN DEVICE (ESD) PLC AND THEREFORE, IS THE REASON GAS CONTROLLER DID NOT RECEIVE A "CALL OUT" ALARM FROM THE SCADA SYSTEM. TC ENERGY OPERATIONS MANUALLY CLOSED THE BLOWDOWN VALVE AT 08:05 HRS. CST. THE STRATIX SWITCH WAS REPLACED AND THE ESD SYSTEM WAS PLACED BACK INTO NORMAL SERVICE AT APPROXIMATELY 12:30 HRS. CST. THE CORINTH COMPRESSOR STATION WAS NOT SHUT DOWN DUE TO THIS INCIDENT.
narrative_clean: on january 17, 2024, at approximately 06:20 hrs. cst, tc energy was notified by the public of a potential gas release at the corinth compressor station. tc energy operations personnel arrived at the corinth compressor station, located in alcorn county, mississippi, and discovered natural gas being released to atmosphere. the unintentional gas release was confirmed by tc energy operations at approximately 07:16 hrs. cst. it was later confirmed that the blowdown valve's (5sh-2d bd) stratix switch, which communicates the valve status to the programmable logic controller (plc), had malfunctioned. this loss of communication caused the blowdown valve to lose its hold closed command from the plc. the valve traveled open due to the loss of signal when the switch failed. the malfunctioning switch also caused no alarm to be conveyed to the emergency shutdown device (esd) plc and therefore, is the reason gas controller did not receive a "call out" alarm from the scada system. tc energy operations manually closed the blowdown valve at 08:05 hrs. cst. the stratix switch was replaced and the esd system was placed back into normal service at approximately 12:30 hrs. cst. the corinth compressor station was not shut down due to this incident.

NAME: WBI ENERGY TRANSMISSION, INC.
NARRATIVE: WBI ENERGY RECEIVED A CALL FROM A CONCERNED CITIZEN AT 4:41 PM ON 1/7/24 THAT THERE WAS A LOUD GAS BLOWING SOUND AT THE GOLVA COMPRESSOR STATION.  A WBI OPERATOR ARRIVED ON SITE AT 5:14 PM AND ASSESSED THE SITUATION.  THEY FOUND THE SUPPLY LINE TUBING FROM THE PILOT THAT HOLDS THE RELIEF VALVE CLOSED HAD FAILED WHICH CAUSED THE RELIEF VALVE TO OPEN AND VENT GAS TO THE ATMOSPHERE.  THE OPERATOR WAS ABLE TO PARTIALLY ISOLATE THE STATION AND REPLACE THE BROKEN SUPPLY LINE TUBING.  THE STATION WAS RETURNED TO NORMAL SERVICE AT 6:34 PM.      THE VOLUME OF GAS RELEASED TO ATMOSPHERE WAS NOT CALCULATED ON THE DAY OF THE INCIDENT.  A SIMILAR INCIDENT HAPPENED AT THE GOLVA COMPRESSOR STATION ON 1/23/24 AND WHEN SCADA DATA WAS BEING REVIEWED, THE VOLUME RELEASED ON 1/7/24 WAS IDENTIFIED AND CALCULATED.  AFTER THE VOLUME WAS CALCULATED AND IDENTIFIED AS BEING OVER THE 3,000 MCF THRESHOLD, THE INCIDENT WAS TELEPHONED TO THE NRC.    WBI PERFORMED AN INVESTIGATION OF THE SUPPLY LINE TUBING FAILURE THAT OCCURRED ON 1/7/24 AND 1/23/24.  WBI'S VIBRATION TECHNICIAN TOOK VIBRATION INTENSITY READINGS ON THE RELIEF VALVE AND ASSOCIATED TUBING AND FOUND AMPLITUDES EXCEEDING ALLOWABLE LIMITS.  WBI REPLACED THE SUPPLY LINE TUBING WITH HEAVIER WALL TUBING AND HAS DEVELOPED A PLAN FOR INSTALLING DIAGONAL SUPPORTS TO THE RELIEF VALVE AND ASSOCIATED PIPING.  THE INSTALLATION OF THE ADDITIONAL SUPPORTS IS CURRENTLY BEING PLANNED AND TENTATIVELY SCHEDULED FOR THE FIRST WEEK IN MARCH.  AFTER THE INSTALLATION OF THE SUPPORTS, ADDITIONAL VIBRATION ANALYSIS WILL BE PERFORMED TO CONFIRM THE VIBRATION HAS BEEN DAMPENED TO AN ALLOWABLE MAGNITUDE.    UPDATE - INSTALLATION OF ADDITIONAL SUPPORTS WERE ADDED TO UNIT #1 ON 2/28 AND TO UNIT #2 ON 2/29.

NAME: ENERGY TRANSFER COMPANY
NARRATIVE: AT 16:06 ON 1/25/24, AN ETC FIELD OPERATIONS MANAGER WAS NOTIFIED OF A POSSIBLE LEAK NEAR FIRE TOWER ROAD, EAST OF SAREPTA, LA.  THE ETC MANAGER DISPATCHED FIELD OPERATIONS PERSONNEL FOR EMERGENCY RESPONSE.  AT APPROXIMATELY 16:30, IT WAS CONFIRMED THAT IT WAS A PIPELINE RUPTURE.  AT APPROXIMATELY 16:35, THE LINE WAS ISOLATED AND DE-PRESSURIZED. CLEARED BY THE  VOLUNTEER FIRE DEPARTMENT RESPONDERS WERE ON THE SCENE AND FIRE TOWER ROAD WAS SHUT DOWN FOR APPROXIMATELY 15 MINUTES AT WHICH TIME THE FIRE DEPARTMENT CLEARED THE SCENE.  THE EMERGENCY ISOLATION VALVES WERE LOCKED AND TAGGED OUT.  ON 1/26/24, AS EXTRA PRECAUTION, ETC FIELD OPERATIONS ISOLATED AND BLEW DOWN ON BOTH SIDES OF THE SECTION THAT WAS BLOCKED IN FOR THE LEAK.  THESE SECTIONS WERE BLOWN DOWN TO APPROXIMATELY 5 PSIG.  THE PIPELINE IS SHUT-IN AND WAITING FOR REPAIRS.  UPDATE 07/20/26: IN DECEMBER 2025, THE INSTALLATION OF A NEW 8INCH PIPELINE WAS COMPLETED TO RE-ROUTE GAS FROM SAREPTA, LA.  THE GAS WAS REROUTED FROM MIN-3-1-3 TO THE NEW 8INCH PIPELINE.  MIN-3-1-3 WAS SEVERED FROM ANY ACTIVE PIPING FROM THE MINDEN GATHERING SYSTEM ON THE WEST END.  THE EAST SIDE OF THE FIRE TOWER ROAD IS ISOLATED FROM ANY GAS SOURCE WITH THE INTENT ON COMPLETELY SEVERING FROM THE MINDEN GATHERING SYSTEM ON THE EAST END IN THE UPCOMING WEEKS.  THE PRESSURE ON THE 10-MILE SECTION OF MIN-3-1-3 WILL BE DROPPED TO LESS THAN 125 PSIG.  THE NEW 8INCH PIPELINE WAS PLACED INTO SERVICE AND STARTED FLOWING GAS ON JUNE 16, 2026.

NAME: TEXAS EASTERN TRANSMISSION, LP
NARRATIVE: ON JANUARY 21, 2024, AT APPROXIMATELY 10:30 A.M. ET, ENBRIDGE WAS NOTIFIED BY THE LOCAL SHERIFF DEPARTMENT THAT A STRANGE NOISE WAS ORIGINATING FROM THE REGULATOR STATION. THE RESPONDING TECHNICIAN DISCOVERED THAT A 3-INCH RELIEF VALVE WAS VENTING, EVEN THOUGH STATION PRESSURES WERE WITHIN NORMAL OPERATING RANGE BELOW THE MAXIMUM ALLOWABLE OPERATING PRESSURE (MAOP).  AT APPROXIMATELY 10:45 A.M. THE RELIEF VALVE WAS ISOLATED ELIMINATING THE GAS FROM VENTING TO ATMOSPHERE.     THE INITIAL INVESTIGATION DETERMINED THE RELIEF VALVE LIKELY BEGAN VENTING AROUND 4:30 A.M. ET.  THE STATION IS LOCATED OFF A RURAL COUNTY ROAD WITH LIMITED TRAFFIC.  THE NEAREST DWELLING WAS APPROXIMATELY 1/2 MILE FROM THE STATION.  THE PRELIMINARY GAS LOSS CALCULATIONS WERE COMPLETED AT APPROXIMATELY 1:10 P.M. ET CONFIRMING THAT THE VOLUME WOULD LIKELY EXCEED THE REPORTING THRESHOLD.  THE NRC WAS SUBSEQUENTLY NOTIFIED AT 1:55 P.M. ET.     THE RESPONDING TECHNICIAN DETERMINED THAT THE RELIEF VALVE MALFUNCTIONED AS THE RESULT OF A BLOCKED PILOT LINE (I.E. FROZEN).  THE TECHNICIAN REPAIRED THE PILOT AND PLACED THE RELIEF VALVE BACK IN SERVICE.
narrative_clean: on january 21, 2024, at approximately 10:30 a.m. et, enbridge was notified by the local sheriff department that a strange noise was originating from the regulator station. the responding technician discovered that a 3-inch relief valve was venting, even though station pressures were within normal operating range below the maximum allowable operating pressure (maop). at approximately 10:45 a.m. the relief valve was isolated eliminating the gas from venting to atmosphere. the initial investigation determined the relief valve likely began venting around 4:30 a.m. et. the station is located off a rural county road with limited traffic. the nearest dwelling was approximately 1/2 mile from the station. the preliminary gas loss calculations were completed at approximately 1:10 p.m. et confirming that the volume would likely exceed the reporting threshold. the nrc was subsequently notified at 1:55 p.m. et. the responding technician determined that the relief valve malfunctioned as the result of a blocked pilot line (i.e. frozen). the technician repaired the pilot and placed the relief valve back in service.

NAME: EASTERN GAS TRANSMISSION AND STORAGE, INC.
NARRATIVE: OPERATIONS MANAGEMENT RECEIVED INITIAL NOTIFICATION OF THIS INCIDENT VIA A CALL FROM ANOTHER OPERATOR ON 1/25/24 AT APPROXIMATELY 18:06 REPORTING THAT THERE WAS A FIRE AT BIG ISAAC COMPRESSOR STATION (CS) (GA-1081). GAS CONTROL RECEIVED SECONDARY NOTIFICATION OF THIS INCIDENT FROM 911 AT APPROXIMATELY 18:10 REPORTING THAT A FIRE DEPARTMENT WAS IN THE PROCESS OF RESPONDING TO BIG ISAAC CS. AT THIS POINT IN TIME, THE EXTENT AND SEVERITY OF THE FIRE AT BIG ISAAC CS WAS NOT KNOWN. BIG ISAAC CS RECEIVES NATURAL GAS FROM H-21912 (PRODUCTION PIPELINE OWNED AND OPERATED BY HOPE GAS), COMPRESSES IT USING A SINGLE ENGINE UNIT (AJAX MODEL #DPC-360LE INSTALLED IN 1999 WITH 360 HP), AND DISCHARGES IT INTO TL-413 (GATHERING PIPELINE OWNED AND OPERATED BY EGTS WITH A MAOP OF 500 PSIG). GAS CONTROL NOTIFIED OPERATIONS MANAGEMENT OF THE SITUATION AT APPROXIMATELY 18:15. OPERATIONS MANAGEMENT DISPATCHED PERSONNEL TO BIG ISAAC CS AT APPROXIMATELY 18:20. GAS CONTROL LOST COMMUNICATIONS WITH BIG ISAAC CS AT APPROXIMATELY 17:19. OPERATIONS PERSONNEL ARRIVED AT BIG ISAAC CS AT APPROXIMATELY 19:24, ASSESSED THE SITUATION, BEGAN UTILIZING FIRE EXTINGUISHERS TO EXTINGUISH THE FIRE ON THE ENGINE UNIT, AND IMPLEMENTED A PLAN TO SAFELY ISOLATE THE FIRE. OPERATIONS PERSONNEL MANUALLY CLOSED VALVE 1081-A AT APPROXIMATELY 19:26. VALVE 1081-A IS LOCATED WHERE THE DISCHARGE OF BIG ISAAC CS CONNECTS TO TL-413 WHICH IS DOWNSTREAM OF THE FIRE. OPERATIONS PERSONNEL MANUALLY CLOSED VALVE 1081-B AT APPROXIMATELY 19:27. VALVE 1081-B IS LOCATED WHERE THE SUCTION OF BIG ISAAC CS CONNECTS TO H-21912 WHICH IS UPSTREAM OF THE FIRE. THE CLOSURE OF VALVES 1081-A AND 1081-B COMPLETED THE ISOLATION OF THE FIRE. THE FIRE WAS EXTINGUISHED AT APPROXIMATELY 19:36. THE RESPONDING FIRE DEPARTMENT DEPARTED THE FACILITY AT APPROXIMATELY 20:20. THE RESPONDING OPERATIONS PERSONNEL SECURED THE FACILITY AND DEPARTED THE FACILITY AT APPROXIMATELY 23:20. NO EVACUATIONS WERE NECESSARY, NO INJURIES WERE SUSTAINED, AND THERE WERE NO ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS AS A RESULT OF THE INCIDENT. BASED ON REVIEW OF THE SCADA DISCHARGE PRESSURE AND FLOW HISTORIES, IT IS BELIEVED THAT THE FIRE ON THE ENGINE UNIT INITIALLY IGNITED AT APPROXIMATELY 17:19 AT WHICH POINT IN TIME BIG ISAAC CS WAS IN NORMAL OPERATION WITH A DISCHARGE PRESSURE OF 197 PSIG AND A DISCHARGE FLOW RATE OF 832 MSCFD. UPON EXAMINATION OF THE ENGINE UNIT FOLLOWING THE INCIDENT, IT IS BELIEVED THAT THE FIRE INITIATED IN THE LOW STAGE DISTANCE PIECE AND WAS SUSTAINED BY THE FLOW OF NATURAL GAS. THE CROSSHEAD PIN AND BUSHING SEIZED CAUSING INCREASED FRICTION ON THE SLIDE ASSEMBLY. THE ADDITIONAL FRICTION INCREASED THE TEMPERATURE ON THE COMPONENTS TO THE FLASHPOINT OF THE OIL (459 DEG F). THE CROSSHEAD RUNNING POSITION WAS ALTERED BY MELTING BABBITT CAUSING THE COMPRESSOR PISTON ROD TO RUB THE PRESSURE AND WIPER PACKING CASES. EXCESSIVE RUBBING OF THE COMPRESSOR PISTON ROD GENERATED EXCESSIVE HEAT INSIDE A GASEOUS ENVIRONMENT WHICH ALLOWED COMBUSTION TO OCCUR. THE INTERNAL FIRE MELTED THE PLEXIGLASS COVER ON THE CROSSHEAD DISTANCE PIECE HOUSING WHICH ALLOWED ADDITIONAL OXYGEN TO ENTER THE DISTANCE PIECE AND SUSTAINED THE COMBUSTION. THE RESULTING DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE UNIT AND THE ASSOCIATED FRAME, SKID, PROTECTIVE STRUCTURE, CONTROL PANEL, COMPRESSOR BOTTLE, FUEL LINE VALVE, AND CONDUIT WAS EXTENSIVE. INITIAL TELEPHONIC NOTIFICATION WAS MADE TO THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER ON 1/25/24 AT 19:28. THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER ASSIGNED INCIDENT REPORT #1389962 TO THE INITIAL NOTIFICATION OF THE INCIDENT. A FOLLOW UP TELEPHONIC NOTIFICATION WAS MADE TO THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER ON 1/27/24 AT 09:04 TO CONFIRM THE INITIAL TELEPHONIC NOTIFICATION. THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER ASSIGNED INCIDENT REPORT #1389962 TO THE FOLLOW UP TELEPHONIC NOTIFICATION. THE DECISION WAS MADE TO ABANDON BIG ISAAC CS AS AN ENGINE UNIT AT LAW CS IS CAPABLE OF MOVING THE NATURAL GAS THAT WAS MOVED BY THE ENGINE UNIT AT BIG ISAAC CS.
narrative_clean: operations management received initial notification of this incident via a call from another operator on 1/25/24 at approximately 18:06 reporting that there was a fire at big isaac compressor station (cs) (ga-1081). gas control received secondary notification of this incident from 911 at approximately 18:10 reporting that a fire department was in the process of responding to big isaac cs. at this point in time, the extent and severity of the fire at big isaac cs was not known. big isaac cs receives natural gas from h-21912 (production pipeline owned and operated by hope gas), compresses it using a single engine unit (ajax model #dpc-360le installed in 1999 with 360 hp), and discharges it into tl-413 (gathering pipeline owned and operated by egts with a maop of 500 psig). gas control notified operations management of the situation at approximately 18:15. operations management dispatched personnel to big isaac cs at approximately 18:20. gas control lost communications with big isaac cs at approximately 17:19. operations personnel arrived at big isaac cs at approximately 19:24, assessed the situation, began utilizing fire extinguishers to extinguish the fire on the engine unit, and implemented a plan to safely isolate the fire. operations personnel manually closed valve 1081-a at approximately 19:26. valve 1081-a is located where the discharge of big isaac cs connects to tl-413 which is downstream of the fire. operations personnel manually closed valve 1081-b at approximately 19:27. valve 1081-b is located where the suction of big isaac cs connects to h-21912 which is upstream of the fire. the closure of valves 1081-a and 1081-b completed the isolation of the fire. the fire was extinguished at approximately 19:36. the responding fire department departed the facility at approximately 20:20. the responding operations personnel secured the facility and departed the facility at approximately 23:20. no evacuations were necessary, no injuries were sustained, and there were no environmental impacts as a result of the incident. based on review of the scada discharge pressure and flow histories, it is believed that the fire on the engine unit initially ignited at approximately 17:19 at which point in time big isaac cs was in normal operation with a discharge pressure of 197 psig and a discharge flow rate of 832 mscfd. upon examination of the engine unit following the incident, it is believed that the fire initiated in the low stage distance piece and was sustained by the flow of natural gas. the crosshead pin and bushing seized causing increased friction on the slide assembly. the additional friction increased the temperature on the components to the flashpoint of the oil (459 deg f). the crosshead running position was altered by melting babbitt causing the compressor piston rod to rub the pressure and wiper packing cases. excessive rubbing of the compressor piston rod generated excessive heat inside a gaseous environment which allowed combustion to occur. the internal fire melted the plexiglass cover on the crosshead distance piece housing which allowed additional oxygen to enter the distance piece and sustained the combustion. the resulting damage to the engine unit and the associated frame, skid, protective structure, control panel, compressor bottle, fuel line valve, and conduit was extensive. initial telephonic notification was made to the national response center on 1/25/24 at 19:28. the national response center assigned incident report #1389962 to the initial notification of the engine unit at big isaac cs.

NAME: ENERGY TRANSFER COMPANY
NARRATIVE: ON JANUARY 24, 2024, AT APPROXIMATELY 01:57, ENERGY TRANSFER (ET) PERSONNEL WERE NOTIFIED BY GAS CONTROL OF A COMPRESSOR SHUT DOWN AT THE GALVAN G5L CDP COMPRESSOR STATION. THIS STATION IS TIED TO THE G5LTS-8 LINE, WHICH IS A TYPE C GAS GATHERING LINE LOCATED IN WEBB COUNTY. ET PERSONNEL ARRIVED ON SITE AT 02:43 AND NOTICED THAT A UNIT WAS ON FIRE. ET PERSONNEL IMMEDIATELY INITIATED AN EMERGENCY AREA SHUT DOWN BY CLOSING THE FUEL LINE SUCTION HEADER VALVE AND DISCHARGE VALVE AT 02:45, WHICH ALLOWED THE FIRE TO BURN OUT.  DAMAGE WAS LIMITED TO THE INDIVIDUAL ENGINE.  THE UNIT WITH THE DAMAGED ENGINE WAS ISOLATED FROM THE COMMON HEADER, WHICH ALSO HAS 3 OTHER UNITS CONNECTED TO IT.  THE FACILITY WAS STARTED UP AND PUT BACK IN SERVICE ON JANUARY 24TH AT APPROXIMATELY 06:41 ON JANUARY 24TH.  THE DAMAGED ENGINE HAS BEEN ASSESSED AND A REPLACEMENT ENGINE HAS BEEN ORDERED.  INVESTIGATION REVEALED THAT THE MOST APPARENT CAUSE OF THE INCIDENT WAS THE STARTER/FUEL GAS SUPPLY DEVELOPED A LEAK AT OR NEAR THE VICINITY OF THE SEALCO VALVE. THE START/FUEL GAS LEAKAGE FOUND AN IGNITION SOURCE. THE HIGH HEAT CAUSED THE SEALCO VALVE TO LOSE ITS INTEGRITY AND SEPARATE INTO PIECES. THIS ALLOWED THE 120# OF FUEL GAS TO FUEL THE FIRE.
narrative_clean: on january 24, 2024, at approximately 01:57, energy transfer (et) personnel were notified by gas control of a compressor shut down at the galvan g5l cdp compressor station. this station is tied to the g5lts-8 line, which is a type c gas gathering line located in webb county. et personnel arrived on site at 02:43 and noticed that a unit was on fire. et personnel immediately initiated an emergency area shut down by closing the fuel line suction header valve and discharge valve at 02:45, which allowed the fire to burn out. damage was limited to the individual engine. the unit with the damaged engine was isolated from the common header, which also has 3 other units connected to it. the facility was started up and put back in service on january 24th at approximately 06:41 on january 24th. the damaged engine has been assessed and a replacement engine has been ordered. investigation revealed that the most apparent cause of the incident was the starter/fuel gas supply developed a leak at or near the vicinity of the sealco valve. the start/fuel gas leakage found an ignition source. the high heat caused the sealco valve to lose its integrity and separate into pieces. this allowed the 120# of fuel gas to fuel the fire.

NAME: SALTVILLE GAS STORAGE COMPANY, L.L.C.
NARRATIVE: ON NOVEMBER 25TH, 2023, AT 10:45 A.M. ET, SALTVILLE GAS STORAGE COMPANY, LLC ("SALTVILLE GAS" OR THE "COMPANY") RECEIVED A CALL FROM A LANDOWNER REPORTING A HISSING SOUND EMANATING FROM HIS PRIVATE WATER WELL. THIS WAS THE EARLIEST INDICATION THAT SALTVILLE GAS HAD OF A GAS RELEASE POTENTIALLY RELATED TO ITS STORAGE FIELD, WHICH IS WHY IT IS IDENTIFIED AS THE INCIDENT DATE/TIME IN A4 AND THE DATE/TIME THAT A "FAILURE" WAS IDENTIFIED IN A13 OF THIS REPORT. THE COMPANY'S INVESTIGATION IS ONGOING, HOWEVER, AND IT HAS NOT YET IDENTIFIED AN EQUIPMENT OR OTHER FAILURE AS A CONTRIBUTING FACTOR TO THIS EVENT.     SALTVILLE GAS TOOK PROMPT ACTION TO INVESTIGATE THE NOVEMBER 25, 2023, NOTIFICATION FROM THE LANDOWNER, AS WELL AS THE LANDOWNER'S NOVEMBER 26, 2023, REPORT OF INTERMITTENT BUBBLING AT COVE CREEK. THE COMPANY DID NOT CONFIRM THAT THE STORAGE FIELD WAS LIKELY THE SOURCE OF THE GAS UNTIL JANUARY 30, 2024, THE DATE AN INCIDENT WAS REPORTED TO THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER (NRC) IN ACCORDANCE WITH PHMSA REPORTING CRITERIA.      ON NOVEMBER 26, 2023, OPERATIONS PERSONNEL BEGAN AN EARLY WITHDRAWAL FROM THE UNDERGROUND STORAGE FIELD TO REDUCE THE PRESSURE IN THE FIELD, A DAY EARLIER THAN WITHDRAWAL HAD PREVIOUSLY BEEN PLANNED. IN THE SUCCEEDING WEEKS, SALTVILLE GAS CLOSELY MONITORED FIELD PRESSURE AND ANY EVIDENCE OF GAS AT THE LANDOWNER'S PROPERTY, AND IT GATHERED AND ANALYZED GAS SAMPLES FROM THE LANDOWNER'S WATER WELL TO CONFIRM THE RELEASE SOURCE. ON JANUARY 30TH, 2024, A GAS SAMPLE ANALYSIS REPORT CONFIRMED THAT THE GAS DISCOVERED IN THE LANDOWNER'S WATER WELL LIKELY ORIGINATED FROM THE STORAGE FIELD. AT THAT TIME, SALTVILLE GAS DEEMED THE EVENT SIGNIFICANT WITHIN THE MEANING OF THE PHMSA "INCIDENT" DEFINITION (SEE 49 CFR 191.3(3)) EVEN THOUGH IT DID NOT MEET THE OTHER INCIDENT CRITERIA UNDER 49 CFR 191.3(1) OR (2). THEREFORE, ON JANUARY 30TH, 2024, AT 9:59 A.M. ET, SALTVILLE STORAGE NOTIFIED NRC.    SUPPLEMENTAL 07/16/2025  ON APRIL 22, 2024, SALTVILLE GAS CONDUCTED NITROGEN PRESSURE TESTS ON STORAGE WELLS EH-87, EH-90 AND EH-93. RESULTS FROM THESE TESTS WERE NOT AVAILABLE IN TIME TO BE INCLUDED IN THE INITIAL 30-DAY INCIDENT REPORT SUBMITTED ON FEBRUARY 28TH. BOTH WELLS EH-87 AND EH-90 WERE ABLE TO MAINTAIN PRESSURE FOR THE DURATION OF THE TESTING PERIOD, INDICATING EACH WELLS' PRODUCTION CASING WAS INTACT. HOWEVER, INITIAL TEST PRESSURES AT WELL EH-93 WOULD NOT STABILIZE, AND PRESSURE DROPPED OFF STEADILY, INDICATING THAT EH-93'S PRODUCTION CASING WAS COMMUNICATING WITH SUBSURFACE. (PLEASE NOTE THAT SINCE DECEMBER 10, 2023, EH-93 HAS BEEN ISOLATED BY DOWNHOLE TEMPORARY PLUGS).    ON APRIL 7, 2025, SALTVILLE GAS COMPLETED ALL PLUG AND ABANDONMENT WORK ON WELL EH-93. THE AFFECTED CASING WAS REMOVED AND SENT TO A THIRD-PARTY LABORATORY FOR ANALYSIS. THIRD-PARTY METALLURGICAL TEST RESULTS CONFIRMED THAT THE THROUGH-WALL DEFECT WAS PRIMARILY CAUSED BY MICROBIOLOGICALLY INFLUENCED EXTERNAL CORROSION.
narrative_clean: on november 25th, 2023, at 10:45 a.m. et, saltville gas storage company, llc ("saltville gas" or the "company") received a call from a landowner reporting a hissing sound emanating from his private water well. this was the earliest indication that saltville gas had of a gas release potentially related to its storage field, which is why it is identified as the incident date/time in a4 and the date/time that a "failure" was identified in a13 of this report. the company's investigation is ongoing, however, and it has not yet identified an equipment or other failure as a contributing factor to this event. saltville gas took prompt action to investigate the november 25, 2023, notification from the landowner, as well as the landowner's november 26, 2023, report of intermittent bubbling at cove creek. the company did not confirm that the storage field was likely the source of the gas until january 30, 2024, the date an incident was reported to the national response center (nrc) in accordance with phmsa reporting criteria. on november 26, 2023, operations personnel began an early withdrawal from the underground storage field to reduce the pressure in the field, a day earlier than withdrawal had previously been planned. in the succeeding weeks, saltville gas closely monitored field pressure and any evidence of gas at the landowner's property, and it gathered and analyzed gas samples from the landowner's water well to confirm the release source. on january 30th, 2024, a gas sample analysis report confirmed that the gas discovered in the landowner's water well likely originated from the storage field. at that time, saltville gas deemed the event significant within the meaning of the phmsa "incident" definition (see 49 cfr 191.3(3)) even though it did not meet the other incident criteria under 49 cfr 191.3(1) or (2). therefore, on january 30th, 2024, at 9:59 a.m. et, saltville storage notified nrc. supplemental 07/16/2025 on april 22, 2024, saltville gas conducted nitrogen pressure tests on storage wells eh-87, eh-90 and eh-93. results from these tests were not available in time to be included in the initial 30-day incident report submitted on february 28th. both wells eh-87 and eh-90 were able to maintain pressure for the duration of the testing period, indicating each wells' production casing was intact. however, initial test pressures at well eh-93 would not stabilize, and pressure dropped off steadily, indicating that eh-93's production casing was communicating with subsurface. (please note that since december 10, 2023, eh-93 has been isolated by downhole temporary plugs). on april 7, 2025, saltville gas completed all plug and abandonment work on well eh-93. the affected casing was removed and sent to a third-party laboratory for analysis. third-party metallurgical test results confirmed that the through-wall defect was primarily caused by microbiologically influenced external corrosion.

narrative_clean: on friday, february 9th, 2024, williams called the nrc to report an incident north of station 190 near milepost 1655 on transco mainline a, original nrc# 1391164. a gas smell was reported thursday, february 8th, 2024. williams employees headed to the scene to investigate the same day but were unable to locate the leak. operations continued to look for the leak and located it the following morning on friday, february 9th, 2024. the affected section of the line was subsequently isolated within 3 hours after the leak was identified. release rate is currently estimated at 2342 scf per day. equipment was mobilized to site to drawdown and excavate. drawdown began sunday, february 11th, 2024 and was completed on the 13th. excavation was subsequently started the same day. excavation and draw down was completed on the 14th. blowdown occurred on the 14th and cut-out/tie-in was done on the 15th. on february 16th, 2024 the coating process was completed and the line was placed back in service. an investigation and root cause was conducted to identify the cause of the failure. after the investigation and resulting metallurgical analysis, the leak originated within an original manufacturing mill weld repair or "squirt weld" pass applied to the dsaw seam weld immediately upstream of the girth weld provided. the leak was the result of solidification cracks present within the external and internal seam weld pass that were positioned immediately adjacent to one another.

narrative_clean: the anderson county 12" or tc-12 pipeline system is a natural gas transmission pipeline located in anderson, henderson and houston counties in texas. on february 10, 2024, m6 midstream llc field personnel were notified by our control center that there were some pressure discrepancies on the tc-12 pipeline system located in anderson county, texas. upon investigation, m6 field personnel assumed that there could be a pipeline leak on the tc-12 pipeline system and begin isolating the pipeline system. the tc-12 pipeline system was isolated and field personnel commenced blow down operations. due to severe weather conditions (high winds, thunderstorm, lightning and localized flooding), and no ambient lighting, the leak location was not confirmed until february 11, 2024.on february 11, 2024, upon visual inspection of failure site it was determined that the leak would be above the reportable threshold amount of gas loss (> 3mmcfd) per 191.3, so notifications were made at this point. the pipeline segment involved at the site of the failure was sent to a third-party testing facility to determine the cause of failure. the lab results concluded the localized failure was due to environmentally assisted cracking caused by external hydrogen embrittlement.

NAME: EL PASO NATURAL GAS CO
