EXCAVATION, DECOMPRESSING OF THE WATER TABLE, AND INVESTIGATION FOUND THAT THE BUBBLES IN STANDING WATER WAS FROM TRAPPED AIR FROM CONCRETE CASING. narrative_clean: during a scheduled remediation project in maricopa county, az on l2000 mlv 43 to 44 a suspected pipeline leak was discovered while potholing a dig on 02/19/24. the vac truck operator noticed bubbling soil at the bottom of the pothole. work was stopped and the area was cleared. operations implemented an immediate 10 percent pressure reduction to further investigate the natural gas leak. operations checked the area with a gas scope and ethane detector and no gas or ethane was detected, but a slight hissing sound could still be heard. estimated gas loss would be 6.3 mcf per day. no emergency responders were involved. on 02/20/24 operations suspected pin hole leak at the location due to the presence of methane from detector. the line was blown down and evacuated of natural gas. excavation, decompressing of the water table, and investigation found that the bubbles in standing water was from trapped air from concrete casing. methane that was detected was from adjacent rotting vegetation. this incident was only a suspected leak. kinder morgan took all measures to confirm leak was actually not from the pipeline.

NAME: COLUMBIA GAS TRANSMISSION, LLC
NARRATIVE: ON FEBRUARY 17TH, 2024, TC ENERGY WAS NOTIFIED BY A LANDOWNER OF A POTENTIAL GAS RELEASE AT THE CLENDENIN COMPRESSOR STATION. TC ENERGY OPERATIONS PERSONNEL ARRIVED AT CLENDENIN COMPRESSOR STATION, LOCATED IN KANAWHA WEST VIRGINIA, AND DISCOVERED NATURAL GAS BEING RELEASED TO ATMOSPHERE. THE UNINTENTIONAL GAS RELEASE WAS CONFIRMED BY THE ONSITE TC ENERGY OPERATIONS. A ESD ACTUATOR FAILED DUE TO FREEZING CONDITIONS, A VALVE ACTUATOR ON THE ESD SYSTEM FAILED AND TRAVELED OPEN. THE PILOT AIR VENT FROZE DUE TO CONDENSATION SENDING A FALSE SIGNAL TO THE TRIGGER, CAUSING THE VALVE TO TRAVEL TO THE OPEN POSITION.  THE SWITCH MALFUNCTION CAUSED NO ALARM TO BE CONVEYED TO THE EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN DEVICE (ESD) PROGRAMMABLE LOGIC CONTROLLER (PLC) AND THEREFORE, IS THE REASON THE GAS CONTROLLER DID NOT RECEIVE A "CALL OUT" ALARM FROM THE SCADA SYSTEM. TC ENERGY CONFIRMED THAT THE CLENDENIN STATION CONTINUED TO OPERATE UNDER NORMAL CONDITIONS. TC ENERGY OPERATIONS INVESTIGATED THE OCCURRENCE, CONFIRMED THE CAUSE, CLEARED ALL OBSTRUCTIONS AND ESD ACTUATOR WAS PLACED BACK INTO SERVICE. THE FIRST NRC NUMBER IS 1391816, & THE 48 NUMBER IS 1391930
narrative_clean: on february 17th, 2024, tc energy was notified by a landowner of a potential gas release at the clendenin compressor station. tc energy operations personnel arrived at clendenin compressor station, located in kanawha west virginia, and discovered natural gas being released to atmosphere. the unintentional gas release was confirmed by the onsite tc energy operations. a esd actuator failed due to freezing conditions, a valve actuator on the esd system failed and traveled open. the pilot air vent froze due to condensation sending a false signal to the trigger, causing the valve to travel to the open position. the switch malfunction caused no alarm to be conveyed to the emergency shutdown device (esd) programmable logic controller (plc) and therefore, is the reason the gas controller did not receive a "call out" alarm from the scada system. tc energy confirmed that the clendenin station continued to operate under normal conditions. tc energy operations investigated the occurrence, confirmed the cause, cleared all obstructions and esd actuator was placed back into service. the first nrc number is 1391816, & the 48 number is 1391930

NAME: NORTHWEST PIPELINE LLC
NARRATIVE: ON 03/09/2024, AT 2:45 AM, THE CISCO COMPRESSOR STATION SUFFERED A POWER OUTAGE ON THE ESD SYSTEM STRING, TRIGGERING AN UNINTENDED EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN (ESD) RESULTING IN A RELEASE OF 45 MMCF OF NATURAL GAS. WILLIAMS GAS CONTROL RECEIVED AN ALARM INDICATING THE CISCO COMPRESSOR STATION EXPERIENCED A FACILITY ESD EVENT. THE COMPRESSOR STATION WAS PRESSURIZED BUT NOT RUNNING AT THE TIME. PIPELINE CONTROL IMMEDIATELY NOTIFIED OPERATIONS, WHO DECIDED TO WAIT UNTIL DAYLIGHT TO RESPOND. THE DECISION WAS BASED ON PERSONAL SAFETY RISKS FROM NAVIGATING THE TERRAIN, AND THE BELIEF THAT THE STATION WAS STABILIZED DUE TO FAIL-SAFE VENT VALVES AND THE SUCTION AND DISCHARGE ISOLATION VALVES ON THE UPSTREAM AND DOWNSTREAM SIDE OF THE STATION. THE SCADA SYSTEM INDICATED GAS PRESSURE ON THE MAINLINE SEGMENT AT CISCO COMPRESSOR STATION WAS DECLINING AND AT 3:45 AM, THE CONTROLLER CONTACTED OPERATIONS TO FURTHER INVESTIGATE. AN OPERATIONS TECHNICIAN ARRIVED ONSITE ABOUT AN HOUR LATER. THE TECHNICIAN IDENTIFIED THE STATION DISCHARGE VALVE OPEN AND GAS VENTING THROUGH THE 8" BLOWDOWN. PIPELINE CONTROL REMOTELY CLOSED A MAINLINE BLOCK VALVE TO LIMIT THE RELEASE OF GAS AT 6:10 AM. THE ONSITE TECHNICIAN MANUALLY SHUT IN THE FACILITY TO STOP THE GAS RELEASE AT 6:18 AM.    THE OPERATIONS TEAM PERFORMED SIGNIFICANT TESTING AND TROUBLESHOOTING TO IDENTIFY THE CAUSE OF THE ESD AND THE FAILURE OF THE STATION DISCHARGE VALVE. THIS REVEALED A LOOSE CONNECTION ON A POWER JUMPER WIRE THAT SUPPLIES POWER TO THE ESD-RELATED RELAY STRINGS, WHICH GAVE THE INDICATION OF A POWER LOSS AND TRIGGERED THE ESD.  ONE OF THE STATION'S DISCHARGE VALVES FAILED TO PROPERLY CLOSE DURING THE ESD DUE TO A SOLENOID MALFUNCTION ON THE DISCHARGE VALVE. AFTER THESE CAUSES WERE IDENTIFIED, FUNCTION TESTS WERE COMPLETED PRIOR TO RETURNING THE COMPRESSOR STATION TO SERVICE.
narrative_clean: on 03/09/2024, at 2:45 am, the cisco compressor station suffered a power outage on the esd system string, triggering an unintended emergency shutdown (esd) resulting in a release of 45 mmcf of natural gas. williams gas control received an alarm indicating the cisco compressor station experienced a facility esd event. the compressor station was pressurized but not running at the time. pipeline control immediately notified operations, who decided to wait until daylight to respond. the decision was based on personal safety risks from navigating the terrain, and the belief that the station was stabilized due to fail-safe vent valves and the suction and discharge isolation valves on the upstream and downstream side of the station. the scada system indicated gas pressure on the mainline segment at cisco compressor station was declining and at 3:45 am, the controller contacted operations to further investigate. an operations technician arrived onsite about an hour later. the technician identified the station discharge valve open and gas venting through the 8" blowdown. pipeline control remotely closed a mainline block valve to limit the release of gas at 6:10 am. the onsite technician manually shut in the facility to stop the gas release at 6:18 am. the operations team performed significant testing and troubleshooting to identify the cause of the esd and the failure of the station discharge valve. this revealed a loose connection on a power jumper wire that supplies power to the esd-related relay strings, which gave the indication of a power loss and triggered the esd. one of the station's discharge valves failed to properly close during the esd due to a solenoid malfunction on the discharge valve. after these causes were identified, function tests were completed prior to returning the compressor station to service.

NAME: ANR PIPELINE CO
NARRATIVE: ON MARCH 15, 2024, THE MONITORING CENTER (MC) RECEIVED A CALL FROM A NEAR-BY RESIDENT THAT A VENT VALVE WAS ACTIVELY RELEASING GAS AT SOUTH CHESTER COMPRESSOR STATION (CS) IN OSTEGA COUNTY, NEAR THE CITY OF JOHANNESBURG, STATE OF MICHIGAN. SOUTH CHESTER CS IS CLASSIFIED AS A TRANSMISSION FACILITY OPERATED AND MAINTAINED BY ANR PIPELINE COMPANY, A TC ENERGY ENTITY. MC PERSONNEL DISPATCHED A TECHNICIAN TO THE SITE TO INVESTIGATE THE REPORTED EVENT. THE TECHNICIAN ARRIVED AT THE SITE AT 20:58 EDT, SHORTLY THEREAFTER, A SECOND TECHNICIAN ARRIVED TO SUPPORT THE FIRST RESPONDER. NAME: UGI ENERGY SERVICES
NARRATIVE: THE INCIDENT TOOK PLACE AT FARMER BROTHERS METERING AND REGULATING STATION BEGINNING AT 20:41 ON MARCH 25, 2024. AT THE FACILITY, NATURAL GAS NORMALLY FLOWS THROUGH A FILTER SEPARATOR WHERE ANY LIQUIDS FLOWING THROUGH THE SEPARATOR GO TO A SUMP. WHEN THE SUMP LEVEL EXCEEDS A CERTAIN THRESHOLD, THE CONTROLLER ACTUATES THE CONTROL VALVE TO THE OPEN POSITION TO RELEASE LIQUIDS TO A WASTE TANK. THE CONTROL VALVE'S MECHANICAL LEVEL CONTROLLER FAILED TO REVERT POSITION ONCE THE LIQUID LEVEL IN THE SUMP HAD DROPPED BELOW THE DESIGN THRESHOLD. GAS FLOWED FROM THE SEPARATOR THROUGH A 2" NPS PIPE INTO A WASTE TANK AND THEN ENTERED THE ATMOSPHERE THROUGH THE TANK BLOWOFF VALVES UNTIL THE AFTERNOON OF MARCH 26, 2024 AT 14:45 WHEN THE INCIDENT WAS DISCOVERED.    UPON ARRIVAL AT THE FACILITY, PERSONNEL IMMEDIATELY SHUT THE MANUAL VALVE TO THE LIQUIDS TANK WHICH CEASED EMISSIONS OF NATURAL GAS TO THE ATMOSPHERE AT 15:07 ON MARCH 26, 2024. THE CONTROLLER ON THE CONTROL VALVE WAS FOUND TO BE MISALIGNED BECAUSE THE SPRING TENSION WAS TOO HIGH, NOT ALLOWING THE VALVE TO CLOSE. THE VALVE'S CONTROLLER WAS IMMEDIATELY RECALIBRATED, RESET, AND TESTED TO ENSURE FUNCTIONALITY.
narrative_clean: the incident took place at farmer brothers metering and regulating station beginning at 20:41 on march 25, 2024. at the facility, natural gas normally flows through a filter separator where any liquids flowing through the separator go to a sump. when the sump level exceeds a certain threshold, the controller actuates the control valve to the open position to release liquids to a waste tank. the control valve's mechanical level controller failed to revert position once the liquid level in the sump had dropped below the design threshold. gas flowed from the separator through a 2" nps pipe into a waste tank and then entered the atmosphere through the tank blowoff valves until the afternoon of march 26, 2024 at 14:45 when the incident was discovered. upon arrival at the facility, personnel immediately shut the manual valve to the liquids tank which ceased emissions of natural gas to the atmosphere at 15:07 on march 26, 2024. the controller on the control valve was found to be misaligned because the spring tension was too high, not allowing the valve to close. the valve's controller was immediately recalibrated, reset, and tested to ensure functionality.

NAME: NORTHERN NATURAL GAS CO
NARRATIVE: MARCH 30, 2024, AT 0702 HOURS, PASSERBY NOTIFIED THE EMERGENCY CALL CENTER OF VENTING GAS AT THE LA CROSSE REGULATOR STATION. GAS CONTROL WAS ABLE TO CONFIRM A CHANGE IN PRESSURE, AND FIELD OPERATIONS ARRIVED AT 0730 AND CONFIRMED THE RELIEF VENTING. AFTER CONFIRMING DELIVERY REQUIREMENTS, THE RELIEF VALVE WAS ISOLATED AT 0810. THE RELIEF VALVE AND PILOT WERE REPAIRED ON SITE AND RETURNED TO SERVICE MARCH 30, 2024, AT 1735 HOURS.    THE POST INVESTIGATION DETERMINED THAT THE MODULATING PILOT SET POINT WAS SET TOO CLOSE TO THE NORMAL OPERATING PRESSURE. THE COOLING EFFECT OF REDUCING PRESSURE THROUGH THE MODULATING PILOT CAUSED MOISTURE TO FORM AND POTENTIALLY FREEZE THE PILOT. SINCE THE INCIDENT, IT WAS DECIDED TO REPLACE THE LA CROSSE RELIEF WITH A HIGHER SETTING PRESET BY THE MANUFACTURER/VENDOR TO AVOID FUTURE OCCURRENCES. THE MEASUREMENT TEAM IS IDENTIFYING LOCATIONS WITH SIMILAR OPERATING CONDITIONS, AND THEY WILL TEST AND ADJUST RELIEF SET POINTS OR REPLACE EQUIPMENT WHERE APPLICABLE.
narrative_clean: march 30, 2024, at 0702 hours, passerby notified the emergency call center of venting gas at the la crosse regulator station. gas control was able to confirm a change in pressure, and field operations arrived at 0730 and confirmed the relief venting. after confirming delivery requirements, the relief valve was isolated at 0810. the relief valve and pilot were repaired on site and returned to service march 30, 2024, at 1735 hours. the post investigation determined that the modulating pilot set point was set too close to the normal operating pressure. the cooling effect of reducing pressure through the modulating pilot caused moisture to form and potentially freeze the pilot. since the incident, it was decided to replace the la crosse relief with a higher setting preset by the manufacturer/vendor to avoid future occurrences. the measurement team is identifying locations with similar operating conditions, and they will test and adjust relief set points or replace equipment where applicable.

NARRATIVE: AT 12:54PM PEPL EMPLOYEE RECEIVED CALL FROM A LANDOWNER THAT HE COULD HEAR A LEAK AND SEE VAPOR EAST OF ROAD N AND SOUTH OF 100 RD. AT 1:00PM NOTIFIED EMPLOYEES AT OLPE STATION TO GO TO LOCATION AND CONFIRM LEAK AND LOCATION. AT 1:15PM THE LOCATION AND LEAK WERE CONFIRMED AND BELIEVED TO BE THE 300L. AT 1:45PM A GAUGE WAS PLACED ON 554-3 DSBO 642PSI TO CONFIRM THE 300L WAS LEAKING BY PRESSURE DROP. AT 1:47PM CALLED LYON COUNTY DISPATCH AND INFORMED OF THE SITUATION AND LOCATION, WAS ASKED IF ASSISTANCE WAS NEEDED, INFORMED THEM THAT NO ASSISTANCE WAS NEEDED AT THE TIME. AT 1:48PM WEST RIVER HEADER VALVE 326W WAS CLOSED, AND AT 1:55PM 516 W-1W WAS OPENED. AT 2:10PM THE STATION PRESSURE WAS AT 569 PSI. AT 2:17PM VALVE 516W-2W WAS OPENED. AT 2:20PM STATION PRESSURE WAS AT 545 PSI. AT 2:28PM STARTED BLOWDOWN. AT 2:38PM 2 GATE 300-400 CROSSOVER VALVE 302-E OPENED. AT 2:39PM 2 GATE 300-400 CROSSOVER VALVE 402-E OPENED. AT 3:19PM ISOLATED SECTION WAS BLOWN FLAT.    ON 4/11/2024 PIPE WAS EXPOSED, AND LEAK IDENTIFIED AS A CRACKED WELD. A 44-FOOT PIPE SEGMENT WAS CUT OUT AND REPLACED. THE CRACK MEASURED 34 INCHES LONG CIRCUMFERENTIALLY ALONG THE BOTTOM SIDE OF THE GIRTH WELD.
narrative_clean: at 12:54pm pepl employee received call from a landowner that he could hear a leak and see vapor east of road n and south of 100 rd. at 1:00pm notified employees at olpe station to go to location and confirm leak and location. at 1:15pm the location and leak were confirmed and believed to be the 300l. at 1:17pm sent an employee to protect leak site and two employees to 300l west river header for isolation. at 1:23pm station valve 554-3 was closed. at 1:45pm a gauge was placed on 554-3 dsbo 642psi to confirm the 300l was leaking by pressure drop. at 1:47pm called lyon county dispatch and informed of the situation and location, was asked if assistance was needed, informed them that no assistance was needed at the time. at 1:48pm west river header valve 326w was closed, and at 1:55pm 516 w-1w was opened. at 2:10pm the station pressure was at 569 psi. at 2:17pm valve 516w-2w was opened. at 2:20pm station pressure was at 545 psi. at 2:28pm started blowdown. at 2:38pm 2 gate 300-400 crossover valve 302-e opened. at 2:39pm 2 gate 300-400 crossover valve 402-e opened. at 3:19pm isolated section was blown flat. on 4/11/2024 pipe was exposed, and leak identified as a cracked weld. a 44-foot pipe segment was cut out and replaced. a specimen was sent to the lab for evaluation and determination of cause. the lab report was completed on 11/1/2024 and found that the leak was caused by a combination of a preexisting delayed hydrogen crack on the internal pipe surface at the toe of the girth weld, the presence of a concentrated axial stress at the bottom of the pipe, and the exceedance of the girth weld's tensile strain capacity. the crack measured 34 inches long circumferentially along the bottom side of the girth weld.

NAME: ENERGY TRANSFER COMPANY
NARRATIVE: ON APRIL 14, 2024, AT 9:43AM ENERGY TRANSFER RECEIVED A NOTIFICATION FROM THE PRODUCER SM ENERGY OF A POSSIBLE LEAK IN THE AREA. ET PERSONNEL ARRIVED ON SITE TO INVESTIGATE AT 11:00AM. AT 11:11AM ET PERSONNEL SHUT IN THE BRISCOE R 21H. THIS IS A 10-INCH TYPE C GAS GATHERING LINE IN A RURAL AREA LOCATED IN WEBB COUNTY NEAR LAREDO, TX. AFTER THE LINE WAS EXCAVATED AND EXPOSED,  ET WAS ABLE CONFIRM DISCOVERY ON APRIL 15, 2024 AT 9:00AM. THE LOCATION OF THE LEAK WAS DISCOVERED AT 28.069722, - 99.934444.  UPON CONFIRMED DISCOVERY IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THIS INCIDENT WOULD BE REPORTABLE DUE TO THE ESTIMATE OF PROPERTY DAMAGE AND REPAIR COST. THIS INCIDENT WAS REPORTED TO THE NRC ON APRIL 15, 2024, AT 10:04AM    AN ESTIMATED 22.5 MCF OF GAS WAS UNINTENTIONALLY RELEASED.    THE LINE WAS EXCAVATED, AND COUPONS WERE SENT TO ADV INTEGRITY FOR 3RD PARTY ANALYSIS. FAILURES WERE FOUND TO BE AT THE 6 OCLOCK POSITION; TWO OF THE PITS MEASURED ABOUT 1/4-INCH IN DIAMETER, WHILE THE OTHER PIT MEASURED 1/8-INCH  IN DIAMETER.  SEDIMENT WAS FOUND, REMOVED, AND ANALYZED AT THE 6 OCLOCK POSITION OF THE PIPELINE.  THE FINDINGS SHOWED THE SEDIMENT HAD PRESENCE OF SIDERITE. AFTER REVIEWING OPERATIONAL AND HISTORICAL RECORDS ALONG WITH A LAB ANALYSIS WE HAVE CONCLUDED THAT THE COMBINATION OF SIDERITE, SAND, IRON SULFIDE, AND OTHER DEBRIS LED TO UNDER DEPOSIT CORROSION AND TO AN EVENTUAL FAILURE. THIS LINE IS CURRENTLY NON-PIGGABLE . OUR EFFORTS TO MITIGATE THIS ISSUE IS TO MODIFY OUR QUARTERLY MAINTENANCE PLAN BY INCORPORATING CHEMICAL TREATMENT FOR IRON SULFIDE AND SOLID DEPOSITS.

NAME: TRANSCONTINENTAL GAS PIPE LINE COMPANY
NARRATIVE: ON 4/16/2024, OPERATIONS WERE PERFORMING VALVE MAINTENANCE ON PL-115 GATE VALVE (WKM VALVE WITH AN EIM ACTUATOR). DURING THE CLOSE ACTUATION, THE VALVE FAILED TO STOP CLOSING WHEN COMMANDED AND RESULTED IN THE ACTUATOR BEING PUSH OFF THE STEM AND INTO THE GROUND.     THE END OF STROKE/LIMIT VALVE FAILED TO ISOLATE POWER GAS AFTER CLOSE, RESULTING IN ADDITIONAL TORQUE ENERGY BEING APPLIED TO THE GEARS HOUSING. ALL THAT ENERGY RESULTED IN THE FAILURE OF THE CAST IRON WELDS BETWEEN THE ACTUATOR AND YOKE/STEM HOUSING. WITH THE GEAR HOUSING OFF THE SHAFT, THE GATE VALVE COULD NOT REMAIN CLOSED AND PIPELINE PRESSURE SLAMMED IT OPEN AGAINST THE BONNET.     AS A RESULT OF THE ACTUATOR FAILURE, A STAINLESS POWER GAS LINE BROKE OFF AND VENTED.    THE EIM ACTUATOR CONTROLS WERE TESTED ON A BENCH WITH PRESSURIZED AIR AND DISCOVERED TO SUCCESSFULLY ACHIEVE THE OPEN LIMIT BUT NOT THE CLOSE LIMIT. THE CAUSE FOR THIS WAS THE CLOSE LIMIT VALVE WAS INSTALLED BACKWARDS, WHICH RESULTED IN THE POPPET BEING UNABLE TO ENGAGE WITH THE CAM AND FAILURE TO ISOLATE POWER GAS TO THE MOTOR ONCE THE VALVE WAS CLOSED.
narrative_clean: on 4/16/2024, operations were performing valve maintenance on pl-115 gate valve (wkm valve with an eim actuator). during the close actuation, the valve failed to stop closing when commanded and resulted in the actuator being push off the stem and into the ground. the end of stroke/limit valve failed to isolate power gas after close, resulting in additional torque energy being applied to the gears housing. all that energy resulted in the failure of the cast iron welds between the actuator and yoke/stem housing. with the gear housing off the shaft, the gate valve could not remain closed and pipeline pressure slammed it open against the bonnet. as a result of the actuator failure, a stainless power gas line broke off and vented. the eim actuator controls were tested on a bench with pressurized air and discovered to successfully achieve the open limit but not the close limit. the cause for this was the close limit valve was installed backwards, which resulted in the poppet being unable to engage with the cam and failure to isolate power gas to the motor once the valve was closed.

NAME: ENERGY TRANSFER COMPANY
NARRATIVE: ON APRIL 17TH 2024, AT APPROXIMATELY 12:00 ENERGY TRANSFER RECEIVED A NOTIFICATION FROM THE PRODUCER SM ENERGY, OF A POSSIBLE LEAK IN THE AREA. ET PERSONNEL PROCEEDED WITH ISOLATING THE LINE AND AT 14:03 THE VALVES WERE LOCKED OUT. AT APPROXIMATELY 14:45, ENERGY TRANSFER PERSONNEL CONFIRMED A LEAK ON THE SME L11 12-INCH PIPELINE   (28.122918, -99.967259) AND PROCEEDED WITH BLOWING DOWN THE LINE. THIS IS A 12-INCH TYPE C GAS GATHERING LINE IN A RURAL AREA LOCATED IN WEBB COUNTY NEAR LAREDO, TX    AN ESTIMATED 22 MCF OF UNINTENTIONAL GAS WAS RELEASED. IT WAS DETERMINED UPON CONFIRMED DISCOVERY THAT THIS INCIDENT WOULD BE REPORTABLE DUE TO THE ESTIMATE OF PROPERTY DAMAGE AND REPAIR COST. THIS INCIDENT WAS REPORTED TO THE NRC ON APRIL 17TH 2024, AT 2:57PM    THE LINE WAS EXCAVATED AND A COUPON (36-INCHES LONG: 0.250-INCH WT) WAS SENT INTO ADV INTEGRITY FOR 3RD PARTY ANALYSIS.  FAILURE WAS FOUND TO BE AT THE 6 OCLOCK POSITION; PIT WAS MEASURED TO BE 0.5 INCHES IN DIAMETER.  SEDIMENT WAS FOUND, REMOVED, AND ANALYZED AT THE 6 OCLOCK POSITION OF THE PIPE.  THE FINDINGS SHOWED THE SEDIMENT HAD PRESENCE OF SIDERITE. AFTER REVIEWING OPERATIONAL AND HISTORICAL RECORDS ALONG WITH A LAB ANALYSIS WE HAVE CONCLUDED THAT THE COMBINATION OF SIDERITE, SAND, IRON SULFIDE, AND OTHER DEBRIS LED TO UNDER DEPOSIT CORROSION AND TO AN EVENTUAL FAILURE.  OUR EFFORTS TO MITIGATE THIS ISSUE IS TO MODIFY OUR MAINTENANCE PLAN BY INCORPORATING CHEMICAL TREATMENT FOR IRON SULFIDE AND SOLID DEPOSITS ALONG WITH OUR ROUTINE MAINTENANCE AND PIGGING

NAME: TENNESSEE GAS PIPELINE COMPANY
NARRATIVE: ON APRIL 29, 2024 TGP EXPERIENCED A REPORTABLE UNPLANNED ESD AT COMPRESSOR STATION 25 DUE TO LIGHTNING IN THE AREA. ONE ESD VALVE IN THE YARD DID NOT CLOSE DUE TO AN OUTAGE ON THE 100-2 LINE. FUEL GAS TO VALVE WAS DISCONNECTED FOR OUTAGE AND WHEN THE ESD WAS TRIGGERED GAS WAS NOT ABLE TO GET TO THE VALVE TO OPERATE.     AT CLEVELAND, POWER GAS IS NEEDED TO OPERATE THE VALVES.  A SEPARATE ESD POWER GAS OPERATES THE ESD VALVES WHEN AN ESD IS ACTIVATED. THE VALVE DID NOT CLOSE AS EXPECTED BECAUSE THERE WAS NOT POWER GAS IN THE ESD.   THE INVESTIGATION DISCOVERED THAT THAT THE ESD SYSTEM DESIGN DID NOT INCLUDE SENDING ESD POWER GAS INTO THIS VALVE.  TGP IS INSTALLING THE CONNECTION TO SEND ESD POWER GAS.      28,100 MCF OF NATURAL GAS LOST. FIRE DEPARTMENT DID SHOW UP TO SITE BUT WAS NOT NEEDED.
narrative_clean: on april 29, 2024 tgp experienced a reportable unplanned esd at compressor station 25 due to lightning in the area. one esd valve in the yard did not close due to an outage on the 100-2 line. fuel gas to valve was disconnected for outage and when the esd was triggered gas was not able to get to the valve to operate. at cleveland, power gas is needed to operate the valves. a separate esd power gas operates the esd valves when an esd is activated. the valve did not close as expected because there was not power gas in the esd. the investigation discovered that that the esd system design did not include sending esd power gas into this valve. tgp is installing the connection to send esd power gas. 28,100 mcf of natural gas lost. fire department did show up to site but was not needed.

NARRATIVE: ON APRIL 26, 2024, AT APPROXIMATELY 05:20 AM, A RUPTURE OCCURRED INVOLVING A THIRD-PARTY GAS PIPELINE FACILITY.  THIS EVENT OCCURRED APPROXIMATELY 270 FEET FROM ATMOS ENERGYS ABOVE GROUND STATION AT THE TERMINUS OF ITS TRANSMISSION LINE, LINE X2-7, WHICH WAS NOT CONNECTED TO THE SUBJECT RUPTURED FACILITIES. THE RUPTURE DAMAGED A PIPE SUPPORT AT ATMOS ENERGYS ABOVE GROUND STATION AND CAUSED IT TO SINK INTO THE SOIL, WHICH THEN CAUSED A 12-INCH VALVE FLANGE TO MISALIGN RESULTING IN A RELEASE OF NATURAL GAS AND SUBSEQUENT FIRE.  AT 07:15 AM, ATMOS ENERGY WAS NOTIFIED OF THE EVENT BY ANOTHER INVOLVED THIRD-PARTY OPERATOR.  THE FIRST ATMOS ENERGY TECHNICIAN ARRIVED ON SITE AND DETERMINED THE CONDITION TO EXIST AT APPROXIMATELY 07:49 AM.  ALTHOUGH ATMOS ENERGY WAS UNABLE TO APPROACH THE STATION YARD AT THIS TIME BECAUSE OF THE ONGOING EVENT, CONFIRMED DISCOVERY WAS DETERMINED AT 09:17 AM BASED UPON THE ANTICIPATED STATION DAMAGE COST.  ATMOS ENERGYS GAS CONTROLLERS, IN COORDINATION WITH ATMOS ENERGYS ONSITE EMPLOYEES, CLOSED VALVES TO ISOLATE LINE X2-7 AND THE UPSTREAM LATERAL LINE X2 FROM THE ATMOS ENERGY TRUNKLINE AT 8:10 AM. BOTH CONNECTED LINES WERE ALLOWED TO BLOW DOWN AT A SAFE DISTANCE FROM THE DAMAGED FACILITY. THE FIRE AT THE STATION WAS ALLOWED TO BURN OUT, WHICH OCCURRED AT APPROXIMATELY 12:45 PM.    ON MAY 3, 2024, THE X2 VALVE AT LINE X2-7 WAS CLOSED SEPARATING THESE TWO LINES. ON MAY 22, 2024, THE UPSTREAM LATERAL LINE X2 WAS PLACED BACK IN SERVICE. narrative_clean: on april 26, 2024, at approximately 05:20 am, a rupture occurred involving a third-party gas pipeline facility. this event occurred approximately 270 feet from atmos energys above ground station at the terminus of its transmission line, line x2-7, which was not connected to the subject ruptured facilities. the rupture damaged a pipe support at atmos energys above ground station and caused it to sink into the soil, which then caused a 12-inch valve flange to misalign resulting in a release of natural gas and subsequent fire. at 07:15 am, atmos energy was notified of the event by another involved third-party operator. the first atmos energy technician arrived on site and determined the condition to exist at approximately 07:49 am. although atmos energy was unable to approach the station yard at this time because of the ongoing event, confirmed discovery was determined at 09:17 am based upon the anticipated station damage cost. atmos energys gas controllers, in coordination with atmos energys onsite employees, closed valves to isolate line x2-7 and the upstream lateral line x2 from the atmos energy trunkline at 8:10 am. both connected lines were allowed to blow down at a safe distance from the damaged facility. the fire at the station was allowed to burn out, which occurred at approximately 12:45 pm. on may 3, 2024, the x2 valve at line x2-7 was closed separating these two lines. on may 22, 2024, the upstream lateral line x2 was placed back in service. the damaged station and the entire 263 feet of line x2-7 will not be replaced or placed back into service.

narrative_clean: on april 30, 2024 at approximately 5:52 pm, gas control received an alarm and dispatched ete personnel to the longville compressor station. ete found the esd system had been set off and the station was blowing gas. main fire gate valve did not seal off and continued to blow gas for an additional forty-three minutes until employees determined which fire gate valve was causing the station not to blow down. it was determined that the esd system was triggered by a faulty wire caused the gas detection system to the south gas detector on 4509 to indicate a false reading with up to 50% lel and over range. after further investigation, it was determined at 4:15 pm on may 1, 2024 approximately 67.68 mmscf of natural gas was released to the atmosphere. main fire gate plug valve was disassembled, inspected, reassembled and greased, tested for functionality and sealing off against positive pressure. equipment was returned to service. supplemental/final -updated time in a4 & a16a -updated c3 to valve

NAME: BEAR CREEK STORAGE CO
NARRATIVE: AFTER REVIEWING THE TIMELINE OF EVENTS AND THE FACTUAL EVIDENCE, THE INVESTIGATION TEAM CONCLUDED THAT WHILE  THERE WAS NOT DEFINITIVE EVIDENCE THAT CIRCULATION OF THE WELL WOULD HAVE PREVENTED THIS INCIDENT, IT  APPEARS THAT THE GAS RELEASE OCCURRED AS A RESULT OF WELL FLUID IMBALANCE. HAD THE WELL REMEDIATION PROCESS  REQUIRED CIRCULATION OF THE WELL FLUID, CONDITIONS IN THE WELL MAY NOT HAVE REACHED A STATE OF IMBALANCE,  WHICH ULTIMATELY LED TO THE LOSS OF WELL CONTROL. THEREFORE, THE WELL REMEDIATION PROCEDURE WAS  DETERMINED TO BE INADEQUATE.    THE FULL ROOT CAUSE FAILURE ANALYSIS WAS SUBMITTED TO PHMSA ON NOVEMBER 19, 2024.
narrative_clean: after reviewing the timeline of events and the factual evidence, the investigation team concluded that while there was not definitive evidence that circulation of the well would have prevented this incident, it appears that the gas release occurred as a result of well fluid imbalance. had the well remediation process required circulation of the well fluid, conditions in the well may not have reached a state of imbalance, which ultimately led to the loss of well control. therefore, the well remediation procedure was determined to be inadequate. the full root cause failure analysis was submitted to phmsa on november 19, 2024.

NAME: COLUMBIA GAS TRANSMISSION, LLC
NARRATIVE: ON MAY 20, 2024, AN INCIDENT OCCURRED ON PIPELINE SR- 538 IN BENTON, OHIO, DURING A SCHEDULED MAINTENANCE PROJECT. AS PART OF THE PROJECT, FOUR (4) TC ENERGY TECHNICIANS AND TWO (2) THIRD PARTY CONTRACTORS WERE WORKING TO INSTALL A SKILLET BLIND FLANGE TO ISOLATE THE AFFECTED PIPELINE SEGMENT. THE CREW OBSERVED A GAS LEAK FROM A 6-INCH VALVE AT THAT TIME AND DECIDED TO GREASE THE VALVE TO REMEDIATE THE LEAK USING A MOTORIZED GREASE GUN. AN IGNITION/FLASH FIRE ENSUED THAT INJURED TWO (2) OF THE TC ENERGY TECHNICIANS AND BOTH OF THE THIRD-PARTY CONTRACTORS. THE INJURED WORKERS WERE IMMEDIATELY TAKEN FOR MEDICAL EVALUATION AND TREATMENT. TC ENERGY COMPLETED AN INVESTIGATION TO IDENTIFY THE FACTORS THAT MAY HAVE CAUSED OR CONTRIBUTED TO THE INCIDENT. THE RESULTS OF THAT INVESTIGATION IDENTIFIED THE FOLLOWING PROPOSED RECOMMENDATIONS:   1. DEVELOP AND PUBLISH AN OPERATING PROCEDURE, OR UPDATE EXISTING PROCEDURES, TO OUTLINE THE REQUIREMENTS FOR INSTALLING A SKILLET BLIND.    2. CONDUCT A CONTROL OF WORK ASSESSMENT FOR INSTALLING SKILLET BLINDS TO PRODUCE A HAZARD CONTROLS DIAGRAM FOR REVIEW BY PERSONNEL WITH THE JOB SAFETY ANALYSIS (JSA).    3. IMPLEMENT IMPROVEMENTS TO PERSONNEL TRAINING MATERIALS TO PROVIDE MORE EMPHASIS ON THE ADEQUATE RESPONSE TO UNEXPECTED LEAKS.    4. CONDUCT RISK ASSESSMENT ON THE USAGE OF CSN SOLUTIONS BLACK WIDOW 20V GREASE GUNS.    5. UPDATE THE JSA FORM TO HAVE OPERATOR CONFIRM THE SPECIFIC PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT (PPE) NEEDED FOR THE TASK (E.G., FLAME-RESISTANT CLOTHING, ETC.)    6. UPDATE APPLICABLE PROCEDURES TO REQUIRE A HOT WORK PERMIT TO BE COMPLETED WHEN INSTALLING A SKILLET BLIND DOWNSTREAM OF A SINGLE POINT OF ISOLATION REGARDLESS OF WHETHER A GAS LEAK OCCURS.    7. COMPLETE ONGOING EFFORT TO ISSUE PERSONAL DIFFUSIVE 4-GAS MONITOR GAS MONITORS TO ALL TC ENERGY FIELD TECHNICIANS AND OPERATIONS SPECIALISTS.   8. UPDATE JSA FORM TO CLARIFY THAT CONTRACTORS MUST ALSO SIGN THE JSA IF THEY ARE ALSO INVOLVED IN THE TASK BEING COVERED.   9. SHARE ADDITIONAL DETAILS AND LEARNINGS FROM THE INCIDENT TO THE ORGANIZATION.   10. UPDATE GAS HANDLING PROCEDURES TO CLARIFY THE AMOUNT OF TIME SINCE THE LAST VALVE INSPECTION / SERVICING THAT WOULD TRIGGER ADDITIONAL INSPECTION / SERVICING BEFORE COMPLETING A LOCKOUT TAG OUT ACTIVITY.      TC ENERGY SENT THE VALVE ASSOCIATED WITH THE INCIDENT TO A LABORATORY FOR FURTHER ANALYSIS.  THE LAB RESULT CONFIRMED THE SOURCE OF THE GAS LEAK WAS THE VALVE. THE FOLLOWING ARE THE RESULT OF TESTS;  1-THE SEAT TESTS CONDUCTED IN GENERAL ACCORDANCE WITH THE 24TH EDITION OF API 6D, SPECIFICATION FOR PIPELINE AND PIPING VALVES, SHOWED THAT THERE WAS A DETECTABLE LEAK AT THE VALVE SEAT OF THE SUBJECT PLUG VALVE AT PRESSURES AS LOW AS 70 PSI.   2-THE SHELL TESTS CONDUCTED IN GENERAL ACCORDANCE WITH THE 24TH EDITION OF API 6D SHOWED THAT THERE WAS A DETECTABLE LEAK AT THE FLANGED CONNECTION BETWEEN THE ROTATING SHAFT OF THE PLUG AND THE SHELL OF THE VALVE AT PRESSURES AS LOW AS 800 PSI.
narrative_clean: on may 20, 2024, an incident occurred on pipeline sr- 538 in benton, ohio, during a scheduled maintenance project. as part of the project, four (4) tc energy technicians and two (2) blind. 2. conduct a control of work assessment for installing skillet blinds to produce a hazard controls diagram for review by personnel with the job safety analysis (jsa). 3. implement improvements NAME: FLORIDA GAS TRANSMISSION CO
CAUSE_DETAILS: VALVE LEFT OR PLACED IN WRONG POSITION, BUT NOT RESULTING IN AN OVERPRESSURE
NARRATIVE: ON 05/31/2024 AT 18:12, THE 12-INCH STATION DISCHARGE HEADER BLOWDOWN INADVERTENTLY OPENED RESULTING IN GAS BLOWING AT APPROXIMATELY 1100 PSI FOR 78 MINUTES. A LOCAL EMERGENCY RESPONDER NOTIFIED THE CONTROL CENTER IN HOUSTON, TX.  CONTROL CENTER CALLED LOCAL OPERATIONS MANAGEMENT AND AN FGT EMPLOYEE WAS DISPATCHED TO COMPRESSOR STATION 27 THONOTOSASSA AND FOUND THE DISCHARGE BLOWDOWN OPEN. THE EMPLOYEE IMMEDIATELY CLOSED THE MANUAL BLOCK VALVE JUST DOWNSTREAM OF THE AUTOMATIC VALVE.     UPON FURTHER INVESTIGATION, THE EMPLOYEE FOUND A THREE-WAY VALVE ON THE ESD LINE IN THE CLOSED POSITION. SEALS IN THE OPERATOR ON THE DISCHARGE BLOWDOWN VALVE HAD BEEN REPLACED ON THE PREVIOUS DAY. THERE ARE TWO VALVES INLINE ON THE ESD SENSING FEED LINE.    THE CAUSE OF THE INCIDENT WAS DUE TO A VALVE LEFT OR PLACED IN WRONG POSITION, BUT NOT RESULTING IN AN OVERPRESSURE.    REPLACING 3-WAY-SWITCHING VALVE WITH A MANUAL BLOCK VALVE IN LINE WITH A MANUAL BLEED BETWEEN THE TWO BLOCK VALVES TO PREVENT POTENTIAL REOCCURRENCE.
narrative_clean: on 05/31/2024 at 18:12, the 12-inch station discharge header blowdown inadvertently opened resulting in gas blowing at approximately 1100 psi for 78 minutes. a local emergency responder notified the control center in houston, tx. control center called local operations management and an fgt employee was dispatched to compressor station 27 thonotosassa and found the discharge blowdown open. the employee immediately closed the manual block valve just downstream of the automatic valve. upon further investigation, the employee found a three-way valve on the esd line in the closed position. seals in the operator on the discharge blowdown valve had been replaced on the previous day. there are two valves inline on the esd sensing feed line. the cause of the incident was due to a valve left or placed in wrong position, but not resulting in an overpressure. replacing 3-way-switching valve with a manual block valve in line with a manual bleed between the two block valves to prevent potential reoccurrence.

NAME: UGI UTILITIES, INC
NARRATIVE: ON MAY 30, 2024, A BODY VENT FITTING ON AN ABOVE-GROUND 12-INCH VALVE BEGAN LEAKING TO ATMOSPHERE AFTER IT WAS OPERATED AS PART OF AN IN-LINE INSPECTION OF A NATURAL GAS TRANSMISSION PIPELINE.  THE 12-INCH VALVE WAS ASSOCIATED WITH THE ISOLATION OF A PIG RECEIVER LOCATION INVOLVED IN THE IN-LINE INSPECTION PROJECT. THE LEAK WAS CONTINUOUSLY MONITORED BY UGI PERSONNEL UNTIL THE VALVE WAS REPLACED ON JUNE 18, 2024.    ON JULY 7, 2025, A SUPPLEMENTAL AND FINAL REPORT IS BEING FILED TO PROVIDE UPDATED INCIDENT INFORMATION.     UGI CONSULTED WITH THE VALVE MANUFACTURER WHO EXAMINED AND INVESTIGATED THE VALVE. UGI SUBSEQUENTLY PERFORMED A ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS OF THE EVENT. UGI CONCLUDED THAT THE ROOT CAUSE OF THIS EVENT WAS ATTRIBUTABLE TO THE VALVE SEALS THAT WERE EXPOSED TO DEBRIS SUCH AS WELD SLAG. WELD SLAG WAS FOUND EMBEDDED INTO THE SEALS AND DID NOT ALLOW THE VALVE TO SEAL COMPLETELY. THE BODY BLEED VALVE ALSO DID NOT SEAL AND WAS STRIPPED WHILE BEING OPERATED AND LEAKED CONTINUOUSLY TO ATMOSPHERE FOR A SHORT DURATION. UGI WAS ABLE TO STOP THE LEAK UNTIL THE FINAL REPAIR COULD BE MADE. BASED ON THE SMALL OPENING OF THE BODY BLEED VALVE, THE ESCAPING GAS WAS NEGLIGIBLE.
narrative_clean: on may 30, 2024, a body vent fitting on an above-ground 12-inch valve began leaking to atmosphere after it was operated as part of an in-line inspection of a natural gas transmission pipeline. the 12-inch valve was associated with the isolation of a pig receiver location involved in the in-line inspection project. the leak was continuously monitored by ugi personnel until the valve was replaced on june 18, 2024. on july 7, 2025, a supplemental and final report is being filed to provide updated incident information. ugi consulted with the valve manufacturer who examined and investigated the valve. ugi subsequently performed a root cause analysis of the event. ugi concluded that the root cause of this event was attributable to the valve seals that were exposed to debris such as weld slag. weld slag was found embedded into the seals and did not allow the valve to seal completely. the body bleed valve also did not seal and was stripped while being operated and leaked continuously to atmosphere for a short duration. ugi was able to stop the leak until the final repair could be made. based on the small opening of the body bleed valve, the escaping gas was negligible.

NAME: PACIFIC GAS & ELECTRIC CO
NARRATIVE: ON WEDNESDAY, JULY 10, 2024, AT APPROXIMATELY 21:04 HOURS, PG&E INCIDENT ON-DUTY PERSONNEL CONFIRMED A RELEASE OF GAS AT KETTLEMAN COMPRESSOR STATION RESULTED IN AN INJURY NECESSITATING IN-PATIENT HOSPITALIZATION.     FOLLOWING COMPLETION OF CONSTRUCTION, CLEARANCE ACTIVITIES TO RE-INTRODUCE GAS AND PURGE AIR FROM THE SYSTEM, INITIATED:   - THE APPROVED CLEARANCE REQUIRED V-56 TO BE "CHECKED OPEN" FOR PURGING, HOWEVER, IT HAD BEEN CLOSED FOR STEM SEAL REPLACEMENT WORK ON JULY 8, 2024, AND ONLY PARTIALLY OPENED PRIOR TO THE PURGE - OPERATIONS THAT HAD NOT BEEN DOCUMENTED NOR APPROVED AS PART OF THE SEQUENCE OF OPERATIONS IN THE CLEARANCE.   - GAS WAS RE-INTRODUCED TO THE SYSTEM FROM A 34'' CONTROL VALVE (V-90), A CLEARANCE POINT WITH 618 PSI. THERE ARE TWO WAYS TO OPERATE V-90, MANUAL HYDRAULIC AND MANUAL PNEUMATIC.   - WHEN ATTEMPTING TO MANUALLY OPERATE V-90 HYDRAULICALLY, OIL UNEXPECTEDLY DISCHARGED FROM THE ACTUATOR'S MANUAL HYDRAULIC OVERRIDE SYSTEM RELIEF VALVE AND THE VALVE FAILED TO OPERATE.   - V-90 WAS THEN PARTIALLY OPENED USING THE MANUAL PNEUMATIC CONTROLS. THIS METHOD IS NOT EFFECTIVE FOR FINE THROTTLING AS REQUIRED FOR PURGING IN DESIGN STANDARD A-38.    GAS FROM V-90 BEGAN TO DISPLACE AIR AT MULTIPLE VENT LOCATIONS PER THE ESTABLISHED CLEARANCE PLAN. IT IS SUSPECTED THAT AS A RESULT OF THE PARTIAL OPEN POSITION OF V-56, A GREATER AMOUNT OF GAS FLOW WAS DIRECTED TOWARD V-78. INSTEAD OF GAS EXITING THE 1/2'' VERTICAL VENT VALVE DOWNSTREAM OF V-78 AS APPROVED IN THE CLEARANCE, GAS EXITED THE FULL 6'' PIPE OPENING HORIZONTALLY WHERE THE BLIND FLANGE HAD BEEN REMOVED ON JULY 9. GAS FLOWED DIRECTLY INTO AN OPPOSING BLIND FLANGE ROUGHLY 20'' AWAY AT V-79. THIS RESULTED IN DEFLECTION IN ALL DIRECTIONS, INCLUDING INTO THE EXCAVATION BELOW. A HAZARDOUS AIR-GAS PLUME DEVELOPED. AT APPROXIMATELY 18:42 HOURS, THE AIR-GAS PLUME IGNITED, RESULTING IN SERIOUS BURNS TO ONE COWORKER AND MINOR INJURIES TO OTHERS. CWS IN THE AREA IMMEDIATELY RESPONDED, ATTENDING TO THE INJURED CW AND EXTINGUISHING VARIOUS SPOT FIRES USING PRE-STAGED FIRE EXTINGUISHERS. A CW CLOSED V-90 TO SHUT IN THE GAS BEFORE IGNITION, ALLOWING THE FLAME TO EXTINGUISH IN ABOUT ONE MINUTE.     PROCEDURE USE & ADHERENCE WAS THE APPARENT CAUSE OF THIS INCIDENT. CONFIGURATION CONTROL WAS NOT APPLIED WHEN CLEARANCE WORK WAS EXECUTED. PRIOR TO PURGING INTO SERVICE, CWS FAILED TO RECOGNIZE A HIGH ENERGY ESSENTIAL CONTROL HAD BEEN DISABLED DURING THE PURGE OUT OF SERVICE. PROCEDURES INVOLVING PURGING GAS FACILITIES, INSTALLATION AND OPERATION OF AIR MOVERS, AND TEMPORARY VENT STACKS PROVIDE A BARRIER IN THE FORM OF REQUIREMENTS TO CALCULATE AND MONITOR PURGE DRIVE PRESSURE, PROPERLY SIZE AIR MOVERS AND FRESH AIR SOURCES, AND INSTALL TEMPORARY VENT STACKS TO SAFELY DISPERSE GAS TO ATMOSPHERE. PROCEDURE INVOLVING NEW CLEARANCES FOR GT FACILITIES PROVIDES A BARRIER IN THE FORM OF CHANGE MANAGEMENT FOR THE CLEARANCE PROCESS AND ENDORSEMENT REQUIREMENTS, WHICH FAILED AS THE CLEARANCE TEAM DID NOT FOLLOW THEM.     THE PRECISE IGNITION SOURCE AND LOCATION COULD NOT BE DETERMINED TO A CERTAINTY; HOWEVER, THE FOLLOWING POTENTIAL IGNITION SOURCES WERE ASSESSED AND COULD NOT BE RULED OUT. AN ELECTROSTATIC DISCHARGE FROM THE GENERATED DUST CLOUD. AN ELECTROSTATIC DISCHARGE FROM EITHER THE PIPELINE ITSELF (DUE TO CHARGING FROM THE VENTING GAS) OR AN ELECTROSTATIC DISCHARGE FROM AN EMPLOYEE IN THE VICINITY OF THE VENTING GAS (DUE TO ELECTROSTATIC ACCUMULATION ON THEIR PERSON). A MECHANICAL SPARK FROM DEBRIS EXITING THE PIPELINE AT HIGH VELOCITY OR KICKED UP BY THE VENTING GAS. ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT IN THE VICINITY OF THE VENTING GAS WAS LOCKED OUT AND TAGGED OUT AND WAS RULED OUT AS A POTENTIAL IGNITION SOURCE.    THE INJURED EMPLOYEE WAS TRANSFERRED BY AMBULANCE TO A LOCAL HOSPITAL AND THEN MEDEVACKED TO A FRESNO AREA HOSPITAL TO RECEIVE CARE. THIS INCIDENT WAS REPORTED TO THE DOT AND CPUC DUE TO A RELEASE OF GAS RESULTING IN AN INJURY REQUIRING HOSPITAL ADMISSION FOR OVERNIGHT STAY.

PRIOR TO THE LOSS OF WELL CONTROL AND IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE WELL WORK PROCEDURE, THE WELL HAD A RETRIEVABLE PACKER INSTALLED AT 1,507 FEET MD AND A PLUG SET IN THE PACKER AT 2,424 FEET MD INTENDED TO FUNCTION AS TWO DOWNHOLE ISOLATING BARRIERS BETWEEN THE RESERVOIR AND THE SURFACE. A FEW ELEMENTS OF THE SCADA MONITORING SYSTEM WERE PURPOSEFULLY DISCONNECTED TO ISOLATE HAZARDOUS ENERGY AND ACCESS THE WELL FOR THE PLANNED WORK, AND THE SCADA SYSTEM FOR THE REST OF THE FACILITY WAS OPERATIONAL AND FUNCTIONING.    AT SOME TIME PRIOR TO 11:27 AM, POTENTIALLY OVERNIGHT, PRESSURE BUILT BETWEEN THE BARRIERS INSTALLED AT 1,507 FEET MD AND 2,424 FEET MD. AT 11:27 AM, THE WORKOVER CREWS BEGAN TO RELEASE THE RETRIEVABLE PACKER INSTALLED AT 1,507 FEET MD TO RETRIEVE IT FROM THE WELL. AS THE PACKER WAS RELEASED, THE FORCE FROM THE BUILT-UP PRESSURE PUSHED THE WORKSTRING AND RETRIEVABLE PACKER OUT OF THE WELLBORE IN APPROXIMATELY 3 TO 5 SECONDS. THE GAS THAT BUILT UP BETWEEN THE TWO DOWNHOLE BARRIERS WAS RELEASED. IN LESS THAN THIRTY SECONDS, THE ONSITE CREWS SECURED THE WELL WITH MULTIPLE BARRIERS (MASTER VALVE AND BLOWOUT PREVENTER ELEMENTS). THE WORKSTRING CONTACTED THE ELECTRONICS OF AN OFFSET WELL, WHICH SHUT DOWN IN THE INTENDED FAILSAFE CONDITION AND PROVIDED THE INITIAL INDICATIONS OF AN INCIDENT TO THE CONTROL ROOM VIA THE SCADA SYSTEM. THE SURFACE PIPING OF THREE OFFSET WELLS WAS CONTACTED AND THEN TAKEN OUT OF SERVICE UNTIL ASSESSMENTS CONFIRMED THE DAMAGE WAS ONLY COSMETIC.    THE WELL WORK PROCEDURE SPECIFIED TO EQUALIZE PRESSURE ACROSS THE RETRIEVABLE PACKER INSTALLED AT 1,507 FEET MD PRIOR TO RELEASING IT. THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROCEDURAL STEP IS TO MITIGATE THE POSSIBILITY OF A FAILURE OF THE ISOLATING BARRIER INSTALLED AT 2,424 FEET MD. THE WELL WORK CREWS SKIPPED THIS STEP. THE FAILURE OF THE ISOLATING BARRIER INSTALLED AT 2,424 FEET MD IS A CONTRIBUTING FACTOR.    THE ESTIMATED RELEASE VOLUME WAS CALCULATED USING THE WELL'S INFLOW PERFORMANCE RELATIONSHIP, THE RESERVOIR PRESSURE, AND THE PRESSURE IDENTIFIED AT SURFACE DURING THE RELEASE. AN ALTERNATIVE METHOD RESULTS IN A LOWER RELEASE VOLUME.

IT WAS DETERMINED THE REPAIRS AND DAMAGES WOULD EXCEED THE $145,400.00 REPORTABLE DOLLAR CRITERIA AND THE NRC AND THE TXRRC WERE NOTIFIED.      THE LOCAL FIRE DEPARTMENT ALLOWED THE FIRE TO BURN ITSELF OUT. THE CAUSE OF THE RUPTURE IS STILL UNDER INVESTIGATION. NARRATIVE: RE: OMO RD COMPRESSOR STATION INCIDENT  NRC INCIDENT REPORT #1413461 & FOLLOW UP #1413594    ON OCTOBER 5, 2024 AT APPROXIMATELY 3:09 AM, EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN (ESD) VENT VALVES (BDV 9010) AND (BDV 9011) OPENED BECAUSE OF A LOSS OF POWER GAS PRESSURE USED TO HOLD THE ESD VALVES CLOSED.  PIPELINE ISOLATION (SDV-9001) WAS ALSO OPEN, RESULTING IN A GAS RELEASE OF ~5.2 MMSCF TO ATMOSPHERE.   THE LOSS OF POWER GAS WAS CAUSED BY OF A COMBINATION OF AN ISOLATION OF THE POWER GAS HEADER AND A LEAKING REGULATOR IN THE POWER GAS SYSTEM.  ON OCTOBER 3, 2024, AT 10:56 A.M., THE FUEL GAS SUPPLY VALVE (SDV 9008) TRIPPED / CLOSED DUE TO HIGH PRESSURE (>475 PSIG).  THE HIGH PRESSURE WAS CAUSED BY DAYTIME HEATING AND THERMAL EXPANSION OF THE GAS IN THE FUEL GAS SYSTEM. THE OMO ROAD COMPRESSOR STATION WAS SHUTDOWN AT THE TIME, MINIMIZING FUEL GAS USE AND CAUSING FUEL GAS HEADER PRESSURE TO FLUCTUATE WITH AMBIENT TEMPERATURE. IN ADDITION TO ITS PRIMARY FUNCTION TO SUPPLY FUEL TO THE NATURAL GAS FIRED ENGINES USED TO DRIVE THE GAS COMPRESSORS AT THE STATION, THE FUEL GAS SYSTEM ALSO PROVIDES POWER GAS TO THE POWER GAS HEADER.  TYPICALLY, POWER GAS PRESSURE IS HIGH ENOUGH THAT THE GAS PRESSURE OVERCOMES THE SPRING TENSION USED TO OPEN THE BLOWDOWN VALVES IN THE EVENT OF AN ESD.   FOLLOWING THE OVERPRESSURE CONDITION, SDV 9008 WAS NOT REOPENED BECAUSE THE COMPRESSOR STATION WAS IDLE AND THE NEED FOR FUEL GAS WAS MINIMAL.  WITH SDV 9008 CLOSED AND THE POWER GAS HEADER ISOLATED, A LEAKING REGULATOR ON BDV 9011 EVENTUALLY BLED OFF ENOUGH PRESSURE FROM THE POWER GAS HEADER TO ALLOW BDV 9010 AND BDV 9011 TO FAIL OPEN AS DESIGNED. THE LEAKING REGULATOR WAS IDENTIFIED FOLLOWING THE RELEASE ON OCTOBER 5, 2024 AND REPAIRED ON OCTOBER 17, 2024.    CORRECTIVE ACTION:  BLUEWATER WILL IMPLEMENT CORRECTIVE ACTIONS TO PRECLUDE REPETITION OF THE INCIDENT, MINIMIZE THE AMOUNT OF VENTED GAS, AND IMPROVE REPORTING TIMELINESS.  1. UPDATE PROCEDURES TO AVOID THE ISOLATION OF THE POWER GAS HEADER:  A. OPTION 1: SDV 9008 (FUEL GAS SUPPLY) WILL BE OPEN DURING NORMAL AND STAND BY OPERATIONS  B. OPTION 2: (TBD) VB-9071 CHANGED TO 'NORMALLY OPEN' TO PROVIDE AN UNINTERRUPTED SUPPLY TO THE POWER GAS HEADER  2. CONTROL LOGIC AT THE SITE ALLOWED FOR THE PIPELINE VALVE (SUPPLY GAS) TO REMAIN OPEN WHEN THE VENT VALVES BDV 9010 AND BDV 9011 WERE OPEN.   A. BLUEWATER HAS UPDATED LOGIC AT THE FACILITY, IF A VENT VALVE IS IN ANY POSITION OTHER THAN "CLOSED" THE PIPELINE VALVE FEEDING THE FACILITY (SDV 9001) WILL CLOSE.  3. SCADA ALARMS TO IMPROVE RESPONSE TIME WILL BE ADDED.    A. "VALVES OUT OF SEQUENCE" NOTIFYING THE OPERATOR THAT THE VENT VALVE AND THE PIPELINE VALVES ARE OPEN OR IN TRAVEL.   B. "LOW PIPELINE PRESSURE" AN ADJUSTABLE ALARM THE OPERATORS CAN SET FOR THE CURRENT OPERATING CONDITIONS ON THE PIPELINES.   C. "LOW LOW PIPELINE PRESSURE" A NON-ADJUSTABLE "HIGH PRIORITY" ALARM SET AT 650 PSIG.  4. REVISE EMERGENCY PROCEDURES TO INCLUDE VOLUMETRIC THRESHOLDS FOR REPORTING NATURAL GAS RELEASES TO FEDERAL AND STATE AGENCIES CONSISTENT WITH EXISTING RULES AND REGULATIONS.   5. TRAINING: ADDITIONAL/REFRESHER TRAINING ON REPORTING REQUIREMENTS I.E. TIME TO REPORT, AND THRESHOLDS FOR REPORTING. BLUEWATER COMPLETED THE TRAINING FOR APPROPRIATE EMPLOYEES ON OCTOBER 15, 2024.

THE CAUSE OF THE BRINE ACIDITY AT THIS LOCATION IS UNKNOWN, BUT A PH VALUE OF 2.92, MEASURED AT AMBIENT PRESSURE, IS IN EXCESS OF WHAT IS POSSIBLE FROM CO2 GAS DISSOLVED IN THE PROCESS STREAM. informed pipeline safety that costs were now likely to eventually exceed the $145,400 threshold due to higher than expected environmental and contractor costs. the leak was called in as an incident at update: laboratory analysis has been completed. the results of the metallurgical analysis indicate that the leak occurred at an area of discrete pitting from internal corrosion at the bottom of the pipe (6:17 orientation). the leak was likely caused by the presence of an acidic brine (ph 2.92, measured at ambient pressure) with high salinity. the localized corrosion likely occurred at breaks in NAME: PEOPLES GAS LIGHT & COKE CO
CAUSE_DETAILS: EXCAVATION DAMAGE BY OPERATOR'S CONTRACTOR (SECOND PARTY)
NARRATIVE: SUMMARY OF EVENT  ON SATURDAY, NOVEMBER 9, 2024, AT 1:33 PM LOCAL TIME (CENTRAL STANDARD TIME) A CONTRACTOR PERFORMING WORK FOR PEOPLE'S GAS LIGHT & COKE (PGL) WAS DOING EXCAVATION WORK ADJACENT TO COUNTY ROAD 2700 NORTH AT APPROXIMATE LATITUDE/LONGITUDE 40.266609/-88.432686.  WHILE PERFORMING THE EXCAVATION WORK WITH A BACKHOE, AT THE COMPLETION OF A SWIPE, THE OPERATOR HEARD A POP/HISS AND OBSERVED GAS BLOWING INTO THE AIR.  THE NATURAL GAS TRANSMISSION LINE BEING EXCAVATED WAS AT APPROXIMATELY 1,750 PSIG.  THE CONTRACTOR PERSONNEL CONTACTED PGL EMPLOYEES WORKING IN THE VICINITY.  PGL RESPONDED WITH ON SHIFT PERSONNEL AUGMENTED BY OFF WORK EMPLOYEES.  THE AREA WAS MADE SAFE AND THE LEAK WAS ISOLATED USING MANUAL TRANSMISSION LINE VALVES.  THE AFFECTED PIPELINE WAS ISOLATED AT APPROXIMATELY 3:00 PM AND WAS DEPRESSURIZED TO ATMOSPHERIC PRESSURE AT 3:30 PM.  AT 4:50 PM, PGL ESTIMATED THE RELEASE TO EXCEED 3,000,000 STANDARD CUBIC FEET (SCF).  PGL NOTIFIED THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER (NRC) AT 5:06 PM AND THE ILLINOIS COMMERCE COMMISSION (ICC) AT 5:29 PM.  A FOLLOW UP CALL WAS MADE TO THE NRC ON MONDAY, NOVEMBER 11, 2024 AT 2:43 PM, DURING WHICH PGL REPORTED A CALCULATED RELEASE VOLUME OF 4.953 MMCF.    CAUSES  THE DIRECT CAUSE OF THE RELEASE WAS DAMAGE CAUSED BY THE BACKHOE SHOVEL CONTACT TO SURROUNDING SOIL AND/OR INSTALLED EQUIPMENT INCLUDING THE FOLLOWING:  A 1" 3,000 PSIG RATED, THREADED W-K-M DYNASEAL QUARTER TURN BALL VALVE INSTALLED AT THE 12 O'CLOCK POSITION ON THE 12" CARBON STEEL TRANSMISSION PIPELINE. ON ONE END (TOWARD ATMOSPHERE) OF THIS VALVE WAS A 1" HEX HEAD PLUG AND ON THE OTHER END (LEADING TO THE 12" PIPELINE), WAS A 1"X3" SCHEDULE 160 NIPPLE THAT WAS SCREWED INTO A THREAD-O-LET THAT WAS WELDED TO THE PIPELINE.     THE ROOT CAUSE WAS AS-BUILT DRAWINGS WERE NOT UPDATED TO REFLECT THE ABOVE EQUIPMENT FOLLOWING INSTALLATION IN MARCH 2024.  DRAWINGS WERE NOT UPDATED BECAUSE THE INSTALLATION WAS THOUGHT TO BE TEMPORARY IN NATURE TO SUPPORT FUTURE PURGING OPERATIONS THAT WOULD BE NEEDED FOR PLANNED CONSTRUCTION.  BECAUSE DRAWINGS WERE NOT UPDATED, INFORMATION REGARDING INSTALLATION OF THE EQUIPMENT WAS NOT AVAILABLE TO THE PERSONNEL PERFORMING EXCAVATION ACTIVITIES.  CONTRIBUTING TO THE EVENT WAS THE BACKHOE OPERATOR PERFORMING EXCAVATION WITHIN THE TOLERANCE ZONE OF 18" OF THE PIPELINE.  THE BACKHOE OPERATOR'S OPERATOR QUALIFICATION WAS REMOVED BECAUSE OF THE INCIDENT AND IS PENDING REMEDIATION AND REQUALIFICATION.      AMOUNT OF GAS RELEASED:  BASED ON FURTHER CALCULATIONS USING RELIEF VALVE CAPACITY METHODOLOGY, PGL HAS REVISED THE CALCULATED RELEASE VOLUME TO BE 5,163,905 SCF. THIS INCLUDES 4,842,969 SCF PRIOR TO ISOLATION AND 320,936 SCF FOLLOWING ISOLATION.  A 1.25" OPENING WAS USED DURING THE CALCULATION.  THIS OPENING PROVIDES A CONSERVATIVE CALCULATION RELATED TO THE 1" THREADOLET CONNECTION, WHICH WAS FORCIBLY REMOVED BY THE BACKHOE AND/OR ADJACENT SOIL BEING COMPRESSED DURING EXCAVATION.      ACTIONS TAKEN  1. ALL WORK ASSOCIATED WITH THE PROJECT WAS SHUTDOWN PENDING PGL INVESTIGATION.   2. DIRECTION PROVIDED TO PGL AND CONTRACT RESOURCES THAT W-K-M DYNASEALVALVES WILL NOT BE BURIED IN THE FUTURE. A PLAN WAS DEVELOPED TO ADDRESS OTHER LOCATIONS WHERE THESE STYLE VALVES HAVE BEEN INSTALLED.  (UPDATE: OTHER LOCATIONS WITH VALVES INSTALLED WITH THE SAME CONFIGURATION HAVE BEEN REMOVED).    3. DIRECTED PGL AND CONTRACT RESOURCES THAT ANYTHING BEING INSTALLED ON PGL FACILITIES IS REQUIRED TO BE DOCUMENTED IN THE AS-BUILT DRAWINGS.  4. DIRECTED CONTRACT RESOURCES THAT ONLY HAND DIGGING WILL OCCUR INSIDE OF THE 18 INCH TOLERANCE ZONE.     5. INFORMED CONTRACT RESOURCES THAT ANY HIT THAT RESULTS IN A RELEASE OF GAS THE EXCAVATOR MUST CALL 911 AND JULIE MUST BE NOTIFIED.

NAME: TENNESSEE GAS PIPELINE COMPANY
NARRATIVE: ON DECEMBER 29, 2024, BATESVILLE COMPRESSOR STATION 63 ON THE TENNESSEE GAS PIPELINE (TGP) SYSTEM EXPERIENCED AN ESD EVENT. GAS CONTROL IMMEDIATELY CONTACTED TGP OPERATIONS AT 01:45 CST. THE OPERATIONS TEAM ARRIVED ON SITE AT 2:05 CST AND CONFIRMED THAT GAS WAS VENTING. THE KM TECHNICIAN IDENTIFIED VALVE 63-1S TO BE UNEXPECTEDLY OPEN AND CLOSED THE VALVE AND SECURED THE GAS RELEASE. THE NRC WAS CALLED AT 3:04 CST BY KM PERSONNEL AND THE INITIAL REPORT WAS CAPTURED AS RECEIVED BY 3:07 CST. A 48-HOUR NRC REPORT WAS MADE TO UPDATE THE GAS RELEASE VOLUME TO 49,399 MCF. INITIAL INVESTIGATION DETERMINED THAT LIGHTNING HAD STRUCK THE BUILDING PROTECTION SYSTEM IN COMPRESSOR BUILDING "B" CAUSING A LOSS OF COMMUNICATION WITH THE STATION CONTROLS. THIS LOSS OF COMMUNICATION ACTIVATED THE TGP ESD FAIL SAFE SYSTEM.     FOLLOWING AN INVESTIGATION REGARDING THE VALVE OPERATION, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE ISSUE WAS THE FAILURE OF AN OBSOLETE ACTUATOR WHICH RESULTED IN THE VALVE ACTUATING TO THE OPEN POSITION RATHER THAN THE INTENDED CLOSED POSITION. THE FAILURE MAY HAVE BEEN ATTRIBUTED TO INTERNAL DEBRIS OR WORN COMPONENTS WITHIN THE ACTUATOR. UPON FURTHER REVIEW OF THE ESD SYSTEM, IT WAS CONCLUDED THAT SIX VALVES, INCLUDING VALVE 63-1S, WERE EQUIPPED WITH ESD ACTIVATION THAT WAS NOT FUNCTIONALLY REQUIRED. AS A RESULT, AN INITIATIVE WAS IMPLEMENTED TO RECONFIGURE THESE VALVES WITHIN THE SYSTEM TO REDUCE THE LIKELIHOOD OF MECHANICAL FAILURES.
narrative_clean: on december 29, 2024, batesville compressor station 63 on the tennessee gas pipeline (tgp) system experienced an esd event. gas control immediately contacted tgp operations at 01:45 cst. the operations team arrived on site at 2:05 cst and confirmed that gas was venting. the km technician identified valve 63-1s to be unexpectedly open and closed the valve and secured the gas release. the nrc was called at 3:04 cst by km personnel and the initial report was captured as received by 3:07 cst. a 48-hour nrc report was made to update the gas release volume to 49,399 mcf. initial investigation determined that lightning had struck the building protection system in compressor building "b" causing a loss of communication with the station controls. this loss of communication activated the tgp esd fail safe system. following an investigation regarding the valve operation, it was determined that the root cause of the issue was the failure of an obsolete actuator which resulted in the valve actuating to the open position rather than the intended closed position. the failure may have been attributed to internal debris or worn components within the actuator. upon further review of the esd system, it was concluded that six valves, including valve 63-1s, were equipped with esd activation that was not functionally required. as a result, an initiative was implemented to reconfigure these valves within the system to reduce the likelihood of mechanical failures.

DURING THIS PIGGING OPERATION THAT WAS CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO CNX PIGGING PROCEDURES AND OPERATIONAL PARAMETERS,  THE PRESSURE INCREASED IN THE 1260 MOR40 U2 PIPELINE (UPSTREAM OF THE PIPELINE BEING PIGGED). BASED ON A TREND OF THE DATA, THE PRESSURE APPEARS TO HAVE REMAINED BELOW THE MAOP OF THE PIPELINE AND THE SET-POINT FOR THE PRV LOCATED UPSTREAM AT THE MOR40 WELL PAD.  HOWEVER, THE PRV OPENED AT THIS TIME. THE PRV REMAINED OPEN AND RELEASED GAS UNTIL A PRODUCTION OPERATOR ARRIVED ONSITE APPROXIMATELY TWO HOURS LATER AND FOUND THE PRV RELIEVING. THE PRODUCTION OPERATOR SECURED THE RELEASE WITHIN APPROXIMATELY 9 MINUTES OF HIS FINDING.  THE PRV WAS SET TO RELIEVE AT 1300 PSIG; BASED ON THE PRESSURE DATA TREND IT APPEARS TO HAVE RELIEVED AT APPROXIMATELY 1126 PSIG. THE MANUFACTURER STATED THAT THIS WEAR COULD CAUSE A POTENTIAL LEAK, WHICH IN TURN COULD CAUSE A VALVE TO ACTIVATE BELOW ITS SET PRESSURE; IN ADDITION, THE MANUFACTURER TESTED THE SPRING FOR PROPER FUNCTION AND FOUND IT TO BE WITHIN TOLERANCE. AFTER COMPLETING THEIR INSPECTION, NO DEFINITIVE CAUSE FOR THE SUB-SET PRESSURE ACTIVATION WAS IDENTIFIED BY THE MANUFACTURER. NAME: TARGA RESOURCES OPERATING LLC
NARRATIVE: A PROJECT WAS INITIATED TO INSTALL A PIG TRAP APPROXIMATELY ONE MILE FROM THE IRION COMPRESSOR STATION.  ORIGINALLY DELAYED DUE TO INCLEMENT WEATHER, THE PIPELINE WAS SUCCESSFULLY ISOLATED AND VENTED TO A FLARE ON JANUARY 29, 2025.  A CONTRACT INSPECTOR WORKING FOR APPLIED CONSULTANTS, ISSUED THE WORK PERMIT, AUTHORIZING THE NIGHT CONTRACT CREW TO COMMENCE COLD-CUTTING AND WELDING OPERATIONS WITHIN A BELL HOLE. TO MITIGATE THE PRESENCE OF FUMES EMANATING FROM BOTH ENDS OF THE PIPELINE INSIDE THE BELL HOLE, CONTRACTORS INSTALLED PLUGS TO FACILITATE HOT WORK. A FORMANS PLUG WAS PLACED AT THE OPPOSITE END OF THE WORKSITE, WHILE A MUD PLUG WAS POSITIONED BEHIND THE AREA WHERE THE WELDER WOULD BE BEVELING AND WELDING. ONCE THE VISIBLE GAS FUMES DISSIPATED FROM THE BELL HOLE, THE WELDER AND HIS ASSISTANT ENTERED THE SPACE TO PREPARE FOR BEVELING. THE FOUR-GAS  MONITOR WAS CHECKED TO CONFIRM THE ABSENCE OF LOWER EXPLOSIVE LIMITS (LELS) IN THE AREA. AT APPROXIMATELY 3:00 AM, THE WELDER IGNITED HIS TORCH AT THE END OF THE PIPE TO VERIFY THE PRESENCE OF ANY RESIDUAL GAS.  MOMENTS LATER, A FLASH FIRE ERUPTED AROUND THE WELDER, IGNITING HIS CLOTHING AND RESULTING IN BURN INJURIES. THE INVESTIGATION SHOWED THAT THE MUD PLUG LOCATED BEHIND THE WELDER WAS LEAKING GAS FUMES INTO THE IMMEDIATE AREA. THE FOUR-GAS MONITOR USED TO DETECT THE LELS, WAS SITTING AT THE TOP OF THE BELL HOLE WITH A THREE-FOOT HOSE HANGING INTO THE SIX-FOOT HOLE, APPROXIMATELY SIX TO EIGHT FEET FROM THE WORK LOCATION. AT THIS DISTANCE AND LOCATION, THE MONITOR WAS UNABLE TO DETECT THE ATMOSPHERE IN THE WORK AREA. THE CAUSE WAS DETERMINED TO BE INCORRECT OPERATION OF GAS MONITORING EQUIPMENT. TARGA HAS INITIATED MULTIPLE EFFORTS TO MITIGATE AND PREVENT RECURRENCE. A MUD PLUG INSTALLATION PROCEDURE HAS BEEN DEVELOPED AS GUIDANCE FOR CONTRACTORS WORKING FOR TARGA. ADDITIONALLY ALL CONTRACT INSPECTORS HAVE BEEN RETRAINED ON SAFETY ENFORCEMENT EXPECTATIONS AND PROPER USE OF GAS MONITORING.
narrative_clean: a project was initiated to install a pig trap approximately one mile from the irion compressor station. originally delayed due to inclement weather, the pipeline was successfully isolated and vented to a flare on january 29, 2025. a contract inspector working for applied consultants, issued the work permit, authorizing the night contract crew to commence cold-cutting and welding operations within a bell hole. to mitigate the presence of fumes emanating from both ends of the pipeline inside the bell hole, contractors installed plugs to facilitate hot work. a formans plug was placed at the opposite end of the worksite, while a mud plug was positioned behind the area where the welder would be beveling and welding. once the visible gas fumes dissipated from the bell hole, the welder and his assistant entered the space to prepare for beveling. the four-gas monitor was checked to confirm the absence of lower explosive limits (lels) in the area. at approximately 3:00 am, the welder ignited his torch at the end of the pipe to verify the presence of any residual gas. moments later, a flash fire erupted around the welder, igniting his clothing and resulting in burn injuries. the investigation showed that the mud plug located behind the welder was leaking gas fumes into the immediate area. the four-gas monitor used to detect the lels, was sitting at the top of the bell hole with a three-foot hose hanging into the six-foot hole, approximately six to eight feet from the work location. at this distance and location, the monitor was unable to detect the atmosphere in the work area. the cause was determined to be incorrect operation of gas monitoring equipment. targa has initiated multiple efforts to mitigate and prevent recurrence. a mud plug installation procedure has been developed as guidance for contractors working for targa. additionally all contract inspectors have been retrained on safety enforcement expectations and proper use of gas monitoring.

NAME: TRANSCONTINENTAL GAS PIPE LINE COMPANY
CAUSE: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD
NARRATIVE: OPERATIONS DISCOVERED GAS LEAK AT MP 97.15 ON SVL-T-T-T WITH HANDHELD LEAK SURVEY EQUIPMENT.  AFTER CONFIRMATION, LINE PRESSURE WAS REGULATED TO 80% OF OPERATING PRESSURE AND EXISTING PRESSURE WAS DRAWN DOWN BY A DOWNSTREAM CUSTOMER.  AFTER EXCAVATION, A TRANSVERSE CRACK WAS VISUALLY IDENTIFIED ON THE PIPE BODY.  THE LINE WAS SUBSEQUENTLY ISOLATED, FURTHER DRAWN DOWN BY CUSTOMERS WITH REMAINING PRESSURE BLOWN DOWN.  THE PIPE SEGMENT WAS THEN CUT OUT AND REPLACED WITH PRETESTED PIPING.  THE CUTOUT PIPE WAS SENT TO A METALLURGICAL LAB FOR ANALYSIS.  LAB ANALYSIS CONCLUDED THE FOLLOWING:  THE PRIMARY FAILURE MECHANISM WAS STRESS CORROSION CRACKING (SCC), DRIVEN BY RESIDUAL TENSILE STRESSES FROM PREEXISTING BENDING DURING CONSTRUCTION IN COMBINATION WITH A MILDLY CORROSIVE, OXYGEN-DEPLETED ENVIRONMENT.  SCC MAY NOT HAVE OCCURRED IN THE ABSENCE OF PIPE BENDING DURING CONSTRUCTION, HIGHLIGHTING THE CRITICAL ROLE OF MECHANICAL LOADING IN THIS FAILURE.  UNINTENTIONAL LOSS VOLUME WAS UPDATED AND REDUCED AFTER FURTHER ANALYSIS.
narrative_clean: operations discovered gas leak at mp 97.15 on svl-t-t-t with handheld leak survey equipment. after confirmation, line pressure was regulated to 80% of operating pressure and existing pressure was drawn down by a downstream customer. after excavation, a transverse crack was visually identified on the pipe body. the line was subsequently isolated, further drawn down by customers with remaining pressure blown down. the pipe segment was then cut out and replaced with pretested piping. the cutout pipe was sent to a metallurgical lab for analysis. lab analysis concluded the following: the primary failure mechanism was stress corrosion cracking (scc), driven by residual tensile stresses from preexisting bending during construction in combination with a mildly corrosive, oxygen-depleted environment. scc may not have occurred in the absence of pipe bending during construction, highlighting the critical role of mechanical loading in this failure. unintentional loss volume was updated and reduced after further analysis.

NARRATIVE: ON MARCH 11, 2025, AT 1335 HOURS, A TECHNICIAN ARRIVED ON-SITE AT THE BLOOMING PRAIRIE, MN BRANCH LINE REGULATOR STATION (MNR-0103) FOR REGULAR MAINTENANCE AND FOUND BUBBLES COMING UP FROM BELOW GROUND NEAR PIPELINE FACILITIES. ON MARCH 13, 2025, AT 1240 HOURS, REPAIRS WERE COMPLETED WITH NEW COMPONENTS AND TESTED FOR LEAKS. LEAK CHECKS WERE PERFORMED AT 100PSIG INTERVALS AS PRESSURE WAS RESTORED WITH NO LEAKS IDENTIFIED. NAME: WILLIAMS FIELD SERVICES
NARRATIVE: ON MARCH 8TH AT ROUGHLY 1924 AN INCREASE IN BUILDING LEL WAS OBSERVED BY PIPELINE CONTROL. AS A RESPONSE TO THE RISING LEL PERCENTAGE, PIPELINE CONTROL SHUTDOWN STATION REMOTELY AND SHORTLY AFTER REMOTELY EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN THE STATION TO COMBAT THE RISING LEL PERCENTAGE IN THE COMPRESSOR BUILDING. FOLLOWING THE COMMAND FROM PIPELINE CONTROL THE DISCHARGE ESD BLOCK VALVE FAILED TO CLOSE. OPERATIONS RESPONDED TO INCIDENT AND FOUND AIR PRESSURE HAD NOT ALLEVIATED FROM DISCHARGE ESD BLOCK VALVE AS DESIGNED, WHICH HELD THE VALVE IN THE OPEN POSITION. OPERATIONS COMPLETED TROUBLESHOOTING ON DISCHARGE ESD BLOCK VALVE AND BELIEVED TO HAVE BLOCK VALVE CLOSED WHICH OPENED ESD VENT VALVES. IT WAS THEN DETERMINED THAT DISCHARGE ESD BLOCK VALVE HAD NOT CLOSED ENTIRELY SO PRESSURE CONTINUED TO BE ALLEVIATED BY ESD VENT VALVES UNTIL OPERATORS WERE ABLE TO MANIPULATE VALVES IN THE FIELD COMPLETELY ISOLATING THE SYSTEM. THIS ALLOWED FOR STATION TO DEPRESSURIZE AS PLANNED AND COMPRESSOR BUILDING LEL ISSUE TO BE LOOKED INTO FURTHER. FINDING WAS A BROKEN SITE GLASS PIPE NIPPLE ON UNIT 4 SCRUBBER BOTTLE.    WILLIAMS OPERATIONS AND I&E PERSONNEL COMPLETED TROUBLESHOOTING ON DISCHARGE ESD BLOCK VALVE AND FOUND THAT VERSA VALVE ON INSTRUMENT AIR SYSTEM WAS OPERATING SPORADICALLY. VERSA VALVE ASSOCIATED WITH DISCHARGE ESD BLOCK VALVE WAS REPLACED WITH NEW BEFORE BRING STATION BACK INTO NORMAL OPERATIONS. FULL SYSTEM TEST WAS COMPLETED ON THURSDAY MARCH 13TH TO ENSURE THINGS WERE FUNCTIONING AS INTENDED.     FURTHER INVESTIGATION IS ONGOING.
narrative_clean: on march 8th at roughly 1924 an increase in building lel was observed by pipeline control. as a response to the rising lel percentage, pipeline control shutdown station remotely and shortly after remotely emergency shutdown the station to combat the rising lel percentage in the compressor building. following the command from pipeline control the discharge esd block valve failed to close. operations responded to incident and found air pressure had not alleviated from discharge esd block valve as designed, which held the valve in the open position. operations completed troubleshooting on discharge esd block valve and believed to have block valve closed which opened esd vent valves. it was then determined that discharge esd block valve had not closed entirely so pressure continued to be alleviated by esd vent valves until operators were able to manipulate valves in the field completely isolating the system. this allowed for station to depressurize as planned and compressor building lel issue to be looked into further. finding was a broken site glass pipe nipple on unit 4 scrubber bottle. williams operations and i&e personnel completed troubleshooting on discharge esd block valve and found that versa valve on instrument air system was operating sporadically. versa valve associated with discharge esd block valve was replaced with new before bring station back into normal operations. full system test was completed on thursday march 13th to ensure things were functioning as intended. further investigation is ongoing.

NARRATIVE: AT 20:52 CDT ON 4/12/2025, AN 8-INCH PRESSURE RELIEF VALVE (PRV) ATTACHED TO A 42-INCH HEADER AT THE MISSISSIPPI HUB UNGSF AND COMPRESSOR STATION WAS EJECTED DUE TO A RUPTURE OF THE PIPE SPOOL BELOW THE VALVE. AS A RESULT OF THE EVENT, THE ON-SITE OPERATIONS CONTROLLER EXPERIENCED A LOSS OF COMMUNICATIONS WITH THE SCADA SYSTEM. HOWEVER, THE STATION ESD SYSTEM FUNCTIONED AS DESIGNED AND SHUT IN THE FACILITY AUTOMATICALLY. THE FACILITY WAS IN THE PROCESS OF PREPARING TO WITHDRAW GAS FROM STORAGE WHEN THE EVENT OCCURRED.       THE ON-SITE OPERATOR WAS JOINED BY OTHER LOCAL EMPLOYEES AND BEGAN INVESTIGATING THE SOURCE OF THE FAILURE WHEN THE EJECTED PRV WAS DISCOVERED. THE PRV WAS LOCATED BETWEEN THE GAS HEATERS AND SEPARATORS DOWNSTREAM OF THE PRESSURE REGULATORS FOR THE COMINGLED GAS STREAM WHICH WAS NOT WITHIN THE UNGSF DEMARCATION. IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE EXTENT OF PHYSICAL DAMAGE AND CORRECTIONS TO COMMUNICATIONS COULD NOT BE FULLY EVALUATED UNTIL DAYLIGHT, BUT THERE WAS NO CONCERN FOR THE SAFETY OF EMPLOYEES OR THE PUBLIC. THERE WERE NO INJURIES TO PERSONNEL, IGNITION OF THE GAS, EVACUATIONS, ROAD CLOSURES, OR MEDIA INQUIRIES.     THE FOLLOWING MORNING, PERSONNEL DETERMINED THE PRV HAD BEEN EJECTED VERTICALLY AND THROUGH A CABLE TRAY, RESULTING IN MULTIPLE DAMAGED CABLES. ONCE THE PRELIMINARY EXTENT OF THE DAMAGE HAD BEEN ASSESSED, IT WAS DETERMINED THE FACILITY WOULD BE SHUT IN WHILE REPAIRS WERE MADE. THE EVENT WAS REPORTED TO THE NRC AT 11:09 CDT ON 4/13/2025 SINCE REPAIRS COULD HAVE EXCEEDED $145,400 AND WE DETERMINED AT THAT TIME THAT THE EVENT RESULTED IN THE EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN OF AN UNGSF.     THE REPAIR WAS COMPLETED ON 4/16/2025, AND COMMUNICATIONS FOR THE FACILITY WERE RESTORED, ALLOWING THE FACILITY TO BE PLACED BACK INTO SERVICE ON 4/18/2025. THE FAILED PIPE UNDERWENT METALLURGICAL EXAMINATION, AND A ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS WAS UNDERTAKEN TO DETERMINE THE CAUSE OF THE FAILURE.     THE METALLURGICAL ANALYSIS DETERMINED THE PIPE SPOOL FAILURE WAS THE RESULT OF AN EXTERNAL OVERLOAD OF THE ASSEMBLY CREATED BY A PRESSURE RELEASE EVENT. THE PRESSURE RELEASE CAUSED A DOWNWARD FORCE AND BENDING MOMENT, TRIGGERING BUCKLING INSTABILITY JUST BELOW THE PRESSURE RELIEF VALVE.    THE COMPONENTS OF THE ASSEMBLY ABOVE THE BUCKLE ROTATED NEARLY 45° FROM VERTICAL BEFORE A PARTING FAILURE OCCURRED.     A BULGE WAS PROGRESSIVELY GENERATED AS THE STRUCTURE BENT OVER, DISSIPATING SIGNIFICANT ENERGY. MICROGRAPHS SHOW THAT THE MATERIAL EXHIBITED SIGNIFICANT PLASTIC FLOW BEFORE FAILURE.     THE OVERALL PLASTIC BEHAVIOR OF THE MATERIAL LOCAL TO THE BULGE WAS CONSISTENT WITH MECHANICAL TESTING RESULTS. MECHANICAL TESTING SHOWS AN ELONGATION OF 32% TO 36% AND A REDUCTION IN AREA OF 66% TO 72%. SUBSIZE CHARPY V-NOTCH TEST SPECIMENS (5 MM X 10 MM) RETURNED AN AVERAGE TOUGHNESS OF 98 FT-LBS  AT 72°F(CONVERTED TO FULL SCALE).    THE FINAL FRACTURE INITIATION WAS CAUSED BY SHEAR OVERLOAD AT THE BUCKLE BULGE TIP ON THE OD.    NO SIGNS OF PREEXISTING ID OR OD CRACKS, DAMAGE, CORROSION, OR OTHER STRESS RISERS WERE FOUND. NO EVIDENCE EXISTED THAT PRIOR DAMAGE WEAKENED THE BUCKLING RESISTANCE OF THE STRUCTURE.     A FINITE ELEMENT ANALYSIS OF THE PIPE ASSEMBLY WAS UNDERTAKEN TO SUPPORT THE CONCLUSION THE PIPE SPOOL FAILURE WAS THE RESULT OF AN EXTERNAL OVERLOAD OF THE ASSEMBLY CREATED BY A PRESSURE RELEASE EVENT. THE PLASTIC COLLAPSE OVERLOAD IS CONSISTENT WITH THE FEA ENGINEERING ANALYSIS RESULTS.

designed and shut in the facility automatically. the facility was in the process of preparing to withdraw gas from storage when the event occurred. the on-site operator was joined by other local employees and began investigating the source of the failure when the ejected prv was discovered. the prv was located between the gas heaters and separators downstream of the pressure regulators for the comingled gas stream which was not within the ungsf demarcation. it was determined that the extent of physical damage and corrections to communications could not be fully evaluated until daylight, but there was no concern for the safety of employees or the public. there were no injuries to personnel, ignition of the gas, evacuations, road closures, or media inquiries. the following morning, personnel determined the prv had been ejected vertically and through a cable tray, resulting in multiple damaged cables. once the preliminary extent of the damage had been assessed, it was determined the facility would be shut in while repairs were made. the event was reported to the nrc at 11:09 cdt on 4/13/2025 since repairs could have exceeded $145,400 and we determined at that time that the event resulted in the emergency shutdown of an ungsf. the repair was completed on 4/16/2025, and communications for the facility were restored, allowing the facility to be placed back into service on 4/18/2025. the failed pipe underwent metallurgical examination, and a root cause analysis was undertaken to determine the cause of the failure. the metallurgical analysis determined the pipe spool failure was the result of an external overload of the assembly created by a pressure release event. the pressure release caused a downward force and bending moment, triggering buckling instability just below the pressure relief valve. the components of the assembly above the buckle rotated nearly 45° from vertical before a parting failure occurred. a bulge was progressively generated as the structure bent over, dissipating significant energy. micrographs show that the material exhibited significant plastic flow before failure. the overall plastic behavior of the material local to the bulge was consistent with mechanical testing results. mechanical testing shows an elongation of 32% to 36% and a reduction in area of 66% to 72%. subsize charpy v-notch test specimens (5 mm x 10 mm) returned an average toughness of 98 ft-lbs at 72°f(converted to full scale). the final fracture initiation was caused by shear overload at the buckle bulge tip on the od. no signs of preexisting id or od cracks, damage, corrosion, or other stress risers were found. no evidence existed that prior damage weakened the buckling resistance of the structure. a finite element analysis of the pipe assembly was undertaken to support the conclusion the pipe spool failure was the result of an external overload of the assembly created by a pressure release event. the plastic collapse overload is consistent with the fea engineering analysis results.

NAME: HARVEST MIDSTREAM COMPANY
NARRATIVE: ON MAY 19, 2025, HARVEST INITIATED A ROUTINE FOAM PIGGING OPERATION ON THE PGGS SYSTEM AT APPROXIMATELY 11:00 AM AS PART OF STANDARD MAINTENANCE ACTIVITIES. THE PIG WAS LAUNCHED WITHOUT INCIDENT; HOWEVER, PRESSURE IN THE PG-02 SEGMENT BEGAN TO RISE UNEXPECTEDLY LATER THAT AFTERNOON. THIS SEGMENT IS EQUIPPED WITH A 6-INCH PRESSURE RELIEF VALVE (PRV) AND EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN VALVE (ESDV-1), MONITORED BY PRESSURE TRANSMITTER PT-201.     DURING THE INVESTIGATION, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE PIG ARRIVED SIGNIFICANTLY EARLIER THAN ANTICIPATED. THE TRAVEL TIME HAD BEEN PROJECTED USING SCADA FLOW DATA. THE PIG WAS EXPECTED TO TAKE UP TO TWO DAYS TO REACH ITS DESTINATION BUT COMPLETED THE RUN WITHIN A FEW HOURS. THIS UNANTICIPATED ARRIVAL LED TO CONDENSATE ACCUMULATION IN THE LINE, WHICH TRAVELED INTO THE ACTUATOR SUPPLY TUBING OF ESDV-1, CONTRIBUTING TO VALVE MALFUNCTION.     AT 5:14 PM, PT-201 REGISTERED A PRESSURE OF 526 PSI. THE HOUSTON CONTROL ROOM DETECTED THE TREND AND CONTACTED PIPELINE OPERATOR, WHO ADVISED THAT THE FOAM PIG WAS LIKELY STILL IN TRANSIT. HE INFORMED THE CONTROLLER THAT THE VALVE HAD PRESSURE RELIEF CAPABILITY AND INSTRUCTED THEM TO RESET THE VALVE IF NECESSARY AND NOTIFY HIM IF PRESSURE EXCEEDED 600 PSI.     AS PRESSURE CONTINUED TO RISE, PIPELINE OPERATOR INITIATED MANUAL SHUT-IN COORDINATION WITH THE HILCORP PLATFORM. AT 5:54 PM, PRESSURE REACHED 550 PSI AND ESDV-1 RECEIVED A CLOSE COMMAND, SHUTTING THE VALVE AS DESIGNED. HOWEVER, CONDENSATE ACCUMULATION IN THE REGULATOR AND ACTUATOR TUBING SUBSEQUENTLY PREVENTED THE VALVE FROM REOPENING.     THE CONTROL ROOM ISSUED MULTIPLE RESET COMMANDS TO ESDV-1 VIA SCADA, BUT THE VALVE REMAINED IN AN 'ERROR' STATE AND FAILED TO REOPEN. AT 6:37 PM, PRESSURE REACHED THE MAOP OF 606.2 PSI, PROMPTING THE CONTROLLER TO ESCALATE THE SITUATION TO OPERATIONS CONTROLS DIRECTOR, FOREMAN, AND PIPELINE OPERATOR.     BY 6:43 PM, SCADA ENGINEER WAS CONTACTED FOR SUPPORT. HE DETERMINED THAT THE ISSUE WAS NOT DUE TO A SCADA MALFUNCTION BUT WAS LIKELY CAUSED BY CONDENSATE IN THE REGULATOR AND ACTUATOR TUBING, WHICH PREVENTED THE VALVE FROM RECEIVING SUFFICIENT ACTUATION PRESSURE. AT 6:50 PM, PRESSURE PEAKED AT 620.9 PSI, EXCEEDING MAOP BUT REMAINING BELOW 110%, AND THE PRV ACTIVATED TO RELIEVE PRESSURE. THE PRV VENTED NATURAL GAS TO ATMOSPHERE FOR APPROXIMATELY 22 MINUTES.     AT 6:57 PM, FLOW THROUGH PG-02 DROPPED TO ZERO. AT 7:00 PM, A MANUAL CLOSE COMMAND WAS ISSUED TO ESDV-1, AND A PERMISSIVE SIGNAL WAS RECEIVED. PIPELINE OPERATORS AGREED TO KEEP THE VALVE CLOSED AND CONDUCT A STAND-UP PRESSURE TEST TO CONFIRM PIPELINE INTEGRITY.     THE TEST BEGAN AT 7:18 PM, WITH PT-201 READING 594.5 PSI. BY 8:01 PM, PRESSURE HAD STABILIZED AT 594.0 PSI. ALTHOUGH THE LINE WAS DEEMED SAFE TO RESTART, REPEATED ATTEMPTS TO REOPEN ESDV-1 WERE UNSUCCESSFUL.     AT 10:19 PM, PIPELINE OPERATOR AND I&E TECHNICIAN DECIDED TO KEEP THE SYSTEM SHUT-IN OVERNIGHT. THE ROOT CAUSE WAS IDENTIFIED AS A LIQUID-FILLED REGULATOR AND ACTUATOR TUBING, WHICH PREVENTED PROPER VALVE ACTUATION. PLANS WERE MADE TO ACCESS THE SITE THE FOLLOWING MORNING AND REPLACE THE AFFECTED COMPONENTS.

narrative_clean: on may 25, 2025, at 7:57 a.m., while maintenance was being performed by an energy transfer company (etc) employee and a contract employee, the west slash unit 2 compressor, caught fire. the etc employee notified the operations manager who then notified emergency services. the employee and contract employee activated the emergency shut down system (esd) successfully shutting down the compressor station. both the etc employee and contract employee were injured when the fire ignited. when emergency services arrived at the location the two injured received medical attention and the fire was extinguished. the internal investigation found that employees failed to properly follow the lockout/tagout procedure located in s-230 hazardous energy control section xii. the investigation also found that the employees wrongfully opened a valve allowing the natural gas line pressure to purge debris from the cylinders. the released gas then found an ignition source supplied by one or more of the running natural gas compressors resulting in the fire. the plan to prevent recurrence is as follows: 1) safety stand down for the entire wester division to review lockout/tagout procedures and acceptable cleaning media. 2) retrain site employees on s-230 with an emphasis on the proper lockout/tagout process.

NAME: NATIONAL FUEL GAS SUPPLY CORP
NARRATIVE: NATIONAL FUEL GAS SUPPLY CORPORATION (NATIONAL FUEL) IS REPORTING THIS NATURAL GAS INCIDENT AS A RESULT OF AN UNINTENTIONAL RELEASE OF GAS, WHICH RESULTED IN PROPERTY DAMAGE WITH ESTIMATED COSTS IN EXCESS OF THE APPLICABLE $145,400 THRESHOLD OUTLINED IN 49 C.F.R. § 191.3(1)(II) AND OCCURRING ON NATIONAL FUELS F1S PIPELINE IN THE TOWN OF LIMESTONE, CATTARAUGUS COUNTY, NY (LINE F1S). ON SUNDAY, JUNE 1, 2025, AT APPROXIMATELY 12:11PM, NATIONAL FUEL GAS CONTROL OPERATIONS CENTER RECEIVED AN ALARM DUE TO A PRESSURE DROP ON LINE F1S. AT APPROXIMATELY 12:14PM, THE PRESSURE DROP TRIGGERED A COMPRESSOR UNIT SHUTDOWN AT LIMESTONE COMPRESSOR STATION, WHICH ISOLATED THE COMPRESSOR STATION FROM LINE F1S. NATIONAL FUEL PROMPTLY MOBILIZED OPERATIONS TO INVESTIGATE. AT APPROXIMATELY 1:06PM, NATIONAL FUEL ARRIVED AT LIMESTONE COMPRESSOR STATION TO BEGIN THE INVESTIGATION INTO THE CAUSE OF THE ALARM, AND, ALTHOUGH A POTENTIAL SOURCE OF THE ALARM WAS NOT YET DISCOVERED, AS A PRECAUTIONARY ACTION, CLOSED VALVE CPC113 AT LIMESTONE STATION, WHICH IS IMMEDIATELY UPSTREAM OF LINE F1S. AT APPROXIMATELY 1:36PM, THE DOWNSTREAM VALVE ON LINE F1S (VALVE RHC111) WAS CLOSED TO ISOLATE LINE F1S. OUT OF AN ABUNDANCE OF CAUTION, AT APPROXIMATELY 2:46PM, NATIONAL FUEL NOTIFIED THE NRC OF A POTENTIAL RUPTURE. AFTER LINE F1S WAS ISOLATED, NATIONAL FUEL PATROLLED LINE F1S, AND, AT APPROXIMATELY 3:16PM, CONFIRMED A RUPTURE ON LINE F1S NEAR THE CROSSING OF RICE BROOK WITHIN ALLEGANY STATE PARK (GPS COORDINATES 42.0603, -78.69133). UPON EXCAVATING AND REMOVING THE RUPTURED SECTION OF LINE F1S, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE RUPTURE OCCURRED ALONG THE LONGITUDINAL SEAM OF AN APPROXIMATELY 50-FOOT JOINT OF PIPE AND ARRESTED 2-3 INCHES BEYOND THE GIRTH WELD IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. THE LONGITUDINAL SEAM WAS ORIENTED AT THE 6:00 OCLOCK PIPE POSITION. THE RICE BROOK FLOWED ABOVE LINE F1S THROUGH TWO PARALLEL CORRUGATED METAL CULVERT PIPES, WHICH WERE DAMAGED AS A RESULT OF THE RUPTURE. THE FLOW OF RICE BROOK WAS TEMPORARILY DISRUPTED, BUT LATER RE-ESTABLISHED WITH MINIMAL ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS. LABORATORY ROOT CAUSE FAILURE ANALYSIS OF THE RUPTURED SECTION OF LINE F1S DETERMINED THE ROOT CAUSE WAS INTERNAL SELECTED SEAM WELD CORROSION (SSWC), INITIATING IN A SAG BEND AT A LOW POINT IN LINE F1S. THE LAB REPORT STATED THAT THE LOW POINT WOULD LIKELY COLLECT WATER AND OTHER POTENTIAL CONTAMINANTS FROM THE SERVICE FLUID, WHICH WOULD AID THE PROGRESS OF INTERNAL SSWC DUE TO LINE F1S'S SEAM HAVING BEEN INSTALLED AT THE 6:00 O'CLOCK ORIENTATION. LINE F1S WAS REPAIRED BY REPLACING APPROXIMATELY 60 FEET OF 6-INCH OD, 0.280-INCH WALL, GRADE X-52 STEEL PIPE WHICH WAS PRESSURE TESTED TO >1.5 X MAOP. NO INJURIES OR FATALITIES RESULTED FROM THE RUPTURE.

pressure drop triggered a compressor unit shutdown at limestone compressor station, which isolated the compressor station from line f1s. national fuel promptly mobilized operations to investigate. at closed to isolate line f1s. out of an abundance of caution, at approximately 2:46pm, national fuel notified the nrc of a potential rupture. after line f1s was isolated, national fuel patrolled line f1s, and, at approximately 3:16pm, confirmed a rupture on line f1s near the crossing of rice brook within allegany state park (gps coordinates 42.0603, -78.69133). upon excavating and removing the ruptured section of line f1s, it was determined that the rupture occurred along the longitudinal seam of an approximately 50-foot joint of pipe and arrested 2-3 inches beyond the girth weld in both directions. the longitudinal seam was oriented at the 6:00 oclock pipe position. the rice brook flowed above line f1s through two parallel corrugated metal culvert pipes, which were damaged as a
