NAME: EL PASO NATURAL GAS CO
NARRATIVE: ON JUNE 15, 2025, AN EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN (ESD) EVENT OCCURRED AT THE WASHINGTON RANCH COMPRESSOR STATION WHILE THE STATION WAS IN AN IDLE OPERATING STATE. SEVERE WEATHER AND FLASH FLOODING IN THE AREA PREVENTED EPNG PERSONNEL FROM ACCESSING THE STATION UNTIL JUNE 16, 2025.  DURING THIS PERIOD, THE STATION WAS MONITORED THROUGH REMOTE SYSTEM ACCESS WHICH INDICATED ISOLATION VALVES AND ESD VENTS WERE IN THEIR PROPER POSITIONS.     UPON ARRIVING ON SITE, EPNG PERSONNEL CONDUCTED AN ONSITE ASSESSMENT AND FOUND ESD VALVE 5107 IN A PARTIALLY CLOSED POSITION. A ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS DETERMINED THAT VALVE 5107 HAD A DEFECTIVE VALVE ACTUATOR THAT PREVENTED FULL VALVE CLOSURE DURING THE ESD EVENT AND CONTRIBUTED TO A RELEASE OF APPROXIMATELY 84,000 MCF OF NATURAL GAS.    THE EVENT WAS INITIALLY CLASSIFIED AS AN ABNORMAL OPERATION EVENT. SUBSEQUENT REVIEW OF MEASUREMENT DATA IDENTIFIED THAT THE VOLUME OF GAS RELEASE EXCEEDED REPORTABLE THRESHOLDS ON JUNE 19, 2025, AT WHICH TIME KINDER MORGAN NOTIFIED THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER OF A REPORTABLE NATURAL GAS RELEASE.    CORRECTIVE ACTION INCLUDED REPLACEMENT OF THE VALVE ACTUATOR ON ESD VALVE 5107 TO ENSURE FULL CLOSURE DURING FUTURE ESD ACTIVATIONS.
narrative_clean: on june 15, 2025, an emergency shutdown (esd) event occurred at the washington ranch compressor station while the station was in an idle operating state. severe weather and flash flooding in the area prevented epng personnel from accessing the station until june 16, 2025. during this period, the station was monitored through remote system access which indicated isolation valves and esd vents were in their proper positions. upon arriving on site, epng personnel conducted an onsite assessment and found esd valve 5107 in a partially closed position. a root cause analysis determined that valve 5107 had a defective valve actuator that prevented full valve closure during the esd event and contributed to a release of approximately 84,000 mcf of natural gas. the event was initially classified as an abnormal operation event. subsequent review of measurement data identified that the volume of gas release exceeded reportable thresholds on june 19, 2025, at which time kinder morgan notified the national response center of a reportable natural gas release. corrective action included replacement of the valve actuator on esd valve 5107 to ensure full closure during future esd activations.

NAME: NORTHERN BORDER PIPELINE COMPANY
NARRATIVE: ON JULY 3, 2025, AT 16:24 MDT, NORTHERN BORDER'S GAS CONTROL (GC) RECEIVED AN ALARM AT MONCHY METER STATION AND AT 16:36 MDT, GC RECEIVED A CALL FROM A CUSTOMER ABOUT A PRESSURE DROP ON THEIR COMPRESSOR STATION THAT MAY HAVE IMPACTED MONCHY METER STATION. AT 18:38 MDT, A SECOND CALL WAS RECEIVED FROM THE CUSTOMER ASKING FOR A TECHNICIAN ON OUR SIDE TO INVESTIGATE A RELIEF VALVE AT MONCHY METER STATION. GC DISPATCHED A TECHNICIAN TO INVESTIGATE A POTENTIAL RELEASE AT 18:45 MDT. UPON ARRIVING ON SITE AT 21:17 MDT, THE TECHNICIAN DISCOVERED NATURAL GAS WAS BEING RELEASED TO THE ATMOSPHERE THROUGH AN EIGHT-INCH RELIEF VALVE. IMMEDIATE ACTION WAS TAKEN TO ISOLATE THE VALVE, WHICH ENDED THE RELEASE AT 21:20 MDT. THE UNINTENTIONAL GAS LOSS WAS CALCULATED TO BE APPROXIMATELY 217,850.1 MCF. THERE WERE NO DAMAGES, INJURIES OR HOSPITALIZATIONS.  AFTER TECHNICIANS DETERMINED REPLACEMENT OF THE PILOT VALVE DID NOT RESULT IN RESEATING, THE FAILED RELIEF VALVE WAS REMOVED AND SENT TO A THIRD-PARTY VENDOR FOR INSPECTION.  THE INSPECTION REVEALED SCORING AND DAMAGE ON THE MAIN VALVE PISTON AND PISTON LINER, IN ADDITION TO DETERIORATION OF THE MAIN VALVE SEAT.  THE SUSPECTED CAUSE OF THE DAMAGE TO THE VALVE IS ACCUMULATION OF DEBRIS OVER TIME, WHICH RESULTED IN THE INABILITY OF THE VALVE TO SEAL AND THE UNINTENDED RELEASE OF GAS TO ATMOSPHERE. A SECONDARY RELIEF VALVE AT THE MONCHY METER STATION IS CURRENTLY PROVIDING OVERPRESSURE PROTECTION TO THE PIPELINE SYSTEM.
narrative_clean: on july 3, 2025, at 16:24 mdt, northern border's gas control (gc) received an alarm at monchy meter station and at 16:36 mdt, gc received a call from a customer about a pressure drop on their compressor station that may have impacted monchy meter station. at 18:38 mdt, a second call was received from the customer asking for a technician on our side to investigate a relief valve at monchy meter station. gc dispatched a technician to investigate a potential release at 18:45 mdt. upon arriving on site at 21:17 mdt, the technician discovered natural gas was being released to the atmosphere through an eight-inch relief valve. immediate action was taken to isolate the valve, which ended the release at 21:20 mdt. the unintentional gas loss was calculated to be approximately 217,850.1 mcf. there were no damages, injuries or hospitalizations. after technicians determined replacement of the pilot valve did not result in reseating, the failed relief valve was removed and sent to a third-party vendor for inspection. the inspection revealed scoring and damage on the main valve piston and piston liner, in addition to deterioration of the main valve seat. the suspected cause of the damage to the valve is accumulation of debris over time, which resulted in the inability of the valve to seal and the unintended release of gas to atmosphere. a secondary relief valve at the monchy meter station is currently providing overpressure protection to the pipeline system.

NAME: ONEOK WESTEX TRANSMISSION, LLC
NARRATIVE: AT 8:05 A.M., A FASKEN OPERATOR NOTIFIED ONEOK PIPELINE CONTROL CENTER OF A GAS RELEASE AT THE FASKEN METER SETTING. UPON RECEIVING THE REPORT, PCC CALLED THE LOCAL MEASUREMENT TECHNICIAN TO HEAD TO THE SITE. THE TECH ARRIVED ON SITE AT 9:25 A.M AND WITNESSED A PRV RELEASING GAS. THE TECH ISOLATED THE PRV AT 9:27 A.M. AFTER BEING ISOLATED, THE PRESSURE DATA WAS TRENDED, AND A PRESSURE CHANGE WAS NOTED TO HAVE OCCURRED AT 5:51 A.M.  THE RELIEF FOR THE VALVE WAS REMOVED AND SENT OFF FOR ANALYSIS. AT THIS TIME THERE ARE NO PLANS TO REINSTALL A NEW RELIEF AS THIS IS A REDUNDANT FORM OF PRESSURE CONTROL FOR THIS SETTING. ONCE ANALYSIS RESULTS HAVE BEEN RECEIVED A SUPPLEMENTAL WILL BE SUBMITTED.    SUPPLEMENTAL- FOLLOWING THE EVENT, OWT CONDUCTED A FAILURE ANALYSIS. THE ANALYSIS CONCLUDED THAT THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE FAILURE WAS THE INSTALLATION OF A PRV WITH A RELIEF TOLERANCE WITHIN THE NORMAL OPERATING RANGE OF THE PIPELINE SYSTEM. THIS ALLOWED THE PVR TO CONTINUE TO RELIEF WITHIN THE NORMAL DESIGN/OPERATING PRESSURE OF THE PIPELINE SYSTEM.  AS A RESULT, THE PVR STEM AND SEATS WERE DAMAGED, NOT ALLOWING THE PVR TO RESEAT. NAME: CONSUMERS ENERGY CO
NARRATIVE: ON SEPTEMBER 10, 2025, AT APPROXIMATELY 08:49, A CONSUMERS ENERGY EMPLOYEE INVESTIGATING A POTENTIAL LEAK INDICATION CONFIRMED THE PRESENCE OF A LEAK ON LINE 2600 NEAR THE JOHNSON ROAD VALVE SITE. LINE 2600 IS A 12-INCH NATURAL GAS TRANSMISSION PIPELINE LOCATED IN LAKE CITY, MICHIGAN (MISSAUKEE COUNTY).    CONSUMERS ENERGY PROMPTLY INITIATED AN ISOLATION PROCEDURE TO FURTHER ASSESS THE SITUATION. THE AFFECTED SECTION OF LINE 2600 WAS SUCCESSFULLY ISOLATED AND VENTED TO 0 PSIG BY APPROXIMATELY 16:46 THE SAME DAY.    FOLLOWING EXCAVATION, THE LEAK WAS DISCOVERED ON A 12-INCH BALL VALVE (VALVE 2622). THE VALVE WAS PRESERVED IN ACCORDANCE WITH CONSUMERS ENERGYS FAILURE INVESTIGATION PROCEDURES AND TRANSPORTED TO THE COMPANYS LABORATORY FOR ANALYSIS.    THE INCIDENT RESPONSE AND REMEDIATION EFFORTS WERE CONDUCTED WITHOUT INJURY TO THE PUBLIC OR OPERATING PERSONNEL.    REMEDIATION ACTIVITIES COMMENCED ON SEPTEMBER 10, 2025. THE SCOPE OF WORK INCLUDED REPLACEMENT OF THE 12-INCH BALL VALVE AND APPROXIMATELY 9-FEET OF PIPELINE. THE PIPELINE SEGMENT WAS RETURNED TO SERVICE ON SEPTEMBER 23, 2025. FURTHER ANALYSIS OF THE FAILED VALVE IS ONGOING TO DETERMINE THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE FAILURE.    LABORATORY ANALYSIS AND POST-INCIDENT INVESTIGATION DETERMINED THE LEAK ORIGINATED FROM A FAILED O-RING WITHIN THE VALVE STEM ASSEMBLY INSIDE THE BONNET. THE FAILURE ALLOWED PRESSURIZED NATURAL GAS TO MIGRATE FROM THE PRESSURE BOUNDARY INTO THE VALVE STEM GREASE BEARING CAVITY WHICH WAS EQUIPPED WITH A ZERK-TYPE GREASED FITTING THAT INCLUDED A SAFETY VENT FEATURE INTENDED TO ALLOW AIR TO ESCAPE DURING GREASING OPERATIONS. ONCE THE O-RING FAILED IT ALLOWED AND UNOBSTRUCTED PATH FOR GAS TO MIGRATE FROM THE BONNET CAVITY INTO THE BELOW GRADE SPACE RESULTING IN A LEAK TO GRADE.
narrative_clean: on september 10, 2025, at approximately 08:49, a consumers energy employee investigating a potential leak indication confirmed the presence of a leak on line 2600 near the johnson road valve site. line 2600 is a 12-inch natural gas transmission pipeline located in lake city, michigan (missaukee county). consumers energy promptly initiated an isolation procedure to further assess the situation. the affected section of line 2600 was successfully isolated and vented to 0 psig by approximately 16:46 the same day. following excavation, the leak was discovered on a 12-inch ball valve (valve 2622). the valve was preserved in accordance with consumers energys failure investigation procedures and transported to the companys laboratory for analysis. the incident response and remediation efforts were conducted without injury to the public or operating personnel. remediation activities commenced on september 10, 2025. the scope of work included replacement of the 12-inch ball valve and approximately 9-feet of pipeline. the pipeline segment was returned to service on september 23, 2025. further analysis of the failed valve is ongoing to determine the root cause of the failure. laboratory analysis and post-incident investigation determined the leak originated from a failed o-ring within the valve stem assembly inside the bonnet. the failure allowed pressurized natural gas to migrate from the pressure boundary into the valve stem grease bearing cavity which was equipped with a zerk-type greased fitting that included a safety vent feature intended to allow air to escape during greasing operations. once the o-ring failed it allowed and unobstructed path for gas to migrate from the bonnet cavity into the below grade space resulting in a leak to grade.

NAME: WILLIAMS MLP OPERATING, LLC
NARRATIVE: THE PUTNAM WELL CONNECT INCIDENT OCCURRED ON OCTOBER 8, 2025, WHEN A LEAK DEVELOPED ON A 2014-ERA X52 STEEL GATHERING LINE IN NORTHEAST OHIO. THE FAILURE WAS IDENTIFIED AT A LOW POINT IN THE PIPELINE, WHERE A THROUGH-WALL PIT (1/4 PINHOLE) ALLOWED NATURAL GAS AND NATURAL GAS LIQUIDS TO BE RELEASED WHICH MIGRATED TOWARDS A DRY TRIBUTARY. THE IMMEDIATE RESPONSE INCLUDED ISOLATING AND BLOWING DOWN THE LINE, DEPLOYING CONTAINMENT AND VACUUM TRUCKS, AND INITIATING SOIL REMEDIATION AND ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING.    THE INVESTIGATION IS ON-GOING, HOWEVER PRELIMINARILY THE MOST PROBABLE ROOT CAUSE WAS INTERNAL CORROSION, LIKELY MICROBIAL-INDUCED CORROSION (MIC). ON DECEMBER 13, 2025, A SMART TOOL (ILI) WAS RUN ON THE PUTMAN LATERAL AND IDENTIFIED FIVE TOTAL AREAS, INCLUDING THE FAILURE SEGMENT, TOTALING APPROXIMATELY 1,000 FEET OF PIPELINE THAT WAS CUT OUT AND REPLACED IN APRIL/MAY 2026. THE 3-FOOT SECTION CONTAINING THE FAILURE LOCATION WAS SENT TO ACUREN IN MAGNOLIA, TEXAS FOR METALLURGICAL ANALYSIS ON MAY 15, 2026. THE PIPELINE WAS PLACED BACK IN SERVICE ON JUNE 12, 2026.     ON JUNE 29, 2026, THE FAILURE ANALYSIS REPORT WAS RECEIVED FROM ACUREN.  THE REPORT CONCLUDES THAT THE LEAK COINCIDED WITH A REGION OF INTERNAL CORROSION APPEARING AS A CIRCULAR PIT AT THE 6 OCLOCK POSITION. ACUREN TESTED FOR BACTERIA AND BASED ON THE RESULTS, THE INTERNAL CORROSION PRESENT IS LIKELY NOT THE RESULT OF MICROBIAL INFLUENCED CORROSION (MIC).   THE CIRCULAR, SMOOTH APPEARANCE IS CONSISTENT WITH UNDER DEPOSIT CORROSION.  THEREFORE, THE OBSERVED INTERNAL CORROSION PITTING, AND THE LEAK, OCCURRED DUE TO DEBRIS, SUCH AS SAND, THAT SETTLED OUT ALONG THE BOTTOM OF THE PIPELINE CREATING A LOCAL CORROSIVE ENVIRONMENT ALONG THE BOTTOM OF THE PIPE.
narrative_clean: the putnam well connect incident occurred on october 8, 2025, when a leak developed on a 2014-era x52 steel gathering line in northeast ohio. the failure was identified at a low point in the pipeline, where a through-wall pit (1/4 pinhole) allowed natural gas and natural gas liquids to be released which migrated towards a dry tributary. the immediate response included isolating and blowing down the line, deploying containment and vacuum trucks, and initiating soil remediation and environmental monitoring. the investigation is on-going, however preliminarily the most probable root cause was internal corrosion, likely microbial-induced corrosion (mic). on december 13, 2025, a smart tool (ili) was run on the putman lateral and identified five total areas, including the failure segment, totaling approximately 1,000 feet of pipeline that was cut out and replaced in april/may 2026. the 3-foot section containing the failure location was sent to acuren in magnolia, texas for metallurgical analysis on may 15, 2026. the pipeline was placed back in service on june 12, 2026. on june 29, 2026, the failure analysis report was received from acuren. the report concludes that the leak coincided with a region of internal corrosion appearing as a circular pit at the 6 oclock position. acuren tested for bacteria and based on the results, the internal corrosion present is likely not the result of microbial influenced corrosion (mic). the circular, smooth appearance is consistent with under deposit corrosion. therefore, the observed internal corrosion pitting, and the leak, occurred due to debris, such as sand, that settled out along the bottom of the pipeline creating a local corrosive environment along the bottom of the pipe.

NAME: ENERGY TRANSFER COMPANY
NARRATIVE: ON OCTOBER 22, 2025, AT 6:30 A.M. WHILE INVESTIGATING LINE SHUT-INS AND COMPRESSOR SHUTDOWNS DUE TO HIGH O2 ISSUES AN OPERATIONS (OPS) TECH OBSERVED THAT THE HEADLEE DISCHARGE LINE HAD 40 PSIG WHEN THE NORMAL OPERATING PRESSURE IS 1250 PISIG. THE LINE WAS SHUT IN, AND FIELD PERSONNEL BEGAN TO INVESTIGATE THE SEVERITY OF THE LEAK. AT 11:15 A.M. OPERATIONS MADE AN INITIAL DETERMINATION THAT THE LEAK MAY EXCEED THE REPORTABLE THRESHOLD AND NOTIFIED DOT COMPLIANCE. THE NRC NOTIFICATION WAS MADE AT 12:06 P.M. TXRRC NOTIFICATION WAS MADE AT 12:15 P.M. CONFIRMED DISCOVERY WAS AT 9:39 P.M. WHEN OPERATIONS DETERMINED THE VOLUME LOST TO BE 7.784 MMCF.     ON NOVEMBER 25, 2025, ACUREN INSPECTION INC. COMPLETED THE METALLURGICAL TESTING. THE TESTS CONCLUDED:    1. THE FAILURE COINCIDED WITH A REGION OF INTERNAL CORROSION PRESENT ALONG THE TOP OF THE PIPE. THE INTERNAL CORROSION OCCURRED IN A MESA-LIKE PATTERN WITH SMALL, CIRCULAR PITS.   2. THE OBSERVED INTERNAL CORROSION OCCURRED IN AN ENVIRONMENT CONTAINING CARBON DIOXIDE AND WATER, COMBINING TO FORM CARBONIC ACID RESULTING IN SIDERITE.   3. THE PIPE WAS CONSISTENT WITH NOMINAL 12-INCH OD X 0.250-INCH WT, API 5L GRADE X52 MATERIAL MANUFACTURED VIA THE HF-ERW PROCESS WITH A POST WELD HEAT TREATMENT. narrative_clean: on october 22, 2025, at 6:30 a.m. while investigating line shut-ins and compressor shutdowns due to high o2 issues an operations (ops) tech observed that the headlee discharge line had 40 psig when the normal operating pressure is 1250 pisig. the employee notified the ops supervisor who then verified the line pressure with another ops tech located at the lupin station. at 6:40 a.m. the ops team began a leak investigation on the 7406642 - lupin to headlee. at 09:37 a.m. field personnel pinpoint the location the leak. the line was shut in, and field personnel began to investigate the severity of the leak. at 11:15 a.m. operations made an initial determination that the leak may exceed the reportable threshold and notified dot compliance. the nrc notification was made at 12:06 p.m. txrrc notification was made at 12:15 p.m. confirmed discovery was at 9:39 p.m. when operations determined the volume lost to be 7.784 mmcf. on november 25, 2025, acuren inspection inc. completed the metallurgical testing. the tests concluded: 1. the failure coincided with a region of internal corrosion present along the top of the pipe. the internal corrosion occurred in a mesa-like pattern with small, circular pits. 2. the observed internal corrosion occurred in an environment containing carbon dioxide and water, combining to form carbonic acid resulting in siderite. 3. the pipe was consistent with nominal 12-inch od x 0.250-inch wt, api 5l grade x52 material manufactured via the hf-erw process with a post weld heat treatment. energy transfer's internal investigation concluded that the root cause of the incident was liquid/water content from producers entering the pipeline. plan to prevent recurrence: implement a cleaning pig schedule to sweep any liquid build up in the pipeline and a corrosion treatment/monitoring program.

NAME: CAPROCK MIDSTREAM SOUTH TEXAS LLC
NARRATIVE: AT 6:23 P.M. ON DECEMBER 10, 2025, A CONTRACTOR WAS NOTIFIED OF A POSSIBLE PIPELINE INCIDENT BY A MEMBER OF THE PUBLIC. THE CONTRACTOR CALLED THE OPERATOR, AND THE OPERATOR CHECKED LINE PRESSURE IN SCADA TO INVESTIGATE LEAK REPORT. OPERATOR IDENTIFIED UPSTREAM AND DOWNSTREAM VALVES BASED ON APPROXIMATE LOCATION REPORTED BY THE PUBLIC. AT 6:34 P.M., OPERATOR CONTACTED THE CONTROL ROOM AND INSTRUCTED THEM TO REMOTELY CLOSE THE UPSTREAM VALVE DUE TO A POTENTIAL LINE BREAK AND STARTED DRIVE DOWNSTREAM MANUAL VALVE LOCATION. CONTROL ROOM PERSONNEL EXECUTED THE COMMAND AND CONFIRMED THE UPSTREAM VALVE WAS SUCCESSFULLY CLOSED. FOLLOWING VALVE CLOSURE, LINE PRESSURE DROPPED SIGNIFICANTLY, AND UPSTREAM PRESSURE WAS CONTINUOUSLY MONITORED. AT 7:34 P.M., OPERATOR PERSONNEL CLOSED THE MANUAL DOWNSTREAM VALVE TO FURTHER ISOLATE THE AFFECTED SEGMENT. OPERATOR ARRIVED AT THE INCIDENT SITE AT APPROXIMATELY 8:00 P.M. TO CONDUCT A PRELIMINARY ON-SITE EVALUATION AND BEGIN PIPELINE REPAIRS. AT 9:01 P.M., THE OPERATOR DETERMINED THE EVENT MET THE PHMSA AND RAILROAD COMMISSION OF TEXAS (RRC) IMMEDIATE NOTICE REPORTING THRESHOLDS (CONFIRMED DISCOVERY) DUE TO AN UNINTENTIONAL LOSS EXCEEDING 3 MMCF. CREWS MOBILIZED TO THE SITE TO CUT OUT AND REPLACE FAILED SECTION OF PIPELINE. ON DECEMBER 16, 2025, AT APPROXIMATELY 7:00 P.M., REPAIRS WERE COMPLETED AND THE PIPELINE WAS PURGED. THE LINE WAS RETURNED TO SERVICE ON DECEMBER 17, 2025, AT APPROXIMATELY 5:00 A.M.  FOLLOWING THE INCIDENT, THE FAILED PIPE SEGMENT WAS REMOVED AND SENT TO BAKER RISK FOR A METALLURGICAL ANALYSIS. THE FINAL REPORT IS EXPECTED BY THE END OF JANUARY, AND A SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT WILL BE SUBMITTED WITH INFORMATION ON THE CAUSE OF THE INCIDENT.  2/3/2026 SUPPLEMENTAL - THE METALLURGICAL LAB REPORT FROM BAKER RISK WAS RECEIVED ON 1/21/2026. IT WAS DETERMINED EXTERNAL CORROSION WAS THE CAUSE OF THE FAILURE. THE FOLLOWING SUMMARIZES THE CONCLUSIONS OF THE METALLURGICAL ANALYSIS REPORT:  1. THE PIPELINE WAS DAMAGED BY PITTING CORROSION.  2. THE PITTING CORROSION WAS LOCATED IN THE VICINITY OF THE 6 OCLOCK POSITION ON THE PIPELINE.  3. THE PITTING CORROSION AREAS COINCIDED WITH THE LONGITUDINAL WELD SEAM STARTING ~36 INCHES DOWNSTREAM OF GIRTH WELD 12460 OVER A LENGTH OF ~84 INCHES.  4. THE WELD SEAM WAS PREFERENTIALLY ATTACKED WITHIN THE PITTED AREA.  5. THE RUPTURE INITIATED DUE TO WALL LOSS AT THE INITIATION SITE.  6. ONCE INITIATED, THE RUPTURE PROPAGATED BY DUCTILE OVERLOAD FAILURE.  7. THE PIPELINE RUPTURE FOLLOWED THE WELD SEAM IN THE JOINT BETWEEN GIRTH WELD 12460 AND GIRTH WELD 12470.  8. THE RUPTURE PROPAGATED IN A DUCTILE MANNER BOTH UPSTREAM AND DOWNSTREAM FROM THE ORIGIN, TERMINATING ~ 4-FEET UPSTREAM OF GIRTH WELD 12460 AND JUST BEYOND GIRTH WELD 12470 ON THE DOWNSTREAM END.  9. THE ILI DATA IS GENERALLY CONSISTENT WITH THE PRESENT OBSERVATIONS AND MEASUREMENTS BUT UNDERESTIMATED THE SEVERITY OF THE PITTING. AT LEAST 56% WALL LOSS WAS PHYSICALLY MEASURED, WHEREAS THE ILI DATA ESTIMATED A MAXIMUM LOSS OF 39%.  NOTE: CAPROCK ACQUIRED THIS PIPELINE ON OCTOBER 1, 2025, AND IMMEDIATELY INITIATED A 5-WEEK REMEDIATION PROJECT (10/15/2025-11/20/2025) BASED ON THE RESULTS OF THE PREVIOUS OWNERS ILI RUN IN OCTOBER 2024.  AS A CORRECTIVE ACTION, CAPROCK HAS SCHEDULED ANOTHER ILI RUN ON THIS PIPELINE FOR THE WEEK OF FEBRUARY 9TH, 2026, AND WILL REVIEW AND ADDRESS DEFECTS OR ANOMALIES IN ACCORDANCE WITH 49 CFR 192.485(A)-(B).
narrative_clean: at 6:23 p.m. on december 10, 2025, a contractor was notified of a possible pipeline incident by a member of the public. the contractor called the operator, and the operator checked line pressure in scada to investigate leak report. operator identified upstream and downstream valves based on approximate location reported by the public. at 6:34 p.m., operator contacted the control room and instructed them to remotely close the upstream valve due to a potential line break and started drive downstream manual valve location. control room personnel executed the command and confirmed the upstream valve was successfully closed. following valve closure, line pressure dropped significantly, and upstream pressure was continuously monitored. at 7:34 p.m., operator personnel closed the manual downstream valve to further isolate the affected segment. operator arrived at the incident site at approximately 8:00 p.m. to conduct a preliminary on-site evaluation and begin pipeline repairs. at 9:01 p.m., the operator determined the event met the phmsa and railroad commission of texas (rrc) immediate notice reporting thresholds (confirmed discovery) due to an unintentional loss exceeding 3 mmcf. crews mobilized to the site to cut out and replace failed section of pipeline. on december 16, 2025, at approximately 7:00 p.m., repairs were completed and the pipeline was purged. the line was returned to service on december 17, 2025, at approximately 5:00 a.m. following the incident, the failed pipe segment was removed and sent to baker risk for a metallurgical analysis. the final report is expected by the end of january, and a supplemental report will be submitted with information on the cause of the incident. 2/3/2026 supplemental - the metallurgical lab report from baker risk was received on 1/21/2026. it was determined external corrosion was the cause of the failure. the following summarizes the conclusions of the metallurgical analysis report: 1. the pipeline was damaged by pitting corrosion. 2. the pitting corrosion was located in the vicinity of the 6 oclock position on the pipeline. 3. the pitting corrosion areas coincided with the longitudinal weld seam starting ~36 inches downstream of girth weld 12460 over a length of ~84 inches. 4. the weld seam was preferentially attacked within the pitted area. 5. the rupture initiated due to wall loss at the initiation site. 6. once initiated, the rupture propagated by ductile overload failure. 7. the pipeline rupture followed the weld seam in the joint between girth weld 12460 and girth weld 12470. 8. the rupture propagated in a ductile manner both upstream and downstream from the origin, terminating ~ 4-feet upstream of girth weld 12460 and just beyond girth weld 12470 on the downstream end. 9. the ili data is generally consistent with the present observations and measurements but underestimated the severity of the pitting. at least 56% wall loss was physically measured, whereas the ili data estimated a maximum loss of 39%. note: caprock acquired this pipeline on october 1, 2025, and immediately initiated a 5-week remediation project (10/15/2025-11/20/2025) based on the results of the previous owners ili run in october 2024. as a corrective action, caprock has scheduled another ili run on this pipeline for the week of february 9th, 2026, and will review and address defects or anomalies in accordance with 49 cfr 192.485(a)-(b).

NAME: KINDER MORGAN TEXAS PIPELINE CO
NARRATIVE: AT THE TIME OF THE INCIDENT, THE KMTP UNIT 2 SUCTION AND DISCHARGE VALVES FAILED IN THEIR LAST COMMANDED STATE (OPEN), WHILE THE VENT VALVE FAILED TO ITS DESIGNED FAIL-SAFE POSITION (OPEN). THE STATION SUCTION AND DISCHARGE VALVES ALSO REMAINED OPEN. UPON OCCURRENCE OF THE UNIT 2 PROCESSOR MAJOR NON-RECOVERABLE FAULT (MNRF), THE LAST VALID PROCESS VALUES AND EQUIPMENT STATUSES WERE RETAINED IN BOTH THE STATION CONTROLLER AND SCADA SYSTEM, RESULTING IN UNIT 2 CONTINUING TO DISPLAY A RUNNING STATUS DESPITE THE LOSS OF PROCESSOR FUNCTIONALITY.  A SUBSEQUENT INSPECTION OF THE UNIT 2 PLC ENCLOSURE IDENTIFIED THE PRESENCE OF A RODENT WITHIN THE ENCLOSURE. EVIDENCE OF RODENT URINE CONTAMINATION WAS OBSERVED ON THE PLC HARDWARE AND ASSOCIATED ELECTRICAL COMPONENTS. THE CONTAMINATION CAUSED AN ELECTRICAL SHORT CIRCUIT, RESULTING IN COMMUNICATION FAILURES AND LOSS OF PROCESSOR FUNCTIONALITY. THE APPARENT ROOT CAUSE OF THE INCIDENT WAS IMPROPER ENCLOSURE INSTALLATION AND SEALING, WHICH ALLOWED ENVIRONMENTAL AND WILDLIFE INTRUSION THROUGH UNSEALED OR INADEQUATELY SEALED ENCLOSURE OPENINGS.

NAME: EQT MIDSTREAM COMPANY LLC
NARRATIVE: ON 5/28/2026, EQT WAS CONDUCTING MOWING OPERATIONS OUTSIDE THE CALLISTO CS FENCELINE, NEAR THE PAJUPG075 (FKA NIJUS021) AND PAJUPG081 (FKA NIJUS029) RIGHT-OF-WAY. WHILE MOWING, THE EQT OPERATOR (EMPLOYEE EE #1) WAS INJURED BY SUDDEN FIRE. THE EQT OPERATOR ESCAPED FURTHER INJURY BY REMOVING HIMSELF FROM THE SCENE AND SEEKING HELP INSIDE THE CALLISTO CS OFFICE. THE INJURED OPERATOR INFORMED EE #2 OF WHAT HAPPENED. ADDITIONALLY, EE #2 INSTRUCTED A CONTRACTOR WHO WAS PRESENT TO CONTACT THE INJURED EE #1S SUPERVISOR, EE #3, AS WELL AS EE #2S SUPERVISOR (EE #4).  AT ~12:26PM, EE #2 CALLED MIDSTREAM GAS CONTROL (MGC) TO REPORT A FIRE NEAR PIPELINE PAJUPG081, REQUESTING THE ISOLATION OF THE PIPELINE. EE #2 ADVISED MGC THAT AN EE HAD SUSTAINED BURN INJURIES TO HIS HAND, AND THAT FIRE/EMS WAS ENROUTE TO THE SITE. MGC CONTACTED THE PRODUCTION CONTROL CENTER (PCC) AND REQUESTED THAT THE UPSTREAM CLEMENTE MM BE SHUT-IN. ADDITIONALLY, MGC SHUT DOWN COMPRESSOR UNIT #4 DOWNSTREAM OF THE SITE.  AT ~12:28PM, EE #4 CONTACTED THE EQT HOTLINE AND WAS CONNECTED WITH EE #5 FROM EHS AT 12:32PM, WHOM HE MADE AWARE OF THE SITUATION. AT ~12:33PM, MGC NOTIFIED EE #6 FROM MIDSTREAM COMPLIANCE AND SUPERINTENDENT EE #3. EE #3 ADVISED PIPELINE OPERATORS AND SUPERVISORS TO HEAD TO THE SITE.  TWO OPERATIONS SUPERVISORS (EES # 7 AND 8) ARRIVED ON-SITE AT ~12:45PM, WITH EE #7 SERVING AS THE OPERATIONS COORDINATOR FOR THE EVENT. AT APPROXIMATELY THE SAME TIME, EMERGENCY RESPONDERS ARRIVED ON-SITE. EE #7 ASSESSED THE SITUATION, AND INSTRUCTED THE FIRE CHIEF TO STAGE THEIR EQUIPMENT, DEPLOY HOSES, AND AWAIT FURTHER INSTRUCTION. THE FIRE CHIEF CONFIRMED THAT NO SUPPRESSION ACTIVITIES WOULD BE INITIATED UNTIL AUTHORIZATION WAS GIVEN. EMS PERSONNEL WERE DIRECTED TO THE CALLISTO CS OFFICE TO CARE FOR THE INJURED EE.  AT ~12:55PM, EE #7, WITH THE ASSISTANCE OF EE #8, BEGAN TO COORDINATE ON-SITE EFFORTS TO ISOLATE THE SOURCE OF THE LEAK, IN CONJUNCTION WITH MGC. EE #7 DIRECTED PIPELINE OPERATORS TO BEGIN CLOSING MULTIPLE VALVES ON PAJUPG081, PAJUPG075, AND PAJUPG086 (FKA NIJUS041) TO ISOLATE POTENTIAL SOURCES OF GAS. NARRATIVE: on august 14, 2022, a crew from frontier earthworks llc was clearing a pasture near prineville, oregon to install a new irrigation ditch for a cattle operation. the crew was supervised by foreman david "dave" murray and included equipment operator larry harris, who was operating a john deere 750e excavator. the work site was situated on the southeast quarter of section 12, township 25 north, range 13 east, in crook county. at approximately 0730, harris began back-filling a trench that had been dug earlier in the day. unaware that a 12-inch, carbon-steel, high-pressure natural gas pipeline (line designation: west-zone iab90234) was buried at a depth of 30 inches and operating at 825 psig, he inadvertently struck the pipe with the excavator bucket. the impact ruptured the pipe, releasing an estimated 5.3 mcf of gas before the automatic shut-off valve activated. the gas ignited when it encountered a nearby diesel generator, creating a brief fireball that singed nearby vegetation. no injuries were reported, but service to the town of prineville was interrupted for several hours. an investigation later determined that frontier earthworks had failed to submit a one-call notification to the oregon one-call center prior to commencing excavation, a requirement that would have prompted line locate marking and could have prevented the strike.

NARRATIVE: a 24-inch carbon steel transmission line operating at 1150 psi, located 2 mi east of bayou city, texas, was compromised during the april 2025 tornado outbreak. the tornado produced wind speeds exceeding 150 mph and generated a 5-foot high surge of water and debris that overtopped the low-lying floodplain. the surge lifted a section of the adjacent earthen embankment, exposing the pipeline's 12-inch girth weld at a river crossing. the force of the moving debris struck the weld, shearing the surrounding pipe wall and creating a 3-inch gash. the pipe's automatic shut-down valve failed to close due to water intrusion in the actuator housing, allowing gas to escape into the flooded area. initial leak detection systems did not trigger alarms because the acoustic sensors were submerged. response crews could not access the site for 72 hours because the floodwaters remained 4 ft deep and the area was declared unsafe. once water receded, divers inspected the damage, confirming a full-depth breach and confirming that the flanged tie-in at the downstream pigging station had been displaced. the line was isolated and a temporary bypass was installed pending repair.

NARRATIVE: march 3, 2025 - a pipeline incident occurred on line lp-57, a wellstream energy llc transmission line, in a remote class 2 location approximately two miles southeast of the town of ridgefield, columbia county, oregon. the 24-inch, api 5l x80 steel pipe, operating at 850 psi, was traversing a narrow mountain valley when a heavy, prolonged rainstorm triggered a landslide that displaced the right-of-way by about three feet. the resulting ground movement exerted a lateral load on the pipe, causing a longitudinal crack near a field girth weld at milepost 112.4. operations personnel received an automated scada alarm indicating a sudden pressure drop to 420 psi and immediately closed valve lp-57-02 to isolate the segment. the downstream valve was also shut, and the section was depressurized and purged. field crews accessed the site, confirmed a 15-inch crack extending 8 inches along the weld, and installed a temporary clamp. a full isolation valve was set, and a hot-tapping unit was mobilized for repair. the line remained out of service pending excavation, pipe replacement, and geotechnical stabilization of the slope. incident reporting was completed on march 8, 2025, and a post-incident review recommended enhanced slope monitoring and the addition of a buried flexible joint in the landslide-prone segment.

NARRATIVE: on february 14, 2024 at approximately 0845 hrs a 24-inch api 5l steel transmission line owned by midwest energy in the hills of western pennsylvania experienced a rupture after a severe ice storm. a combination of 2-inch ice accretion on surrounding trees and a 55-mph wind gust caused a 45-foot ponderosa pine to fall onto the right-hand side of the buried line, crushing the pipe at a 30-degree bend near milepost 12.7. the line was operating at a normal operating pressure of 1180 psi and the impact created a 3-inch longitudinal split, releasing an estimated 4,200 mcf of natural gas into the shallow soil. field crews initiated emergency shut-in of the adjacent block valve (bv-34) within eight minutes, and the gas was diverted to the parallel 20-inch line. post-incident investigation revealed that the pipe segment had not been coated with an anti-icing epoxy, and the surrounding drainage ditch had become clogged with snow melt, increasing soil saturation and reducing pipe support. corrective actions include installing additional protective backfill, applying ice-resistant coating to vulnerable pipe sections, and clearing drainage ditches before the next winter season.

NARRATIVE: on may 14, 2025, at approximately 03:27 cst, a severe thunderstorm passed over the midland compression station in jackson county, missouri. the station, operated by western gas transmission, llc (operator id 8421), is equipped with a 30-inch carbon steel mainline operating at 720 psi and a 12-inch downstream distribution line at 210 psi. a direct lightning strike hit the station's primary control building, damaging the 480 v main switchgear and a 250 amp circuit breaker protecting the plc system. the loss of control power caused an automatic shutdown of the 5-stage centrifugal compressors, but the backup diesel generators failed to latch onto the bus within the required 10-second window due to a mis-set voltage sensing relay. as a result, the low-pressure safety valve on the 30-inch line opened, releasing an estimated 3.8 mmcf of natural gas into the surrounding area. emergency response teams from the local fire department and the agency for toxic substances arrived within 12 minutes. the gas plume dissipated without ignition, and no injuries were reported. restoration crews repaired the switchgear, re-programmed the relay, and performed a full functional test of the backup generators before returning the station to service at 17:02 cst.

NARRATIVE: on 4 august 2022 at approximately 07:14 utc, western pipelines inc. received an urgent call from the county sheriff's office reporting a sudden collapse of a 24-inch, schedule 40 carbon steel transmission line crossing the south fork of the colorado river near milepost 132. the line, normally operating at 1150 psig transporting dry natural gas, had been isolated for routine maintenance two weeks prior, but the isolation valves on the upstream and downstream mainline remained closed. field crews arrived within 45 minutes and observed a deep, water-filled trench exposing a 30-foot section of pipe that had been ripped from its supports. investigation revealed that a rapid snow-melt flood, intensified by a localized thunderstorm, caused scour of the riverbank, removing the bedding material and creating a free-span condition. the ensuing vortex-induced vibration led to a fatigue crack at the toe of a longitudinal seam, ultimately rupturing the pipe. the rupture released gas, which ignited briefly before being extinguished by the river's flow; no fire persisted. western pipelines promptly notified the national response center, phmsa, and the state oil and gas commission, and began emergency isolation and pressure relief procedures while environmental crews monitored the river for contamination.

NARRATIVE: on june 22, 2025, at 0815 hours, field operators observed a sudden pressure drop on the 24-inch carbon steel mainline (api 5l grade b) serving the highland valley gas gathering system. the pipeline, rated for 900 psig, was operating at 750 psig when an automatic shutdown was triggered. visual inspection revealed a 4-foot section of the pipe exposed at the base of a steep ravine where a rapid snowmelt flood had scoured the earthen cover and deposited a thick layer of ice. ice expansion exerted lateral forces that fractured the pipe wall at the welded joint identified as tag-34-b. emergency response teams were dispatched, the area was isolated, and a temporary bypass valve was installed to restore limited service. after water levels receded, a crew excavated the damaged segment, removed the broken pipe, and installed a new 24-inch x 12-foot replacement section with a reinforced steel sleeve and additional concrete backfill to mitigate future scour. hydrostatic testing to 1200 psig confirmed integrity. the line was returned to normal operation at 1630 hours on june 23, 2025. post-event review cited extreme melt-water flow combined with freeze-thaw cycles as the primary natural force contributing to the failure.

NARRATIVE: on march 14, 2025, southwestern interstate energy corp (si ec) 36-inch x 3500 psi stainless steel line #4054 in north dakota experienced an accidental break during a routine road maintenance project. the line was located beneath state highway 15, approximately 400 m east of the town of fargo. at 09:12 am local time, a heavy-duty hydraulic excavator used by the state department of transportation was operating on the roadway shoulder. the operator inadvertently struck a 2-foot high concrete retaining wall adjacent to the pipeline. the impact transmitted a force of approximately 2.5 kips to the wall, causing a 3-inch diameter gouge in the pipe wall at the junction of the 4-inch pig leg. at 09:18 am, the automatic pressure control valve (apcv) on section 4054-01 shut in at 3 250 psi, triggering a partial loss of pressure. at 09:23 am, the pipeline monitoring system reported a drop in pressure to 2 100 psi and a rise in differential pressure across the valve. the on-site operator crew mobilized the incident response team and notified the state emergency dispatch. by 09:45 am, a crew of 8 engineers from si ec arrived and performed a visual inspection; the gouged area was identified. by 10:07 am, the pipe was isolated, and the pig leg was sealed with a temporary weld. at 10:30 am, a 2-ton jackhammer crew from the state department of transportation ceased all excavation operations and cleared the area. at 11:15 am, the pipe was inspected by a licensed welding inspector, who approved a 50-ft weld repair. the repair was completed by 12:30 pm, and the line was re-pressurised to 3 500 psi under controlled conditions. the incident was reported to the national regulator within 24 hours, and a post-incident investigation found that the force from the excavator impact was the sole cause of the pipeline damage. no secondary failures or corrosion issues were identified.

NARRATIVE: on september 12, 2023, at approximately 14:30 local time, a 24-inch natural gas transmission line suffered a rupture in central county. the incident was triggered when a third-party heavy equipment operator struck the pipe with an excavator bucket while conducting grading work for a private driveway expansion near the facility right of way. the operator had failed to contact the utility locating service prior to starting work, despite the presence of clearly visible yellow property markers and the required one-week notice window having passed. the impact punctured the carbon steel pipe wall, resulting in an immediate jet leak and rapid pressure drop from the operating pressure of 700 psig to near atmospheric levels within minutes. an estimated 12,500 mcf of natural gas escaped before emergency isolation valves were remotely closed by transmission monitoring center personnel. upon arrival, local emergency response teams found no immediate fire or explosion, but the area was cleared due to the strong odor and high-velocity release. field crews installed a temporary stopple to seal the leak and bypass the damaged section using a spliced connection with a 24-inch x 1 ft coupon of seamless pipe. permanent repairs involved digging out the affected area, removing 12 feet of damaged pipe, and welding in a new replacement segment using btw joint welding procedures. integrity testing via ultrasonic thickness mapping confirmed remaining wall health in the surrounding areas. investigation determined the equipment operator was working within 5 feet of the pipeline without proper shoring or direct visual supervision of the dig, violating safe excavation practices.

NARRATIVE: during routine maintenance on the 24-inch transmission line at the grand prairie compressor station in may 2012, operators failed to verify the isolation of an upstream inventory trap. as the work crew opened a manual valve to relieve pressure for a flange replacement, residual gas escaped through a small gap in the packing gland of an adjacent 6-inch line. a slow leak persisted for approximately forty minutes before being detected by a portable gas monitor. when the emergency slow-down was initiated, the sudden drop in system pressure caused the standing liquid in the low-point trap to flash into vapor rapidly. the resulting two-phase flow swept through the 18-inch inlet piping, striking the outlet check valve of compressor unit 3 with significant force. the impact failed the check valve disc seal, allowing uncontrolled backflow into the hot-gas header. this backflow interacted with the still-rotating turbine blades, triggering a rapid spool down. although no fire erupted, the unexpected hydraulic shock damaged the internal components of the turbine seal system. the unit was taken offline for a full teardown inspection. the investigation revealed that the standard operating procedure for multi-point isolation did not explicitly require a positive pressure verification step for the inventory trap, a gap identified during the root cause analysis. all personnel involved were retrained on enhanced isolation protocols, and the check valve assembly was replaced with a hardened alloy component rated for higher differential pressures. the incident was reported to the texas railroad commission and the nrc within the required timeframe, noting no significant environmental impact beyond the minor stain observed within the fenced facility perimeter.

NARRATIVE: during a scheduled valve replacement on the 24" x70 grade b carbon steel mainline at the mid-river crossing, the field supervisor ordered a temporary isolation of the line and instructed the crew to vent the segment to atmosphere. the venting procedure was carried out using a 4" flanged vent stack that had been previously de-rated for a maximum pressure of 500 psi, but the line was still pressurized to 850 psi due to an oversight in the pressure relief sequencing. when the crew opened the vent, high-velocity gas escaped through the undersized stack, striking a nearby portable generator set that was idling for power. the generator ignited the released natural gas, producing a brief flame front that singed a section of the work platform and damaged a crew-owned hydraulic jack. no personnel were injured, but the generator and jack were destroyed, and the incident resulted in a loss of approximately $42 000 in equipment. the line was subsequently isolated, depressurized, and repaired with a new vent stack of appropriate rating. the event was documented and reported to the phmsa under the property-damage reporting threshold.

NARRATIVE: during a routine inline inspection on 03/14/24, a 30-inch x70 grade b pipeline carrying 720 psi of natgas experienced an unexpected pressure drop of approximately 180 psi over a 2-mile segment near milepost 145. the pigging crew reported a sudden increase in pig resistance and audible grinding noises as the tool passed the location. immediate isolation of the line was performed using the nearest upstream and downstream shut-in valves, and the affected section was depressurized to 50 psi for safety. first responders from the site emergency team arrived within ten minutes, establishing a 100-ft perimeter. a small venting plume of natural gas was observed, but no ignition occurred. after a thorough visual inspection, a 2-inch longitudinal split was identified in the pipe wall, likely caused by a combination of thermal fatigue and stress corrosion cracking, though the exact initiating factor could not be conclusively determined. the incident was reported to the pipeline safety authority, and a temporary bypass was installed while a detailed metallurgical analysis is underway. recommendations include revising integrity management intervals for high-risk segments, implementing enhanced corrosion monitoring, and reviewing recent temperature cycling data for similar pipe sections.

NARRATIVE: on april 17, 2025 at approximately 14:35 hrs a maintenance crew was performing a scheduled valve replacement on a 24-in carbon steel pipeline transporting 650 psi natural gas near the river bend segment. the valve was isolated with a lock-out/tag-out procedure and a portable gas detector was positioned upstream. while the crew removed the 12-in gate valve, the supervisory control system automatically initiated a pressure reset on the main line after a transient loss of signal from the remote transmitter. the sudden pressure increase to 720 psi propagated through the isolated section before the valve was fully sealed, causing a rapid surge that ruptured a 6-in branch pipe that had been previously cut for pig launcher installation. a high-energy jet of gas escaped, igniting when it contacted a nearby welding torch that had been left on standby. the flash resulted in minor burns to two technicians and a small fire that was extinguished by the on-site fire suppression system within five minutes. an investigation team was convened on the same day; findings highlighted a lack of coordination between the control system reset and the manual isolation work, an outdated pressure relief setting on the branch line, and the presence of an active ignition source in the immediate vicinity of the isolated pipe. corrective actions include revising lock-out/tag-out protocols to require system interlock verification, updating relief valve setpoints to 800 psi, and implementing a hot-work clearance checklist for all maintenance zones. the incident was reported to the pipeline safety authority and is pending final review.

NARRATIVE: on july 3, 2024 a routine pig run on the 24-inch, 70-grade carbon steel main (design pressure 1 250 psig) detected an unexpected pressure drop to 820 psig at mile-12. field crews were dispatched and used handheld gas detectors, confirming a faint methane plume near the right-of-way. the segment was isolated by closing the upstream and downstream block valves and the area was secured with a 30-meter exclusion zone. investigation of the exposed pipe revealed a localized gouge approximately 2 inches deep and 4 inches long on the external coating, likely caused by a recent heavy-equipment maneuver that displaced a backfill rock. the damaged section was cut out and a 24-inch, 70-grade steel replacement spool was welded in place, followed by non-destructive testing of the welds and reinstatement of the coating system. additional bracing was installed around the pipe at the site of the incident to prevent future mechanical impact. a temporary increase in patrols of the right-of-way was ordered, and the maintenance schedule for coating inspections was revised to include quarterly visual checks in high-traffic zones.

NARRATIVE: on august 14, 2025, western pipelines received a telephone alert from a local landowner reporting a possible oil seepage near milepost 112.3 of the 24-inch api 5l carbon steel main that traverses the foothills of the green ridge. western field operations dispatched a leak detection crew at 06:45 am. upon arrival, the crew observed a thin sheen on the grass approximately 15 ft downstream of a recently installed road crossing. pressure at the upstream station was 850 psi, while downstream pressure read 430 psi, indicating a pressure drop of roughly 420 psi. the crew isolated the segment by closing the upstream block valve at milepost 111.9 and the downstream valve at milepost 112.7, and subsequently depressurized the isolated section to 5 psi. a visual inspection revealed a 0.4-inch crack in the pipe wall at the point where the crossing's concrete encasement had been repaired three months earlier. the cause of the crack is under investigation; possible factors include improper backfill compaction or residual stress from the recent repair. the affected pipe section was excavated, removed, and replaced with a new 24-inch api 5l pipe coated with a three-layer polyethylene system. the line was reinstated and pressure restored to normal operating levels at 15:20 hrs. the incident was logged as case number 842761 and reported to the nrc.

NARRATIVE: on 03/15/2024 a low-pressure leak was identified on a 24-inch api 5l x65 carbon steel transmission line operating at 850 psi near the riley ridge valve station in north dakota. the leak was first observed during a scheduled aerial patrol when a faint vapor plume was noted approximately 0.6 mi east of the station. ground crews were dispatched and, after confirming gas odor, commenced excavation. exposure revealed a 0.35-inch longitudinal crack at the toe of a girth weld on a recently installed pipe segment that had been placed in 2019 during a capacity expansion. visual inspection showed no obvious corrosion, impact damage, or external stress. the affected pipe section was isolated, the cracked weld cut out, and a 15-foot splice was installed using a reinforced sleeve. the removed pipe and weld coupon were sent to an independent metallurgical laboratory for failure analysis. preliminary reports indicate the fracture surface exhibits intergranular features suggestive of a possible hydrogen-induced cracking mechanism, though no definitive source of hydrogen has been identified. the investigation remains open pending full laboratory results. meanwhile, the operator has initiated a review of recent welding procedures and post-weld heat-treatment records to mitigate any similar occurrences.

NARRATIVE: the 20" carbon steel pipeline, grade api 5l x70, operating at 950 psi, was being cleared with a foam pig when the pigging crew noticed an abnormal pressure drop of 120 psi over a 3-minute interval. further inspection revealed that a previously installed temperature sensor housing had become dislodged during a recent unrelated subsea inspection by a third-party contractor using a remotely operated vehicle. the housing struck the pipe wall at station 14-b, creating a 0.75-inch gouge that compromised the pipe wall integrity. the breach allowed a low-density natural gas release into the surrounding water column, which was quickly detected by the pipeline's emergency shutdown system. the e s d system isolated the section at valve stations 13-a and 15-c, and the area was declared a hot work zone. divers were deployed to assess the damage, and a temporary clamp was installed to stop the leak until a replacement pipe segment could be fabricated. the incident required a 48-hour shutdown of the line, resulting in an estimated loss of 1.2 mmcfd of gas throughput. the root cause was determined to be unintended equipment impact by an external contractor during non-pipeline-related activities.

NARRATIVE: 04/22/2025 - at approximately 1430 hrs utc, a release was observed on the 24-inch, 600-psi x70 carbon steel mainline (segment a-b) of the mid-state transmission corridor, located near milepost 112.3 in the oak ridge valley. the incident was initially detected by the scm system, which recorded a sudden drop in downstream pressure from 598 psi to 432 psi and a corresponding increase in acoustic emission signals. field crews arrived within 45 minutes and confirmed a visible plume of natural gas emanating from a ~3-inch longitudinal crack in the pipe wall, approximately 12 feet below the ground surface. the line was isolated using the nearest mainline isolation valve (valve 4-a) and depressurized to 0 psi before a hot-tapping operation was performed. divers were deployed to expose the damaged section, and a plidco repair clamp was installed on 04/24/2025. the pipe was returned to service on 04/26/2025 after pressure testing to 650 psi. because the pipe segment had been in service for 18 years and no recent excavation activity was reported, the exact initiation mechanism of the crack could not be determined. further metallurgical analysis is pending. for further information contact jason murray, pipeline integrity manager, 816-555-0198, jason.murray@midstatepipelines.com.

NARRATIVE: while conducting a scheduled inline inspection on the 30-inch carbon steel main (api 5l x70) the pig became lodged near station 412+18 after encountering a buildup of scale and a small piece of corrosion product. the crew attempted to push the pig forward using the launch pump at 1 500 psi, but the pressure downstream rose to 2 200 psi and the pig remained immobile. a decision was made to open the vent manifold on the adjacent pig trap to relieve pressure. the vent valve was manually opened, but the release line was partially obstructed, causing a rapid pressure drop in the main while residual gas remained trapped behind the pig. when the clamp securing the vent manifold cover was loosened, the vent housing swung open with enough force to strike a technician standing on the platform, causing a bruised rib and minor lacerations. after the incident, the pig was recovered using a back-pull unit, and the obstructed vent line was cleared. the main was depressurized to 600 psi, inspected for damage, and returned to service after confirming no breach. the event was logged as incident #2026-1123 and reported to the safety office.

NARRATIVE: on 14 august 2024 a 30-in. api 5l x65 transmission pipeline located in western karnes county, tx experienced a rapid pressure surge that resulted in a gash approximately 0.75 in. in diameter on the mainline at station mr-12. the line, installed in 2005, operates at a maximum working pressure of 900 psi and is coated with three-layer polyethylene for corrosion protection. during routine maintenance, a subcontractor was tasked with cleaning the valve pit at the downstream pressure-reduction station. the crew inadvertently installed a temporary sandbag seal on the isolation valve instead of the specified steel block. when the control system commanded a normal blow-down to 400 psi, the valve remained partially closed, causing a sudden pressure differential of roughly 500 psi across the downstream section. the resulting water hammer induced a high-frequency stress wave that exceeded the pipe's fatigue limit, tearing the steel wall at a weld joint that had previously undergone a hot-tap installation. natural gas escaped for approximately six minutes before the automatic shut-down system isolated the segment. emergency responders evacuated a nearby mobile home park of 22 units as a precaution, and a 0.5-mile stretch of county road was closed pending repair. subsequent investigation highlighted the improper temporary seal as the primary factor, prompting a revision of field-procedure checklists.

NARRATIVE: incident description: on september 12, 2024 at approximately 07:42 local time, a venting event was reported at the silver creek gathering station on the 24-inch, 900-psig mainline serving the northern field. a 911 call from a nearby ranch indicated a strong odor of natural gas near the south-side pig trap. operations personnel arrived on site at 08:10 and observed continuous venting from the pig trap vent valve, which displayed a closed position on the hmi but was releasing gas at an estimated 4.8 mmscfd. the vent valve was manually isolated at 08:23, and the associated line was purged and depressurized by 09:01. the incident resulted in a total loss of approximately 6,120 mcf of gas before isolation. initial inspection revealed an unexpected fracture in the vent valve stem, likely caused by a foreign object that had entered the valve housing during a recent pigging operation. the object was identified as a piece of pigging sleeve metal that had broken off downstream. to mitigate future occurrences, a supplemental seal inspection program has been scheduled for all vent valve assemblies on the line, and an additional pressure-differential alarm will be added to the scada to detect abnormal vent flow. the root-cause investigation remains ongoing, and a supplemental report will be filed upon completion.

NARRATIVE: the 30-inch api 5l x70 pipeline ruptured during a routine pressure test at 850 psi, exceeding its design test pressure of 800 psi. the line was operating at 600 psi when the test was initiated. at approximately 14:20 local time the pressure gauge spiked to 860 psi and an audible pop was heard near the right-of-way marker at milepost 42.3. immediate shutdown was executed by closing the upstream and downstream block valves, isolating the 15-foot section of pipe. field crews arrived within 30 minutes and confirmed a gash approximately 8 inches long on the south side of the pipe, with a clear water ingress zone extending 3 feet downstream. the damaged segment was cut out, tagged, and placed on a nitrogen blanket for transport to the metallurgical lab. samples were sent to the western petroleum research institute for fractography, ultrasonic thickness mapping, and chemical analysis. preliminary lab results show deep pitting corrosion on the interior wall, reaching 45 % of the nominal wall thickness, and the presence of hydrogen sulfide corrosion products. tensile testing indicated the steel met api 5l x70 specifications, but micro-structural examination revealed localized grain boundary weakening. further investigation will include a review of cathodic protection records, recent soil moisture surveys, and possible wildlife activity in the area. remediation work is scheduled to begin next week, with plans to install additional concrete weight coating and a secondary protective sleeve over the affected right-of-way.

NARRATIVE: while performing a scheduled hydrostatic test on the northern segment of the 30-inch api 5l x70 transmission line (design pressure 1500 psi, test pressure 2250 psi) a sudden loss of pressure was observed at gauge station 12-b. the test crew halted the pump and isolated the section with the nearest block valve. inspection revealed that a recently installed 90-degree stainless-steel elbow (2-in-schedule 80) had fractured at the weld throat. the fracture surface showed a classic "cup-and-cone" pattern consistent with a brittle failure rather than overload. further examination of the weld joint indicated a lack of proper pre-heat during fabrication and an inadequate post-weld heat treatment, which had left residual tensile stresses in the base metal. the pipe segment was depressurized to atmospheric, the damaged elbow was removed, and a new 90-degree miter bend with correctly controlled welding procedures was installed. after a repeat hydrostatic test confirmed no further leakage, the line was returned to service at its normal operating pressure of 1200 psi. the incident was documented and the welding contractor was required to provide additional quality-assurance records for future work.

NARRATIVE: during a scheduled cathodic protection inspection on the 30-inch carbon steel transmission line (schedule 40, api 5l) that transports 850 psi of sweet natural gas from the processing plant to the distribution hub, the field crew installed a temporary bypass clamp on a corroded section of pipe near milepost 12.5. the clamp was rated for 1200 psi and the line was isolated with the mainline isolation valve (il-02) and a downstream block valve (bl-07) as per the lock-out/tag-out procedure. however, after the inspection crew completed the ultrasonic thickness measurements, the supervisor authorized a premature restart of the line to meet the day's throughput target. the bypass clamp had not been fully tightened and the secondary seal gasket was displaced during the clamp removal. when the line pressure was raised to 800 psi, the clamp failed, creating a rapid vent to the atmosphere for approximately 12 seconds. a nearby contractor was performing hot-work on an adjacent valve housing, and the escaping gas ignited, producing a flash fire that singed the contractor's coveralls and caused a minor facial burn. emergency shutdown was initiated, the leak was isolated, and the bypass clamp was replaced with a welded repair section. the incident was documented and a review of restart procedures was ordered.

NARRATIVE: a 24-inch carbon steel pipeline operating at 900 psi experienced a sudden pressure drop when a manually operated isolation valve failed to seat fully during routine maintenance. the valve stem had been inadvertently over-torqued during a previous inspection, causing the packing gland to deform and allowing a slow leak at the valve bonnet. operators observed a minor hydrocarbon vent to the surrounding grassland, triggering an automatic shutdown of the affected line segment. the leak was contained within 15 minutes by activating the emergency isolation system and deploying a portable containment boom. a hazmat crew arrived on scene, sampled the vapor, and confirmed that the released gas was below flammable limits. the valve was removed, the stem and packing replaced with new stainless-steel components rated for 1500 psi, and the line was pressure-tested to 1200 psi before returning to service. total downtime for the 2.4-mile loop was approximately 6 hours, and repair costs were estimated at $78 000, including labor, parts, and environmental monitoring. the incident was recorded as a non-fatal, non-injury event with no offsite impact.

NARRATIVE: on 6/5/24 at approximately 14:12 while conducting a scheduled pigging run on the 24-in sch 40 carbon steel main (design pressure 350 psi, operating at 300 psi), the automated pig launcher failed to retract after release. the launcher remained engaged, causing a rapid pressure rise as the pig was forced downstream. pressure sensors recorded an increase to 420 psi within two minutes, triggering the high-pressure alarm. the control system automatically opened the downstream isolation valve (dv-12) to relieve pressure, resulting in a brief vent of hydrocarbon vapor to the low-lying drainage swale. the vent dissipated within five minutes with no ignition source present. the incident was reported to the operations supervisor, joshua mendoza, and the integrity engineering lead, karen li. a rapid response team de-energized the segment, isolated dv-12, and performed a visual inspection. no visible damage to the pipe wall or the pig launcher was observed, and a portable pressure gauge confirmed the line pressure had returned to 290 psi after isolation. the launcher was removed for a full functional test, and a software patch was applied to the launch sequence logic. a follow-up report will be filed by the integrity team, and the segment will remain out of service pending a hydraulic test scheduled for 6/12/24.

NARRATIVE: during a scheduled pigging operation on the 30-inch, api 5l sch 40 carbon steel transmission line (design pressure 1250 psi, operating at 1150 psi, maop 1500 psi) a mis-set launch pressure caused the smart-pig to stall near a 90 degrees bend at station riley. the control system failed to detect the stall because the pressure transducer upstream of the launcher was calibrated for static pressure only and did not alarm on the transient pressure rise. as the pig remained lodged, downstream flow continued and pressure began to build in the isolated segment. after approximately eight minutes the pressure exceeded the pipe's burst pressure, reaching roughly 1600 psi. the sudden over-pressurization forced the pipe at the bend to rupture, releasing natural gas into the surrounding right-of-way. emergency shutdown valves (esdvs) downstream opened automatically, but the upstream esdv failed to close due to a faulty solenoid coil that had been replaced three weeks earlier without proper testing. the gas plume ignited when it encountered a nearby diesel generator, resulting in a flash fire that burned three crew members; two required hospitalization for smoke inhalation, and one sustained second-degree burns. the incident was contained after 45 minutes, and a post-event investigation was launched to address pig launch procedures, pressure monitoring, and esdv reliability.

NARRATIVE: during routine pigging of a 24-in. x-70 api 5l pipeline transporting 70 % crude and 30 % natural gas at 1 200 psi, the downstream pig trap was found empty. the control system indicated a pressure rise to 1 350 psi in the 0.5 mi segment upstream of the trap. operators initiated an emergency vent by opening the manual vent valve located on the pig receiver, but the valve failed to open due to corrosion-induced binding. after a 15-minute delay, a secondary vent line was opened, releasing the trapped pressure gradually. the sudden depressurization caused a 24-in. main door on the pig receiver to swing open with enough force to strike a maintenance technician standing nearby, resulting in a bruised ribcage. subsequent inspection revealed that the vent valve seat had accumulated scale and debris, preventing proper operation. the door latch mechanism was found to have excessive wear, reducing its holding capacity. the pipeline was shut down, the vent valve was disassembled, cleaned, and replaced, and the door latch was repaired with a new hydraulic clamp. after confirming all safety interlocks were functional, the line was repressurized and returned to service.

NARRATIVE: on 17 june 2025 at approximately 1415 hrs the control room received a low-pressure alarm on line 3, a 24-in api 5l x70 steel pipe transporting 1100 psig natural gas from the north field to the main hub. the alarm triggered an automatic shutdown of the upstream booster station, but the downstream valve failed to close due to a stuck actuator caused by a recent maintenance override that had not been fully re-qualified. as a result, gas continued to flow at reduced pressure (750 psig) into the downstream segment, creating a pressure differential that exceeded the design limits of a recent tie-in flange installed three months earlier. at 1428 hrs field crews arrived on site and observed a sudden release of vapor at the tie-in location near milepost 212.5. inspection revealed that the flange gasket had been improperly seated during the prior installation, leading to a rapid blow-by and a 12-ft long gas jet. the leak was isolated by manually closing the downstream isolation valve at 1442 hrs, and the area was ventilated. a temporary metal plug was installed while a replacement flange assembly was fabricated. after purging, pressure testing to 1500 psig, and coating verification, service was restored at 1730 hrs. the incident is under review to determine why the maintenance override documentation was incomplete and why the gasket installation did not meet the specification.

NARRATIVE: on 14 september 2024, personnel conducting routine pressure testing on a 24-inch carbon steel transmission line (api 5l x70) in the panhandle region of texas noticed a sudden drop in pressure from 950 psig to 720 psig within a few minutes. the line had been isolated and purged of gas, then filled with nitrogen to 1000 psig for the test. after the pressure loss was observed, the control room initiated a leak detection sequence and recorded a faint acoustic signal near milepost 212. a dive team was dispatched to the buried segment; divers inspected the pipe interior and found a small, irregularly shaped gouge approximately 0.03 in. wide near the 7-o'clock position, but no obvious external damage. subsequent magnetic flux leakage scanning of the surrounding right-of-way did not reveal any external corrosion or third-party intrusion. the incident was classified pending further analysis, with the probable cause attributed to a manufacturing defect in the pipe wall that manifested under high-pressure nitrogen testing. the line was depressurized, the damaged section was cut out, and a new 24-inch spool with matching wall thickness was installed using a field welding procedure. after hydrostatic testing to 1500 psig, the line was returned to service with no injuries, no environmental release, and minimal property impact.

NARRATIVE: at approximately 1430 hours on 22 july 2024, a transco maintenance crew was conducting a routine valve inspection on the 30-inch carbon steel transmission line (spec 30-h2) near milepost 87.3 in the foothills of the central valley. the crew noticed a faint odor of natural gas and a small sheen of oil on the right-of-way. visual inspection revealed a 2-inch gouge on the lower flange of a recently installed pressure regulator station that had been placed on a wooden cradle without the required steel support bracket. the missing bracket allowed the cradle to settle unevenly during a prior heavy rain event, causing the flange to flex and the weld to crack. the crew isolated the segment, depressurized the line from 720 psig to 0 psig, and reported the situation to transco operations control. emergency response was coordinated with the county fire department and the state oil and gas commission, which arrived on scene at 1505 hours. the damaged flange was removed, a new support bracket was fabricated and installed, and a full splice repair was completed by 1800 hours. no injuries occurred, gas release was limited to less than 0.05 mmcf, and the incident was logged as a non-release event. the investigation noted the omission of the bracket in the as-built drawing and prompted a review of all recent regulator installations for similar documentation gaps.

NARRATIVE: a routine inspection on the north ridge 12-inch carbon steel pipeline (design pressure 1 200 psi) identified an abnormal pressure drop downstream of a valve station. field engineers isolated the segment and performed a pig run using a magnetic flux leakage tool. the pig returned with indications of localized metal loss on a 24-inch tie-in branch that had been repaired two years earlier with a welded sleeve. however, the pig data did not reveal any clear defect. a handheld ultrasonic thickness gauge measured the wall thickness at the suspect area and showed a reduction of roughly 30 percent compared to the original specification. further visual examination required a hot-tap to expose the interior, revealing a corrosion pit that had propagated behind the sleeve, likely due to moisture trapped during the previous repair. the pit was approximately 3 inches deep and 6 inches long. the compromised section was cut out, a new 24-inch schedule 40 pipe segment was installed with a fully radiographed weld, and the sleeve was removed. additional cathodic protection was installed on the adjacent pipe runs, and the area was re-pressurized and monitored for 48 hours before returning to service.

NARRATIVE: the 30" x80 api 5l carbon steel transmission line crossing county road 112 experienced a sudden loss of pressure during a scheduled pigging run. the control room noted a drop from 840 psig to 610 psig within minutes and an automatic alarm triggered. field crews dispatched to the incident zone confirmed a faint hissing sound near the right-of-way, and a small vapor cloud was observed downwind. the segment was isolated by closing the nearest block valve at the 12.4 mile marker and the downstream valve at the 15.2 mile marker; the line was depressurized to atmospheric and purged with nitrogen. a visual inspection revealed a longitudinal crack originating from a girth weld on a 12-in schedule 40 elbow that had been installed two years earlier. the weld defect was attributed to a non-conforming filler material identified during post-weld radiography review. the affected section was cut out, a new 30" x80 api 5l pipe splice was fabricated and welded in place, and the weld was heat-treated in accordance with api 1104. after hydrostatic testing to 1.2x the maximum operating pressure (1000 psig), the line was returned to service. no injuries were reported, and the surrounding property owners were evacuated for 45 minutes as a precaution. the incident was logged with the state pipeline safety board and a corrective action plan was issued to audit all recent girth welds on similar segments.

NARRATIVE: during a scheduled integrity verification on 04/22/2024, a 24" api 5l x65 carbon steel transmission line operating at 950 psi was isolated and depressurized to 150 psi for inline inspection using a smart pig. after the pig was retrieved at the downstream pig trap, maintenance personnel opened the isolation valve to re-pressurize the line. an unexpected valve seat fracture occurred on the newly installed 1-inch manual shut-off valve, causing a rapid pressure surge that blew the valve body off its bonnet. a 3-inch vent stack released a white vapor cloud composed of residual natural gas and condensate, which drifted across the adjacent grassland and entered a nearby cattle feedlot, coating equipment and livestock pens. emergency shut-down was initiated within 45 seconds and the affected section was isolated. response teams contained the spill, removed the vapor-soaked feed, and decontaminated the area. the incident was reported to the nrc (event #1260457) at 13:22, with a 48-hour follow-up (event #1260602) logged at 15:48. investigation identified a manufacturing defect in the valve seat as the root cause and recommended replacement of all similar valve assemblies on the line, revision of post-pigging pressurization procedures, and additional non-destructive testing of valve components.

NARRATIVE: on september 3, 2025 at approximately 07:42 a.m., field operations received a low-pressure alarm from the 30-inch api 5l sch 40 steel main located 2.3 miles north of the silver ridge pumping station in cheyenne county, wyoming. the alarm was triggered after a routine pressure test on the adjacent 24-inch gas-oil pipeline, which was being pressurized to 950 psi. at 07:50 a.m. the control center dispatched a field crew and initiated an automatic isolation of the affected block valve (bv-12) and the upstream valve (bv-9). by 08:05 a.m. the crew arrived on scene, observed a small spray of natural gas near a weld joint at the 12-o'clock position of the pipe, and confirmed a leak rate of approximately 150 mcf/hr. emergency services were notified, and a hazmat team was on site by 08:30 a.m. the leak was contained by fully closing bv-9 and bv-12, and a hot-tapping crew installed a temporary repair clamp at 09:15 a.m. the pipeline was depressurized to 0 psi, purged, and later re-pressurized to 200 psi for testing. the incident was reported to the nrc and the state oil and gas commission. full restoration of service was achieved on september 5, 2025 at 14:20 after a permanent weld repair was completed and the line was pressure tested to 900 psi. the exact trigger for the weld failure remains under investigation.

NARRATIVE: on 3/7/25 at approximately 0830 hrs a 24-inch carbon steel transmission line (api 5l x70) located at milepost 112.4 experienced a sudden pressure drop from 820 psig to 340 psig during routine pigging operations. the pigging crew reported hearing a metallic "ping" as the smart pig entered the high-point section near the river crossing. visual inspection by the field team revealed a 4-inch longitudinal split in the pipe wall just downstream of the cathodic protection anode ring, which had been installed three years earlier. the split correlated with a previously undocumented change in pipe coating thickness; the original coating spec called for a 2-mil epoxy, but field notes indicated a 1-mil coat was applied during the 2022 retrofit. immediate isolation of the segment was achieved by closing the adjacent isolation valves (isolation valve a-112 and b-112). emergency response crews erected a temporary steel containment box and installed a 24-inch steel repair sleeve, secured with 4-bolt flange connections, to restore line integrity. after pressure testing to 900 psig, the line was returned to service at 750 psig. the incident was logged, and a review of all coating records was initiated to prevent recurrence.

NARRATIVE: on 6/3/24 at approximately 09:45 am the crew was performing a routine pressure test on a newly installed 30" api 5l x70 carbon steel line (design pressure 1500 psig) in the northern segment of the gulf coast mainline. after the line was pressurized to 1400 psig, a low-frequency vibration was noted at the 12-mile marker. inspection revealed that a 24-inch expansion joint installed two weeks earlier had been incorrectly oriented, causing the joint bellows to be exposed to axial load beyond its rated limit. the mis-alignment produced a hairline crack in the bellows housing which was not detected during the initial hydrostatic test. the line was immediately depressurized to 200 psig and isolated with a double block and bleed. the expansion joint was removed, the bellows replaced, and a proper torque sequence was applied per the manufacturer's installation guide. the incident was reported to the operations manager, j. rodriguez, and the engineering lead, s. patel, who initiated a design review of all recent expansion joint installations. a corrective action plan was issued on 6/5/24 requiring additional verification steps for joint orientation and a supplemental training session for field crews. the line was returned to service at 1200 psig on 6/7/24 after successful leak-free testing.

NARRATIVE: on august 14, 2023, at approximately 18:45 local time, the oak ridge compression station experienced an unplanned vent of natural gas from unit three. the station was operating at a discharge pressure of 960 psig on a 24-inch api 5l carbon steel pipeline, with unit three running at 78% turbine speed. a routine pressure check by the control room operator showed a gradual rise in suction pressure to 420 psig, exceeding the normal range of 350-380 psig. the alarm for high suction pressure triggered, and the operator initiated an immediate shutdown sequence. however, the suction vent valve remained partially open, resulting in a continuous low-rate release estimated at 1.8 mmscfd. emergency response crews were dispatched at 19:10 and arrived on site at 19:45, where they confirmed a visible gas plume extending approximately 150 feet downwind of the station. the vent valve was manually closed, and the station was placed in a safe state. gas loss calculations later indicated that the 3-hour release threshold of 3 mmscfd had been exceeded. a preliminary investigation revealed that the valve actuator had suffered corrosion damage to its hydraulic piston seal, likely due to prolonged exposure to moisture during recent rain events. the seal failure prevented the valve from fully seating. the incident was reported to the nrc, and a corrective action plan was issued to replace the affected actuator, install additional moisture monitoring sensors, and update maintenance procedures to include quarterly hydraulic seal inspections.

NARRATIVE: on 4/22/2025 a routine inline inspection was scheduled on the 24-inch carbon steel transmission line (api 5l x70, design pressure 1500 psi) that runs from the petrochemical complex near houston to the coastal storage terminal. the pigging crew had completed the launch when a subcontractor's back-hoe, working on a nearby storm-drain project, inadvertently struck a buried fiber-optic cable that was co-located with the emergency shutdown (esd) valve actuator. the impact sheared the cable, causing a short circuit that forced the esd valve to open automatically. natural gas at approximately 1300 psi was released from the 24-inch main into the surrounding low-lying grassland. at the same time, a welder from the same subcontractor was performing hot-work on a steel support structure 30 ft away. the released gas found the ignition source and a brief flame front developed, producing a visible fireball that burned for about 30 seconds before being extinguished by the facility fire-water system. local fire-rescue units arrived within 8 minutes; no injuries were reported, and the fire was fully contained. the incident was logged as a "significant event" and reported to the phmsa and ferc under the appropriate reporting thresholds.
